en: Example of Piedmontese architecture of the eighteenth century.

Invaded built between 1963 and 1968, with 163.6 hectares of surface, which irrigates the plain of Partinico and supplies Palermo; since 1994 it is Oasis of protection and shelter of the fauna on 580 hectares.
A nineteenth-century science cabinet remained intact.

The fortified walls were built by the Caetani at the end of the 13th century, with nine towers and three gates; inside, winding alleys and narrow stairs, on a hill surrounded by the woods of the Lepini.
The main church of the center.

Since 1936 in the eighteenth-century palace De Nicastri-Cavalli, in the historic center; dedicated to archaeology and the history of the city, with objects often exposed without cases, specialized library and workshop for restoration of the finds. Closed on Mondays; audioguide available.
A monumental complex not known of the extensive countryside.
Remains of a Roman villa at the opposite end of the gulf, on a natural terrace overlooking the sea.
Mantua before Gonzaga.
The most beautiful Romanesque of Lunigiana, with medieval beast capitals.
On the trail of the holy missionary of the country.
A private picture gallery on Silence Bay.

Variant of the Francigena between Pistoia and Bologna, quoted around 1250 by the abbot Migliore. The didactic route from Pàvana to the Castello di Sambuca (CAI 163 trail) is about 2.4 km long, with 254 m of difference in altitude and average slope of 10.4%, about an hour of walk on a 2.20 m wide pavement; passes through La Capanna, mentioned in the cadastre of 1587. Along the way many houses carry ancient masks carved in stone.
The prehistory of Beigua in a small village museum.
The college baroque.
The church that houses some of the most beautiful paintings of the seventeenth century Rimini, including the Pala dei Carmelitani by Guido Cagnacci.
today hotel with congress center according to the card of the City: visit of the interiors to be verified
The octagonal baptistery in Verona pink marble started by Benedetto Antelami in 1196, with statues of the months and sculpted portals; next, the cathedral museum.
A frescoed Romanesque parish, the historic heart of the village.

Inside the walls of the castle of Cornacuna in Fiordimonte, of which remain a stretch and the entrance portal: church to a nave oriented to the north for defensive needs, with stone portal and coat of arms; on the background wall of frescoes by Girolamo di Giovanni of 1456, restored in 1992-93, and a fresco of 1613 attributed to Peregrino di Milano.
The square of historic pasta factories.

It was built by the Normans between the 10th and 11th centuries against Saracens and pirates and was also the residence of the monks of the Abbey of Tremiti, and Frederick II added the tower called imperial rock and baronial enclosure, and in the eighteenth century it was rebuilt in its present form. It is privately owned, but you can visit the dungeons, once prisons and weapons depots, with instruments of torture from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance, and a small terraced garden on the sea.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 7 of the 14 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

The parish church, at the top of a staircase, was built in the early eighteenth century at the behest of Antonio Genta; the interior decorations are from 1875 and the ceiling is made of wooden boards. The Oratory of Santa Croce, the ancient parish church of the 11th century, is attached to it, which preserves on the façade some hanging arches, with a sixteenth-century bell tower in Lombard style.
The lava organ cannae in the centre.
The Byzantine rite in Calabria.
The King's Alps.

Reserve of 21 hectares established in 2000 and managed by Legambiente Sicilia: it protects the Grotto of Sant'Angelo Muxaro, also called Cave Ciavuli, in total 1,760 meters long on two branches and reached by the entrance hall with an almost flat path, and the Infantino Hooker, with a vertical well of about 10 meters. Host amphibians, reptiles and bats.

The gulf stretches between the tip of Ranco and the tip of the Fornace of Ispra and is indicated as the only extended stretch of coast of Lake Maggiore facing north. It is one of the few stretches of shore far from large roads and railways, little inhabited, with dense vegetation, numerous erratic boulders, low and sandy seabeds and morainic deposits. The Verbano Trail, cycle path between Ispra, Angera and Sesto Calende, crosses Ranco. Free access.
The medieval castle overlooking the sea.

The village is walled on the northern shore of Trasimeno, dominated by the medieval fortress with a 32-metre tower and the Boat Museum; on the lakefront the boats leave for the islands, and in the hilly hamlet of Castel Rigone stands the Renaissance Sanctuary of the Madonna dei Miracoli.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione dell'Ovadese gathered around the 12th century castle and its tower, between Dolcetto d'Ovada and white truffle.

Horse-iron square with aerial balustrade and marble monument to Pope Pius VI, overlooking the Georgica Academy and the Town Hall; from here the view extends over hills and fields and, on clear days, up to Mount Conero and the sea. The village preserves walls of the thirteenth century and towers.
Neoclassical palace of 1781 by Francesco Schiavi with frescoes by Giovanni Battista Canal with the Liberated Jerusalem and mythological stories.

The most famous commercial gallery in Italy, neo-Renaissance, among the great examples of iron architecture: cross plan, Octagono with dome of 47 meters, 250 meters between Duomo and Scala; you can also walk on the rooftops.
The Ventimiglia fortress on the highest point.
The original landscape of the Gold Conca.
A Visconti castle became a country villa of the Trivulzio.
The tower on a rocky promontory in Caprona, remembered by Dante in the Comedy.

On a plateau above the Tiber Valley, the excavations of the University of Perugia since 1995 have brought to light a sanctuary of the fourth century BC and above it a factory of sealed earth, lamps and bricks of the end of the first century BC, whose signed vases were found throughout the Mediterranean; excavated about 2,000 m2 with potters' posts, clay processing areas and furnaces. The area was then inhabited until the fourth century AD.

Wanted by the legacy of Benedetto Rizzo of 1497 and consecrated in 1505, it was officiated for about two centuries by the Servants of Mary; reduced between 1786 and 1792 by Count Orio, it preserves the golden wooden main altar with the altarpiece of Paolo Ongaretto, a wooden statue of St. Prosdocimo, a Crucifixion of 1828 and the tomb of the family Orio in sacristy.
Sea and seabed of the Tyrrhenian Sea.

The Sala delle Lance retains the prizes won by the four districts in the editions of the Sarapino Giostra, a joke version of the Saracino di Arezzo born in the post-war period, in which the horse is replaced by an Ape car; also exhibited the costumes of the participants, the accessories of the carousel and works of the local craftsmanship.

Castle-fortress built in 1320 by the Counts Cepollini, lords of Alto and Caprauna, on a spur above the Val Pennavaire; the wing towards the valley with the loggia is of the fifteenth century. Plucked and partly destroyed by the French in 1796, at the end of the nineteenth century it was transformed with the lowering of the towers and a layered roof, under which remain the Ghibelline blackbirds. Visits only by reservation.

Medieval village at 676 meters between the streams Volvara, Tassaro and Scalucchia, feud of Dalla Palude that held the salt warehouses, reached by an ancient via matildica selciata still existing; it preserves a sixteenth-century tower house and portals of the sixteenth-sixth century. Nearby is a monumental chestnut, among the oldest in the province.
The sea of Pisticci.
The majolica bell tower.
You visit with the archaeologists who dug it.
A one-way village.

The village, about 500 meters away, is said by La mia Liguria \'il borgo della luce Â" and offers a 360 degree panorama of mountains, valleys and sea; there you climb from Chiusavecchia among dry walls with age-old olive trees of Taggiasca. The Baroque parish church of 1688 has frescoed interiors, a marble altar attributed to G. Door and B. Stella and an organ of G. Cavalli di Lodi; nearby remain the ruins of the feudal castle of the twelfth century, linked to the Ventimiglia. It was a feud of the Counts of Ventimiglia and Lascaris, passed to the Savoys in 1575 and became an autonomous municipality in 1688.
The Greek vases of the necropolis of Polizzi.
Genoa seen from above.

The fountain was built in Florence in 1554 by the sculptor Francesco Camilliani for the garden of Don Luigi di Toledo and arrived in Palermo in 1574, bought by the Senate; groups of river gods, tritons, nereids and mermaids in Carrara marble. The square is closed by Palazzo Pretorio, Santa Caterina and the Bonocore and Bordonaro palaces.
An open-air museum in the mountains.

Among the oldest buildings in the village, the former Benedictine church of the abbey of Farfa built between the XI and XII century, until the Napoleonic edict was also a cemetery inside the walls. Inside, restored, cross vaults and altar in a high arched gallery on two slender octagonal columns; outside two travertine grifos hold the architrave of the portal.
The stables built for Cosimo I around 1548 by the Tribolo, today exhibition center with library and the Ardengo Soffici Museum and of the Italian twentieth century.
The matrix reborn after 1783.
On the slopes of Monte Marone, the cylindrical tower bears witness to the Arab domination; next to it stands the Convent of the Capuchins.

18th century (first stone in 1729), with monumental façade, dome of 18 meters of diameter and floor in white Carrara marble and Bardiglio; at the altar of the Blessed Sacrament the Last Romanino Supper (about 1542). Free admission every day.
The first sure work of Pordenone.
It dates back to the year 1000 and preserves the reliquary case of San Grato, the pavement mosaics and the frescoes of the attic.

Built in 1716 by Cardinal Acquaviva, abbot of Santa Maria d'Altofonte, and relocated in 1824 by the Baron Mayor of Leccia: in carved marble, it has a rectangular tank, eight cinnamons, four Latin inscriptions and the cardinal's coat of arms, with fence and liberty cast iron lamps.
The relics of the Passion.
Baths and walks in the woods just a stone's throw from the vineyards.
The most famous square-chessboard in Italy.
private residence, visits only by reservation for groups and schools of at least 15 people

Borgo dell'Alto Monferrato between Acqui and Ovada: the castle was born as a watchtower around the Mille, with the octagonal tower of the fourteenth century, the Romanesque oratory in the shelter, the ancient parish church of San Martino among the vineyards and the ethnographic museum of the peasant civilization.
Romanesque church of the thirteenth century along the Sambro, with sailing bell tower and porch on the façade; in the Middle Ages it was used as a lazzaretto.
From 2 December 2025 some rooms are closed for works and only the reduced rate applies
The skeleton of a Byzantine church in the country.
from November to March open only by reservation for guided tours (MiC)
The birthplace of the saint of flights, destination of pilgrims.
The village of red marble.
Asia in the Quadrilateral.
Guided tours in the underground city, which preserves the remains of the Roman viaduct with which the via Salaria exceeded the Velino's full to enter the city.
The sacred art of the valley.
Hiking or mountain biking that starts from the village and touches the most characteristic farms, scattered on the sunny and sweet slope above Sant'Orsola.
The manor of the marquises who dominated the upper valley.

Underground gallery of about one kilometer excavated in the galena line of the Arburese and Guspinese, up to the well Sant'Antonio, begun in 1852 by the Royal Anglo-Sardinian Company from which it takes its name. Guided tour of about 40 minutes; constant internal temperature of 15-16 °C, recommended closed and low shoes. From November to March Saturday and Sunday a departure at 13:15, on the other days by reservation; ticket office in Montevecchio, 15 minutes before.
Fenoglio's house.
A glimpse of the Costa degli Dei.
On the trail of Buzzati.

In the medieval village the Church of Santa Caterina has a Romanesque portal and a marble statue of the saint; the fourteenth-century Church of the Holy Spirit is located at Porta Giovan Guerino. In via Mastropaolo you can see the Baroque portals of Casa Messina-Ballarino, carved in the seventeenth century by Isardi from Naples, and Casa Mastropaolo; among the points of interest are the fountain of Gattuso, "u roggiu" (a fountain of Gattuso).

In Villa Mainona (1670-1672) in Tremezzo, it collects ancient prints of the lake from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century, historical photographs between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, a multimedia system with maps and a section on the films shot on the lake. Open from Easter to the end of October, Thursday-Sunday, 10-12 and 14-18.

On a panoramic hill overlooking the valley of the Trigno, in Calcatello, it was the main place of worship of the Sanniti Pentri and the political center of the confederation, the most important place of worship of the Sanniti state. Between the third and first centuries B.C., the Samnites built a smaller temple on the remains of a building destroyed by the Carthaginians of Hannibal (beginning of the second century B.C., the podium remains), the major temple completed at the beginning of the first century B.C. with its imposing podium and semicircular cavea known as the Theatre of the end of the second century B.C., probably destined for assemblies and particularly well preserved. In 2002 on the south-west terrace was identified the Domus publica, probably the seat of the supreme Sannite magistrate; the excavations are still ongoing. Hours indicated by the Regional Direction Museums: Tuesday-Sunday 8.45-19.15, last entrance 30 minutes before closing, Monday closed.
Along the rus.

On the Langfenn, the highest point of the Salto plateau, at 1,525 m and visible from afar, rises on a land frequented already in prehistoric times; next to St. James, patron saint of the wayfarers, the altar with Saints Rocco and Sebastiano. You can reach it by car from the Schermoos car park or by bus 204 and 157.

Medieval village on a hill just over 200 meters, with the districts of Terranova and Terravecchia, walls, Clock Tower and the terrace of Fortellezza, and a hamlet to the sea with more than three kilometers of sandy beach several times Blue Flag; in Tortoreto Lido the Roman villa of the Muracche.
caves for speleologists: no access information for the public in the source

It comes from the chapel of the castle ...Santa Maria di Conzano, mentioned at the end of the XII century; the building and the Romanesque bell tower are of the fifteenth century, consecration in 1843 and last renovation in 1904. Frescoes by Luigi Faini, four tables of a sixteenth-century polyptych dismembered by the Spanish school (San Maurizio, Santa Caterina, Santo Stefano, Santa Lucia) and the altarpiece of Santa Lucia in 1862.

Crotti, natural cellars at constant temperature under the rocks on the left bank of Mera, used since ancient times to age the wine and season cold cuts and cheeses, today partly in taverns; the square with plane trees and nineteenth century hippocastans hosts in September the Festival of Crotti.
The largest ethnographic collection of Friuli Venezia Giulia.
Walk or cycle for miles.

Built in 1200 on a building perhaps of the VIII-IX century and collegiate since 1353: portal of Raimondo di Poggio (1326), fifteenth-century portico, 47-metre bell tower, wooden ceiling with coffers, frescoes fourteenth-century attributed to the Master of Offida, wooden statue of St. Michael of the fourteenth century and seventeenth-century choir.
The works saved from the rubble, again on display.
private property, visitable only on telephone agreement with the owner

Built between 1247 and 1303, it preserves the Romanesque-Gothic style outside; the portal of 1303 is now in sacristy, while the restorations between the mid-sixteenth and mid-eighteenth centuries gave the Baroque look inside.
Three orders of nineteenth-century stages.
Medieval village born as a fortified castle in the thirteenth century; its tower has become the bell tower of the church of San Biagio.
The heart of the city.
A rare architecture of river navigation.
The peasant tools in an eighteenth-century mill.
Remains of temples, theatres, agora and necropolis of the Greek city.

Medieval village on the south-eastern side of Montiferru, known for the weaving of carpets and the processing of knives, boots and saddles. The trail of the sources touches Silbanis, the old wash-house on Sauccu and the park of Funtana longa; the panoramic terrace of Sa Rocca has a statue of the Christ of Edgardo Mugnoz. At Carnival Via Roma hosts the horse race of Sa Carrela 'and Nanti, at the end of August the Ardia of San Lussorio around the parish of San Pietro.
View from Etna to the Aeolian Islands.
Medieval frescoes in the rock above the sea.

The ancient entrance of the city from the pier, between the columns of San Teodoro and San Marco, the loggias of Palazzo Ducale and the Marciana Library; at the bottom the Clock Tower with the Moors beating the bell.
By bike along the leonardic canal.
the interior frescoes are visible only to some visitors according to In Lombardia
The ruins of a residence of the judges of Gallura among the granite boulders.

The seat of the most important sanctuary of the Siculi, dedicated to the Palici brothers, the sons of Zeus and the nymph Talia, excavated since 1995 and opened to the public since 2006. In front of the cave at the foot of the hill of Rocchicella remain the structures of the sanctuary, with a terrace accommodation of the fifth century BC with a building for banquets and two arcades; on the top the remains of a city of the fourth century BC. Open from Monday to Friday 8.30-13.30.
The legend of oak and tin.

Itinerary of the Municipality from Piazza Plebiscito, with the fountain of 1898 and the church of San Giovanni Battista (formerly Dominican convent, relics of San Felice), on Via De Petra with registered houses, carved balconies, a bifora of the thirteenth century and a Roman column, the Palazzo De Petra and the sixteenth-century palace with loggia, up to Corso Vittorio Emanuele with the church of San Nicola, ex-grancia of the Knights of Malta where Celestino V and Carlo II d'Angiò stayed, and the fountain "Ace of cups"; then the remains of Roman villas and baths and the bridge of the Maddalena.
High ground and untouched nature.
the MiC card says it is closed every day; check at 0423 482072
Ring of about three hours without any particular difficulty, between waterfalls, walkways and wooden bridges.

Pieve attested in 1290, renewed and erected as collegiate by Pope Urban VIII in 1635; on the singing hall above the entrance an organ of 1776 Gaetano Callido, the greatest exponent of the eighteenth-century Venetian organ school.
The oldest church, rebuilt by a glassmaker.
The botanical garden of the University of Parma in the Farini street, part of the university museum system, with greenhouses and plant collections.

Belvedere on the valley reachable with a walk, linked to the story of the late nineteenth century Polish musician Maximilian Prihoda and his painter wife, who here threw themselves together into the void.
Just outside the walls, in the historic gardens of the Bourbon Palace of the Mount, a stone polished in the shape of a plate where according to legend the witches celebrated their sabba.
The castle is only visited with guided tours on established days; the museum is open from 22 March to 15 November 2026
Remains of the bridge of the Roman city of Iulia Concordia, recorded by the Ministry of Culture.
Our Lady of Capo Colonna.
Sunny village among orchards and vineyards of the Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle, restored in the original architecture, with Châtelard castle and frescoed chapels.
To learn about the secrets of dams and hydroelectric power plants.
The glacier falls.
The memory of a mountain Waldensian country.
Walking and cycling routes of different difficulty between vineyards and agricultural villages.
The 14th-century crypt.
€7 whole / €5 reduced
The cannob's gorge.

The territory is part of the Montecucco denomination (red, Sangiovese, white and Vermentino); wines and oils are tasted in companies and cellars along the Montecucco Wine and Flavour Trail, and at the end of September-early October the Grape Festival brings the parade of the floats of the three districts and the open cellars.
Understand the battle of the Tagliamento of 1917.
Sulphure waters with approximately 1 mg/l of hydrogen sulphide, indicated by the Common for liver, bile, stomach and bowel.
private property used for hospitality, internal visit not guaranteed
How the Stone of Luserna was hand-crushed.
Aragonese castle in red stone on the island of Sant'Andrea, overlooking the port.

Among the most important mining areas of Tyrol in the Middle Ages, closed at the beginning of the twentieth century and recovered by local associations: 16 galleries for about 20 km, for two thirds excavated by hand, from which were extracted silver, galena, copper and blend, advancing 8-12 meters per year. Guided tour of the Elisabeth gallery (about 1 and a half hours) and, on Wednesdays in July and August, of the Elisabeth and Lorenz galleries (about 2 and a half hours).

The philosopher Giambattista Vico lived in Palazzo Vargas in Vatolla from 1686 to 1695, as tutor of the grandchildren of Monsignor Rocca, and spent the study days there. The palace is home to the Giambattista Vico Foundation, which houses the Library of the Park and a museum dedicated to the philosopher in the place where he lived for nine years; in the courtyard of the castle is held every summer the Festa della Cipolla.
Calette and cliffs of the Riviera dei Cedri.
The cathedral rebuilt in the nineteenth century with the chapel of the patron saint: the xylography escaped the fire of 1428 and the dome frescoed by Carlo Cignani.

Started at the end of the sixteenth century as the church of St. Ignatius of the Jesuit complex on a project by Father Giovanni de Rosis, remained empty after the suppression of the Jesuits (1773), since 1796 it is Collegiate and has welcomed many works of the demolished parish church of St. Stephen; the facade has remained unfinished. It preserves a Martyrdom of Santo Stefano attributed to the school of Pomarancio and an organ Bazzani of 1848; the Chapel of the Peasants has the walls frescoed by Benedetto Biancolini with scenes of life and rural devotion.
Spa resort of Val di Lima, frequented by Shelley and Byron.
the site of the municipality indicates the museum as temporarily closed
The theatre above the Castles.
The starting point for the trails of the Valle del Giovenco.

Country of the upper Camonica Valley at the foot of Adamello, in the Pontedilegno-Tonale area; to see the White War Museum in Adamello, the parish church of San Bartolomeo, the small churches of Sant'Alessandro and Santa Giulia and the Val d'Avio, the largest valley of the Adamello Park.
Included in the visit to the Duomo
Arezzo before the Middle Ages.
The oldest nucleus, animated by saints and living nativity scenes.
The fifteen arches bridge.
A live village.
Country of ceramics that climbs inland from the coast, with the Roman remains at the station, the medieval nucleus on the Riobasco, the Eugenio Montale promenade and the Manlio Trucco museum.

On Mount Sovero, at 954 meters, it dominates the valley; a chapel is attested already in the sixteenth century, while the current church was built from 1779 to 1783 after the pilgrimage that, according to tradition, ended the great drought of 1779. Among the customs of pilgrims, drink from the well of miracles and ring the big bell; the feast is celebrated from 1780 on the day of the Most Holy Trinity.
An hour along the lake.
The flavors of the lake.
Built between 1490 and 1494, it houses works by Perugino.
Medieval frescoes and an underground under the floor.

The San Nicolò Museum offers a wide view of the daily life of the peasants of the valley. Open approximately from mid-May to late October in the afternoon (in 2026 from 17 May to 25 October, 14.30-17.30); guided tours on request.

On a hill near the village, the ruins of a center lived between the 8th and the 3rd century B.C. on the border between the Sican and the Punic-Elimo world, then Carthaginian fortress: necropolis with chamber and chest tombs, walls with the South and North gates, a sacred area with betiles, a tripartite temple on the acropolis and a Hellenistic sanctuary of Demeter and Kore. Open every day 9-17.30.

Set up in the sixteenth-century forge of Sarezzo, it offers a museum and ecomuseum itinerary on the Valtrumpline traditions of iron: the "Sala Magli" with three great sweaters and, on the first floor, the Sanzogni collection of tools of the local blacksmiths and the Pellegrini collection with over 200 scientific instruments of the twentieth century; children's games retracing the cycle of metal. It is the first stage of the "Via del Ferro e delle Miniere" in the Valle Trompia Eco-Museum.

Liberty-style villas built between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries by prominent architects, testimony of the period tourism that made Bratto-Dorga a holiday destination from the beginning of the century.
Nobile architecture of vanvitellian school.

Park established in 1984 on about 1,200 hectares, with nature trails in the valleys; the path of the Biedano Gorges is dedicated to the ancient stone millstones along the river. In the equipped area of the Caiolo (parking, tables, barbecue, fountain) starts the visit to the necropolis; visitor center and naturalistic museum 100 meters before the entrance of the village.

On September 27, 1917 the Austro-Hungarian troops bombed the country and the fire that followed destroyed much of the town. A multimedia itinerary with QR code in the historic centre shows what the town was like before and after the bombing and reconstruction project; the center, pedestrian and crossed by small wooden bridges, revolves around Piazza XXVII September.
A 14th-century chapel became a library.
The turquoise blue of one of the deepest karst springs in Europe.

About 5 km of equipped pebble beach, with free beach stretches and music and festivals in the establishments; according to recent findings the hamlet was a Roman settlement, perhaps a changed on the coastal road.

In the Oratory of the Rosary, Dominican building of the eighteenth century, 31 works of the collection of Giovanni Spano (1803-1878), donated to the church of San Pietro in 1873, including a San Domenico of 1340-1350 attributed to Francesco Neri of Volterra, a Madonna with Child and Saints attributed to Domenico of Michelino, the Stimitates of San Francesco attributed to Pietro Cavaro and a Holy Family of the Master of Ozieri; 29 other works are in the Rectoral House. Guided visits with the curator only, by telephone reservation.
Former fishermen's vote.
The Blue Flag sea with views of the island.
Chamois, prehistory and flora of Majella on one visit.
The viewpoint on the two lakes.

Ceramics, sculptures, coins, votive objects and instruments of the Greek colony founded in the 7th century BC, in chronological order from the traces of the Bronze and Iron Ages to the Roman conquest.
The grand duke's winter hunting chimneys.
Part of the sight of the square.
Royal eagles and griffons on limestone walls.

What remains of the grandiose parish designed by Alessandro Antonelli, the author of the Mole di Torino, which had to be almost as big as St. Peter: the works, begun in 1842, stopped in 1846 due to lack of funds. The circular perimeter walls in stones of the Orco and Piova streams are still alternated with red bricks, which in summer frame the Ceramics Exhibition.

Medieval castle, once among the most important garrisons of the area: the imposing remains are restored and the pentagonal tower is the core of the defensive system. It houses art exhibitions and the route of the Museo del Territorio della Riserva, in five rooms with plastic and reconstructions, from the history of the Peligni to the Middle Ages to the popular traditions.

Created by Andrea De Bernardin at the foot of the Marmolada and then expanded, he tells the White War on the front of the Marmolada with well-preserved Italian and Austro-Hungarian relics, largely returned by the glacier in retreat; he has a bookstore on the war in the mountains and a room for vintage films.

Free pebble and sandy beach about 150 meters long, with a large lawn and a pier, awarded with the Blue Flag FEE 2023-2024. Kiosk bar open from May to September, toilets and showers, lifeguard on weekends; always open and accessible by wheelchair.
The house where Petrarca spent the last few years, with a view of the Euganean Hills.
Nature intact in the Friulan Dolomites Park.
Under Piazza Cesare Battisti, born in the 1930s, by cutting down the ancient district of the "giro al sas," you can visit the Roman city of Tridentum.
Art and landscape together.

The ancient center stretches on the slope of a green valley surrounded by beech woods and secular chestnut groves; born from the Arab settlement, it is cited as an example of Arab-Turkish urbanism in Calabria, and there are relived ancient crafts and rural traditions.
The river and the Picena countryside told the kids.
17th century church of Gothic architecture that houses the diocesan museum, with liturgical vestments, sacred silvers and a 17th century crucifix used for Holy Week.

He exhibited the works of the Veronese painter Pino Casarini, who donated his collection to the parish of Sacile in two films (1982 and 1988): paintings, drawings and sketches for the settings of the Verona Arena, covering about fifty years of activity, from 1920 to 1970. Open on the first and third Sundays of the month 10-12; on the other days on request, with mandatory booking (tel. 0434 780702).
Airons and cranes in Italy's largest inland marsh.
18th century bridge on the Adda through which you enter the historic center.
The Byzantine domes of the ancient abbey.

Neoclassical villa (formerly Villa Isimbardi, today hotel) with terrace garden connected by a staircase and rare plants. In 1839, the musician Fanny Mendelssohn, Felix's sister, was guest; in 1838 the painter Eduard Gurk portrayed the procession of Emperor Ferdinand I who left the villa on the steamer Lario. From 1 November 2026 to 10 January 2027 the garden houses the Villa Cipressi Christmas Garden.
A pleasant center of historic cafés and seventeenth-century churches, on the ascent to the castle.
To walk into a UNESCO heritage Longobard fortress.
Route on the old railway path along the coast to Bonassola and Levanto; from the station an elevator descends to the marina.
The castle symbol of the village.
A fortress suspended on the rock.
Villas and gardens on the lake.
At the highest point of the country, it takes its name from the first lords of Ottone and was residence of the Doria until 1797; it is privately owned.
The biggest barrel in Europe.

Monotorre in large blocks of limestone, probably of the middle Bronze (XVII-XIV century B.C.), about 1,000 meters on the slopes of Mount Tonneri, about 13 km from the village: remain the lower floor with a tholos vault and the helical staircase; around the traces of an antemural with secondary towers, huts, a village, the remains of a tomb of giants. It is visible from a panoramic road; near the fortified village of Serra on Casteddu.

Museum path that tells the hidden history of the basilica, built on the tomb of the Olbian martyrs and became the cathedral of the ancient diocese of Civita; underground there emerged a temple dedicated to the cult of Ceres and numerous burials. Monday-Saturday 10-17, guided tours; entrance fee.

Mountain town of Val di Susa at the foot of the Rocciamelone (3538 m), with the hamlets along the Cenischia stream and over thirty villages on the slopes; from the sanctuary of Pietrastretta starts the mule track for the summit, where stands the highest sanctuary in Europe, and along the road there are pre-Roman rock carvings.
The largest archaeological museum in Italy north of Rome, with the Chimera di Arezzo, the Arringatore and the second collection of Italian Egyptians after Turin.

Church of thirteenth-century origin several times renovated, with bell tower in low and thick stone and facade of the twenties of the twentieth century; in the single nave with neo-Gothic trusses a Madonna del Rosario with Saints Gregorio Pagani (1597) and a relief in majolica of Robbiano style with the Madonna, the Child and St. John.
One of the great archaeological museums of the Mediterranean.
The manor from which the country takes its name.
The goddess back from Malibu.
A little church on a Roman altar.
The last island of the Cimbri.

In the historic center around Piazza Regina Margherita, born in the area liberated after the demolition of the walls in 1884: every morning fruits, vegetables and the fish market, the city's landmark. Open Monday to Saturday 6:30-13.
It goes with the Tieni Tower, ex customs extense on the Po di Volano.
The earthquake of 1783 told inside its ruins.
Small village at 1373 meters at the foot of the Comba di Bosses, on the Via Francigena towards the Gran San Bernardo.
A medieval castle intact at the gates of Bolzano.
Ruins of a fortified high medieval nucleus among the pine trees of the homonymous hill.

The polygonal walls of the 4th century B.C. develop for about 6 km and are among the largest in the italic world; the monumental Gate of the Arch was one of the three main gates of the ancient city and introduces to the historical center, where you can also see Roman tombs and inscriptions re-used in the buildings.

Stele with the star of David for the 28 foreign Jews interned in the village from 1940 to 1944, including Grete Bloch, friend of Kafka, and actress Grete Berger: on April 6, 1944 sixteen were deported to Auschwitz and only four survived. The memorial was inaugurated on 27 January 2023.
The heart of the Brandolini manor.
The castle in the heart of the city.

16th-century villa Corner-Tiepolo, Chiminelli today: in the western neighbourhoods more than one hundred tools and machines of the Bassanese tanneries, in the barchess more than 2,000 objects on life and work in the Venetian countryside of the past.

Lake north of the Lario between Verceia and Novate Mezzola, with an unusual mild climate for an Alpine valley: calm waters for kayak, canoeing, stand-up paddle, rowing and boat trips, a bike path along the shore between the two villages and reeds towards the mouth of Mera. From Novate you can reach the Romanesque temple of San Fedelino by boat.

Borgo della Riviera di Levante among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with its ancient nucleus around the church of Sant'Antonio Abate, two towers against pirates, the long beach between the cliffs and the inland paths.
A little church on the lake.
The finds of the Greek colony, from prehistory to the sea.
Of the original church remain the bell tower and a single chapel, entirely frescoed in the fifteenth century; fifteenth century is also the entrance portal of the cemetery.
From Neolithic to nuraghi in a few kilometers.
The parish museum.
The highest destination reachable from Anterivo, with refreshment at altitude.
The sculptor of the village in his church-museum.
Inside the galleries of medieval miners.

Established in 2006, it includes the Island of Sant'Andrea, flat limestone island with the only nesting colony of seagull run on the Adriatic and Ionic coasts of Italy, and the coast of Punta Pizzo with Mediterranean maquis, gariga, orchids (including the rare Orchis italica) and wetlands near the channel Li Foggi, stop of migratory birds.
Necropolis dated between 3200 and 2800 B.C.
The cathedral with its roots in the 6th century, remodeled in neoclassical forms in the 18th century, with seven frescoed domes, the Romanesque crypt and the Annunciation Pala of Tiziano.

"Casteddu," the Pisan-fortified neighborhood on a limestone hill overlooking the sea: narrow streets remained almost unchanged, artisan workshops, churches, historical buildings, towers and bastions with 360 degrees views of the city.
The golden baroque of the mother church.
On the temple of Jupiter.
A Roman town in the countryside.

The village of stone at the foot of Monte Bracco, the "Montagna di Leonardo": the historic center with the castle above Piazza della Madonna, the Baroque parish church of San Giovanni Battista, the ethnographic museum La Brunetta and the former railway workshop of the Barge-Bricherasio line.
The ornaments of women from the upper Sele Valley.
The sea view.
In Covarey, with an interactive naturalistic museum on rocky environments, wetlands and forests.
A fifteenth-century church on the road to Memmo.

City of the Murge with the Norman-Svevo castle that houses the National Archaeological Museum and, a few kilometers away, the archaeological park of Monte Sannace, center peucetius flowered between the VI and III century BC.
The Capestrano Warrior live.
The fortress above the Brenta.
The viewpoint on the bastions.

Built between 1893 and 1898 on a project by Guido Quercioli and dedicated to the Immaculate Basilica since 1980: facade in Mendicino stone with statues of Ernesto Biondi, two 31-metre bell towers and 35-metre dome, bronze door, a single nave of about 50 meters with a frescoed vault by Vincenzo Montefusco and organ of about 3,000 reeds; in the chapel the bronze urn of Blessed Angel.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione on Lake Maggiore, last before Switzerland, with the fourteenth-century nucleus of Palazzo della Ragione and the sanctuary of Pietà on the lakefront.
after the earthquake of 2016 municipal museums are partially usable (Let's Marche)
private house, visit to be arranged with the Pro Loco
Fashion and costume in the villa.
A parish church of early medieval origin.

The municipality of Brianza sul Seveso, on the edge of the Groane Park, which preserves two fourteenth-century oratories linked to the Porro family, Santo Stefano with the cycle on the life of the saint and Santa Maria di Mocchirolo, as well as the MuDi with the civic naturalistic collection and the Lake Azzurro in the park.
The last village under the rock spires.
The living room of the village overlooking the lake, with the Palazzotto of 1582, seat of the Community of the Riviera of San Giulio.

Geosite recognized in 2005 after twenty years of studies at the University of Zurich, among the sites in the world that mark a geological limit: in 2009 on the bed of Caffaro was placed the golden nail that marks the border between Anisico and Ladinico, in the Triassico.

Borgo delle Madonie about a thousand meters away, with churches rich in Gaginian marbles such as Santa Maria de Francis and the Mother Church of San Giorgio, the ethno-anthropological museum, the ruins of the castle with views from Etna to the Aeolian Islands and, in the territory, the Gorges of Tiberius dug by the river Pollina.
Cited in documents since 1164, but probably older, perhaps as a baptistery of the area.

The Candigliano flows north of the village between deep gorges and narrow valleys, with streams, waterfalls and mirrors of water, and is frequented for excursions, fishing and rafting; its tributary Fosso dell'Eremo has rocky walls loved by climbers. Above the valleys rise the Nero and Montiego (975 m), covered with beech, oak and conifers.
Church under which the excavations brought to light the remains of a Roman domus.

The oldest church of Grado, built around the 5th century and rebuilt in the 6th century: the floor mosaics on two levels show the two phases and contain the only fish depicted in Grado; three naves on marble columns all different and a wooden statue of the Madonna delle Grazie, a destination of devotion of the Grado.
The Venetian palace of power, frescoed.

Overlooking the southern lagoon of Venice, the municipality includes the WWF oasis of Valle Averto, state nature reserve and Ramsar wetland, and in the fishing valleys the Casone di Valle Zappa, a Dutch-style hunting casino of the 1920s; in the village the town hall is located in the sixteenth-century Villa Colonda Marchesini.
Modern art in a medieval palace.
The parish church grew up on a church of the sixteenth century.

Private museum founded in 1966 by the entrepreneur of the Guido Fisogni fuel sector at Palazzolo Milanese and transferred in 2015 to Tradate, in renovated spaces attached to the historic Villa Castiglioni. It is the world's largest collection of antique petrol pumps, certified by the Guinness World Record: thousands of pieces from 1892 to the years 2000 collected in over 40 years, with oil signs, advertising posters, oil cans, compressors, hydrometers and promotional gadgets. Admission fee.
The Italian theater of the city.

Station built from 1881 on the Gottardo line towards the Swiss border, on a project directed by the Livorno engineer Alfredo Giambastiani; the large metal shelter is the work of Giovanni Battista Biadego. After work the railway beam exceeded 1 km in length by 131 m wide, with 14 tracks, 5 of which for travellers under the shelter; the tourist guides of the time often cited it as a monument to progress.
Military history along the panorama.
The medieval face of the village.
Designed in 1972, it gathers about 500 species of plants of the group Cansiglio-Cavallo ordered for environments on about one and a half hectare, with a collection of medicinal plants.

Medieval village on a hill overlooking Puglia, next to the daunio-Roman center of Forentum: in the territory the ruins of the Roman villa called "Casa del Diavolo" , the medieval frescoed church of Santa Maria del Principe and, in the village, the Museum of peasant civilization and the Civic Antiquarium.
Palazzo Rocca, the church of Sant'Andrea on the ruins of an ancient parish church and the eighteenth-century Santa Maria delle Grazie.

The center of the new land founded in 1299, first called San Giovanni in Altura and then Castel San Giovanni: a large square divided into two, Piazza Masaccio and Piazza Cavour, around the Palazzo d'Arnolfo, and Corso Italia flanked by medieval and Renaissance buildings. In January, for Sant'Antonio Abate, in Piazza Masaccio, pets and courtyard animals are blessed. The walk proposed by Visit Tuscany takes about 2 hours with the museum.

Ruins of one of the most important Augustinian convents of the Zumpani Congregation in the 17th century, which once kept works of art; they are reached during the naturalistic trekking around the lake.
The work of the past, from printing to the cinema.
Small medieval church outside the centre of the 11th century, with a fresco of 1518 of Our Lady supporting the pierced Christ.
The former monastery of the Hermits of the 14th century which houses the archaeological museum, with the Augustinian church of the village.

Natural lake formed by the colossal landslide of July 27, 1642 detached from Mount Pozzuoli, which buried about forty houses and a hundred inhabitants and cleared the torrent Troncone; since 1926 it acts as a reservoir for the central of Rovesca. The Slow Trek from Antronapiana (about 6.5 km, 250 m of difference in altitude, 2 hours and a half walk, from May to October) passes through the stone village of Cimallegra, between the rockfalls of the landslide and on a walkway suspended inside the Sajont waterfall (not recommended with heavy rains or ice).
Sixteenth-century clear painted in a shovel.

First parish church of Adro, rises on the top of a hill in the area of the ancient castle and offers a wide panorama. Built in the 15th century, it contains large apse frescoes and a cycle of 16th century frescoes.
The great Marian feast of September 8.
Ticket €10 with Civic Museum, Galleria Estense and Avia Pervia

Rocca mentioned as a castle from the twelfth century, Matilde di Canossa and from 1212 of the Montecuccoli, then Este and from 1756 of the Malaspina: two walled enclosures side by side, the feudal palace and the tower rebuilt in 1393 with shoe base and Ghibelline blackbirds. It was struck in the last war and restored by the Municipality and hosts the Historical Museum, from the first archaeological evidence to the post-war period, and the Artis Museum Forum with a hundred contemporary sculptures by artists from 16 countries.
Vallombrosan monastery documented since 1037, sold at auction in the Napoleonic era and today winery with hospitality.
Under the church of San Lorenzo, the fifth century basilica where the tomb of San Grato was found.

Powered by the sulfur source of Alloch, known since the late fifteenth century and the only of this type in Trentino, which flows about 1,320 meters in the Monzoni group at 9.5 °C; the modern spa opened in 2003, with conventional care. The wellness area on more than 4,000 m2 and three levels has Japanese bathrooms, saunas, rooms of the rooms, outdoor dining rooms, Kneipp path and swimming pools.
The 16th-century convent outside the door.
The heart of the country, with wines from the Riviera.
The frescoes of Borremans.

Three rooms that cover over three thousand years of history of Polesine: the Bronze Age with ceramics and objects in bone and horn from the palafittic inhabited of Canàr, Canova and Marola along the Tartarus; the Roman era (II century BC-II century AD) with objects of daily use, ceramics and coins; the graffiti and glazed ceramics of the XIV-XVI centuries found along the White Canal, where stood the customs tower called "Croxeta" . Open every day by reservation, 9-12 and 15-19 (tel. 0425 850202).

Already church of Minori Observanti, with classical exterior and large dome; inside a monumental marble altar of Varvella (1771), marble statues attributed to Pietro Bernini by F. Negri Arnoldi and an Immaculate woodwork (1833) by Vincenzo Sapphiro di Serra.
Modern Marina on the Ionian for 450 boats, even over 30 meters, with two basins, yard and control tower, surrounded by pine forests and palm trees; awarded with the gold anchors.
The hug of the colonnade.

On the Hochmuth, under Steinegg, a gerla-shaped platform recalls the cultivation of the steep Muthöfe farms, where with winches they pulled on soil and manure; views over Merano, the Val d'Adige and the mountains, with two telescopes and panels on the peaks and ancient crops.
The palace of the lords of Gazoldo on the town square.
Rebuilt from 1687 and completed in the 19th century, it preserves works by Elisabetta Sirani, Adeodato Malatesta and Francesco Stringa.
Fat plants.
Cima's only shovel left in Conegliano.
The last Liberty villa in Via Roma.
Norcia Cathedral.
The prison graffiti cells.
The viewpoint of Piazza del Popolo.
The ancient prison of Tullianum, over which in the sixteenth century the church of St. Joseph of the Falegnami was built.

The first pearl of the Amalfi Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997, famous for its ceramics: the majolica dome of the Cathedral of St. John the Baptist, the Municipal Mosaic Villa, the Ceramic Museum of Villa Guariglia in Raito and the village of Albori, among the most beautiful villages in Italy.
Museum space on the ground floor of the town hall, about 1.5 km from the excavations, which collects finds from the site of Libarna.
Objects and documents on the war and the massacre of civilians in 1944.
The graves of two medieval popes.
Palma il Giovane, Bassano and the 20th century of Casarini under the same roof.

The church of Carmine (Sixth century), already of the noble Mesiani, has a late Renaissance façade; that of the Immaculate (Seventh century) a late Baroque stone portal; San Rocco (Five hundred), damaged by earthquakes and then restored, is used for the Greek-Byzantine rite.

Ancient water lilies of the imperial villa of Gradola, which placed statues of Tritoni and Poseidon there; destination of travelers and artists since 1826, can be reached only by boat and is not visitable by the rough sea.
Taste the typical wine of the village.
The forum and temples of ancient Ardea.
The two main roads that cross the Four Songs.

Environment reconstruction with characters like Francesco Crispi, Emanuele and Vincenzo Navarro, George Sand and Vincenzo Giordano Orsini, who tells the hospitality given to Sambuca to the garibaldina column of Orsini, to which he joined Emanuele Navarro della Miraglia, indicated by Sciascia as a precursor of Verism.
The pedestrian street that climbs from the station to Piazza Grande, passing in front of the Pieve di Santa Maria.
Sacred art in the cloisters.

The fifteenth-century chapel, probably erected during a pestilence on an ancient Roman necropolis outside the walls, enlarged in 1521; the altarpiece of San Rocco painted by Francesco Morone in 1529 was moved to the parish. In 1890 the abbot Gottardi overturned its orientation, preserving the bell tower with a dome in terracotta pine. Simple interior with tombs and altar of St. Anne.
A stretch of the path from Aquileia to the mountains.
The bridge over the Noncello with the eighteenth-century statues of Jupiter and Juno, which tradition has renamed Adam and Eve.

Founded in 1984 and opened in 1989 in the former oratory of the Filippini Fathers (1632) and in the church of San Filippo Neri, on two floors of works Messinese from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century: a Salvator Mundi attributed to Polidoro da Caravaggio, a painted cross of the fourteenth century, a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century, the funeral monument of Geronimo Rosso by Antonello Gagini, a polyptych of the late fifteenth century and a table of Antonello de Saliba.
The neo-Gothic parish of Velturno.
The ceramic bench.

In the seventeenth-century wing of Palazzo Luzzago, already a guest house, born in 1985 from the exhibitions of the local Archaeological Historical Group and today on about 500 square meters in two halls set up by the architect Andrea Perin. The chronological path tells the population of the low plain from Neolithic to the post-Medieval age with finds of the excavations conducted since 1983 under the direction of the Superintendence: ceramics, daggers, funerary furnishings, silver drachma of the Galli Cenomani, Renaissance ceramics and the only coin known in Italy of King Ariperto I (653-661); the second room hosts temporary exhibitions.
Pay up to the island in front of the Rock.
A wild beach for walkers.
Mountains, forests and abandoned mines of the Iglesiente.
Closed due to the 2016 earthquake
The altar has a golden wooden statue of the Virgin given by the Cathedral of Aosta with six golden candlesticks.

Quadrangular fortress with four corner towers and a double loggia Renaissance courtyard, rebuilt and enlarged by Bartolomeo d'Alviano on the core of an older castle (the first plant dates back to the 10th century). Purchased in 1654 by Donna Olimpia Pamphili Maidalchini, it owes its name to the Doria Pamphili, the last private owners, and since 1920 it has been a municipality. On the courtyard opens the Chapel of the Rondini with 17th century frescoes of the life of St. Francis, including the saint who asks for silence to swallows.

The painted sea in the area of Geremeas along the panoramic view for Villasimius: polished granite pebbles that leave the place in white sand, crystal clear water and hills of maquis; from the parking lot on top of the hill a path descends to the beach.
The eighteenth-century villa became a town hall.

Archaeological and botanical park above the village, in a basaltic amphitheatre with centuries-old oaks, holm oaks and maquis, inhabited by the Neolithic (3800 BC). The path on the left, easy, leads to the necropolis of about fifteen domus de Janas excavated in the walls of sa Carona Arrubia; the one on the right, challenging, rises to the plateau of Taccu Idda with wide views. There are also the polylobed nuraghe is Allonis, the corridor nuraghe Su Motti and the drywalls of the "tancas" .
The villa of the founders of Pineto.

Castle of 1293; the castle church of the Annunziata, of the fourteenth century, contains an Annunciation in majolica dated 1460 and the cycle of the Stories of Saint Lucia frescoed by Gerardo Dottori in 1949.
The tools and traditions of Sila.
The double medieval portico of Via del Mercato.

In the workshop I Vetri di Sandro Bormioli we can see the craftsmanship of the incandescent glass; the Artistic Showcase Amantzio Bormioli produces blown or shaped objects in borosilicate glass (trophys, furnishings, sacred art, animals) and welcomes tourist and school groups on weekdays (tel. 0109 58254).

Built by the Cantelmo after the earthquake of 1349, in Gothic style, in the highest point of the village, with windows double-fore and Gothic portal; it preserves a mosaic of the II century A.D. and the chapel of Sant'Onofrio with frescoes of the XIV century. From 1655 the hall became theater, active until 1939; today it is the seat of the City Hall, Historical House of Lazio, and hosts exhibitions and events.

About 300 meters from the castle of Pedres, a funerary collective monument of more than 4,000 years ago, among the largest of the kind in Sardinia: born as allée couverte in the culture of Bonnanaro, around 1600 BC was transformed into a tomb of Giants with exedra and stele. Approximately 28 meters long and 6 meters wide, it has an inner chamber of about 10 meters; in the center of the exedra stood a stele of granite about 4 meters high.
The medieval civic symbol.
The Underground Matera.
Monumental fountain in the square of the same name, one of the many monumental fountains in the historic centre.

For more than three centuries, the alunite was excavated in open air, leaving crevices, craters and vertical walls over 50 meters tall similar to canyon; the invention of the artificial alum at the end of the eighteenth century led to the definitive closure in 1941. The CAI has traced the Miner's Way, a network of rings between old quarries and chestnut and beech woods.

Built in place of the old Collegiate Danger: works started in 1808, open to worship in 1840 on a project by the architect Pietro Maggi, with neoclassical interior with a single nave and six lateral altars. It preserves the relics of St. Cyrinus, the fourth century martyr who arrived in 1653, the country's companion.
Wooded massif behind the village, with the mountains Ferru and Entu over a thousand meters.

It is located in via Roma in the eighteenth century Palazzo Brunenghi-Salvago, together with the civic library, and documents the human presence in the territory from the Mesolithic to the Early Middle Ages.
Boys and enthusiasts like him a lot.
Medieval frescoes in an ancient lazzaretto.
€5, reduced €4; with guide €6
The overflow symbol of the coast, with a bath in the cove.

It collects traces of the past agricultural and pre-artisan activity of the country and documents uses, customs, traditions and local culture; the regional portal indicates it as one of the most valid initiatives realized in the Lombard Prealps. It tells a country whose history is linked to iron and to the processing of scissors and knives, still flourishing crafts at an international level.
Small fortified villages scattered in the municipal territory, which preserve the 14th-XV century plant, among them the castle of Avacelli.
Parish of the seventeenth century that combines late-Gothic and Renaissance elements.
The walls with bastions strengthened by the Spanish in the 16th century, with imposing doors; the Port Medina Coeli is from 1697.
The walled village of the Caetani.
The Romanesque pantocrator.
In the hamlet of Casteldilago, there are 16th century frescoes by artists from the school of Giovanni di Pietro known as Spain.
The memory of the anti-mafia.
The rosette and the Renaissance sculptures.
The museum dedicated to Federico Fellini, between the fortress of Sigismondo Malatesta, Piazza Malatesta and the Palazzo del Fulgor with the cinema of "Amarcord."
Seasonal closure: the Parco del Monviso indicates reopening on July 15th 2027
The painted village.

Cedar of Lebanon grown on a small shore where today there is a municipal park near the center: it exceeds 25 meters in height, with a stem of 5 meters of circumference (160 cm of diameter) and a large and globose hair. It is a green monument that can be visited freely.
With Renaissance loggia and staircase, one of the oldest in Lombardy (XI-XIII century), a short walk from the Duomo.
At the eastern end of the village there are four arches of an aqueduct from 1476 and, next to it, a half-nineteenth-century fountain donated by a duke after the cholera epidemic of the 1930s.
Paid fishermen's ferry
Works of contemporary Piedmontese artists.
A late-Gothic church next to the castle.
A work praised by Vasari.
JoB pass and chair for access to the sea

Village overlooking the valley of Simeto and Etna, ancient Greek-Roman city: the Regional Archaeological Museum with the head of Augustus and the Centuripini vases, the Roman monuments of the Castle of Corradino, the Customs and the Thermal Baths of Contrada Bagni, the churches of the center and the abandoned village of Carcaci.

The old town, the piedicastello, stretches over the ridge of the hill to the church and is closed by a wall with three entrance doors and several towers, overlooking the lake. The village was born in the Lombard age around a Roman tower then abandoned, it was occupied by Ruggero II of Altavilla in 1130 and in the eighteenth century it was named city; here was born the writer Francesco Jovine.

In the eighteenth-century palace on Piazza Dante, home of the library and historical archive: artistic section with works by Guercino and Giovan Francesco Guerrieri, the Madonna and Child in stone of the thirteenth century, frescoes by Andrea da Bologna and a polyptych by the Vivarini; archaeological section with finds of the historic center and the territory. Entire 2 €, reduced 1 €.

Medieval village infeudated in the tenth century by Emperor Otto III, with a cylindrical tower of the fifteenth century 25 meters high and the church of Santa Croce, with a wooden cross of the eighteenth century and paintings of the sixteenth century.
From 1260, with Romanesque crypt and a tempera table of Umbrian-Sienese school.

Borgo on a hill at 257 m rises on the ruins of the ancient Pollitium, known for the Basilica of the Holy Face that has guarded the veil with the face of Christ since 1506; in the plain the Cistercian abbey of Santa Maria Arabona with the nearby Roman villa.

Villa at the foot of the fort built in 1812, in the Austrian age, instead of the Gonzaga palace (tourist sources date it differently); the park is a small botanical garden with cedars of Lebanon, alders and cypresses.
One of the gates of the Roman city, with imposing towers, next to the cathedral.
The Gothic door and the view of the bay.
Main square with the Collegiate Church, the Romanesque Civic Tower with its 17th-century onion spire and the Teatro "Giacomo Leopardi."
A small museum in the centre of Rango that conserves objects and teaching materials from the first half of the twentieth century.
Mills, waterfalls and woods a stone's throw from the village.
One kilometer underground in the life of miners.
The rural life of the hinterland in the houses where it took place.
An ancient city on the mountain.

The oldest preserved Farnesian residence of the 13th century: the Renaissance renovation of Antonio da Sangallo the Younger remained unfinished; recently a Renaissance loggia was reopened walled for centuries.

Neoclassical church started on October 15, 1807 and completed in 1815 to accommodate a small wooden statue, perhaps the polena of a ship, found in 1800 near Tunis by a carlofortino reduced to slavery after the raid corsair of 1798 and brought back home to the ransom of 1803. The statue is venerated as a protector of tabarchins.
The San Stè cheese and the baskets.
The Romanesque-Gothic masterpiece of the center.
The four Lottos of Recanati.

Village of road lying on the ridge of a hill, with walls more than ten meters high, fountains, numerous speaking doors, the Malaspina castle and the church of Santi Gervasio and Protasio, whose bell tower dominates the village.
The face of Frederick II.
Roman river port on the left bank of the Tiber, under the cliff, discovered in 1962: testifies the role of Orte as a shopping center in direct contact with Rome.
Ruins with a view of the plain.
In the rooms of the Royal Palace the history of the cathedral and Veneranda Fabbrica.

Municipality of the Costa dei Gelsomini divided between the medieval village on the hill, surrounded by four gates and dominated by the castle, and the marina, where on the promontory of Punta Stilo the archaeological park and the museum guard the ancient Kaulon, achaea colony with the Doric temple and the great mosaic of dragons and dolphins.

Botanical garden terraced with about 300 species of medicinal plants of the Scuola Medica Salernitana, connected by a stairway with pergola and views of the sea and historic center; inside the Tisaneria.

A fraction of narrow streets and brick houses with the church of San Leonardo Hermita, built in 1837; you arrive for the provincial road that crosses the Ponte Attilio Vergai on the gorge of the Corfino stream.

Romanesque church outside the walled village, probably rest of the ancient town of Rondinaria destroyed in 1166, was parish until the sixteenth century and today is a cemetery chapel: hut roof, bell tower, semicircular apse. Inside the cycle of the Stories of the Passion of the Master of Lerma, with St. Christopher on the façade, Christ in almond with the Tetramorph in the basin and the twelve prophets. You can reach it with a short path from the old town (about 20 minutes walk from the accommodation), starting from Palazzo Baldo, home of the Park.
A Venetian villa frescoed with a collection from Moroni to Longhi.
