A cycle of frescoes from 1196 in a cave.
The island-snake with the sighting tower.
The park that leads to the Torrione della Brunella, with a spectacular view of the valley.

An intermorenic lake formed by the withdrawal of the ancient Balteo glacier, Special Conservation Zone with flat and accessible shore; it is reached on foot from the castle, also by bike on dirt road. There were found two pirogues, one of about 250 A.D. (1912) and one of about 1450 B.C. (discovered in 1978), and the remains of a palafittic village of the final Bronze; some finds are at the Museo del Territorio Biellese and the Museo di Antiquità in Turin.

It was built at the beginning of the 10th century on a cave, where according to tradition St. Francis stayed in the 13th century. Succeeded in 1860, since 1926 it is a female Franciscan hermitage, the one of the "Allodole" of St. Francis.
Etruscans and butters in the same museum.
The view over the valley from the castle of the village.
The wooden theater built in 1618 in the Armored Room of the Pilot for Ranuccio I Farnese, with the large step cavea and the monumental proscenium.
The church of the patron saint and the Madonna del Rosario.
The view of the Great War on Valsugana.

Built in 1201, it has enjoyed since the early times of great fame and devotion among the populations of the valley and the plain; it preserves an unusual Black Madonna and is a stop of the Varaita Trekking Valley that climbs from Verzuolo.

The Capua Longobarda on the handle of the Volturno: the Campano Museum of Matres Matutae in the Palazzo Antignano, the Duomo with the bell tower of the IX century, the churches "a Corte" , the Norman castle of the Stones, the castle of Charles V and, in Sant'Angelo in Formis, the largest cycle of medieval frescoes of the South.
A thousand steps to the sea.
In the surroundings of the village, described by the regional portal as the largest artificial invader in Italy, among woods; it is habitat of herons, ducks and wolves.

Municipality at the mouth of the Magra with the village of Montemarcello, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, from the Roman camping path, overlooking the Gulf of Poets in the park of Montemarcello-Magra-Vara.
Cassini's stars.
Valico can be reached on foot, along the path the stone bas-reliefs of the stations of the Via Crucis.
The oldest bell tower in the village.
The village designed by Amedeo di Castellamonte between 1667 and 1690 at the service of the palace, with the square as a focal point.
The last walls of the fortress city.
Thirty years of excavation on the prehistory of Canavese.

Documents, photos and materials on the Feast of the Daggers, floats surmounted by a poplar tree or cerro with scenes of life and work in the fields, parading the third Sunday of May in honor of Saint Isidoro, patron saint of the farmers.
Vernazza from above.
Medieval site on the hill with the ruins of the castle of San Michele, also called the Abatemarco, and the church of the same name, entirely frescoed, built on an ancient Basilian monastery.
Built in the 13th century with a Romanesque Gothic façade, it overlooks Piazza Duomo next to the cathedral.

On the Linas river, near the border with Domusnovas, the waterfall reaches a jump of about 45 meters; it is reached with the path CAI 113 from the forest of Montimannu and is also a destination of canyoning and climbing.
Collection of miniature nativity scenes dedicated to Guido Colitti, in Piazza della Vittoria.

Built between the end of the sixteenth century and the beginning of the seventeenth century in Gothic-Catalan style, it preserves a precious wooden altar and statues of the Madonna del Rosario and various saints of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
Walking in the Roman city.

A dozen palaces from the Seven-nineteenth century with portals made of local stone (Irpina breccia), restored after the 1980 earthquake, along the route from Via Roma to Vico San Pietro passing through the former cathedral square: Capobianco, Filippone, Pelosi, Flammia, Gella-Calò and Testa-Cipriano, with paved courtyard, well-tank and stone staircase. They are admired from the outside; in the Town Hall the plaster busts of the sculptor Carmine Genua (1851-1924).
the MiC card (updated to March 2021) indicates hours \"closed" every day and the Park describes the antiquarium in preparation: check opening and ticket (MiC: €2, reduced €1)
The fortress on the island.
A curious urban facility.

Parish of the eighteenth century appreciated for the portal, with frescoes by A. Capello. The 17th-century high altar has a monumental tabernacle and an ancon attributed to Pietro Ramus; the palace is the work of Giovanni Giuseppe Piccini.
A rare place of underground worship.
In the hamlet of Uzza rise the church of San Rocco, probably of 777 and rebuilt in 1491, and the octagonal church of the Blessed Virgin of Mercy, of the early eighteenth century.
Square and stocky tower of the 11th-XII century, witnessing traffic control towards the Valais.
Archaeology of the foreground.
Walking on Scaliger blackbirds.

Large church of the historic center with a single nave with three entrances, rebuilt entirely after the earthquakes of 1930 and 1980. It preserves two 17th century paintings attributed to the school of Luca Giordano, the Fall of Jesus and the Deposition. Open during function hours.
The fortress church.
The bell tower in tiara.
Antonello and Caravaggio.
The view from Sabina to Soratte.
Romanesque basilica and baptistery flanked, with Roman re-utilization stones.
The monastery of colors.
Water sports in the crater.
A medieval village with temple and Etruscan signs.

Along the fossil river you will encounter a bed of prehistoric river intact with its pebbles; the fossil beach of San Lazzaro testifies to the ancient presence of the sea, with bivalves, echinoderms, gastropods and a shark tooth found in 1998.
Tools that tell about mountain viticulture, difficult and tiring, and its evolution over time.
Romanesque-Gothic cathedral of the 13th century on the hill of Girfalco, with richly decorated interior and a beautiful rose window.
The Renaissance loggia overlooking the square of the village.
An eighteenth-century gallery in Salento.

Country of Salento at the northern foot of the Serre Salentine, with a historic center of courts, wells, arches and "focaliri" and the seventeenth-century Doge's Palace on the main square, located since 1982 of the Museum of peasant civilization and popular traditions of Salento.

Borgo dell'Alta Pusteria was born from the Benedictine monastery founded in the 8th century by the dukes of Bavaria, with the Romanesque Collegiate, considered the most important Romanesque sacred building in the Eastern Alps, the Museum of the Collegiate (MIK), the Holy Sepulchre seventeenth century and the DoloMythos museum in Villa Wachtler; above the village the Rocca dei Baranci with chairlift and summer sled.
The chapel of Our Lady of the People.
€3 whole, €1.50 reduced; free with FVGcard

The municipality of the Upper Trompia Valley is linked to the mining tradition: you can visit by train and on foot the galleries of the Marzoli Mine with the Museum           . The World of Miners and the Iron Art , the ORMA Museum in the ancient Broletto of Mondaro and the church of Sant'Apollonio Vetere with frescoes of the Renaissance of Brescia.

A few meters from the waterfall, the last watermill in the area: in the seventeenth century the mills fed by Funtana Manna were eight, and this was used for over two centuries to grind the wheat. Restored, it preserves the ancient tools of work and is visitable.
To the Citadel.
Ten centuries of sea fortifications.
From the mosaic to the sea by bicycle.
The Peace Palace.

Borgo dell'Orvietano was born as a castle of Lerona, outpost of Orvieto in the twelfth century, of which two walls and doors remain; in its territory the Selva di Meana with Villa Cahen, the only Liberty building of Umbria with an Italian garden, the Museum of Geological Cycles with marine fossils and the exhibition of Pugnaloni.
The great bronze symbol of the city.
On a promontory overlooking the sea above the cliff of Coreca, a circular plant with a conical base and cylindrical body; probably built in the sixteenth century.
A stone village that you visit as a museum.
Get down into the galleries of a historic mine.
Cansiglio fauna in an hour.
Perfectly preserved because it lived until yesterday.
In the former Classe sugar factory, the history of Ravenna from prehistory to the Middle Ages; part of the Archaeological Park with the Old Port.
The first Walser village in the Lys valley, where the töitsu is still spoken, with the church of the Last Judgment and the valley of San Grate.
The oldest Cuneo.
Entering a village 3,500 years ago.

The old town occupies a limestone island connected to the mainland by a masonry bridge and preserves the original urban layout with Baroque churches and palaces. It is surrounded by a bastion fence of about 2 km, built after the Turkish sack of Otranto (1480), of which remains the lower part after the demolitions of 1879-1887; the panoramic road of the Riviera runs along the walls and allows the tour of the island.
Gothic and Baroque in the same complex as the museum.

Città della Costa degli Etruschi with the Archaeological Park of the Roman Villa of San Vincenzino and the Archaeological Museum in Villa Guerrazzi (La Finquantina) in Marina di Cecina the Blue Flag beach and the Tomboli pine forest.
The work of the fields in the hinterland of Nisseno.

Inaugurated on June 19, 1993 and dedicated to the fallen of all wars, the square hosts the bronze complex of the Pistoiese sculptor Jorio Vivarelli - Via della Resistance - historical parabola - the last challenge: a four-metre-high figure represents the dominated and killed humanity, from which a road of Resistance and hope leads to a second sculpture, container of life. Next to the former elementary school is the bust of the discolored father Filippo Cecchi, physicist and director of the Ximenian Observatory since 1872.
A fortified village at the foot of the castle.
Amphitheatre of the second century AD, partly visible and incorporated into the buildings; in the sixth century the Goths of Totila built a fortress there.

It preserves a Renaissance canvas by Orazio Iacobotta da Spinazzola dated 1583, with the family of Alfonso Abbatemarco in prayer, rich in details on clothes, objects and environment, which offers a glimpse of the ancient Good cockpit.

A historic mountain village in the Val Canale valley, where you will find Julian and Carnic Alps and Latin, Slavic and Germanic cultures: the Tarvisio Forest, the Fusine and Predil Lakes, the sanctuary of Mount Lussari, the Cave del Predil mine and the military historical museum.
Stop between the center and the port.
The statues of the sculptors of Serra San Bruno.

The remains of the Roman city of Valentia, from the 2nd century BC to the VII AD: public baths with calidarium and frigidarium, domus with courtyards and rainwater collection and a stretch of road; from here come the mosaics of the Four Seasons, the Nereide and the starry sky.
Frescoes from 1564 in a small mountain church.

Pre- and protohistoric fortress on the edge of the plateau of Sa Struvina: a protonuraghe in corridor of the age of the ancient and middle Bronze (about XX-XIV century BC), with a tholos cell intact, was incorporated in the XIV-XIII century BC in a four-tower quadrilobed bastion around a large courtyard, where huts built inside the walls were dug, case without comparison in the nuragic world. There is also a megalithic wall at the end of the third millennium B.C.; in the late Roman age the site was re-used for pagan, Christian and Jewish cults. Guided tours from the park guides, with information center; views of the Rio Mogoro valley, the Costa Verde and the Campidano.

The plateau is about 800 meters away by paths marked between woods and high meadows, including ancient mule tracks of transhumance; from the plateau the view ranges over San Daniele and Friuli hills. The old houses of transhumance host a popular hotel; bike routes with the school of Daniele Pontoni.

Urban fabric rich in medieval and Renaissance remains: via del Castello, via di Sotto e Porta della Rapa, the buildings Tonna, Avolio, Massa and Grenata, the seventeenth-century fountain with octagonal tub of Piazza del Popolo, the stone wash-house of the Canaje and the "Preta tonna" (Price tonna), measured for the wheat where the insolvent debtors were exposed to the gogna. From the west side the view of the Peligna Valley.
A century and a half of history told in the postcard.
Guided tours for a fee from the Visitor Centre (on foot or by electric boat)

Country of the Camonica Valley bathed by the Lanico torrent, whose strength has fed for centuries the processing of iron: the ethnographic iron Museum tells of it "Le Fudine" in the ancient forges of Serini and Dwarfs; in the village the two churches of Sant'Andrea, the "old" with frescoes from the XV-XVI century and the eighteenth century parish church.

Cremonese municipality of Roman origin, documented by findings, which preserves the birthplace of the composer Amilcare Ponchielli, today Ponchielli civic museum, and the church of Santo Stefano with its bell tower of about 54 meters.
The castle Visconteo-forzesco became villa dei Litta, heart of the village.

Collecting more than 100,000 shells from all over the world, some 5,000 fossils, hundreds of embalmed and mummified fish, fish and cetacean skeletons, naval and fishing equipment, seashells and handmade corals and 400 marine paintings.
The patron saint of Val Nure.
A green oasis on Via Foria.

Dedicated to St. Moderano, abbot here since 719, rebuilt between the 12th and 13th centuries and renovated in the 16th and 19th centuries, when the façade was rebuilt in sandstone after a collapse of the ground; it preserves the portal trumpeted of the 12th century with bezel and architrave in relief and the interior with three apsed aisles. It preserves the relics of St. Moderano and St. Abbondio. Open every day 7-19.
Archaeology in the green.

Rebuilt between the end of the 17th and early 18th centuries (the bell tower bears date 1709), it has facade in Lecce stone and Baroque interior: mosaic floor by Giuseppe Peluso (1885-86), high altar with relics of San Quinziano, three altars attributed to Placido Buffelli, the altar of the Madonna of Constantinople of 1594 and an unusual baptistery of 1594.
€5, free under 18 and people with disabilities
The palace on the square, the heart of the political life of the village, with four Gothic windows and a sundial; next to the thirteenth-century tower on a green stone base.
The eighteenth century in the square.
An area once abandoned, today lively neighborhood with university venues, shops, bars and art galleries, with the fountain of the hospital of Santa Maria dei Battuti.
€12, students €9, free under 8 years
Baroque church of the Barnabite Fathers, first stone in 1607, with works by Moncalvo and Daniele Crespi and wooden carvings by confessionals and pulpit.
The shrine.
The study of the fourth state
Frescoes from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century in a fortified monastery.
In the foundations of Palazzo Graziani Baglioni since 1974, designed by Giorgio and Maria Grazia Lungarotti, he tells five thousand years of culture of vine and wine.
The golden altar of Bencivinni.

The Lost Village of Lunetta is a small stone village with a medieval bridge, an ancient mill and the church of San Giovanni, near the Belbo Reserve: the springs of the stream are natural reserve, walkable, on horseback, by bike and in winter with cross-country skiing.
The medieval castle rebuilt in 3D.
guided tours only by appointment (tel. 0766 28493)
The objects of the ancient city.

Natural reserve reachable on foot or by mountain bike; inside the Garden of Giovannino, which takes its name from the pastor who cultivated a vegetable garden from May to September, reached by forest roads and paths.

Built by the Knights of Malta in carparo between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, in Renaissance forms; inside paintings by the Bianchi brothers, painters of Manduria, a wooden crucifix of the seventeenth century and the Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament.
Nine resorts on 35 km of coast, from Casal Borsetti to Lido di Savio, with dunes and pinewood behind; Marina di Ravenna is the closest to the city.
The building tied to the mill by a gallery.
€14, reduced €12
Church and cloister, the "da non persare" of Cori.

UNESCO MAB reserve since 2018 between the Tiber and Peglia basins, formed by the municipalities of San Venanzo, Orvieto, Parrano and Ficulle: holm oak, cerro and maple woods, 44 species of wild mammals and the extinct volcanoes of San Venanzo, with rocks present in very few other places in the world, including China, Uganda and Brazil.
The cathedral was born from a Roman temple.
Etruscan tomb in the countryside of Casole, signalled by Visit Tuscany together with the parish church of Pievescola.
Gothic frescoes in an isolated hermitage.
The castle on the spur between two streams.

Set up in the rural buildings of the Ricci Curbastro estate, unique in Franciacorta, it collects thousands of tools and objects of rural life with particular attention to viticulture. Opened in 1986 after more than thirty years of research by Gualberto Ricci Curbastro and expanded by his children, it hosts temporary exhibitions, cultural events and guided tastings, and a library of over 2,000 volumes of agricultural history and local traditions. Admission fee (tel. 030 736094).
The church rebuilt in 1791 by Leandro Marconi, which preserves the bell tower and the pronao of the fifteenth-century building.

The Town Hall, of medieval origin, was among the few buildings spared from the destruction of the Second World War and houses a work by Girolamo della Robbia, ...Jesus and the Samaritan at the well. Next to the sixteenth-century Palazzo Pretorio and the nineteenth-century Logge del Grano, accessible from both palaces.

In the bishop's palace completed around 1860, on two floors: Roman marbles re-used by Ruggero I in the abbey of the Most Holy Trinity, the fourteenth-century sarcophagi of Ruggero Sanseverino and Giovanna d'Aquino, sacred furnishings of the cathedral, ceramics, paintings and an ivory crucifix attributed to Alessandro Algardi, who arrived in Mileto in 1851.
A tropical garden populated with butterflies.

Private collection of over 3,000 pieces documenting the rural civilization and artistic culture of Marche between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, in four paths: the rebuilt rooms of the farmhouse sharecropping, the meeting places, the workshops of the old crafts and the collections of ceramics, copper and iron, with environments animated by images and sounds.
Transparent waters and rich seabeds for diving and snorkeling, with seahorses and walls covered with sponges and gorgonies.
With a precious wooden crucifix and 17th century frescoes.
Birdwatching in the last swamps of the Tablekeeper.

At 1760 meters, in an area formerly dedicated to the cult of Mars, it was a hospice for travellers between Valle Grana and Valle Stura; the complex combines an ancient part and an extension between the Seven and the Nineteenth Century. The fifteenth-century frescoes attributed to Pietro da Saluzzo depict evangelists and doctors of the Church, the Passion and the holy martyrs of the Thebes. Open on Saturdays and Sundays until June, every day from June to October (indicatively 9-18); guided tours on Sundays in July and August at 14:30 (5 €). On 19 August, for the patron saint's feast, the Baia di Castelmagno parade.
Above the big "zardin."
The noble rooms of Bentivoglio.
On the hill of San Cristoforo; in the chapels a Crucifixion attributed by some to Van Dyck but probably of a local painter and an eighteenth-century altarpiece of the Immaculate of Giuseppe Palmieri.
A walk between washbasins and mills.
The Savoy Palace.

The main square, dedicated to the founder of the ENI: at the center the octagonal fountain in white stone of 1587, designed by Lattanzio Ventura of Urbino, with four deities marine; around the government palace, documented since 1271, the civic tower, the loggia of 1511 wanted by Ascanio Ottoni for the trade of wool and the municipal palace. Who runs seven times around the fountain receives from Pro Loco the morning patente.
Residence built by Prior Giorgio di Challant, with fifteenth-century frescoed chapel.
Viuzze in pebbles that descend from the Fortezza to the small stretch dominated by the Duomo; the Bavarian Quarter preserves the houses built in 1328 by the soldiers of Ludovico il Bavaro.
The heart of the city among medieval buildings.
On Via Roma, the church with its sinuous curved façade and Palazzo Aufifreddi with its austere red terracotta façade.
The church next to the Devil's fountain.
Vittone and the civic museum.

Borgo della Murgia Barese grew up around the Caracciolo Castle, home of the Museo della Civiltà Contadina (Museo della Civiltà Contadina) Dino Bianco, with the Baroque church of Maddalena, the neoclassical matrix church, the clock tower, the apotropaic masks on the portals and the 'vignali' of the historic center.

Country at the foot of the Rocca di Cavour, isolated inselberg in the plain and nature reserve since 1980; at the entrance of the village stands the Abbey of Santa Maria, which houses a crypt with the oldest altar of Piedmont and the Archaeological Museum Caburrum, dedicated to the Roman town hall of Forum Vibii Caburrum from which derives the name of the village.
The tomb of the Praetor Caius Cestius inspired by Egyptian models after the conquest of Egypt of 31 B.C.
The main church of the medieval village.

Dedicated to politician and writer Raffaele De Cesare (1845-1918), he collects ceramics, coins and instruments of the Roman age, an ethnographic section with tools from the nineteenth century to the mid-Twentieth century and a geological section with plio-pleistocene and clay materials of the territory.
The Sinnasian villas countryside.

17th century, built in the same period as the Cistercian monastery, then destroyed: it preserves a wooden reliquary, the "brocca di Sant'Ugo" (an Arabic vase), a wooden crucifix and the Annunciation of Stethera (1570).
The main church of the city.
With the Lion of San Marco above the portal and frescoes inside, it testifies to the Venetian influence on the city.

In the village of Varano Marchesi a noble palace of medieval origin and Renaissance appearance, formerly residence of the Pallavicino; in a distant and dominant position remain the ruins of the castle's castle, probably of thirteenth century origin.
One of the most beautiful mountain villages in Friuli.
A historical hike in the park.
The door in pine loricato.

Parish of the Diocese of Alife-Caiazzo: according to the CEI census was built in 1326, it became parish in 1590 and was rebuilt in 1774 with the title change, with restorations in 1805 and 1876. The ICCD card describes the eighteenth-century building, the work of local workers, with a single nave and rectangular plan, with tuff masonry, barrel vault and roof with layers in tiles.
The striped façade.
€8, residents €4, children 2-8 years €3

In the gorge excavated by the Anapo and the Calcinara, about 5,000 grotticella tombs dug into the rock between the XII and the IX-VIII century B.C., a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005. At the top of the remains of the Anaktoron, the Prince's Palace, in the necropolis of San Martino tombs with tholos and Byzantine catacombs such as the Cave of Sant'Anna; of the Byzantine villages remain San Micidiario (about 150 houses and a church), the frescoed oratory of San Nicolicchio and the Cave of the Crucifix.
The most beautiful wooden Gothic hall in Tyrol.

Castle of the Counts Gallesio-Piuma dating back to the 12th century, with a quadrangular body and three semicircular towers. It rises on a terrace with three gardens inside the walls, surrounded by a park in which there is a seventeenth-century snowfall; it houses the Welsh Study Centre, dedicated to Giorgio Gallesio, and a small museum of material culture. Visits by reservation (tel. 0144 375628); adheres to open castles with opening on the first and third Sundays of the summer month.
The story of the shoe and the sports shoe where it was born.
The rural stone cores of the Bergamo mountain.
The ancient parish church of the village, abbey church since 1754.

Set up inside Palazzo Rasini, it is a plastic of about 11 square meters in 1:10 scale that reproduces a typical farmhouse brianzola complete with tools, furniture, woodshed and barn, made with the same materials as the original.

Nine domus de janas excavated on two rocky outings near the rivers Temo and Curos, used by the Neolithic end at the ancient age of Bronze (cultures of Ozieri, Campaniforme and Bonnanaro); known since 1903 and excavated in 1987-88. The tomb VIII stands out, with beams and roof of carved hut, where a statue of goddess mother was found, and the tomb IX with ritual fireplace and cups in the floor; on the walls carved taurine horns. Open Tuesday-Sunday 10-13 and 15-18, with guided tours.

On a rocky spur at the top of Cabu Abbas, almost 250 meters above the Gulf of Olbia, with views up to Tavolara: circular tower of about 8 meters of diameter of the XIV-XIII century BC, surrounded by a wall of about 220 meters that encloses the rocks. Under the ladder a sacrificial pit with burning bones; in the excavations of 1936 a female bronze with amphora appeared on the head.
The Byzantine rite in the arbëreshë heart.
The Bonapartes in Rome.
The Palace of the Marquises in the heart of the city.
The tools of the peasant world, told in dialect.

The castle, built around 1100 on a rocky spur in the upper part of the village, is on three levels and houses a museum pole: the Geopaleontological Museum with Abruzzo fossils, including the Prolagus of the collection Di Carlo, many from the geosite of Capo di Fiume; the Pinacoteca Casa degli Artisti e degli Men Illustri di Palena and the room dedicated to the critic and screenwriter Ettore Maria Margadonna.
The neoclassical in town.
An island of woods in the middle of the Po.

Masonry building of 1569, born as a warehouse of goods in transit between Ossola and Switzerland and then prison, guard post and seat of the Ammano, the governor of the valley. Today it hosts the ethnographic museum and exhibitions on the life and history of the Walser, with wooden statues from the German school of the XV-XVI centuries. Open in July and August on Tuesday and Saturday 15:30-17:30, groups by reservation; two floors with stone stairs, without elevator.

Collection formed from 1904 with Roman and Roman works of art: the archaeological section on the ground floor of Palazzo Biancalana (nineteenth century, neoclassical; here the entrance) exhibits pre-Roman and Roman materials of the territory, including a marble head of Aphrodite; the gallery on the first floor of the Palazzo del Podestà has the Sant'Antonio da Padova and the Madonna della Misericordia del Perugino, works by Dono Doni, the pupil, Tiberio d'Assisi and Giuseppe Ribera, a terracotta glazed of Robbiana school and a bust of Canova signed and dated 1812. Some of the works, stolen in 1987, were found in Jamaica.

Borgo del Matese beneventano where about 110 million years ago there was a lagoon: here Ciro was found, the Scipionyx samniticus, the first dinosaur discovered in Italy, told in the Paleolab of the geopaleontological park; in the village the church of Santa Maria Assunta and the alleys of the center.
A stone village with the Malaspina tower.
the MiC card indicates the museum closed every day; the regional portal indicates museums that can be visited only partially
The village of tuff with its proffers.

The village of the eastern Marmilla, which grew up around the parish church of San Lorenzo, known for the nuraghe Su Mulinu on the valley of Rio Mannu, where a Nuragic altar of the Iron Age was found in the form of nuraghes, now rebuilt in the civic museum.
€5, reduced 11-18 years €2,50

A small prior church, already Santa Maria de Incertis: it preserves a ciborium of the fourteenth century and frescoes three to four centuries old, including a Madonna with Child and a Madonna enthroned.
The only nuragic altar in the form of nuraghes.
the regional data sheet indicates closed museum for earthquakes
The Via dei palazzi in the Venetian Renaissance style with magnificently frescoed facades, starting from Piazza del Duomo.
The village of Etruscan origin at the foot of the castle, famous for the cherries celebrated with a feast between the end of May and the beginning of June.

Large village at the gates of Sila: the Basilica of Sant'Angelo with the remains of Blessed Angelo and its museum, Palazzo Sanseverino-Falcone with the frescoes of the eighteenth century and the MACA dedicated to Silvio Vigliaturo, the church of the Annunziata, the oldest in the city.
The green side of the coast.
It houses the Treasure, the library, the capitular hall, the sacristies, the lapidary, an archaeological collection and valuable fabrics.

Opened in 2018 at the departure station of the cable car of Sass Pordoi and curated by the Historical Cultural Association Col di Lana: over 3,000 exhibits on 450 m2 on the war in the Dolomites between Col di Lana and Marmolada, with rebuilt barracks, trenches with machine guns, vintage photographs and objects made by soldiers with splinters, rifles and barbed wire.
The Renaissance houses of Via Maier.
Walk in the countryside of the Fortore valley.
A 1910 power station where you follow the drop of water to the electric current.

In the sixteenth century Town Hall, founded in 1920 by Oreste Nardini and reopened permanently in 1992: about 400 exhibits from the protohistory to the Middle Ages. The strong piece is the Sarcophagus of Velletri (II century A.D., found in 1955) with 184 figures between the labors of Hercules and scenes of the underworld; then the Lastra dell'Orante (IV century), the Volsche terracotta of the VI century B.C. and a copy of the Pallade of Velletri, whose original is at the Louvre.
Park with the Funari trail, once used by ropemakers, home to a music festival with international artists.
The most beloved excursion in the park.
visit only by appointment with reservation required according to the MiC

Fortress of the eighth century, gastaldale headquarters and military outpost, several times modified, with a pentagonal watchtower called "Rocca" (Rocca), today remains the ruins and the doorway, in front of the parish, whose original level was higher than the current one.
Hiking and cycling trails of the Arroscia Valley towards the Ligurian Alps Park, including the ancient Clavesian paths and the Via del Sale.
The peasant life of the Cimini in a frescoed convent.

In the ancient mill mentioned in the second half of the fifteenth century and active until the 1950s, next to the hydroelectric plant inaugurated in 1910: life-size reconstruction of the mill with hopper and original millstones, section on wool and transhumance, route on wetlands and lakes and river diorama with rare aquatic animals of the Park. Open on weekends and holidays, every day in July and August.

One of the seven great Austro-Hungarian forts on the line of about 30 km from Cima Vezzena to Serrada, built between 1911 and 1914 to connect the forts Dosso delle Somme and Cherle: three floors of which one only above ground, three revolving steel domes, covered from 2.80 to 3.80 meters after the first battles of 1915. You can reach it in about 15 minutes from Rifugio Stella d'Italia or 20 from Passo Coe.

Built in the first decade of the seventeenth century, it owes its name to the position on a rise of the ground; it has late-Renaissance façade, a wooden crucifix by G. Bertesi on the high altar and an eighteenth-century Way of the Cross painted on crystal.

The most picturesque route on the island: about 2 km (30 minutes) by the lake between Peschiera Maraglio and Sensole, between centuries-old olive trees and old piers of fishermen, overlooking the private island of São Paulo; picnic area and bar along the way. The full tour of the island measures about 9 km (2 hours and 30 hours).
The convent complex overlooking Piazza Garibaldi.
Church that preserves the Deposition from the Cross of Giorgio Vasari.

Frazione about 2 km from the capital, rare example of rural architecture and starting point of many itineraries. At the centre is the church of San Giacomo, which preserves the original structure and a golden and polychrome wooden altar of the Fantoni workshop (XVII century), according to tradition the ancient high altar of the parish of Castione.
The tower of the Fabbs on the way of armies.
The medieval Nadro, a stone's throw from the engravings.

The capital and main port of Elba, the Cosmopolis fortified by Cosimo I de' Medici since 1548 and residence of Napoleon in exile: the Medici fortresses, the Palazzina dei Mulini, Villa San Martino and the white beaches of Capo Bianco and Samson.
Lake Hades, today for walks.
The wine of the territory.
The museum of the Archdiocese of Trani-Barletta-Bisceglie on Piazza Duomo, next to the Cathedral.

The palace, built on the remains of a previous structure, preserves the architecture of the sixteenth century and was restored in the mid-18th century; it houses the Town Hall and the naturalistic museum, active for over twenty years, with digital dioramas on local habitats, environmental education and guided tours also to the educational garden in the municipal park. Accessible to people with disabilities.
A Romanesque crypt in the village.

Crossing caves almost a kilometer long, explored in 1926 by Baron Carlo Franchetti and open to tourists in 1927, on two levels: a lower active branch with underground river and a higher fossil branch rich in concretions. At the entrance there is a curtain of polychrome stalactites, then ten rooms: the Sala del Lago Blu, with a waterfall of about 10 meters in a deep lake 5, the Sala del Salice Ciangente and the Sala dei Bpistrelli, which still houses a colony. Guided tour only, in groups up to 12 people; summer (1 April-1 November) 9-19, winter 10-16; recommended booking on weekends, pets not allowed.
The sanctuary-belvedere above the Trompia Valley, on foot from four villages.
The village on the Roman road.
The city park that closes the one-day itinerary in Palermo.

The parish church, next to the Town Hall, was built at the end of the seventeenth century on the remains of a Romanesque building of the thirteenth century and is considered the oldest in the Val Trebbia.
The park is the highlight.
The first covered theatre of the modern era.
Area of the Majella National Park adjacent to the abbey, a few kilometers upstream of the village, with free access: the roe deer are observed from the slitholes along the fence.
A nuraghe inside the village, almost unique case.

In the farmhouse called Cascina Palazzo was born on 25 November 1881 Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli, pope from 1958 to 1963 and saint from 2014. You can visit the arched porch, the wooden staircase that goes up to the simple rooms, the bedroom of birth with a double bed, drawer-desk and a painting of the Virgin, and a small museum of memories. Not accessible to people with motor disabilities.

At km 85 of the Via Appia, Mesa is identified with the Roman state Ad Medias; the Palazzo della Posta, of the eighteenth century, was wanted by Pius VI and in the atrium it preserves two milestones of the Appia and numerous funerary gravestones. Nearby stands a large Roman mausoleum without the covering, which a tradition attributes to the freedom of Clesippo and to the matron Gegania.
The Madonna of the Good New, fresco of the thirteenth century in the rock.
From the Apennines to the sea in one look.

Borgo della Vallesina on a rocky spur surrounded by the Esino, among the vineyards of the Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi: from the remains of the castle and the Belvedere Loggetta the look comes to the sea, and Villa Coppetti hosts the Civic Museum; at Christmas a large luminous tree lights up on the hill.
The mummy of Savoca's notables.
Walk through the Acaja palaces under the arcades.
The balcony over the Umbra valley.
The church of the nuns of St. Alphonsus.

Borgo on a ridge that divides the valleys of the Arno and Solano, with views of the Casentino, narrow alleys between leaning houses and a square tower castle that dominates it. Every year there is the cattle fair dedicated to the Chianina breed.
Walk through seventeenth century palaces from the castle to the ancient walls.
In the high town built under Siena the fortress with the Candeliere Tower, with the best view of the area.
The mother church of the valley.

Ancient transhumance road, 244 km long, between L'Aquila and Foggia, the longest of the five Regi Tratturi: there passed the flocks that from the mountains of Gran Sasso, Sirente and Maiella descended to the pastures of the Tavoliere delle Puglie. Abruzzo Turismo indicates it among the testimonies of the territory of Canosa Sannita.
Nature and Napoleonic history.
The temple on the ridge of the Valley.
Mosaics of one of the great Roman villas of the lake.
The oldest megaron temple on the island.
Ancient hamlet along the Rhine, stage of the cyclovia.

The Court of Giarola is home to the Regional River Park of the Taro, a belt of about 2,600 hectares along twenty kilometers of river, accessible on foot or by mountain bike, where more than 200 species of birds have been observed, with willows, poplars and the rare Coriaria myrtifolia. Free entrance from sunrise to sunset; the naturalistic area Le Chiesuole is open Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 15-18 (€1).
In the former Franciscan convent of Santa Maria del Riposo, founded in 1247, Etruscan and Roman sarcophagi and furnishings of the local necropolis, including the sarcophagus of the Curunas family.
The most famous terrace on Alto Garda.
UNESCO is a World Memory (document record), not a World Heritage
MiC card updated to April 2020 with contradictory timetables: check opening and prices before the visit

In the upper part of the village rustic houses, narrow alleys and noble palaces; From 1927 to 1971, Cuglieri hosted the Pontifical Theological Faculty, the first outside Rome. The other churches are visited during the festivities, open monuments and Holy Week.

The permanent exhibition entitled to Concetto Valente, with painting and sculpture of the nineteenth century of the provincial collection: works by Giacomo Di Chirico, Angelo Brando and Michele Tedesco and portraits of Giuseppe Mona, Vincenzo La Creta and Andrea Petrone.

Ethnian country linked to the cult of the holy martyrs Alfio, Filadelfo and Cirino, whose seventeenth-century sanctuary rises where tradition wants the three brothers to pause in 252 and holds almost a thousand tablets ex-vote painted between 1870 and 1970; in the historical center the Mother Church of St. Nicholas and the church of Mercy.

Medieval village born from the imperial abbey of Santa Croce al Chienti, still surrounded by the walls with the fourteenth-century doors and dominated by the Gerosolimitana Tower of 28 meters: the Romanesque collegiate church of Mercy frescoed by Pomarancio, the art gallery with the polyptychs of Vittore Crivelli and the footwear museum.
Two thousand years carved into stone.

Tower of sighting on the promontory between Foxi Manna and Foxi Murdegu, transformed into bunkers in the Second World War (the regional boards date to the XVI or the beginning of the XVIII century); below, a small pebble beach. Here stood the original village, perhaps heir of the Roman city of Saralapis; to the south of the marina the port of Santoru, used between the eight and twentieth centuries for minerals.
The history of women and hemp in the high Maira Valley.

Founded in 1939, Pomezia has a rationalist historical centre, in the Latium Historical Houses Network, with its representative core (Municipio, Civic Tower, Poste, Church of San Benedetto, Casa del Fascio, GIL school) on Independence Square. In the center the Museo Città di Pomezia is the workshop of the '900 tells the city from its foundation to the 1950s and 1960s; the Ugo Tognazzi Library (about 25,000 volumes) has an external mural inspired by the myth of Enea.

In the hamlet of Castello, where the castle of the tenth century rises, the church of Santa Maria Assunta is a national monument since 1927; the dating is discussed, between the 10th and the 5th century according to other sources.
The protected dunes of the teramana coast.
Optional booking: tel. 0985 9969, Sabap-cal.scalea@cultura.gov.it
Municipality of Montalbano with the Medici Villa La Magia, UNESCO heritage, and its park land art museum.

In the hamlet Calda, part of the MULA+ pole, in two rooms (Prehistory and Historical Age): finds of the caves of Calda from 8000 to 1300 BC and accessories of the necropolis probably enotria of Colle dei Greci (VII-V century BC), with Greek vases, weapons, bronze kisses, statuettes, ambres and the skeleton of a burial of about 2500 years ago. Open Friday-Sunday and holidays 10-13 and 16-19.
In front of Porto Levante there is the Sacca Cavallari, separated from the Adriatic by a scano called Porto Levante beach; in summer a ferry connects the port to the beach.

Since 1871 in a neoclassical building the Etruscan, Roman and Longobard finds of the territory: ceramics, sculptures, the famous canopies closed, painted urns, jewels and reconstructions of the main tombs.
The lake seen from above.
The Birth of Venus and Spring in the same hall.
The symbol of the city, surrounded by the moat still full of water.

"La Rotonda," octagonal temple with porch designed by Francesco Zamberlan, pupil of Palladio: double cycle painting of the seventeenth century Venetian, wooden choir, gold leaf altar and 57-metre bell tower of Baldassarre Longhena.
The symbolic monument of Byzantine Calabria.
The history of Monselice and the oldest San Francesco of Veneto.

The city of wool at the foot of the Small Dolomites: the High Factory and the Lanificio Conte recount the 19th century textile industry, between the historic buildings of the center and the Cathedral of San Pietro.
Roman bridge in travertine with three arches of the first century BC on Tessino, along the Via Flaminia, linked to the legends of the martyrs.

The village preserves its main monuments, Casa Pinabello-D'Amico, Palazzo Civico and Palazzo Ducale Carafa, and the church of Sant'Andrea Apostolo, patron saint celebrated with the patronal feast; according to Visit Molise a thirteenth-century mausoleum was then transformed into an angioin castle.
The violet of Valdieri where it was discovered.
The stone village on the hill.

The palace of the Barberini Column on the terraces of the sanctuary is still the residence of the prince; in addition to the museum you can visit the Barberini Nympheo, the garden of the prince of the second half of the seventeenth century, and the frescoed room where Pope Urban VIII received the guests.
Collection of devices of great historical value, including the directional antenna used on the Elettra yacht by Guglielmo Marconi.

It rises on the stable, near the walls, where in 1603 Giuseppe Maria Desa was born, then San Giuseppe da Copertino, famous for the levitation during the Mass and repeatedly suspected by the Holy Office of Naples and the Inquisition. In 1754, one year after the beatification, the University of Copertino had the current sanctuary built, incorporating the stable of irregular stones.
One of the most original monuments of the Lombard Renaissance.

Works born in the 2016 and 2017 editions of the Totart Festival, cycle of initiatives for social cohesion in the area affected by the earthquake: Ericailcane and Bastardilla on the walls of the music school Luigi Restani, Basik with Luke tuning his own picture according to its diagonal size , Giorgio Bartocci with Reversible Abstraction and Luca Zamoc with murals inspired by the Fall of the Giants of Giulio Romano and the ceramics of Filippo Tagliolini. Map on the URBANER regional portal.
A votive church with a suggestive crypt.

Established in 1977 in Palazzo Torriani (1730, now also the seat of the Town Hall), it houses the most important collection of works by Luigi Spazzapan (Gradisca 1889 - Turin 1958), about 87 works from the collection of the Turinese Eugenio Giletti, displayed in rotation on the first floor; the second floor hosts temporary exhibitions. Free with FVGcard.
The sundial hamlet.
16th century church on the edge of the village with a portal in carved sandstone, now home to the Museum of Sacred Art.
The place of the horse race of the country.

Isolated towards the sports field, it was annexed to an important Benedictine monastery, now in ruins, founded by Queen Margherita of Navarre: portal in red marble, stuccoes of the Serpottian school and high altar in golden wood with canopy of Don Corrado Oddo (1704).

Cathedral of the diocese, documented since 1146, has guarded the remains of San Cono patrono since 1261: portal and pulpit in stone (1271) of Melchiorre da Montalbano, the tomb of Enrico Sanseverino di Tino di Camaino (1336), the tombs of Bear Malavolta and Stasio d'Heustasio, the chapel of San Cono. Closed on Monday.

19th century house where Filiberto Farci, writer and co-founder of the Sardinian Action Party was born in 1882 with Emilio Lussu: the study with objects, letters and library, the kitchen with wood-burning oven, the bedroom and a section of costumes; on the ground floor the reconstruction of a workshop of the late 19th century and a section on the mine of anthracite of Fund'e Corongiu, in the basement tools and a forge, in the cellar wooden presses and a large still in copper matricola "Cagliari 0001" (a section on emigration reminds Augusto Bissiri.

Inaugurated in 1990 in Fort Sangallo, it tells the Allied landing of 22 January 1944 on the coast of Anzio and Neptune with documents, original photographs, maps, newspapers, uniforms, helmets, weapons, diaries and personal objects of soldiers and war material found in the area.
the Park indicates that the visits are booked at the Municipality (tel. 0183 328731)
Good Friday furniture.
The patron's places.
The history of hemp in the Aniene valley.

Medieval manor tied to Riccardo da Pietravalle, lord of the place in the thirteenth century, became in 1484 of the Capua, who transformed it into a Renaissance noble residence by destroying most of the military structures. In 1550 Vincenzo di Capua commissioned Donato da Copertino (called Decumbertino), formed in the school of Giorgio Vasari, a cycle of celebrated frescoes of the family, considered among the most complete of the Kingdom of Naples in the sixteenth century: mythological and biblical episodes, ancient figures, landscapes and allegories in the Salone delle Virtù and in the rooms of the Masks, the Fireplace, the Pergola, the Canneto and the Fire, as well as the Studiolo. It also houses collections of modern and contemporary art (Romeo Musa, Antonio Pettinicchi, Eliseo collection) and a permanent photographic exhibition on Maitunate; hours indicated by the Regional Direction: Tuesday-Sunday 8-19, closed on Monday.

Historical fish-bone core that climbs up the hill, with narrow and twisted alleys often closed by the defensive "meniali" and houses partly dug into the tuff; remains the Port'Alta with ogival arch, only of the three doors, and in via Tappeto the only surviving medieval house-tower. The caves "Preta" are now cellars, once a refuge of shepherds.
Sea half an hour from Rome.

Church and monastery of Farfense origin documented since 936, consecrated in 1125 according to two inscriptions; on the left bank of Chienti, it has three aisles, two floors and double-level apse with walkway and radial chapels, scheme of pilgrimage churches. In the upper apse frescoes with scenes from the childhood of Christ, a Madonna with Child attributed to the Master of Offida and two fifteenth-century statues in terracotta; the façade was rebuilt between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and next to it was rebuilt a caroling garden.
MiC card, updated to 2020, indicates the closed museum every day: check before the visit
Roman Bridges of Flaminia.

Opened in 2002 inside the park, on a floor with three rooms (the Earth, the Sacred, the Sea): a corinzio helmet in bronze of the fifth century, a stone with the dedication to the athlete Phayllos, a statue of Zeus Meilichios and a small group in marble of Love and Psyche recovered at sea; around the Garden of Hera.
The eighteenth century in Cesena.
A trail of about 2 km along the homonymous stream, with walkways, wooden bridges and galleries, which starts a short walk from the village; suitable for families.
From Ponte near Acciaroli follow the ancient road connecting with Pollica, touching the Torre della Macchia and Cannicchio with about 2 km on asphalt road; from Pollica the path of the
Pieve fuori Radda, which, despite the reconstructions, preserves the Romanesque plant and numerous works of art.
Industrial archaeology reused.
Private property, only guided tours by reservation (visite@cervara.it) on the 1st and 3rd Sunday of the month from March to October, groups of at least 30 people all year round
At Colle Don Bosco, the museum of rural life in the 19th century Monferrato, the world in which the young Giovanni Bosco grew up.
Music according to Renzo Piano.
Itinerary at 1,650 meters of altitude accompanied by wooden bells, music box, drums and trumpets, where artificial sounds blend with natural ones.

18th century farmhouse for the breeding of horses, built in 1741 on a project by Giacinto Baijs, collaborator of Benedetto Alfieri, along the ancient road to Cavaglià and Ivrea; of the plant remains the perimeter of the large court closed by two pavilions, the main one with red brick facade in need of restoration.
From the 12th century, rebuilt in Baroque forms in the 18th century.

Locality at 1,580 meters in the Stelvio National Park, at the beginning of the road to the Passo di Gavia, among the most interesting natural areas of the surroundings for landscapes and fauna along numerous paths. The source of mineral water, to which were once attributed healing virtues, was the object of never realized thermal projects between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries and has remained free: it is customary to stop at the fountain before the excursions.

Inaugurated on September 7, 2013 by Angelo Dedomenici to preserve the knowledge related to the production of Salame di Varzi, it is divided into three rooms: vintage documents, photographs and special pieces; the shop of a salumier rebuilt as it was in the thirties; a winery of ripening with the tools of processing. It is on the ground floor, barrier-free; free entrance.
The most beautiful view of the gulf.

Pre-Alpine village of the Elvo Valley, under the reserve of Monte Mars and the Macrone, already feud of the Avogadro and Laniero center; it is famous for the Passion of Sordevolo, represented every five years from 1816 (next edition 2027), with the museum in the church of Santa Marta, and for the Trappa in the high valley.
The institute that still today restores the masterpieces of Italy.
The church in the walls.
A tour through the historic villages of the valley.

Promoted by Maria Adriana Prolo, founder of the Museo del Cinema in Turin, and built in 1973 in the halls of Villa Caccia. It gathers, largely for the gift of citizens, peasants and artisans, the testimonies of the local agricultural and wine civilization: tools and agricultural machinery with a press about 13 meters long (with 3D reconstruction), the phases of the wine production and the cellar of the villa, the crafts with historical photos, and reconstructions of kitchen, room, school and tavern. Open from 15 March to 30 November, Saturday and Sunday 15-18.30; groups and schools by reservation (tel. 342 1631245).
Roman bridge of the end of the 1st century AD, about 172 meters long on 21 arches, which connected the axis of the Appia and Sinuessa to Sessa.
The home of those who created the Sacred Wood.
The prehistoric tombs of Sulcis.
The foundry that gave Italy almost all its antimony.
Alpine village of the Alta Val Chisone, Orange Flag and the most beautiful village of Italy, divided into five villages: the hamlet of bread and murals, the sundials of Balboutet, the lake of Laux.
The palace wanted by Pope Paul II in 1466 and rebuilt in 1782, with the bronze statue of Pius VI in the loggia and on the ground floor the gallery of the great exhibitions.
Woods with paths and nature trails.

Reserve established in 1997 and entrusted to the LIPU, with marsh vegetation and riparian: it is important for the wintering, the nidification and the stop of migratory birds, with mothsmen, spatulae, a colony of pendolini and the only Sicilian site of nesting of the partridge of sea; there live also the discoglosso painting and the endemic Leopoldia gussonei. Hiking is free, without leaving the marked trails in zone A.
The sacred art of the diocese next to the Duomo.
A melancholy place that enchanted romantic travelers.
A Piedmontese baroque with Mary's life cycle.

It was born from a small chapel annexed to the Bishop's House, where there remains a fresco of the Madonna and Child between two saints dating from around 1500; in 1742 it became parish church in place of St. George Martyr on the hill, and the works, begun in 1766, ended in 1913. The interior with a single nave, with five chapels on each side and semicircular apse, is richly decorated with stucco and preserves a sixteenth-century table of the Virgin of the Rosary with the fifteen Mysteries and a bas-relief of the Flagellation on the pulpit; on the stone portal the inscription "Laicalis Ecclesia S. Maria Mercy.
The Etruscan princes of Vetulonia.

Museo-cantiere in buildings of the gorge near the river port, dedicated to the river and navigation: industrial archaeology with tools and machinery used especially in the first half of the twentieth century by the Civil Genio. The name recalls the 432 km that separate Boretto from the source of the Po al Monviso.
The city cathedral, signposted among the places of worship to visit in the historic center.
The daily life of the Sand Valley told object by object.
The island to discover.
Adventure among the family pine trees.

Mountain village in the upper Val Brembana, at the foot of the Bobbio Planes: a museum path that combines the ethnographic museum in the House of the Pretura, the mill and the sweater with the wind trumpet of the Oasis of the Bolgià, reached by a mule track and a stone bridge, and the water sawmill on the stream Val Marcia.
Piazza Saffi with San Mercuriale, the Musei San Domenico with the Ebe di Canova and the great exhibitions, the Rocca di Ravaldino and a district of rationalist architecture unique in Italy.
The artificial canal that crosses the village leads a path between ancient forges, wash basins, closed and elevated canals.
Early Christian mosaics of the Aquileian type in Carnia.

Italia.it indicates it as the most beautiful of the ancient churches in the country; it is named after Saint Francis, who according to the local tradition reported by Let's Marche passed from Camerano.
The only Liberty in the country and a restored glacier.
For the Madonna del Rosario del Polinori.
The ruins of the castles above the valley.
A small amphitheater theatre.
A walled village with views of the Riviera delle Palme.
Aragonese Gothic and red porphyry bell tower.

Built in a dominant position with the horizon up to Novara and Canavese, with a double circle of walls; the origins date back to around the Mille and in 1152 Frederick Barbarossa assigned it to the bishop of Vercelli. After the Fieschis (1394) and the Savoys, at the end of the fifteenth century the Duchess Jolanda transformed it from a Romanesque fortress into a Renaissance residence and died there in 1478; in 1650 she rejected a Spanish attack. Damaged by a fire at the beginning of the 19th century and abandoned, it has been restored since 1972 and opened to the public in 1996.
The bridge over the canyon.

Small village on a hill above the Pennavaire Valley, dominated by the 14th-century castle of Counts Cepollini, with the loggia from which on clear days you can see the sea; three kilometers away is the sanctuary of the Madonna del Lago, the theatre in July of the Procession of Christs.
Lonely chapel of the seventeenth century at the entrance of the village, with paintings and frescoes dedicated to the saint, made as thanksgiving for the received.
The fourteenth century and the contemporary in the same room.
A break among the olive trees in the name of the botanist of the village.

Artisan workshop of the early twentieth century, today a museum of local crafts supported by the Gruppo Ricerca Storica di Breganze. It is located along the path of the ancient opifici that leads from via Castelletto to Maglio Tamiello. Visits by reservation, lasting about one hour.

Borgo del Vibonese in the Regional Natural Park of the Serre, on the edge of the WWF Oasis of Lake Angitola: in the district Pendino the five-cruci Calvary and the museum house Il Romitorio, at Palazzo Mannacio the Museum of identity, in the surroundings the ruins of Rocca Angitola and the convent of Santa Maria della Croce.
Mosaics on the Roman Forum.
Entirely in large basalt blocks: trilobed nuraghe of the Middle Bronze (XV-XIV century B.C.), antemural with towers and remains of a village of huts until the Iron Age.
White alleys and arches around the medieval castle.
Taste the wine of the Lepini where it is born.
The museum in the vineyards.

Sanctuary with two naves in the capital, preceded by a pronao on pillars with round arches, roof in stone louse, frescoed facade with religious subjects and statue of the Madonna with Child on the tympanum, brick bell tower. The Cantellino is linked to the patronal feast of the Nativity of Mary.

Permanent exhibition set up by the Municipality on rural houses of raw earth, built with the technique of the  "massone" , a mixture of straw, water and land; recognized for over thirty years (celebrated in 2023), it is located in Villa De Lollis and is the heart of the Festa della Terra in September, with workshops, seminars and exhibitions on architecture on earth.
The Alpine fauna.
Ancient seat of the court, residence of the Podestà and school; until the 1960s he hosted the prisons, including the  "Marza" (Marza), a hard cell to which was accessed from a trapdoor.
The oldest neighborhood, with the walls bastionata of the sixteenth century.
The beaches of the municipality, from the promenade of Milano Marittima to the Riviera dei Pini.
The forum of the Roman city crossed by the Decuman, today Augustus course; the name recalls the three partisans hanged here on August 16, 1944.
Torre del Greco is the most populous center of the park; from the city start excursions to the crater and in the port and in the historic center are visible the lava banks of the past eruptions.
€8; €2 EU citizens 18-25 years old; free under 18; cumulative with Memorial €12 (only at the premises)
A Vallesina peasant party.
Gothic Angevin in the center.
Where the country survived the battle.

It is located in Codogna in the eighteenth-century Villa Camozzi, today also town hall. Ecomuseum and visitor centre with sections of fauna, flora, paleontology and ethnography and a section dedicated to Val Sanagra (orography, paths, ecology). From May to September the second and last Sunday of the month, from October to April the last Sunday, 10-12.30 and 14-17.30; also indicated the opening by reservation.
The beach in the cliffs.

Founded in 1828 with the legacy of naturalist Giambattista Brocchi, from 1840 in the former convent of San Francesco: the largest collection of Jacopo Bassano and his workshop, a wing dedicated to Canova with plasters and monochromes, and the crucifix of the Guariento.
The largest and best preserved of the Roman arches, completed in 315 A.D. for the victory of Constantine over Maxentius, with sculptures taken from other monuments.
A canvas by Pietro Novelli.

A noble residence born in the early seventeenth century from the union of two sixteenth-century houses, still owned by the descendants of the powerful Swiss family of Salis: facade with two towers and baroque portal designed by Vignola, courtyard of the frescoed sundial, staircase, Salone delle feste and Saloncello with frescoed ceilings in the eighteenth century, cellars and glaciers. The museum trail of 10 rooms exhibits antique furniture, paintings and documents on the family and Valtellina; the Italian garden is a rarity in the Alpine area. Guided tours of about 50 minutes from April to the end of October, in the rest of the year only by reservation (minimum 4 people).

In the old town hall, it tells the history of the village: the foundation by Savoiardi shepherds, medieval migrations from Bergamasca and Valsesia, smuggling after the decline of the mines and the birth, in the nineteenth century, of the mountain guides protagonists of the mountaineering in Turin. The core is a collection of great vintage photos of mountaineers and expeditions, with equipment, relics, posters and documents; complete the section itinerary on flora, fauna, minerals and Franco-Provençal culture and a historical-naturalistic itinerary. Visits by reservation (tel. 0123 82902); accepts the Museums Subscription.
The traditions and nature of the village in an original museum.

Church of the fourteenth century near Porta XX Settembre, with Romanesque elements in facade and bell tower in terracotta begun in 1429; inside frescoes of the fourteenth century, an eighteenth-century organ and a Madonna with saints of Palma il Giovane.
Ancient and characteristic village at 827 m, with about 300 inhabitants: stone buildings with wooden balconies used to dry chestnuts and corn, arched windows and roofs in lovable.
Temporarily closed for renovation works (SardiniaCulture card updated to 13/10/2026); can open for parties and events
closed since August 2017 due to risk of falling boulders, area forbidden to vehicles and pedestrians; still closed in June 2023 with ongoing work (Sicily Region)
the card of the Municipality (agg. 15/10/2024) indicates the temporarily closed structure
A curious Renaissance saintly aquarium.
The church in the shape of trullo.

Remains of part of a Roman villa with first plant of the first century BC, used after various renovations until the Constantine era: testimony of the settlement in the valley of the Sele and the Roman Eburum, town hall as attested by an honorary inscription of the second century A.D.
Aperitif and evening walk on the river.

The capital of Irpinia: the 36-metre-high Clock Tower, the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and San Modestino, Piazza della Libertà with the Bishop's and Caracciolo palaces, the ruins of the Longobard Castle and the Irpino Museum in the former Bourbon Prison.
Cathedral, Ghirlandina Tower and Piazza Grande have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997. A unique ticket opens Galleria Estense, Museo Civico, Gipsoteca and room immersive Avia Pervia.

An arched bridge built directly on the rock, in its current form since 1591, with two eighteenth-century newsstands (one dedicated to St. John Nepomuceno, protector from the floods). In the Middle Ages it was the only crossing of the Frodolfo torrent, with a customs for those who arrived from the pass Gavia.

It exhibits about 1,000 Sardinian minerals, 300 fossils from Paleozoic to Quaternary, insects and lepidopterans, about 400 species of Sardinian birds, 70 mammals, 200 types of sea shells, amphibians, reptiles, fish and a large turtle Caretta caretta.
Where the Maira Valley is born.
Borgo on a rock spur among the chestnut groves, famous for its red marble and thermal waters at almost 50 °C.
Baroque palace of Corso Magenta managed by the Regional Direction National Museums Lombardy, which can be visited at public events and reservations.

Vico's bakeries have developed a more crisp variant of Neapolitan pizza, also served \"to the metro"; from the Lattari Mountains come the Provolone del Monaco DOP, cheese with seasoned spun pasta, the chestnuts of the priest, walnuts for the walnut and the extra virgin olive oil DOP Sorrentine Peninsula.

Romanesque church considered the oldest religious building in the city, probably of Lombard or Carolingian origin; the bell tower, about 23 meters high, is inclined, but the slope has never compromised its stability.

Traditional buildings in wood and stone, once home and family farm, scattered throughout the valley and symbol of its history; walking and winter trails with snowshoes connect them to the huts, even with guided excursions of the Park. Small hamlets like Valorz and Pedergnana preserve the traditional system.

It includes the Lachea Island, the Faraglione Grande, the Faraglione Piccolo and four other cliffs arranged in arch, with hundreds of species of algae, prairies of posidonia, saraghi, octopus, starfish and sponges; it is explored with snorkeling and diving or by boat, even with transparent background or with small gozzos of fishermen of Aci Trezza, appreciated at sunset.
Contemporary art in an ancient palace.

Inaugurated in September 2017 in the former Convent of the Augustinians, under the protection of the National Superintendence for the Underwater Cultural Heritage, it holds many finds emerged from the excavations of the Messapian necropolises. According to the MiC card the visit of the cloister is on reservation.
The green along the river.
Alpine hamlet between ovens and terraces.
The park of 30 hectares with works by international artists spread in the landscape and the Wood of Magic, protected area with 26 species of butterflies.
The majolica of Rapino, the tradition that made the country known.
A fully Baroque church with a cedar statue of the Madonna of Loreto of Lebanon, which the tradition wants carved by Saint Luke.
Woods, flowers and stars.

Small church built around 1850 on a cliff overlooking the sea, in the venerated place as the first burial of the martyrs Gavino, Proto and Gianuario: three rooms partly dug into the rock, of Roman and early medieval funerary use, a barrel chapel probably of the seventh century and, over a grate on the square, a Roman hypogeum. Normally closed, it opens throughout the month of May, when you bring there the wooden simulations of the three saints kept in the basilica.
The parish church on the square, with a painting by Bernardo Strozzi.
The walled village on the promontory of Circe.

Hiking trail (grade E) of about 3 km and 190 m of difference in altitude along the Ovesca stream, from the square of San Bartolomeo to the hamlet Boschetto, among deep waters appreciated for sport fishing. Touch the church of San Bartolomeo, the Napoleonic Bridge, the church of Piaggio, the church of Noga and the hydroelectric power station, with bulletin boards, panoramic points and parking areas.
The highest viewpoint in the village.
Church of 1749 on a project by Giuseppe Rossetti, seat since 1999 of the Museum of Sacred and Liturgical Art.
The summer of 1944 in Apennines.
The tools of the world.
Woods and panoramas at the entrance of the Abruzzo National Park.
Where today's calendar was born.
The only intact medieval building in the village.
The bridge suspended on the gravina that divides the city in two.

Castello documented from the 11th century, of the Ubertini and then divided with the monks of Camaldoli, submitted to Florence in 1386; from 1870 the Bastogi family had it rebuilt in neo-Gothic and neo-romantic style by an architect who had worked in Brolio. Rotate around a cloister with the small church of Santa Maria a Valenzano; today it is private and houses a hotel, with the stone mill still active and exhibitions in the cellars. You can visit the garden; in July the Valenzano Symphony festival.
Stop along the cycle path of the Molini Canal.
The last gallery of Alabaster Scaglione.
Germanic's bronze.

Born between 1660 and 1670 as a barn, it was transformed into a theatre in 1792; almost destroyed in the Great War, it was rebuilt in 1923 with the porch on the square, reopened in 1929 and, after a long closure, returned to the public on April 21, 2009. Eleonora Duse and Mina performed there.
The Cuneo market.
Medieval gate on a steep slope on the sea along the coastal path, crossed over the centuries by popes, Machiavelli, Carlo V and Napoleon.
The aristocratic residence of the collector Gian Giacomo Poldi Pezzoli, museum since 1881, with paintings of the Italian Renaissance and decorative arts: weapons, porcelain, carpets and watches.
An unfinished work.
A cool corner between the river and the canal.
Built in wood in 1823 inside the then municipal palace and opened in Carnival 1830: 22 stages for the families of the village and two public, the pontifical governor and the magistrate.
The imposing fortress, probably from Romanesque times, historic residence of Castruccio Castracani, with the nearby Palazzo del Forte.

Built in the second half of the first century AD under Nero, Vespasian and Titus, third in size after the Colosseum and the amphitheatre of Capua: up to 40,000 spectators on three orders of steps; the underground at 7 meters of depth, the best preserved part, with devices for raising animals and sets.

Founded probably between the 11th and 12th centuries on a variant of the Via Francigena towards the Passo del Tea, between pastures, fields and vineyards on the border with Garfagnana, owes the current Baroque aspect to a renewal of mid-eighteenth century. A portal bears the Malaspinian symbol of the dry plum, inside there is a canvas with the Last Supper and on the façade is walled the fragment of a pilgrim figure, the only marble element dating back to the Middle Ages.
The polyptych of Vivarini under the majolica dome.
Rebuilt environments with tools, domestic tools and ethnographic collections on the cycles of rural life.

In 1183 the Paduan family of the da Baone gave the castrum Baonis and the lordship to the Marquis Obizzo d'Este. The castle, in trachyte with a large tower that was also the residence of the lord, controlled the eastern entrance to Este together with the castle of Monte Cero and the fortification of Calaone; in the mid seventeenth century it was already destroyed and the walls transformed into vineyard. The ruins can be reached with a stone staircase along the path n. 8.
Next to the cathedral are the works of Filippo Lippi, Donatello and Michelozzo, including the original panels of the pulpit.

Large square with baroque palaces and the Collegiate Church of San Martino, designed by the royal engineer G. B. Manni was completed in 1733, with the facade preceded by a curved ramp staircase. The Palazzo del Genio is also located on the square.
The Iris Garden opens only from the end of April to 20 May, free of charge
A walled hamlet in lava stone under Vesuvius.
The garden of the Savoy.
Fashion capital.

The hilly village of Sabina, called Aspra until 1947 and quoted by Virgilio in the seventh book of the Aeneid; the historic center, entirely pedestrian, preserves walls, medieval towers and walks and rises up to the church of San Giovanni Battista, while just outside the village stands Santa Maria in Legarano.
after the earthquake of 2016 the old town is partially accessible and some areas are red areas with no access
