Renaissance city on the ridge between Valdichiana and Val d'Orcia, home of Vino Nobile, with Piazza Grande and the temple of San Biagio under the walls.

The little church is mentioned from the fifteenth century together with the convent of the Servants of Mary, but it is probably older; originally dedicated to the prophet Daniel and then to the Madonna del Carmine, it preserves a Roman walled inscription. Not far away, on the river Mezzaruolo, the Balabardo Bridge dates back to 1647 but is probably older.

Of very ancient origins, it rises in a dominant position on the site of a chapel destroyed in the medieval struggles between Prince Bishops of Trento and Castelbarco; damaged in the Great War, it was reconsecrated in the present form in 1929. It has a baroque portal surmounted by the statue of the Assumption, nine altars in polychrome marble, a altarpiece of Saint Lucia patron saint of the velvet makers attributed to the school of Cignaroli and a collection of vestments in 18th century alense velvet.
The Venice of the eighteenth century inside a period palace.
A corner of Liguria in Monferrato.
An outdoor art gallery.

The parish church houses a statue of the Madonna    \ Consolatrix Â of Giulio Monteverde; next to it stands a slender medieval tower, the only rest of the castle of the fortified village of 1253, dismantled by the Spanish after the war of Spanish succession.
The villa of the first Empress.
The frescoes of the village.
The other shrine.

New land founded by the Florentines in 1299 with plant attributed to Arnolfo di Cambio and birthplace of Masaccio: between Masaccio Square and Cavour Square overlook the Palazzo d'Arnolfo with the Museo delle Terre Nuove, the Basilica of Santa Maria delle Grazie with the Museum of the Annunciation of Blessed Angelico, San Lorenzo and the Pieve di San Giovanni Battista; on Corso Italia the Casa Masaccio, contemporary art center.

The town of Val Brembana is home to the Baroque painter Carlo Ceresa, whose birthplace is now a museum; on the Via Mercatorum the ancient village of Oneta houses the House of Arlecchini dei Grataroli, traditionally linked to the birth of the famous mask.
One of the two districts of the Sassi, to the south, where the presence of the caves is more visible: a maze of alleys, cave houses, terraces and tunnels dug into the rock, inhabited until the 1950s.
The unfinished palace of contemporary art.
Enter the dome of a historic Italian telescope.
A thirteenth-century church with 18th-century frescoes.
The ruins of Deledda's barons.

The porticos were born in the Middle Ages, when the village was rebuilt under Bishop Sicardo, and run on two rows along Via Roma, with shops and shops, from Torrazzo towards Borgo Serio; they were refurbished in 1849. The porticoed houses have medieval and Renaissance structure. Every second Sunday of the month the centre hosts the antique market, born in April 1988, the first of the province of Cremona.
The Cremonian Middle Ages at a glance.
Fountain formed by two arched bodies, built in several phases.
A picture gallery inside a village church.
Outside the center, cited in 998 as St. Petri de Melesino; it preserves a baptismal font and Gothic frescoes.
The largest historical market in Lake Maggiore.
The Municipality describes the site as totally in abandonment and ruin in slow unraveling
The castle on the spur.
For a walk in the plain.
The peasant life painted on the walls.

About a kilometer from the old town, a small rock church with an underground crypt dating back to the IX-X century, in the Lombard age; on the crypt the church was built. For centuries, Byzantine monks lived in the area, leaving artistic and spiritual traces, and it is an important place of worship and Marian pilgrimage.

On the top of the hill, it was born in the III-II century B.C. (they remain a wall in isodome blocks and seats with inscriptions), but what is seen is largely the Roman renovation of the first half of the second century AD, attributed to Trajan or Hadrian; between the second and third century it was transformed into a arena. With 109 metres in diameter it is the largest in Sicily after that of Syracuse; the scene retains the two lateral openings and the columns of the frons are a nineteenth-century reconstruction. In the Casina degli Inglesi an epigraphic collection with Greek inscriptions of the II-I century BC; Goethe wrote that never before did the audience of a theater have such a spectacle.
One of the historic spas of Italy.

Country of the high valley of Pescara, with origins in a dress centre, famous above all for the Benedictine Abbey of San Clemente in Casauria, founded in the ninth century on the Via Claudia Valeria and rebuilt in the twelfth century by the abbot Leonate, which houses the Antiquarium ...Pier Luigi Calore.
A master court with his tower.
A quiet basilica.
The house where Raphael was born, today a small museum.
Beaches awarded for families.
Norman Romanesque Basilica documented since 1071, with a mosaic of 1160 and the cap of San Cataldo, begun in 1630 and frescoed in the dome.
The church carved in the rock on the sea.

To the north of Velva, on the border with Maissana, the sanctuary was started in the 19th century on the project of architect Maurizio Dufour, at the will of the population. It preserves a wooden crucifix and the wooden group of the Madonna della Guardia carved by Antonio Canepa in 1892, brought to Velva in 1894 after the exhibition in the Genoese churches of Santa Maria delle Vigne and San Torpete. On August 29, a procession climbs from the village to the sanctuary.
The almond wine where he was born.
The crypt is the strong piece.
Where Dante quotes Treviso.
A surprising neo-Gothic.
The high village of the Cinque Terre.
Pavilion on Lake Fusaro commissioned by Ferdinand IV of Bourbon to Carlo Vanvitelli and completed by 1782, reachable by a wooden bridge.
An enigmatic medieval maze.
The marble altar inlaid.
The medieval living room of Marca.

The municipality of the Upper Antrona Valley, in the Nature Park of the same name: Lake Antrona, born from the landslide of 1642, the Baroque parish of San Lorenzo rebuilt after the catastrophe, the basins of Campliccio and Cavalli under the Pizzo Andolla, the mountain pasture of Cheggio and the gold mine of the Taglione open to guided tours.
The largest protected sea in Italy.

A village in the Trompia Valley among mountains that many call the Brescia Dolomites, with the Ethnographic Museum and Farm House in the hamlet of Invico, the eighteenth-century sanctuary of the Holy Cross reachable on foot and the pine forest of the Alpine Park at the foot of the Caspai.
18th century residence with the garden designed by Borgese in 1751.

Supported by the homonymous association founded in 1977 by teachers of the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Turin, it preserves about 1,600 objects, from simple tools to agricultural machines of historical interest, all inventoryed and catalogued. Times to check with the museum.
granite bays for all winds.

Naturalistic Museum dedicated to the Tiber and linked to the Tiber-Farfa Reserve, founded in 2000 in the former granaries and stables of the Savelli Castle. Interactive paths follow the river from the source to the mouth, with aquariums, reconstructions of habitats, micro-organisms and insects; the naturalistic section, didactic, has 3D microscopes and photos, the archaeological fossil finds of Nazzano and the middle valley of the Tiber, and the room of temporary exhibitions overlooks with large windows on Piazza della Rocca.

Square with square plan built at the end of the eighteenth century, with the central fountain of 1909 by engineer Giovanni Paolucci; Palazzo Jelardi, built in 1850, is overlooking it by the Jesuit Giovan Battista Iazeolla and restored between 2012 and 2016, with the Museum of Advertising in the attic, and Palazzo Colarusso, home of the Town Hall since 2015. Not far away, between Via and Largo Vicidomini, stands Palazzo Zurlo, former marquisal palace of the Cavaniglia with terraces and turret.

The construction was promoted in 1606 by the Confraternity of the Holy Trinity; it has a single nave, six side chapels and a choir-oratory, with wooden sculptures of the sixteenth century. It was reopened to worship in 2001 after extensive restoration.
The famous waters of the village, at the source.

Medieval tower of Angevin age overlooking Piazza Cavour, reopened in July 2023 after a conservative restoration financed by the Metropolitan City: the interior and exterior spaces host exhibitions and events, and the ring terrace on the square has returned public space.

The present appearance dates back to the reconstruction after the earthquake of 1732: the ceiling paintings are by Antonio Vecchione da Nola (XVIII century), with a major altar in polychrome marble and statues of the Seven-Ottocento. In the hypogeum remain the early medieval building (VIII-IX century), a Roman re-utilization column and the ancient scroungers; an inscription in the church recalls the architect Antistius, designer of the Roman cisterns.
A medieval castle near a nature reserve.
The stone that paved the cities of the North.
An experiment of working city on the Bisenzio.
Rare Roman windows of Lomellina inside a Visconti castle.
Baroque and the fountain of Di Sangro.

Baroque church of the early eighteenth century built on the site of a 15th century church, restored in 2001. It preserves the Annunciation of the Annunciation of the Antonellian coveted (early XVI century, frame of 1560), the cross painted on the table of the SS. Crucifix, patron, in the middle of the fifteenth century, the eighteenth-century choir in walnut with 24 barns and the marble statue of Saint Catherine of Alexandria coming from St. Francis.
Paths on volcanic hills just a stone's throw from the spa.
The shopping streets of luxury, along with the vintage shops of the Cinque Vie.
The highest mine in Europe, between tunnels and mining village.
A village of novenanti in the country.
Visitor center of the diffused ecomuseum of the plain of Osoppo-Gemona, dedicated to earthquake and reconstruction; guided tours by reservation.

Born in the second century BC as a pastoral market at the intersection of Flaminia and Salaria, it became a town hall in the Cesarian age and is mentioned by Pliny; not a city but a complex of public buildings: civil basilica, forum, temple perhaps dedicated to Hercules, thermal baths, amphitheatre in wood, tabernacles and aqueduct. Among the olive groves next to the church are stretches of paved road, walls in cross-linked work and arches of the aqueduct.
restoration of the fountain started on 31/3/2025 and redevelopment of the square in project (page updated 11/11/2025): check if the works are finished
The largest lake in the Apennines.

Show permanent "Tiere Motus." History of an earthquake and its people are on the first floor of the sixteenth-century Palazzo Orgnani-Martina: photos, videos and documents on the earthquake of May 6, 1976, from the day of the shock to the reconstruction, with a 3D simulation of the collapse of the cathedral.

Inaugurated in 2022 in the former Habsburg barracks of San Tomaso, next to the homonymous church: the evidence of archaeological research in the city and in the territory of Verona, from prehistory onwards, including the "Sciamano" (Sciamano), perhaps the oldest human figure in the world.
The seventeenth century Lombardy in the center.
The treasure of the tombs of San Giuliano.
Manenti's self-portrait dressed as a pope.
The Messengers of Oria.
Cobblestone streets, stone houses and traditional architecture; some buildings are still in clay, typical construction technique of the area.
A Romanesque parish church and the fifteenth-century statue of the saint.
The church of the village with the waterfall behind it.
One of the most complete Maserati collections open to the public, born from the passion of the entrepreneur Umberto Panini; from June 2025 in the new headquarters of Marzaglia.
Built by the survivors of the plague of 1656, it overlooks Piazza Roma and is known for its crypt.

Overlooking the lakefront, it is documented as early as 1224, the year of a pact between the archbishop of Milan and the local nobles. It preserves the Romanesque bell tower and, inside three aisles, a Romanesque stone head walled in a bench, an architectural fragment over a holy water table and furnishings that testify to the richness of the families of the village.
Private property for residential use (SIRBEC card); the villas open thanks to the owners during the walk between the villas (Common)
A popular museum where contemporary art and sabino oil meet.

Coast tower built around 1550 by order of Viceroy Don Pedro of Toledo against the Saracens and entrusted to the Knights of Malta: square plant, pyramidal trunk, four rooms and terrace on top; appears in the city coat of arms.

Inaugurated in 1996, it contains about thirty works by Eugenio Pellini (1864-1934), his son Eros Pellini (1909-1993) and Adriano Bozzolo (1927-2011), in a country linked to the tradition of the plasterers and the "picapietra" ('picapietra'). On 1 May 2016, the new headquarters was opened; access is free (tel. ) (a.k.a

The Gori & Zucchi corporate museum, a historic goldsmith's manufacture, is reported by Visit Tuscany.

UNESCO vineyards within walking distance.
Frescoes in the countryside, a stone's throw away.
A Romanesque oratory outside the door.
A park full of surprises.
A peasant house the way it was.

Cited in 864, rebuilt around 915 by Berengario I and consecrated in 997; held a Urban II Synod in 1095 and a Paschal Council II in 1106. The present Romanesque aspect comes from the works of 1926-31; inside a baptismal font of the IX-X century and a Madonna and Child in terracotta attributed to Guido Mazzoni.

The primitive church of the 12th century, in the center of the village, was also a destination for pilgrims from outside Abruzzo; the current, designed by Alessio Mancini in modern Romanesque style, was started in 1954 and inaugurated in 1963. Inside the golden stuccoes of the Bravo brothers of Atessa, a reproduction of the Annunciation attributed to the Reni in the vault, the mosaic of the bezel with San Mauro among the sick and, in the niche of the altar, the polychrome terracotta image of the seventeenth century; in front of a portico and a bell tower isolated in red bricks with the 'campanella of San Mauro', which the devotees bite against the toothache. The churches are usually closed: you visit by contacting the parish (0872 860113); opened on the last Sunday of the month 7-12 and on 15 January, feast of the saint.
Six hundred Brescia, with the crucifix by Maffeo Olivieri.
A little church of the fourteenth century with stratified frescoes.
The memory of Grande Torino in over a thousand relics.
The ancient crafts of western Friuli.

Built by the Austro-Hungarians in 1880-1882, twin of the fort of Tenna, 660 meters on the hill south of the lake: Porphyd and granite housematte with moat, four levels and central corridor, originally armed with four 12 cm cannons and two obici in revolving armoured domes. Disarmed in the spring of 1915, it was only an observatory and a warehouse in war; partly restored for the centenary of the Great War. From the thermal baths you go up via San Biagio and then a dirt road; guided tours in the program
Torrent that flows into a narrow and high valley, among spectacular rock formations.
The house of flour is an ethnographic museum with agricultural tools; in the city some houses of Campidanese preserve frescoed ceilings and floors in tiles with geometric motifs.
The hexagonal piazza Campo del Palio and Piazza Vittorio Alfieri; the Palio is the medieval reenactment of the first half of September.
One of the highest beech forests in Europe, just a few minutes walk from the country that dominates from above.
From 1000 to Baroque in a few churches.

Collection of stuffed animals of the Lombard fauna, ordered in five sections: invertebrates, fish, amphibians and reptiles, birds and mammals. Open Tuesday and Friday 15-18.30 and Saturday 10-12.30, the other days on request; guided tours available, entrance and parking accessible by wheelchair.
Historical and naturalistic itinerary equipped from the village to the fort, with views of the Lemme Valley.
Theater can be visited by reservation or with the guided tour of the archaeological museum
A place of memory of the Resistance.
The Romanesque church.
Sea of the Costa degli Aranci under the village.
In the middle of Via Cavour, the basilica with the fifteenth-century portico that houses Michelangelo's Moses of 1513, part of the tomb of Julius II, and the chains of St. Peter under the high altar.
Fossils of the Paleozoic a stone's throw from the village.
A well-preserved old Salento center, among Renaissance palaces.

The Baroque town of Ragusano is located around Piazza Fonte Diana, with the fountain linked to the myth of Diana and the loggia of Palazzo Iacono-Ciarcià attributed to Rosario Gagliardi: the Mother Church of Santa Maria delle Stelle, the Basilica of the Annunziata, the Naselli Theatre, the Civic Museum of Natural History and the Foundation dedicated to Gesualdo Bufalino.
At the Fara, the former monastery now seat of the University of Bergamo, surrounded by a park.
Historic garden with centuries-old trees around the villa, whose oldest part dates back to the last thirty years of the seventeenth century and which today houses the Museum of the Great Turin.
The church of the Godfather on the rock spur.
second In Lombardy open only from July to the end of September, Friday-Sunday 14-18 (groups on request); the Touring indicates Friday-Sunday 14-19

Involucre and bell tower of the fifteenth century, facade and interior with three aisles of the eighteenth century: Baptism of Christ of Bastianino, fifteenth-century Crucifix and paintings by Giuseppe Maria Crespi and other Emilian painters. Seriously damaged by the earthquake of 2012, with the collapse of part of the facade and of the times, it was restored with seismic improvement and reopened to worship in May 2024.
Small and sumptuous, in the heart of Verdi's land.
Secular holm oaks, mouflons and a nuraghe become a glacier.
The beach for families with views of Vesuvius.

Renaissance church leaning on a tower of the walls, which became the apse; it has two sacred rooms superimposed with Umbrian-Marches frescoes from the 15th to the 16th century. The name comes from an image of Our Lady of Liberator, called "Madonna de Libera" (Madonna de Libera).
An eighteenth-century sober near the center.
The cargo of a Roman ship as it was stored.

The historic centre, with the Palazzo del Pretorio and the church of Santa Maria Assunta, overlooks a lakefront with tree-lined avenues, meadows and small ports suitable for walks and picnics. Since 2016 the Museo Diffuso has connected dozens of historical, artistic and landscape monuments of the village, the Capronno and Barzola villages and the surroundings with open-air rooms.

Borgo su Poggio Ballone, about 260 m, which preserves castle, arches, doors, walls and palaces with medieval towers; in the thirteenth century lands and castle were Pannocchieschi. Every August the historic center houses the Salto della Contessa, re-enactment in costume dedicated to Pia de' Tolomei.
A century of Mantua painting.
Theme exhibitions on the car that change every season.
An underground canyon, different in every season.
Useful before the caves.
Where Levi lived the Confino.
discordant times: MiC card (updated 2021) indicates closed every day, Tourism Marches indicates festive and daily openings in summer (ju-set)

An eighteenth-century Marian shrine in the hamlet Gera, on the right bank of the Adda, covered inside and outside with golden and polychrome marbles and mosaics dedicated to the Virgin, the work of Fr.Pietro Mizzi, pastor until 1999; it houses an interactive exhibition on its history.
The 108 angel heads and the canvases of Peccheneda.
An Etruscan rock theatre.
the MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day: check opening

Beech woods and clearings where they graze free Maremma cattle and horses, indicated as one of the oldest woods of Lazio, with trees of over five hundred years; the Natural Monument is managed by the Municipality of Allumiere.
Simone's 16th century polyptych from Florence.

Terraced path built by the Spaniards in the eighteenth century that descends from the city to the seaside village of Santa Maria La Scala; it is accessed from the bridge on the National Road from Via Romeo.
The ancient tower of the Cassero, from whose top opens the view of the city; if it is closed, the green of the Park Sant'Angelo behind it still offers a view of the valley.
Giotteschi frescoes and panorama of the Passiria.

Palazzo dei Conti Savoiroux along the main road: a single body on three floors, of severe and massive style, without balconies or loggias, with a shady park dominated by a century-old ginkgo biloba. It hosts the two-year Casalbeltrame Award "The Golden Frog" and the Materima exhibition spaces, open on Saturday from 10 am to 6 pm.

At the Alpe di Pampeago, the stage finishes in five editions of the Giro d'Italia, you will climb by chairlift towards the Latemar, where in summer there is RespirArt, an art park with contemporary installations and concerts at the Teatro del Latemar; in winter the Ski Center Latemar, connected to Predazzo and Obereggen, has about 45 km of slopes. At Malga Pampeago you learn to milk and make butter.

The Palazzo Comunale, with a beautiful eighteenth-century façade, was built after the earthquake of 1751 destroyed the previous Palazzo dei Rectori delle Arti e dei Priori; the 12th-century Civic Tower is the only surviving part of the Palazzo del Podestà. In the center also Santa Maria di Tadino, the oldest church in the historic center, today seat of the Giochi de le Porte (revocation in the last week of September).
Romanesque church of the thirteenth century in the lower part of the village (Cotronianu and josso).
The glass blown live.

The hilly village of the Acquese is dominated by the castle, enlarged by the Malaspina, the counts of Lodron and the Genoese princes Centurione, with views of the Bormida valley from Monte Rosa to the Ligurian Apennines. Next, in Piazza Castello, the sixteenth-century parish church of San Bartolomeo; outside the center the country church of San Pasquale.

Country north of Novara, on the road to Lake Maggiore, in the area of the civilization of Golasecca and mentioned for the first time in a document of 885. The heart is the seventeenth-century Villa Soranzo, now the seat of the Municipality with the Archaeological Museum and the Pinacoteca "Cesare Belossi" (Cesare Belossi), next to the Romanesque parish church of Saints Vincenzo and Anastasio and the sanctuary of Our Lady of the Rosary.

Born in the fifteenth century with Roberto Sanseverino, renovated by Francesco Farnese with the fountains of Proserpina and Trianon by Giuliano Mozzani, then French with the Bourbons (parterre by François Anquetil called Delisle on a project by Petitot) and English with Maria Luigia (1816-1823), with the lake and the island of love.Renovated between 1998 and 2000 restoring the parterre del Delisle. Open every day from 7am to 6pm (to 8pm with daylight saving time); audioguide €3 at the ticket office.
Street art in the Roman Castles.
Ruins of a village mentioned in 1078 and 1291, along the Via Francesca, reachable in about ten minutes for a mule track.
From Conero to Maiella at a glance.
The Spanish in the cathedral.

In the historic centre, a short walk from Villa Durazzo and the castle, a multimedia and interactive setting on the life and work of the writer Camillo Sbarbaro, born in Santa Margherita; is part of the museum complex of Villa Durazzo.
The shrine is between the holly.
Rare example of medieval architecture in Rome (VI century) with, under the porch, the marble mask of the Mouth of Truth made famous by Roman Holidays.
Twelve monumental clocks scattered across the streets of the country, a real open-air museum freely accessible at any time.

On the promontory above the port, the arch is what remains of the bell tower of a missing church or a watchtower, destroyed by the earthquake of 1930; next stands a bronze monument to fishermen. The nearby viewpoint dominates the port and coast.
Neoclassical arena designed by Ireneo Aleandri and built in the twenties of the nineteenth century with a private subscription; every summer it hosts the opera festival outdoors.
The sacred architecture of the twentieth century.
A walk between the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.
The castle of the Abbots of Fruttuaria with the tower of the mint.
The country grew up with sulfur mines.
Church of the fourteenth century that dominates the historic village with its characteristic square, at the foot of the Castle Brancaleoni.

Former mining site in Zone A (full reserve) of the National Park of Alta Murgia, recovered by the Park Authority: the quarries are observed from above from educational areas and panoramic points, while the descent is forbidden. From September 2024 the visits are regulated and managed by Pro Loco Torre and Pino, only by reservation from Friday to Sunday, with hourly shifts (9-12 and 16-18); free standard visit, specialized environmental guide for payment.

In the centre of the village, Stura falls with a jump of some tens of meters, overwhelmed by a bridge inspired by the one built at the end of the nineteenth century by the guide Antonio Castagneri at the initiative of the CAI. Around an ancient mill, the buildings to cool the milk, an ice-box dug into the rock of the gorge and, at the base of the jump, a small power plant inaugurated in 1909 and still in operation.

Built in the thirteenth century by the Atranese as a votive church to thank the Virgin of protection from the Saracens: a unique room with barrels with two large windows and baroque façade; in the small sacristy a Roman urn in white marble. The majolica dome and the square bell tower are the symbol of the Atrani profile.

Country of Salento near Otranto called "Giardino megalithico d'Italia" for the numerous menhirs and the seven dolmen still intact scattered between center and countryside, including the Dolmen Stabile and the Menhir of São Paulo. In the village the Crypt of St. Saviour of the eighth century, the Column of St. Rocco and the underground mill 16th century Trappitello del Duca.
The frescoes by Andrea de Lithium.
A Titian in the cathedral.
Walk on a lava flow of a volcano \"bonsai" .
The integral reserve of Sasso Fratino is not open to the public: it can be seen from the external paths
The walk overlooking the Fortress of Angera, on the Lombard shore.

Since 2009 in the 15th century complex of Sant'Agostino: finds from prehistoric times to the Enotri and Brettii, which in 356 BC had in Cosenza their center, accessories of the necropolis of Torre Mordillo and relics of the Risorgimento linked to the Bandiera brothers.

Public museum excavated in the rock in Monte Stino, outside the town: it occupies two galleries with barrel vaults of the stations that the military command had fortified since 1914. Founded in 1980 in the same fortifications, it is owned by the Municipality and managed by volunteers of a non-profit association; exhibits war finds of the First and Second World Wars, with guided tours.

In the northern Casertano, Carinola preserves the ruins of the Norman castle of Count Riccardo (1134) rebuilt by the Aragonese with Catalan traits, the thirteenth-century convent of San Francesco a Casanova and the Sanctuary of Maria SS. delle Grazie with a fifteenth-century icon.
A second castle in the hills.
The church of Sant'Antonio is in a dominant position on Mount Alino; on the mountain there is also the giant bench, 80a of the Big Bench Circuit project, panoramic view over the valley.
beach currently not accessible due to risk of falling boulders

Founded in 1977 mainly for archaeological finds of Biassono of the Group of Archaeistorical Research of Lambro, next to Villa Verri. On the ground floor there is the ethnological section with ploughs, sowers, wine presses, a leaf cutter for mulberry, a rare incubator for silk baco eggs and the reconstruction of kitchen and bedroom; on the upper floor there are local finds and the numismatic collection, with the storage room of 2235 Roman bronze and silver coins found at the Roman villa of Cascina Sant'Andrea. Detachable sections: since 2006       ©Segno Scrittura Stampa , on the history of communication, next to the library, and since 2009 the peasant world under the arcades of Cascina Ca' Nova.
The "colleague" of the spirit is above the village.

Umbrian capital on a hill between Etruscan walls and medieval palaces: Piazza IV Novembre with the Fontana Maggiore and the Palazzo dei Priori, the Umbria National Gallery and the underground of the Rocca Paolina.
The plaster ceilings of the peasant houses, a unique decoration.
House museum in the palace of the family Sorbello, which gives the name to the Etruscan well below.
Remains of military Flaminia on the ridge.

It collects the finds of the ancient Corfinium, capital of the Italian peoples during the social war, documented at the beginning of the twentieth century by the local scholar Antonio De Nino: stones and materials from the excavations of Piano San Giacomo, Sant'Ippolito, via di Pratola and Impianata, with eighty-six funeral epigraphs from the first century BC to the second century A.D. According to the MiC card is open by reservation, on summer weekends and in August also 10-13 and 16:30-19.
The most famous snowshoe blooming of the Wine Road.
The ancient theatre suspended on the sea.
Roma umbertina.
The Sacred Mount of Canavese.
Church of the village with a Romanesque bell tower partly walled.
A small museum on the protection of protected species.
Memories of the village in the early twentieth century.

The seventeenth-century palace of Corbera, passed to the Filangeri of Cutò, the maternal family of Giuseppe Tomasi of Lampedusa, who spent the summers from 1905 to 1914 and made it the model of the palace of Donnafugata; lost by the family due to debts and almost destroyed by the earthquake of 1968, which spared only the facade, was partly rebuilt and houses the Town Hall, the Teatro Sant'Alessandro and the museum. The museum exhibits the manuscript and typescript of the novel, letters, notes and vintage photos, multimedia posts, the unpublished 1956 recording of the writer reading  Â"Lighea" and a small wax museum with a scene of the film by Luchino Visconti.

Piazza dedicated to the Master, with his statue in the center, surrounded by buildings of the years of fascism including the Chamber of Commerce, headquarters of the Consortium Liutai      Â Antonio Stradivari Â .
The Roman baths where the water still comes out warm.
An easy speleological experience, also suitable for children from 4 years.

The first castle dates back to the 10th century; since the 12th century the Fontanabona built a manor house, loggia, stables, chapel, circular tower and walls. Today it is a country villa of the eighteenth century on three levels, with arched portal and coat of arms, a chapel of kindness of sixteenth-century forms and a section of the wall of belt with a sharp sixth window; a lightning destroyed the tower at the beginning of the nineteenth century. Since 1969 it is owned by the Region: the castle is inhabited, while the park annexed is indicated for use of public park.

Ancient parish church that gave its name to the village, mentioned in the testament of Speronella of 1192; rebuilt in 1946 with a single nave, it preserves a baptismal font in marble dated 1490 and three altarpieces of remarkable artistic value.
The baroque cathedral of Benedetto Alfieri.
Oratory that is supposed to date back to the fifteenth century; inside is preserved a processional crucifix of the seventeenth century.
To get to know the fauna of the park before leaving.
The cliff on the Ofanto.
The Flemish Madonna donated by a pope.
Romanesque among the vineyards.
The wet area that embraces the village.
A nineteenth-century jewel reopened.
Dalí and De Chirico on the Course.
Borgo della Valle del Messa made of characteristic streets, stone houses, narrow alleys and panoramic views; among the places of interest the Mother Church and other ancient churches.

Highland on the Trentino side of Mount Baldo, between Adige and Garda, in the Natural Park: paths in the woods with lake view, alpine pastures where you can taste cheeses, the trail of the Regole on the ancient medieval paths and the wild Val del Parol, rich in flowers. In the spring, a tour goes from Polsa to Bocca d'Ardole and the Horn of Fear to Monte Vignola; in winter you can ski in Polsa, San Valentino and San Giacomo.
On the western side of the island, it is called Spiaggia del Postino because it was one of the sets of the movie Il Postino (1994) by Massimo Troisi.
An evening at the theater in the historic center.

The Veio Regional Natural Park, established in 1997, covers about 15,000 hectares north of Rome with 99 km of trails marked by the CAI, including the Via Francigena. Around the village it contains the Etruscan-Capenati necropolis of Belmonte, Monte Fiore and Vaccareccia; in Belmonte a large rock necropolis and the ruins of a medieval village with a thirteenth-century tower.
Two villages of the municipal hinterland, with a medieval castle and a panoramic view of the Maremma.
The patron's shovel.
One foot in Italy, one foot in Slovenia.

The medieval nucleus contains towers, ogival windows, underpasses and stone lions on guard; in Piazza Municipio overlook the Cathedral and the Torre Frumentaria. Lower down the eighteenth-century city has straight streets and large squares.

The first museum dedicated to the tower clock and bells, dedicated to the founder Roberto Trebino and set up in the old Trebino plant: you can see how a clock is built and how a bell is made, in about thirty historical pieces, from the French, German and Austrian watches of the seventeenth century to the modern ones radio-synchronous; the oldest piece is a medieval bell of 1290 of about three quintals. The history of the Trebino family began in 1824 with a first wooden tower clock, then installed in the church of San Siro di Struppa in Genoa. Visitable in office hours by appointment (tel. 0185 919410.
Small lake of the hinterland of Casarza born from phenomena dating back to the glacial era, in a territory of olive groves, chestnut groves and panoramic paths.
A village still closed by its medieval walls.
The so-called Customs is actually a Roman funeral structure of the II-III century AD; in the Bagni district remain the baths of the imperial age.

At the foot of the hills, the land of the Torcolato DOC, Breganze revolves around Piazza Mazzini and the 90-metre bell tower, the third of Veneto; around, a plot of six-seventh-century villas also linked to the Great War, fifteenth-century dovecotes, the ancient opifici of Maglio Tamiello and Officina Radin, the Museo Moto Laverda and the Colle di Santa Lucia with the panorama of the plain.
Church of the XVI century built together with the Augustinian monastery, dominated by white, with internal walls decorated with paintings on the life of the Madonna delle Grazie.
The oldest spas in Italy.
Jacopone and the view from the bell tower.
One of the best preserved medieval structures of the city, along the route of the walls.
The splendid Carthusian of Santa Maria, founded in 1173: a late Renaissance complex very extensive, behind which the Marguareis Park opens to fan.
The city lounge among historic buildings.
€7, free under 6 years
The wooden altar carved in the eighteenth century.
Oil presses and tools of Parteolla.

Municipality of Isontino between Gorizia and Gradisca, known for the eighteenth-century village of Colmello di Grotta, home to the Museum of the Friulian peasant civilization, and for the Museum of Automobile and Technology with the assembly line of the Ford T.
The Vivarini and the art gallery wanted by Parazzi.

Born in 2000 on proposal of prof. Nicola Rizzi, is located in the upper part of the building of the Museo Anelli and is managed by the Astronomical Cultural Association Sirio. The evenings    Â One night with Sirio Â Â , in summer, combine an introduction to astronomy with minerals and meteorites in the museum's teaching room and guided observation of the sky to the telescope from the terrace; there are proposals for families (€10 a child with an adult) and special events for full moons and eclipses.

Franciscan Basilica in Romanesque-Apulian style built in 1384 by Raimondello Orsini del Balzo, a national monument since 1886. The three aisles are entirely frescoed, almost all in the fifteenth century on the commission of Mary of Enghien: Apocalypse, Seven Sacraments, Genesis, Life of Christ, Stories of the Virgin and, in the presbytery, Stories of Saint Catherine; there is also an octagonal chapel of the fifteenth century. A recent restoration has involved roof, windows, lighting, cloister and bell tower, and in the former refectory there is a museum.

Built between 1450 and 1465 by Pier Maria Rossi for Bianca Pellegrini, from which the name is: plain castle with walls, central courtyard, corner towers and high mast; on the noble floor frescoes and stuccoes. The cycle of the Stories of Griselda from the Decameron, which decorated the first tower, is today at the Castello Sforzesco in Milan. After the Pallavicino and Rangoni (1524) he passed in 1901 to the Facchi and then to the knight Mario Scaltriti, who restored it and opened it to the public. Guided tours at fixed times on weekends from March to November and on the first weekends in December; closed January to February.
Larics, glaciers and fauna on an ancient track.
The highest village in Pollino.
In the old dairy of Frisanco, reconstruction on a 1:10 scale of the rural life of a time made by a local craftsman.
The city hidden under the city.
The masterpiece of the Piedmontese Romanesque.

An example of Baroque design by the Lonate Paolo Soratini, third reconstruction on the same site, with large dome and facade adorned with marble; inside frescoes, stuccos and shovels by Venetian artists such as Balestra, Cignaroli and Licino. Basilica minor since 1980 by concession of John Paul II.

We descend with a Baroque staircase of more than one hundred steps; the sanctuary, begun in 1729 on a chapel older and open to worship in 1737, stands on ancient Basilian laureates. On the high altar the icon of an Odegitria della greca della XII secolo, flanked by two marble deer for the legend of the discovery; inside, three naves, canvases and organ of the eighteenth century. The Madonna della Scala has been the main patron of Massafra since 1776.
In the former convent of the Celestines, home to the Conservatory since 1826, the museum with musical instruments, portraits and relics of the great musicians of the Neapolitan school.

In the Laechler residence, next to Kraus Square, exhibits South Tyrolean costumes worn in festivals and popular celebrations. Open all year round, Monday-Saturday 8.30-12 and 14-18; in the same place the museum of nostalgic skiing, on the evolution of skiing in the decades.
The seventeenth-century palace of the family that named the village.
The liberty and eclectic villas of the Ardenza district, behind the promenade.
Butterfly park.

Medieval village in the hills of Molise transformed from the nineties into a museum of contemporary art in the open air, the MAACK, with the civic gallery and the museum of the buffoo, the tool barrel of tradition.

Arborea is a city founded in 1928 on the pond of Sassu just reclaimed, with regular plant and Art Nouveau and Neo-Gothic buildings; the Museum of Reclamation tells the story and preserves the finds of the Roman necropolis of S'Ungroni. On the coast there are the lagoon of S'Ena Arrubia, oasis Ramsar for birdwatching, and the beach with pinewood of the Marina of Arborea.
The baroque fountain in front of the Collegiate.
An intact medieval house.

The area is called "Valle dei Profumi" (Valle dei Profumi) by a European project involving 15 companies on 18 hectares between Santa Luce, Orciano Pisano, Castellina Marittima and Lorenzana. The main fields are along the provincial road for Orciano Pisano and on a hill overlooking the village; the flowering is in June and July.
The Matilda court where St Bernardino stayed.
Two villages and a bridge in the heart of Val Nure.
One of the most beautiful beaches of the overflows.

Born from the collection collected in over 40 years by Giancarlo Tibaldo: more than 10,000 working pieces that tell more than 200 years of audio, video and music communication, science and technology. A laboratory offers experiments on electromagnetism, electrostatics, battery operation and Stirling engine.

Neoclassical parish church started in 1762 on the project of Count Alessandro Alessandri and inaugurated in 1783, with the façade of Vittore Farina in Brembate strain; about 70 meters long, it has six lateral altars. It preserves a deposed Christ attributed to Tintoretto, twelve statues of apostles, two wooden pulpits of the Fantoni school and frescoed by Servalli in the restoration of 1924.
The mural of the movie in front of the sea.
Locality just north of the country where, according to tradition, the saint received the first manifestation of stigmata; today it is a destination of pilgrimage.

The traditional houses have large courtyards and arched portals; the town, provincial capital for a short period in the nineteenth century, preserves the artisan traditions of copper and weaving. In June the feast of St. John the Baptist brings traditional costumes to parade from all over the island.
The 16th century matrix.
Fracanzano and Dupré on a short ride.
In the Park, they host the only wheel with blades still working.

Romanesque, begun around 1140 probably by the Camaldolese monks and completed in the first quarter of the thirteenth century: the upper part of the façade alternates rows of golden limestone and dark basalt, with three blind arches and diamond motifs as in Santa Giusta. Inside there is a polychrome baroque wooden altar with statues of Saints John, Peter and Paul and three sixteenth-century paintings of Catalan school (Saint Paul, Crucifixion, Madonna and Child). It rises in the cemetery, where Italian and German soldiers are resting dead in the bombing of 1943.
The fortress of the Farnese peaks on the lake.

Centre of culture of the ancient Venetians at the foot of the Euganean Hills, Este is surrounded by over a kilometer of walls and towers of the Carrara castle, with public gardens inside; in the city the National Museum Atestino in Palazzo Mocenigo, the Cathedral of Santa Tecla with the altarpiece of Tiepolo, the Basilica of Santa Maria delle Grazie, the Romanesque San Martino and Piazza Maggiore. Byron and Shelley stayed there.
Walk to the front of a large alpine glacier.
The lives of transhumant shepherds.

The balcony of Irpinia is a medieval village on a ridge between the valleys of Ofanto and Calore, with the Cathedral of Sant'Amato, the churches of the centre, the remains of the Longobard castle and the Abbey of Fontigliano.
A 17th century villa with stables and gardens.

The ancient Roman amphitheatre beyond the area of the springs, incorporated into the urban fabric; part, with theater, nymph, ancient roads and an aqueduct of about thirty kilometers, of the Roman Venafro.

The village preserves the medieval plant with three ancient arched doors (Porta S. Maria, Porta S. Pietro e Porta S. Angelo) and ancient road crosses, among stone alleys, arches, fountains and noble palaces. The Baronial Palace is located where the Longobards had built a castle: in the twelfth century it was by Raynaldo di Pietrabbondante and since 1771 it belongs to the Zampini family. The complex of Santa Chiara, founded in 1367 and also used as a prison, since May 1995 hosts the Town Hall; in the village there is also the monument to the knifemaker, a craftsman standing at the anvil.

Piazza Vittorio Emanuele rises on the stretch of river, covered in front of the Town Hall, which separated the two original farmhouses of Spio and Cornuti, with the colonnade and the fountain in front of Palazzo Bocchetti; in Piazza dei Martiri the fountain with four stone lions. In the center also the seventeenth-century Chapel of the Crucifix and the former convent of the Clarisse.
The fifth century basilica.
Baths, castles and cherries: the two villages of the Pisan hills united in a single municipality.

Until the fifties, the production of wood charcoal was essential for the economy of the country: in spring the charcoal trees climbed into the woods and built wooden huts and leaves. At some times of the year, you can see the construction of a "poiat" and the production of coal; the "A Smoky Tale" app tells the craft as a guiding thread to explore the territory.

On a church of the 6th century with a baptismal dive font, the late-Gothic cathedral of Bishop Novelli rebuilt in neo-Gothic style in the mid-19th century: wooden choir of 1512 by Bernardino Fossati, chapel of St. Teobaldo with the marble ark; the bell tower rises to 40 meters.
For an aperitif downtown.
The highest waterfalls of the Apennines.
Reserve overlooking the river Albegna, important for birdlife: it hosts rare birds of prey such as biancon, lodolaio, sparrow and lanario.
The city in layers.

The city of the zolfare of the Nisseno, known as the town of sulphur until the 1960s, preserves the Museum of natural history and mining art and, towards Riesi, the Trabia-Tallarita Mine, one of the oldest Sicilian sulphites; in the center, grown around the Palazzo dei Principi of Trabia, the Civic Tower with the Liberty clock, Palazzo Di Bartolo with the artistic nativity scene and the ethno-anthropological museum.
The relic arrived from Paris in the woods.
The giant torches of the Agnonese Christmas.
Closed on visits waiting for restoration and consolidation, according to the Municipality
The Greek bronze re-emerged from the sea.

Small church of the historic centre built between 1876 and 1882, with a modest façade on Piazza Dante; the sober interior with a single nave houses in the presbytery a wooden altar, a baptismal stone font and statues of St. Michael the Archangel and the Risen Christ, as well as a Pietà by Michele Pomes di Grottaglie on a sketch by the local sculptor Cosimo Carlucci.
A thousand years of religious history in one parish.
Ancient municipal seat also called Palazzo del Priore, in Romanesque-baroque style, with a large external clock.
A romantic garden with fake ruins in the heart of the village.
Contemporary art in the city.
One of the best preserved Renaissance residences in the Alps.
The story of Albingaunum.

Romanesque church with circular plan, built between 1130 and 1150 with three overlapping cylinders (nave, tiburium and lantern), perhaps inspired by the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem: capitals of reuse all different, fragments of frescoes (Madonna on throne with Child, Annunciation in the Matroneo) and portals bas-relief. At the equinoxes a ray of sun crosses the roundabout and hits the tabernacle; the former monastery next door houses the European Romanesque Antenna study centre.
Ancient crossroads of the Val d'Ayas at the foot of the Corno Bussola, between ancient irrigation canals, a restored mill and the sanctuary of Sant'Anna.

In the chapel of the Madonna del Carmine on the main street of the hamlet Melezet: wooden statues, goldsmiths, paintings, fabrics and vestments from the 15th to the 19th century coming from churches and chapels of the basin, over 300 objects displayed in rotation according to the theme of the year.
The city of the legend of the tortellino.
€5 whole; free on the first Sunday of the month and under 18 years; courtyard of honor free
A sandstone parish.
The Superior lakes of Mezzo and Inferiore, born from the arrangement of the Mincio of 1190 by Alberto Pitentino.
A city-palace of the Gonzaga.
Marine archaeology and views of the Egadi.
€12 whole; €5 from 6 to 16 years
evenings from May to October with reservation required at the Tourist Office Val Vestino (tel. +39 0365 745060)
Four centuries of frescoes on a spur overlooking the valley.
The Faraglioni from above.
Boat party on the Lemene.

On the hill remain the remains of the 11th century castle, erected by the Bourbon marquises of Monte Santa Maria to protect a hospital for pilgrims, which would give the city its name; where the monastery of Sant'Angelo stood there today is the church of Santa Croce.
The Carnic architecture and the history of Linussio.

A hundred metres from the centre, the little church of San Mauro is the starting point of the 5 km botanical educational trail created with the students of the Istituto Comprensivo Valle Versa: it crosses the centuries-old forest of Baccano and reaches a natural lake fed by a spring near La Cà, near Casa Guastoni, on the border with Emilia-Romagna.
The peasant memory of the Savato valley.

The palace of the XII-XIII century was the seat of the Captain of the People; in the central hall frescoes with peasants working in the countryside. Next to the Esperia Tower, with the bell melted in 1318 by an Orvieto master, symbol of the free municipality, who called the citizens at the assemblies. You enter from Porta Burgi, 12th century gate on the path of Flaminia.
Church vaulted cruising, restored, which preserves six works of Nicola Peccheneda dated 1769, including the "Christ" and the "adultera" and "The Blood of the Redeemer."
One of the oldest churches in the village, in the historic center near the original walls.
The sarcophagus of the labors of Hercules, a unique of Roman art.
A rare fifteenth-century facade born against the plague.
Natural plateau in an unspoilt landscape of Matese, voted Place of the heart FAI in 2020; the area around is rich in waterfalls and small streams.

Founded in 1949 and unique in Italy, it is located in the Santa Giustina complex, in the basement of the MuSa: military valor decorations, Risorgimento relics and materials of the two world wars to tell the decorated from 1793 to today, with uniforms, flags, weapons and coins.
The twentieth century in front of the great masters.
Romanesque frescoes of the 12th century under the Baroque guise.
The flora of the Cansiglio reunited in one path.
The Last Live Dinner.
The Vallo di Diano in an interactive path.
Fraction known for the precious red marble (saxo rubeo) extracted on site, which gives a characteristic shade to the landscape and buildings.
A Roman city under the abandoned country.
A romantic view.
A century of Italian military history in a family building.
A Madonna of the Rosary of the sixteenth century.

The oldest and fortified nucleus of the village, of Lombard age, rises on the hill and is dominated by the Civic Tower; built between the 11th and 14th century with pyramidal plan, it has at the southern entrance the Arch of the Pelasgi. In the castle also the sixteenth century Evangelist Palace, with cycles of civil frescoes of the sixteenth century.

Of fourteenth-century origin, rebuilt in 1895-1899 with two naves and presbytery dome; it preserves a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century, a baptismal font in stone of the early sixteenth century and a Pietà by Pomponio Amalteo of about 1540.

Medieval pyramid-shaped village, called the hamlet of the Templars, dominated by a Romanesque tower with cusp and overlooking the Conero and the Sibillini as far as the Gran Sasso, the Maiella and the sea; it houses the temple church of Santa Maria del Borgo, the fifteenth-century Universal Judgment of Saints Peter and Paul and a collection of Byzantine icons, with the hamlet of Ripaberarda and the sanctuary of San Bernardino in the surroundings.
Purchased by Henry II Del Carretto and donated in 1216 to the Cistercian nuns of Santa Maria de Betton.
The leader of the myth of Ulysses and the sirens.
A Punic city became a bishop's seat.
To the north, beyond Via di Mezzo, a series of late medieval houses overlooking the alleys.
An ancient dedication to the monastery of Santa Giulia.
Outdoor reconstruction of a village of the Carolingian age, where archaeologists and young people in costume animate daily life.

A hilly village in the province of Chieti a few kilometres from the Adriatic, surrounded by vineyards, with the castle mentioned already in the 13th century; in the 16th century Palazzo Martucci is home to the Museum of War for Peace, while the Wine Paths cross vineyards, olive groves and woods.
Probably from the fifteenth century, the only door that survived the demolition of the ancient walls.

Designed by Leon Battista Alberti in 1472 and finished in 1765 with the dome of Filippo Juvarra; there is the funerary chapel of Mantegna and in the crypt the Sacred Vases, destination of the procession of Good Friday.
The treasures of Tharros.

In the seventeenth-century house of the Chiarvesio family, called Cocèl, since 1994 tells the rural life of Friuli from the nineteenth to the mid-Twentieth century with objects donated by citizens: kitchen with fogolar, rooms of a rich family and a poor, lace workshop (the school was founded in 1892 by Cora Slocomb), granary with grater for silk bugs. Outside, dairy, tavern, age school hall, Bee Museum and a mill from Majano; in the courtyard live donkeys, cows, goats and courtyard animals, and volunteers show crafts such as knife, basket and blacksmith. It is part of the Ecomuseum Il Cavalîr; times to check (MiC card: Monday-Friday 9.30-12.30).
The Benedictine monastery with the Renaissance church and the spices where the monks still produce herbal teas and herbal products.
The stairs of the village.
A historic shop on the square.
Historical palace of the restored center at the will of the Fondazione Sicilia as a cultural center, with museum services managed by Civita Sicilia.
The masterpiece of Benozzo Gozzoli.
The history of the mine in tools and photographs.
The shovels of St. John.

Medieval village on the inner hills of the Maremma, the land of Morellino di Scansano DOCG; in the surroundings the Etruscan settlement of Ice Forte, in the village the Pretorio Palace with the Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Life and Wine, the Collegiate Church of San Giovanni Battista and, on the hill, the Convent of Petreto.

Roncade is dominated by Castello Giustinian, the only Venetian villa still surrounded by crenellated walls, now a wine estate; in front there is the church of All Saints with an eighteenth-century pictorial cycle of the Tiepolesque school, while in Biancade the church of San Giovanni Battista rises on the banks of the Musestre.

Opened on 14 January 1926 with the Bohème di Puccini, designed by engineer Antonio Panizzi and architect Italo Costa; animated until the 1950s, it became a cinema. Purchased by the Municipality, restored since 1988 preserving its late liberty characters and reopened in 1998, it hosts up to 420 spectators with stage to mobile platforms.

In Scauri, which takes its name from the consul Marco Emilio Scauro (162-90 BC), remains of the maritime villa a double arched portal, a corridor with parietal paintings of the third Pompeian style and seven blind arches of the II-I century BC; the villa produced wine for export. The fourteenth-century Torre dei Molini, today space for events, is visited when it is open. The complex is part of the Latium Historical Houses Network.

Located on a hill at 430 meters in the Fiastra valley, it preserves spiral streets, staircases and stone houses connected by small overhangs; in recent years they have reopened workshops and craft workshops.
Climb the tower and read the history of the castle in the finds.
In the castle exhibits the finds of the excavations and archaeological collections of the territory.

In the area of the Old Cemetery, outside the village, there is a basalt Roman road, a domus in the archaeological area of San Marco and the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria, the most important medieval church of Atina.
Borgo della Valdichiana aretina overlooking the Val di Chio, with the loggias attributed to Vasari.
The Franciscan church of the village.
A karst cave about two kilometers long.

In the former Benedictine cenobium of San Vittore exhibits the Genga Ittiosaur, a fossil of marine reptile about 3 meters long discovered in 1976 in Camponocecchio during the works for a gallery of the SS 76.
Visitable only on request (tel. 0322 81897)
The dome that welcomes those who arrive from the sea.

The Cathedral dedicated to the Assumption and to St. Pardo, bishop of Greek origin, consecrated in 1319: the Gothic façade is the work of Francesco Petrini of Lanciano, with sculptural compositions of biblical inspiration and thirteen columns instead of twelve, the thirteenth to represent Judas; the back of the building is instead crooked and irregular. Inside, frescoes, paintings, tabernacles and altars of different eras. At the end of May (25-27) the feast of San Pardo brings to the city over one hundred carts drawn by oxen and decorated with paper flowers.
A moving museum.
Collegiate from the 12th century with the cenotaph of Beltramo Aringhieri; next to the Archaeological Museum and the Collegiate with Etruscan art and sacred artworks.
The refuge of the Second World War inserted in the circuit of museums and galleries of the Municipality.
the Park card describes the previous state of the earthquake of 2016

Medieval fortification of the second half of the thirteenth century, renovated in 1938, with high-pitched windows and frescoes from the early fifteenth century; today it houses a community of Orsoline Sisters. From Torrione starts a route of about 9 km towards the valley of Chiavone Bianco.
Paths a stone's throw from the walls.
The promenade of the first half of the twentieth century on the Great Sea, overlooking the Cheradi islands, flanked by Palazzo del Governo, Poste and Banca d'Italia.
The illuminated codes of the oldest library in Friuli.
Leave Tuscia in a tower.

The wood covers the Montello hill, a relief stretched from east to west in the heart of the high plain of Treviso, up to 369 meters, bordered to the north and east by the Piave. Protected from Venice from the fourteenth century for the oak for ships, it was largely deforested after the Bertolini law of 1892; cross it from north to south the 20 's' open in 1893 and the underground karst houses caves like the Busa of Castel Sotterra.
Ardesie and majolica in the Saracen tower.
The medieval castle of the village.

A 16th century square-plan sighting tower, also known as Turrazzo or Galilee, built against the incursions of Turkish pirates; privatised in 1863, it was rebuilt in neo-Gothic style and renamed by Charles V. It rises near the Botanical Garden.
temporarily closed to the public (Comune di Anzio, updated on October 2, 2025)
On a bike in the old Bisenzio factories.
Every Wednesday morning, from the Medici Fortress to Viale XXV Aprile, one of the largest traditional markets in Tuscany: clothing, fabrics, household goods.
The shrine of the festivals of the country.
An open-air ceramic museum.
Guided tour €5, reduced €3 (children up to 14 years); theatricalized tour €10, reduced €5
The garden on the Aventine among the panoramic terraces of the city.

From Piazza Monte Grappa, with the Palazzo Gadaldini seat of the Town Hall, you pass through Riccardi, already Santa Caterina, and via Duca d'Aosta with the fresco of the Immaculate Church to Piazza Bonvicino, dedicated to the 16th century painter Moretto di Ardesio. Here the 12th century Bishop's Palace, with the hall of the Congregation of the Dead from the 1672 stone portal and the fresco of a macabre dance; just beyond the great parish church of San Giorgio.
To understand the Walser community in the valley.

In the municipal park of the former Villa Boghi, now home to the Town Hall and surrounded by citrus fruits, olive trees and Mediterranean plants, the museum preserves objects, photos and tools of the traditional crafts of the lake donated by the fishing families and the local association.
The main square dominates with its size, a few steps from Sant'Antonio Abate; next door, in the former town hall, is the Guarneriana Library.

Neoclassical fountain built between 1865 and 1893 on a project by the Melfi architect Giuseppe Antonio Loccuratolo, brick amphitheatre full with a living stone frame, two ramps and wrought iron railing. On the arch stands the statue of Ceres, called "Sand'Abbbunnanza" , about 1,5 meters high and dated between the first century BC and the I AD, found in the nineteenth century in Pila Grande. In 1978 it was depicted on a stamp of the series "Fontane d'Italia" .
Among the most important churches in Barbagia.

The Marinzen mountain hut, about 1,500 meters above the village, is reached by cable car: panorama, playground and trails like that towards the Schafstall hut; in winter skating rink with views of the Sciliar. Nearby, the Chairs of Witches (Hexenstühle) are a viewpoint linked to local legends.
Cycle paths along the Adda and, at the Bergardino Woods, a walking path accessible to the blind.
Among the places to see in the historic center of Senigallia.
The center of the country.
In the park of Palazzo Corsini, the museum with sections of archaeology, art and nature, and a Madonna dello Scheggia, brother of Masaccio.

On the Colfiorito plateau, along the road from Plestia to San Martino, a sanctuary built in the sixteenth century instead of a small crossroads kiosk; damaged by the earthquake of 1997, it was restored.
Surrounded by a park open to the public with rare species and monumental trees.
the theatre is open only for events (theatrical seasons, concerts)
The mitreum, among the testimonies of Sutri's glorious past.

The largest lake in South Tyrol, created by the Montecatini group by combining the natural Resia Lake and Lake Curon (or Mezzo) with a dam for hydropower; the level was raised 22 meters above the ancient village. Exposed to the wind, it is suitable for sailing, kitesurfing, canoeing and kayaking, with boat tours; from the Malga di Resia you can enjoy the view of the lake.

16th century church in via Calvi: on the façade the Roman plaque of Minicio Esorato, imperial official of the first century, found in the lake and located here by the humanist Francesco Calvi, and a key of fifteenth century arch with the castle of Menaggio, today municipal coat of arms; inside seventeenth century paintings and a medieval source.
It preserves the stone on which, according to tradition, St. Gennaro was beheaded.
Horses, vineyards and Monte Rosa on a half-day walk.
More than 6,000 hectares between Marzabotto, Monzuno and Grizzana, places of the 1944 massacre, with the path of memory.

At the gates of Caserta, along the ancient Appia street, the Bourbon complex of the Real Convitto di Santa Maria delle Grazie houses the Museum of Rural Civilization; not far away is the eighteenth-century church of Santa Maria degli Angeli, built with the tuff of the quarries of the Reggia.
Built between 1961 and 1965, one of the largest in Europe, it collects 105 million cubic metres of glaciers water; it gets by car to the invaded.
The most famous Medici villa.
Rural trails and views of fields, vineyards and green areas, suitable for excursions, photography and quiet walks.
The place from which the Fiume enterprise started.

Silver and gold embroideries of the mother church.
Beaches on Lake Maggiore for sunbathing, swimming and water sports. Dogs allowed on a leash in the village, with restrictions on the lake and on the beach.
The life of the fields in Lomellina, in the shadow of a castle.
The Longobard Palace flanked by the Ercolani Tower, one of the survivors of the more than 200 towers mentioned in medieval documents.
In the park of Villa Antonia, eighteenth-century, unique in Italy, pays tribute to the history of small chimney sweeps.
The Juvarra silver mark.

The medieval village is located on the slopes of Monte Calamita and in its narrow arched alleys, the "chiassi" houses artisan shops, wine and food producers, restaurants and cafes. The streets are spread by works of art: the iron of Kurt Mergenthal on the façade of the Town Hall with the anchor and the dolphin of the coat of arms, the homage of Michelangelo Venturini to Maria and Lorenzo in Piazza Matteotti, the installation of the sun and moon by Italo Bolano at the viewpoint of Via Roma. In the center there is also the amphitheatre La Vantina, dedicated to the legendary Amelia Vantini linked to the exile of Napoleon (1814-1815), home of festivals and small concerts.

karst cave over 2 km long, with 15 meters high entrance at 1,475 meters above sea level: among the highest visitable caves in Europe, explored since 1704 and open to tourists since 1893; 1,360 meters, with salt such as the enchanted Forest, the Hall of the Elephants, the lakes of Splendore and Ornella and the Pantheon. In 1904 Francesco Paolo Michetti took it as a model for the scene of the second act of the  "Daughter of Iorio" by D'Annunzio. It is one of the geosites of the UNESCO Geopark of Majella; climbing with the Colle Rotondo-Cavallone cable car, reopened in 2022, or on foot in about two hours; guided tours in the summer months.

Permanent exhibition on the material culture of the Arbëreshe communities: on the ground floor six rooms, each dedicated to a theme, with objects and photographic documents arranged to evoke the context of use, not reconstructed environments. Each object has a caption in arbërisht, in Calabrian dialect, in Italian and, where possible, in English, with a brief description of the function. He tells about domestic and working life as it was until about half a century ago and introduces to the section on traditions. For timetables and visits: Municipality, tel. 0984 527209.
The neighborhood of the Saint.
Trekking overhanging the sea.
The synagogue and the Viotti Theatre, home to an important international music competition, along the path of the center.
Castrated, tuma and honey cakes.
The water Napoleon liked.

A hunting reserve built by Federico da Montefeltro in 1465, with park, villa and convent of San Giovanni Battista (founded in the fourteenth century and rebuilt in the eighteenth century in style inspired by Vanvitelli); it was the retreat of Pietro Bembo, Tasso and Ariosto and a favourite place of Francesco Maria II Della Rovere. It is reached from the Doge's Palace with the Duke's Path, 1.5 km along the Metauro; there are ceramic workshops held by the Friends of Ceramics.

Embedded in the Palazzo Comunale, the current theatre of 1863, fourth in the history of Ostra, is the work of the architect Francesco Fellini of Barbara: horseshoe plant, 29 stages on two orders and loggia, decorations with symbols of the Theatre and Music, curtain with the Town Hall and ancient scenic machinery still working. Closed in 1980, it was reopened on 6 January 1998 and hosts prose, theatre for children and concerts.
The most beautiful vase in the world is in a castle.
The prehistoric statues-stele next to the hermitage.
Contemporary outdoor art.
seasonal openings; from January to June visits on request (tel. 0973 877676); building not accessible to persons with disabilities

In the visit centre Vallenatura, which is also House of the Park, the museum is dedicated to the art of the production of charcoal, a traditional craft with ancient secrets. In July and August open every day, holidays included, 9.30-12.30 and 15.30-18.30.
The ferruginous water of St. Anthony.
To be checked: admission to museums at extra charge
The sea in Milan.

Path from Piazza Cays (380 m) to the summit (1150 m) in about an hour and a half: after the 18th century chapel of San Rocco and the sanctuary of Sant'Abaco, a steep ridge path rises to the monumental Cross, 15 meters high, built in concrete reinforced by the cottages in 1901 with materials carried behind the village. From the top the circular panorama embraces the Alps, the Valley of Susa and the plain of Turin.

The Po Delta between the Po di Venezia and the Po di Levante, with a part of the mainland and a lagoon of fishing valleys, born from the union of Donada and Contarina: the Pineta di Fornaci on the fossil dunes, the 63 meters high bell tower of Donada, the eighteenth-century church of San Bartolomeo with the organ Callido, the Venetian cut of the Po and, on the sea, the fishing village of Porto Levante.
We'll fresco it of the Templars.

Geosite can be reached with a cross-country route: three large limestone rocks, near which you can see the entrance of a deep cave with a tunnel, not yet explored.

Consecrated in 1826 on a project by the architects Cardone and Cattaneo, it has neoclassical façade and Baroque interior with the fresco of the patron of Luigi Peretti; the organ Felice Bossi & Son of 1855, the largest to a single manual of the diocese of Ivrea, restored and inaugurated in 2019, plays in the Organale review. Open during functions.
A walk along the stream that combines the main places.

Medieval plant with its original nucleus on the highest part, surrounded by walls of Roman origin rebuilt in the twelfth century, of which remains stretches and towers; in the village the eighteenth-century buildings Misciatelli-Pallavicini and the Palazzo dei Conti Bulgarelli di Marsciano.

About 1.5 km from Gremanu, perhaps linked to his village: four similar tombs of Giants, arranged amphitheatre and oriented to the east, with taurine protome; next to the first the stele of Madau, granite slab with symbols perhaps referring to the Pleiades. Italia.it indicates it as the most representative site of the area.
The medicinal plant garden created by the Medici in 1545, one of the oldest in the world, with nineteenth-century greenhouses and monumental trees.
Walking through the Forums.
About 18 km on a nineteenth-century railway track, between old tollgates, farmhouses and countryside.
Val d'Arbia village crossed by the Via Francigena, with a fortified mill of the fourteenth century.

Park built by the Municipality in 2019, a 20 minute walk from the village along the fossil path: hundreds of fossils emerged in the excavations of the 1970s and 1980s in the riverbed of the Rio Ponticelli, which contributed to the UNESCO recognition. Another 15 minutes lead to the former bituminous shale mines, from which light bulb oil and ichthyol were obtained and where fossils were discovered in the nineteenth century; viewpoint on Prealpi, Switzerland and Ceresio. The ring of Varese Turismo da Besano is 5 km, about 2 hours, easy.
A lioness-shaped rock with a sacred cave.
The mountain life told along the alleys.
The village and the western Elba from above.
From the Tower of Arnolfo you can see the dome at the same height.
Place in the woods where on November 11, 1944 partisans were massacred; the route that leads there is taken by ANPI. In Micialetti is located the house of "Mille" , seat of the partisan command.

The parish church with three naves consecrated in 1313, on the homonymous square; on the façade a large fresco of St. Christopher, inside the most famous work is the Deposition from the colored stone cross.

Small neo-Gothic villa with square plan, rebuilt in 1848-1850 by Pietro Scapin on the site of the seventeenth-century holiday house of Alvise Lucadello, with swallow-tailed blackbirds inspired by Palazzo Ducale; it takes its name from the family that owned it from 1874 to 1965 and since 1972 it is owned by the Municipality of Abano Terme. The interiors are bare and host conferences and events; the park of about 30 hectares, halfway along the coast of Monte Alto, includes part of the forest with trails, including the route Villa Draghi and Monte Ceva, about 10 km in the Regional Park of the Euganean Hills.
Wanted by Francesco II in the early sixteenth century, it houses the City Museum with maps, views, documents and multimedia stations, and the Risorgimento section.

Borgo del Matese Molise above the valley of the Tammaro: about 3 km, in the locality Altilia, the ruins of the Roman city of Saepinum with walls, monumental gates, basilica and theatre; on the mountain the Sannite area of Terravecchia-Saipins and, in the village, the church of Santa Cristina and Palazzo Attilio.
Next to the Arch of Traiano, part of the provincial museum network and can be visited with the unique ticket of the Sannio Museum.

Official residence of Napoleon during the exile, between the Fort Falcone and the Fort Stella, overlooking the sea: it combines two grand-ducal houses furnished in Empire style, with reception room, officer room, study and emperor's room.
Built at the beginning of the 12th century, with a Latin cross with a bell tower; today it is used as a conference room.
closed in winter, season 2026 from 28 March to 8 November (merano-suedtirol.it)
Get off at the sea in the gardens of the Costa Viola.
A 19th-century museum house.
The Middle Ages a stone's throw from the Duomo.

The municipality is 1,182 metres in the Alta Valsesia Natural Park, made up of 16 terrace hamlets: it is the oldest Walser colony in Valsesia, inhabited since the 13th century, and preserves the Filippa Museum, the first civic museum in Piedmont (1836), the Walser Ethnographic Museum and the parish church of San Michele.
The village of the most famous castle of the Aosta Valley, fortress and residence of the Challant with the frescoed courtyard, at the entrance of the valley of Clavalité.

Permanent Museum set up in a large and bright room, which offers a picture of sheep breeding and shepherding in the mountains of Cuneo and nearby France. Guided tours on the first weekend of the month from 15 to 18 (in July and August all weekends); on the other days you can visit independently from 9 to 18 with automatic opening by token. It is advisable to check the opening before the visit (tel. 0171 955555).
An intact castle village on the Orvieto hills.
More than 30 meters, called "Campanon" for the large bronze bell; symbol of the city on the Town Hall, you climb up to the top.
Two campestri churches of the seventeenth century; in Santa Caterina, during the Time in Jazz festival, musicians improvise by day, and the feast of the saint falls in early June.
The voice of the Temple tenor.
Half a million years of Anglona in a few rooms.
The millennial cathedral with its Golden Pala.

The convent complex next to the Duomo, seat of the Diocesan Museum: bronze statues of Cosimo Fanzago, the surviving statues of the triptych Gagini, paintings of Monteleoneese painters and works attributed to Paolo De Matteis and Francesco Curia, with the mitria of San Leoluca di Mattia Condursi (1854).
A walking itinerary between stones erected from the village to the countryside.

Palazzo di proprietà comunale, dal 2023 nella rete musale del Castello del Buonconsiglio: the rooms on the noble floor have frescoes from around 1870 and furnishings from the eighteenth-nineteenth century. The Provincial Textile Museum is being set up here.
A Roman villa in the countryside.

In the countryside between Stuffione and Rami di Ravarino, built between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries by Marquis Aldobrandino Rangoni; today it is a private property used as a venue for events.
A walk through the chestnut trees to the 14th century church.
Church of the historical center among the places indicated by the regional portal.

Of Lombard origin (about the 9th century), it was part of the defenses at the border between the principalities of Benevento and Salerno, and in the towers remains a medieval masonry; in the Norman age it grew around a trapezoidal courtyard with three round arches covered with marble, and in the eighteenth century it was enlarged by the Imperial princes of Genoa. Damaged by the 1980 earthquake, it has been restored; visit by reservation (tel. 0827 23094).
frescoes of the fifteenth century at the entrance of the village.

Ancient village of Carbonai, 720 metres above Lake Idro, at the south-west end of Trentino on the border with Lombardy, among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2018: alleys, arches and steps with devotional frescoes on the facades, the fourteenth-century parish church of the Nativity and, on a spur on the lake, the Castle of San Giovanni dei Conti Lodron.
Baroque noble Palaces of the Six and eighteenth century frescoed by Francesco Carrega, along the alleys that descend to the sea.
The medieval village reborn stone on stone after the earthquake.
Church started in 1682 and completed in 1714; according to an inscription inside it was wanted by the family of Duke Ceva Grimaldi and archpriest Buonhome.

A noble palace built in 1734 by Giovanni De Lieto as the first hospital in Maratea, restored and today the Ministry of Culture. On the first floor the picture gallery dedicated to the Marateot painter Angelo Brando, the painter of femininity, in four themed rooms with self-portraits, portraits, domestic scenes, still lifes and sacred subjects; there is then the collection of finds, including Roman anchors, recovered from the backdrops of the islet of Santo Janni. Visit of about 60 minutes, free entrance.
The Panza collection, from Turrell to Flavin, in a villa of delight now managed by FAI.
Remains of one of the rare Byzantine cross-buildings of the island, between the IX and XI century.
The river between the rocks, on suspended walkways.

Panoramic village on the Tronto valley, at the end of the Via Salaria Marchegiana: under the church of Maria Santissima Assunta the Museum of the Crypt exhibits about twenty mummy of the XVII-XIX century, under the noble palaces run underground routes and the seventeenth-century convent of San Francesco houses the Civic Museum.

The main place of power of the city, begun in the fourteenth century to protect the papal governor at the top of Corso Garibaldi; it houses the provincial administration and museum collections, with a panoramic terrace.
A short distance from the building, the ancient medieval manor house in good state of preservation, historic center of Stupinigi.

Walled city on the Flaminia, famous for its waters: on top of the hill the Duomo and the tower of the Bell Tower, in Piazza Caprera the Civic Museum in the church of San Francesco with the polyptych of the pupil, the Archaeological Museum with the Lombard finds; outside the city Bagni di Nocera with the Angelica Source.
A church of the 13th century.
Five white coves inside a protected park.
Laurana and Antonello in a small village museum.
The carved pulpit of Fortunato Capero.
The botanical garden of the University, part of the University Museum System and the Lombardy Botanical Gardens Network.
The Romanesque Cathedral consecrated in 1106, with the dome frescoed by Correggio with the Assumption of the Virgin and the Deposition of Benedetto Antelami.
Paintings on the table linked to Carlo Crivelli and his followers and the Death of St. Francis Xavier of the Baciccia.

Where the marble of the Duomo of Milan is born.
One of the oldest churches in the Val d'Adige.
The fifteenth-century church with a single aisle at the end of the Town Hall; it houses the nineteenth-century coffin of the Dead Christ carried in procession on Good Friday.
White sand in the pine forests.

The ancient village on the promontory, an example of medieval urbanism, is reached by a large steps staircase that survived the modern levelings; on the entrance door is still visible the coat of arms of the Sanfelice dukes, who bought the feud in 1660. It preserves walls, the typical "scaloni" and ancient city gates such as the Gate of Earth.
