The crenellated palace next to the cathedral, with the Civic Tower, seat of the Diocesan Museum Tridentino with sacred works, architecture and Christian finds.
The medieval fortified heart.
The Roman door of Flaminia on the sea.
Walk through centuries-old trees and animals.
seasonal opening, closed from November to March

Around 1818, the silksmith Pietro Monti transformed an ancient cloth crowd, moved by a hydraulic wheel on the stream Val Zerbo, into a silk spinning mill; in 1869 the spinning mill was added, closed in 1903, and the spinning mill worked until 1934. Purchased by the Municipality in 1978 and restored since 1981, the museum opened in 1998: the heart is the large circular torch-piece of 1818 (5 m in diameter, 11 m in height, 972 casts), put into operation, with three rectangular torcuits and, since 2021, an tapestry embroidered in silk by Filippo Biagioli on the legend of Grigna.
From February 6, 2025 the stretch of path 11 between the terrace of the Tomb of the Deer and the Tomb of the Queen is closed for archaeological site (linking with path 9)
San Gaudenzio al Borghetto, Baroque (1716-24), and Sant'Ulderico in Piazza Ferruccio Nazionale with the Romanesque bell tower embedded in the façade.
€5, reduced €2; cumulative with the archaeological area €8

Ibleo village rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693, with the  "Via Sacra" lineing five Baroque religious buildings (Carmine, San Sebastiano, Chiesa Madre, Sant'Antonio, Santa Maria), the medieval quarter of the Old Prisons and, a few kilometers away, the rock necropolis of Pantalica, UNESCO World Heritage site with Syracuse.
Piedmontese painting of the sixteenth century in the church of the village.

First and largest protected natural area of Rozzano, curated by the volunteers of APE Natura, where there were once the rice fields of the Count of Belgioioso and, in the fifties, clay quarries for a brick furnace. Inside the House of Nature, born as a refuge for swallows, is a small open-air museum with the original mill mill of Cascina Follazza, nests, eggs, animal skeletons and panels on the local flora and fauna.
Sacred and Etruscan furnishings under the basilica.

Former Augustinian church with late Baroque interior and nineteenth-century façade. It is the destination of the historical procession of Medieval Pergola, which recalls the arrival in the city of the remains of the saints Secondo, Agabito and Giustina.
The deconsecrated church where Cardinal Giulio Alberoni was baptized, today a private art gallery.
Mountain life in 600 objects.

According to tradition in 1490 a huge tuff rock detached from Monte Cavo stopped a few meters from a traveler who had invoked the Virgin; on the site there was a chapel, a destination of pilgrimages. The current church, designed by Don Salvatore Spadaio, was inaugurated in 1932 by the Trinitarians in 1892, the ceiling has wooden panels with coffers and the image of the Madonna on the rock is attributed by the Municipality to Antoniazzo Romano.
The most famous underground city in the Marche region.
The peasant life of Langa and the remains of the castle.
The most remote and silent Aeolians.
The "Boemia d'Italia," where over 95% of the Italian crystal is produced, on the Via Francigena; home of Arnolfo di Cambio, divided between Colle Alta and Colle Bassa.
Ancient Benedictine monastery in travertine and alabaster nine kilometers from Montalcino, among the masterpieces of the Italian Romanesque; legend wants it founded by Charlemagne in 781.
The Romanesque Church of the Corso.

Built between 1790 and 1798 by Francesco Maria Ciaraffoni, modified by Cosimo Morelli and inaugurated in 1798; known for acoustics and rococo decorations, it has the historical curtain of Luigi Mancini (1850) and hosts every year the Festival Pergolesi Spontini.
Small church on the road to Francavilla, with frescoes from the 13th century in the crypt.

Itinerary in the memory and Italian costume of the twentieth century, the result of more than fifteen years of research by the collectors Guido Minetti and Sylvia Pizzorno: themed rooms with motorcycle workshop, '40s emporio, lounge, appliances, Olivetti machines, Vespa dealership and tribute to Guzzi, bicycles, toys, juke-box and pinball machines, many objects still working.
The story of San Salvo in a square.

It exhibits the thirteen "ingenious processionals" created by Paolo Saverio Di Zinno (1718-1781), who parade through the city on the day of Corpus Domini, with costumes of the fifties, vintage films and a screening room; edited by the Association Mysteries and Traditions.

Castle donated by Ludovico II to the monastery of Casauria and then passed to the Varano; the annexed church, of thirteenth-century origin, has frescoes of the first fifteenth-century of the Master of Rasiglia and paintings of Nobile da Lucca, Giovanni and Simone De Magistris of the first half of the sixteenth century.

Elliptical plant with double acropolis with Roman and pre-Roman walls: the Romans built a hole and temples in Cibele and Esculapio, in the Middle Ages there were added watchtowers and the castle on the highest point, from the sixteenth century palaces and churches with large portals. Today it is a maze of alleys, stairs, arches and small stone buildings, with an epigraphic route of Roman inscriptions scattered among palaces and streets designed in 2000.
The story of the reclamation told by the tools of those who made it.
A neoclassical roundabout by Andrea Vici.

The ancient center preserves several churches; Piazza Roma is dominated by the Church of San Rocco and from the highest point you can see the Valle del Bradano and, in the distance, the Gulf of Taranto.

The largest of the five glacial lakes of the Morenic Amphitheatre of Ivrea, between Chiaverano and Ivrea, and the only one fed by a source: it has no immissaries on the surface. The Piedmont Region has recognized it as a place of significant environmental interest and is one of the few bathing lakes in the area, with two establishments, free beach, tennis courts and restaurants. Along the banks were the traces of the Roman aqueduct of Ivrea.

Born where the cattle market was held, when in 1557 Alberico I Cybo Malaspina enlarged the walls and moved the political center of the city; in the center the monument to Maria Beatrice d'Este, around palaces and fountain adorned with marble.
The dome in sandstone with the windows of Guillaume de Marcillat, the Magdalena di Piero della Francesca, terracotta by Andrea della Robbia and a source with a relief of Donatello.
Neoclassical theatre built in 1886-87 in the historic center, home to a theatrical season.

Excursion starting from Murenz, hamlet of Pontebernardo (1567 m), on a dirt road in the pine forest signposted GTA, which over 1850 m becomes a path; about 700 m of altitude difference and 2 hours of climbing, hiking difficulty, recommended from June to October. At about 1950 m there is a first fortification: the area hosted defensive works that controlled the passage of the Barricades. The top is a panoramic point.
The town hall on Europa Square.
In Valnontey, over a thousand species of plants with butterflies and lichens.
The Roman city.

One of the main Romanesque monuments of the Marches, probably born as a private monastery of the Attoni-Alberoni-Gozoni family in the marshland area ('moja') near the Esino; the sources date its construction between the 11th and the first decades of the 12th century. In blocks of limestone, it has an inscribed Greek cross plan, three aisles and five apses, a central nave with barrels and a portal with three arches decorated with branches and braids; the cylindrical bell tower remains the base.
The large exhibition district of Fuorigrotta, one of the largest in Italy, with historic pavilions, green spaces and a rich calendar of fairs, congresses, exhibitions and concerts.
A monastery became home to music.
Roman mosaics in the park.
The liveliest market in Sicily.
The Agati organ.

The largest humid zone in Tuscany, born from an ancient brackish lagoon slowly reclaimed, borders the beaches of Versilia and is a stopover for migratory birds; it is part of the Park of Migliarino, San Rossore and Massaciuccoli. From the small port of Massaciuccoli you can observe the birds along the shore trails and in summer they start crossing by boat, even evenings with observation of the stars or opera shows; on the other side you can see Torre del Lago, the village of Puccini.
A village among castles and frescoes.
Silence and stone among the vineyards.
One Sunday in the stalls.
18th century science in the original rooms.
Rock and castle on the sea.

Borgo della Vallesina between hills of vineyards and olive groves, closed by Renaissance walls with small loggias and polygonal towers; it houses the International Museum of Postal Image, linked to the patron Saint Rufo, protector of the portals, and outside the walls the collegiate of Santa Maria della Misericordia and the sanctuary of the Madonna del Sole.

The large square at the foot of the Lower Castle, with the chessboard drawn on the floor, hosts the Chess game to living characters, re-enactment Renaissance in the second weekend of September of even years.

Next to the chapel of the Madonnina (already existing in 1581, rebuilt in 1791, with a rare bell tower with a triangular plan) the Balconies, ...The Balcunets, offer a view of the center and go down with a staircase to the old bridge, now pedestrian; the name comes from the Dojra gate of 1356. In 1741 the municipality added a civic tower above the bell tower of Santa Croce, church of 1714 with an organ of the nineteenth century. In Piazza IV Novembre the Art Nouveau fountain of 1904 by Giacomo Guglielmotti, dedicated to Napoleon Leumann.
The Rock of the Sforza.
The last expansive fortress, with views of Apuane and Apennines.

Born in the late 19th century, a port of departure for La Maddalena: the Rock of the Bear, a natural monument and symbol of the village, the Fortress of Monte Altura of 1887-1889, the Ethnographic Museum and a coast of beaches and windy bays such as Porto Pollo and Isuledda.

Medieval village of fishermen gathered around the port, on the shore of the lake; there stands the Oratory of San Sebastiano, Romanesque jewel with a hut facade, apse to hanging arches and bell tower with three orders of windows.
Where the travelers of Cassia stayed.
Fossils, minerals and meteorites in an astronomical observatory.

In the cloister of the abbey of Lamoli, it tells of vegetable pigments from ancient times to the early twentieth century, when synthetic dyes replaced them: archive documents, books and herbs, including the ford (Isatis tinctoria), resource of the valley in the Renaissance. Color extraction laboratory and dye plants cultivated in the meadows around; visits only by reservation (+39 347 860 7585).
The mills that produce extra virgin olive oil Taggiasca.
Sea and granite on the gulf.

Anthropological demoethanological museum inaugurated in 2003 in a former kindergarten converted with transparent facades, along the Appia route; dedicated to Michele Pezza called Fra' Diavolo, born in Itri in 1771. The path, curated by Vincenzo Pavilione, has three sections: "Ragioni della Storia" (a century of repression), "Ragioni del Mito" (flying leaves, operas, novels, films) and "Ragioni del Luogo" (the "Terra dei briganti" (the "Terra dei briganti") as heritage. MiC timetables: closed on Mondays; morning Thu, Sat and Sun 10-13, afternoon Mar-Dom 16.30-19 (winter) or 17.30-20 (summer).
The historical source of the waters of Nocera.
Archaeological area in the Courtyard with remains of Roman and late Roman houses, streets and public buildings, seat of the International Center of Photography.
Refined Renaissance residence reopened after consolidation work, with furnishings, ceramics and a renewed path.
The great church of Renzo Piano and the tomb of Padre Pio.
Small medieval village whose origins would date back to a settlement of Basilian monks, today the village hotel is with about thirty reception facilities.
Bosses' house.

Benedictine abbey founded in the late 10th century (first abbot Sign in 986) and rebuilt in 1256 in bricks with three naves; very elevated presbytery with imposing staircase and crypt with a polychrome terracotta statue of the 15th century Saint attributed to the Della Robbia and Roman materials of reuse.
A bourgeois house in the heart of the country.
Visits suspended for works according to Tourism Rome
The Medici sign in the middle of the village.

Cistercian Abbey founded by the monks of Rivalta Scrivia, of the Burgundian line of La Ferté (1180 according to the abbey card, 1204 according to that of the village), which takes its name from an ancient branch of the Po called Acqua Lunga; the bishop of Vigevano is still the abbot. The complex includes the monastic church of the XII-XIII century, the abbey palace renovated in the sixteenth century by the abbot Galeazzo Pietra, the first bishop of Vigevano, and agricultural structures of the eighteenth-nineteenth century.

Set up in the rural houses of the eighteenth century built on the structures of the Roman theatre, of which follow the curved shape, with sinks, fireplaces, ovens and niches still visible. The finds, almost all from the area of Saepinum and surroundings, range from prehistory to the Middle Ages: from the paleolithic stone instruments of the middle valley of the Tammaro to Roman life, between symposium, leisure, crafts and funeral rites.
The port for trips to the archipelago.

Fortified village between Senigallia and Jesi, surrounded by the Scarpa, the walk of covered round about 300 meters from which you can see from the Sibillini to the Conero; in the basement of the castle the Museum Utensili on the sharecropping culture, and in the vineyards around the Lacrima of Morro d'Alba DOC.
The green rising of Genoa.
Medieval village between holm oak and chestnut woods where the Fountain of Napoleon flows, already Fonte Acquaviva, so called for the emperor's stops in exile; there is a fountain for free supply.
An open history book, free of charge.

Santena is the city of Camillo Benso di Cavour: the eighteenth-century family castle houses the Memorial Cavour and the tomb of the statesman, surrounded by an English park of 23 hectares designed by Xavier Kurten; in the village, the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul with its high bell tower.

Small village at 455 meters at the entrance of the Valcellina, inside the Natural Park of the Friulian Dolomites, with stone houses and wooden balconies (showers) is the village of the eagles for the avifauna area and the recovery center of the raptors, and houses the Museum of Art and Rural Civilization.

Established in 1985 to protect the fossiliferous deposit, it extends for 4 hectares in the immediate hinterland of Ceriale, about one kilometer from the beaches. The torrent has dug the rocks of the formation of Ortovero revealing layers of the Pliocene in exceptional state of conservation: the shells of molluscs predominate, with over two hundred species, but there are also corals, briozoa, otolites of fish, echinoderms and crustaceans. The site has been studied since the nineteenth century; the museum     . Silvio Lai is a few hundred meters away.
Panorama on the Liri Valley and the feast of the Madonnas Kiss.
In the former monastery of Sant'Egidio, with the study of Trilussa.
MiC card (updated in 2020) indicates "Closed" every day of the week; call before the visit

In an ancient building of the center on three levels: Pinacoteca and provincial gipsoteca with about 120 works from the sixteenth to the twentieth century, the permanent collection of the Rotella Foundation dedicated to the Catanzarese Mimmo Rotella and a center for contemporary culture.
The mounds of the Iron Age.
Welcome up close, out of the way.
The parish church of the Candeliers of Ferragosto.

A 16th century watchtower built by the Spanish against the Saracen pirates, about 1 km north of the village at the end of a sandy bay: square plan without external staircase, shoe base of about 15 meters, about 18 meters high; it communicated with Torre Casarea and Torre Lapillo and in the Second World War hosted an artillery station. Today it is part of the project "Le Torri Fortificati Vedette della Legalità" for monitoring the marine protected area.
Remains of the fort and views of the lower Val Chisone from a giant bench.
The Scala fortress that closes the peninsula on the water.

Romanesque church with three naves near the Tower of Galatrona, perhaps built on the site of an ancient pagan temple. It preserves three glazed terracottas of Giovanni della Robbia made between 1517 and 1521: the baptismal font, the statue of St. John the Baptist and a ciborium.
The oldest incisions in the Camonica Valley.

In the fifteenth century Palazzo Guidobono, rebuilt with a Gothic façade in 1939-42, tells the ancient Dertona: the sarcophagus of Publius Elio Sabino, the tombstone of soldier Aurelius Veterano, a stele of gens Latinia, a togata statue, two polychrome mosaics and three fistulae of the aqueduct. Open Saturday and Sunday 15.30-19, with free guided tours on Saturday.
Villa seat of the Pinacoteca of the Fondazione Sicilia.
The Milanese Nobel study rebuilt in a station.
One of the most curious fountains.
A century of Friulian mechanics with cars and collectible motorcycles.
The church in the rock.
The medieval arch on the lava gorges of Simeto.
Two stone churches within walking distance.
SardiniaCulture (Add. 16/7/2026) indicates the museum as closed, without reopening date
The Byzantine icon at the bottom of the staircase on the gravina.

The spa uses the waters of the springs of San Giacomo, the Three Saints and others for beauty treatments and treatments; from the new complex of 2017 offers wellness center, indoor thermal pool with whirlpool and outdoor swimming pool with solarium.
The castle on the village.
The scenic hill.
The octagonal temple of the source.
The green and panoramic lung of the city.
We're going from here to the hamlet.
The eighteenth-century door that tells the flood of 1705.
At the foot of the Doge's Palace, set according to a nineteenth-century project.

City museum polo with two permanent exhibitions: the lapidary "Le parole della pietra" (The words of the stone), with inscriptions that tell the history of the Marsica, and the multimedia museum of the drying up of the Fucino "Il filo dell'acqua" (The water thread).

In a karst territory rich in caves, swallowholes and resurgents, the Bussento, born from Monte Cervati, disappears into the subsoil near the Rupe to emerge after about 4 km in Morigerati, in the WWF Oasis, on the opposite side of the mountain.
The cathedral on the course.

The association, founded in 1996, has at its headquarters a documentation centre with panels, photographs, documents and machinery on the history and production processes of the perosine textile industries: the mill Bolmida of 1835, the silk waste silk factory started by Berthelot in 1870 and then taken over by the Gütermanns, the cotton factory of Jenny and Ganzoni of 1883. The route is about 3 km long, with ten panels in four languages, and crosses the country between working residences, boarding houses, kindergartens, after-work and hydroelectric power stations. Self-guided tour of about 2 hours; guided tours by reservation.

Borgo at the foot of the hill, mentioned for the first time in a document of 6 December 1123, with historical center of medieval installation; on the hill the neo-Gothic Castle of Roccolo of the Marquis Tapparelli d'Azeglio with its romantic park, chapels frescoed by the brothers Biazaci and the Hermitage of Belmonte.
The kingdom of the Sardinian deer.

I1 trail of the Parco da Civitella Alfedena (about 3 hours, difficulty E, 845 m of difference in altitude) between beech and pine trees up to Passo Cavuto (1,980 m) and the refuge of Forca Resuni, with frequent sightings of chamois.
A park of iron sculptures among secular trees.

Village of the Nebrodi Park on a panoramic hill about 1000 meters, dominated by the ruins of the Arab-Norman Castle: a historic center with 25 churches, including the Mother Church of Saint Lucia, noble palaces, Porta Palermo and many fountains, the Regional Museum of Silvo-pastoral Traditions and, in the surroundings, Lake Quattrocchi and the Cascate di Ciddia.

In the former Baronial Palace Cornacchia di Poggio Canoso, with rooms dedicated to woods, river environment, agricultural landscape and peasant civilization, dioramas, panels and naturalistic collections, plus a didactic workshop with projection room.
Aniene's peasant life in two thousand objects.
The village hanging from the rock.
The Great War between Galicia and the Dolomites in three floors.

It rises where the underneath door was and its bell tower is one of the two towers of the gate. The original parts date back to the fifteenth century; inside the circular choir and a wooden statue of the Clement. Next to it is the brotherhood of the Annunziata of the late sixteenth century.
the MiC card is closed every day: visit only by booking by phone
the villa is used by the Municipality for events; visits must be agreed with the Municipality of Desio (Lombardy)
Ligabue in his country.

The territory is a landscape of hills and olive groves that descend towards the coast; the village is part of the Città dell'Olio and produces DOC and DOCG wines to be tasted in the local farms. The Wine Route, about 30 km between hills and tastings, starts from Controguerra and reaches Torano Nuovo, Ancarano, Corropoli and Colonnella; in summer the Wine Festival and the Wine Bike animate the historic center and vineyards.

Built in 1595 in late Renaissance rural style on the slope of Montechiaro Alto, it houses the venerable relic of the Sante Spine, a 14th century stone tabernacle, a popular wooden pulpit and an eighteenth-century Madonna of Margliano school; three naves divided by columns in local sandstone. Under the church, the Oratory of St. Anthony, recovered, houses a museum on the Sacred Spines with paintings by Severino Baraldi and a copy of the Shroud. Free access during functions.
On foot or on horseback on the way to transhumance.
Mother church of the 11th century, under the castle, visible from afar for its large dimensions.
The ancient heart of the capital.

Stone houses with wrought iron balconies and roofs in coppi; the parish church of Santa Maria Maddalena preserves a marble baptismal font with reliefs dated 1644 and a polychrome wooden statue of the saint, the eighteenth-century church of St. John the Baptist the chariot of the procession of the Madonna del Carmelo at the end of July.
Grotto in plaster discovered by Francesco Orsoni in the nineteenth century and reopened in 2008, with an important protohistoric settlement; Luigi Fantini found a necropolis of the Copper Age.
An unexpected museum in an industrial building.
18th century plasters and frescoes in a mountain hamlet.
The Guercino looks up close and goes up into the dome.
28-step staircase in oak wood that the pilgrims climbed on their knees to obtain the plenary indulgence; the name dates back to 1772.

On the top of Mount San Leonardo, about 4 km from the village towards Arzachena: a holiday residence of the judges of Gallura, already built in the first half of the 12th century and destroyed by the Aragonese in the 15th. There remains a rectangular three-room building, the remains of a tower, traces of double walls in granite blocks without mortar and a cistern. A few meters west is the chapel of the castle, San Leonardo, of the twelfth century: among the smallest Romanesque churches on the island, all granite with roof in slabs of shale. You climb up with a staircase in the rock of about 100 m.
The peasant life of an Arbëreshe community.

The only center of the island of San Pietro, founded in 1738 by Ligurian families arrived from Tabarka and included among the most beautiful villages in Italy: caruggi and eighteenth-century forts, the Civic Museum Casa del Duca in the oldest fort, the Madonna dello Schiavo and, outside the village, Capo Sandalo, Cala Fico, Le Colonne and La Conca.
According to Emilia Romagna Turismo is the only natural lake in the province.
Seven centuries of art and mysteries.
The green lung of the city.
The limestone canyon on which the country was born.
The myth of Hollywood's first Latin star in his hometown.

Small church of the 13th century with a nave and a single altar, with votive paintings and frescoes of the 2nd and 3rd centuries; it was the main church of the village before the title passed to Santa Margherita.

The museum occupies a gallery that served as a storage of explosives and tells, with images, sounds, stories and anecdotes, the phases of the mine and the hard work of the miners; the mines of pyrites, active since 1898 and among the most important in Italy, closed in 1981. The entrance is in the Park of the Rocks, with welcome and infopoint; it is part of the National Park of the Metalliferous Hills.
Cycle path of 80 km from Lake Caldonazzo to Bassano del Grappa passing through Borgo, where you can rent normal bikes and pedal assistance.
Gardens with views of the gulf.

Next to the cathedral, from a panoramic point you can access the Tribu space and the museum that exhibits the sculptures of Francesco Ciusa, first prize at the Venice Biennale of 1907, including the Mother of the killed.
The road to trade.
A small museum that preserves the memory of the local traditions and crafts of Val d'Intelvi.
The walled village of Badia.

Medieval village of the Roman Castles enclosed by walls of the fifth century BC, the ancient Lanuvium of the Sanctuary of Juno Sospita, whose finds are in the Civic Museum Lanuvino; in the center the Palazzo Colonna where Marcantonio Colonna was born, the Fountain of the Scogli by Carlo Fontana and the Rocca with the wine shop of Colli Lanuvini.
Church of the 14th century, rich in works of art, the main city of the hundred churches.
The Baroque parish.
A little known underground path.
Church with Greek cross plan dating back to 1408.
The highest mountain in the province.

Piazza Municipio and Piazzetta San Giuseppe, next to the amphitheatre and Palazzo Del Gaudio Campagna, the cultural centre of the village; in Piazza del Duomo the church of San Nicola di Bari, with the facade in tuff of Mendicino, and the church of San Sebastiano.

In 1744 Charles of Bourbon expropriated the farm and the land of the princes of Caramanico: over 2,000 hectares of woods and fields partly swampy and covered with cardoons, from which the name. Carlo started there the real industry of buffalo straw and the breeding of the horses of Persano; Ferdinand IV built the neoclassical residence, by Francesco Collecini, co-worker of Vanvitelli, a double-t plant, and made it an experimental farm. Inside the staircase with stuccoes by Carlo Beccalli, the hall of rural painting on drawings by Philipp Hackert, the vault of the hall frescoed by Fedele Fischetti (1791), the room of the Four Seasons by Giuseppe Cammarano and the neoclassical chapel; on the ground floor the royal kitchens, the Sala dei Camini and the church of the Ascension, and in the complex the Bourbon stables and an immersive hall. Since 2016 it is managed by the Fondazione Carditello; the museum area is visited only with guided tours, Saturdays at 15 and 16 and Sunday at 11:30, 12:30, 15 and 16.
The most spectacular medieval square.
Long sandy beach between two crowns of cliffs.
The regional museum on Piazza Mazzini, opposite the Duomo.

On the hill Serralonga, about three kilometers from the village: according to tradition in 1709 Our Lady appeared to the farmer Giuseppe Mastrostefano and caused a spring to spring. On August 15th the eighteenth-century statue is taken in procession to the village; the main feasts are August 24th and August 25th and on 26th the statue returns to the sanctuary.

Trinitapoli is just outside the village the Ipogei Archaeological Park, one of the most important necropolis of the Bronze Age in Italy, and a civic museum with bronzes, avori and the Trinitapoli Table. The historic centre is made of white houses, alleys and churches such as the Mother Church of St. Stephen.
The birthplace of the Capuchins, in the silence of the woods.

The beach is about 7 km long and with Platamona, the beach of the sassaresi, forms a 15 km wide stretch from 10 to 30 meters; dunes sheltered by pines, junipers and dwarf palms, emerald green water and sandy seabed that slopes rapidly, sunsets with views of the Asinara. Suitable for kite and windsurf all year round; pinewood behind, rent and refreshment. Further east are the beaches of Pulchili, near the mouth of Silis, with shallow waters, Maritza and La Tonnara, pebbles.
The nuraghe that dominates the plain.
The building already houses the Confraternity of the Holy Spirit, whose frescoes illustrate its activity, then became a dairy.
A thousand years of glass in a Liberty villa, with the furnace on.

Palace of the Ricci Petrocchini family, to which belonged Father Matteo Ricci, protagonist of the mission in China started in 1582. Inside the studio of the self-taught painter Fabio Failla (Lucca 1917 - Roma 1987), descendant of the Ricci.
Ski resort in the natural amphitheatre of Monte Terminillo.
Visitable if open (Italy.it)

Borgo del Crotonese, known as the village of Sardella, with the historic center on the hill and the marina of Torretta sullo Ionio; it houses the Palopoli archaeological collection, the Pacchiana museum and an astronomical observatory on a plot confiscated from crime.
A waterfall inside a cave.
The city from above.

Medieval village on a hill between the valleys of Vincio and Nievole, among chestnut woods, gathered around the Pieve di San Niccolò; around Serra Pistoiese, the ruins of Sant'Andrea di Furfalo and Casore del Monte with the Museum of Rural Culture.
Fontana Defenza, Fontana San Giovanni, Fonte dei Frati and the fountain of sulphur water Ria Rigola, recently renovated.
A stage of medieval pilgrims.
A wellness break just a stone's throw from the sea.
The tour of the medieval walls.

Ring path that starts and arrives at the little church of San Pietro, in the countryside along the Musone stream, in nine stages: the remains of the Botte di San Pietro where Muson passed under the Muson, the Roi canal with dotted tritons and water scorpions, the five great elms, hedges of farnia, robinia and hawthorn, the closed field, the large permanent meadows (228 hectares, 17% of Prai), a typical farmhouse and the grove along the Muson.
Understand ten thousand years of history of the Rock before going up there.

Historic nucleus of ancient origins above Spadafora, which until 1817 was a fraction of it; the feud included five houses registered under Frederick II. The Santa Colomba square, inaugurated in 1990, dominates the slope with a circular fountain. The church of San Martino, rebuilt in the twenties-thirties of the twentieth century, conserves altars in polychrome marble of the eighteenth century recovered from the original church; opened during the celebrations.

Small town of the valley of the Visone, dominated by the castle of the Counts Gallesio-Piuma (XII century), seat of the Welsh Studies Center; from the village starts the hiking route  "Collinando" towards the Fortress of Visone, between ancient churches and panoramic points.
It is the best example of rationalist architecture in the city.
Former Benedictine priory, today space for modern art, with a room dedicated to Innocenzo Manzetti and his automa flautist of 1840.
Romanesque country.
Where the Italian railroad was born.
Two hundred million years under a Renaissance palace.

On the island of Spargi, four small white sandy beaches between dunes with junipers and marine lilies and the rock of the witch , in the dry lies the wreck of the Roman ship exposed to the museum Lamboglia. Accessible only by sea with mini cruises between the islands.
The memory of Reggio's ghetto.
Part of the Medici complex of Poggio a Caiano, the large farm with its land wanted by Lorenzo il Magnifico.
The strangest of the Venetian villas.
The Bourbon utopia of silk.

Diocesan shrine and since 1958 parish of Mompantero, built in 1957-58 on a project by Emanuele Godone where there was a small chapel, at the entrance of the mule track for the summit. Modern building in concrete, wood and stone, with bell tower behind the apse surmounted by a statue of the Madonna and apsidal windows open on the slopes of the mountain; on August 5 there are the celebrations.

Born in 1979 at the initiative of the Municipality and Mario Realini, with donations mainly of minerals and fossils; in 1984 Realini discovered the shell Emiliomya malnatensis. Recognized by the Region as a museum collection in 2004, since 2007 it has been in the liberty Villa Braghenti, in the public park of the same name, with eight sections: psammophile, litological, mineralogical, paleontological, palethnological, gemological, zoological and temporary exhibitions. Open on Friday 9-12 and 14-18, Saturday 9-12, first Sunday of the month 14.30-17.30; guided tours and workshops on reservation for a fee.
The most evocative panoramic point of the city, on the expanse of white houses with grey roofs; recommended at sunset.
The shrine on the meridian.

High to parish between the Three and the fifteenth century, it has a structure probably sixteenth century, the eighteenth-century appearance and a restoration of 1863; it preserves paintings including a Martyrdom of Saint Catherine of the Veronese school.
The X century square castle that dominates the village, the most evident testimony of the medieval past of the village.
Woods and clear waters in the heart of the Metalliferous Hills.
A fresco by Michelino da Besozzo kept inside the architecture of Pellegrini.

Rebuilt with a single nave after the earthquake of 1895, it has a chestnut door carved in 1912 of the Caminiti family with the Assumption and the Annunciation. It houses a marble Madonna from the Messinese school, paintings and statues by Raffaele Angelo Musitano (San Rocco 1894, San Raffaele with Tobia 1892), Carpente del Lecce Giuseppe Malecore and, on the high altar, an Assumption that is believed to come from the old church of Paracorio, before the earthquake of 1783.
Small nucleus of Malatesta origin on the borders with the Duchy of Urbino, already seat of Municipality; the church with the canonical and the mighty walls of the 13th century remain.
Carnival horned masks.
About 5 hectares between via Paolucci and the northern promenade, recovered in the 2000s from a former parking area: plants and animals of the Mediterranean coast, with marsh turtle and earth turtle.
A frescoed cloister outside the circuits.

Country at the foot of the hiking area of Monte San Vigilio, near Lana, referred to as "Villa Cerones" in 857: above the village Castel Monteleone (Lebenberg), of the thirteenth century, with frescoed chapel and rococo garden, and from here starts the Waalweg of Marlengo towards Tel.

Ruins of the monastery in the valley of the river Bai, on a spur of trachyte halfway between Roccastrada and Montemassi; there remains also the crypt, which the municipality defines as a small treasure of the territory.
Walking through them is the best way to live Bologna, with the sun and with the rain.
Armors and memories of the battle of 1530.
Flemish Tapestries in Sicily.

Romanesque roundabout of the XI-XII centuries on a hill near the castle of San Maroto, cited as priory in 1240, among the most singular Romanesque works of the Marche: circular plan with four apses decorated with hanging arches and concentric stone ring dome built without centimeters. The bell tower dates back to the first fourteenth century; inside a Madonna enthroned from the second half of the thirteenth century and a table of the Madonna del Rosario di Venanzo da Camerino.

From Rore the marked path goes up for 1 km (about 45 minutes a way, from 890 to 1,010 m) the Ciantorane stream in the forest, between irrigation channels, wooden and stone bridges and a rocky gorge, up to the Tumpi waterfall the Pisso that falls into a rocky pool; it is the theme of Sarvanot, the hairy and spiteful goblins of tradition. With a short steep detour you will reach the Big Bench of Chris Bangle, a panoramic view over the valley. Suitable for everyone but not for strollers, snow-free; beautiful in autumn.

At the centre of the village, on a panoramic hill, it combines a castle with an essential military facility, with prison cells, armory room and accommodation on the ground floor and a large portal with sharp sixth on the upper floor, and a baronial palace on the back, transition between the Renaissance and Baroque; two successive cylindrical towers flank the façade, with Guelph battlements on the front and Ghibellines on the north-east side.
At the end of the long Corso, in Piazza VII Aprile, it preserves works and paintings by important artists; the convent has a loggia on two levels.

Country on Monte San Leonardo, in the Lucane Dolomites, overlooking the valley of the Basento between the monoliths of the Rocca del Cappello and the Devil's Chair; it was a Longobard fortress and preserves the mother church of the Assunta, the museum of poor toy and the wood of Cupolicchio.
A historic journey at altitude.
The Gothic building of Piazza del Grano, among the historic architectures of the center of Bolzano.
Green Valley of the Appia Antica Regional Park with entrance from Via Latina.
Chieti's religious heart.
The Holy Face and Ilaria, two masterpieces.
Granite and gravy on the roof of Mount Acuto.
Consecrated in 1625, it rises on the site of a previous chapel dedicated to the same saint.
A green museum at the foot of the castle.
Masterpiece statues, few tourists.
The polychrome ceramic roof and the civic tower on the main square.
An entire country transformed into a Bible illustrated on the walls.

On the ancient road Pretoria, it was born from a castle probably guarding the bridge; in the sixteenth century the Cocciano-Di Rosa built the present building, restored by the Ziletti family, today owner. You can see the cornice with shelves, the portal in marble with rustic rocks and the coat of arms.

The church was restored in the fourteenth century by Roberto de Capua and transformed in the sixteenth century by Bartolomeo III de Capua (on the façade date 1500), who enlarged the nave, frescoed the walls and gave it the current title; among the designers mentioned Giovanni Donadio called Mormando and Francesco di Giorgio Martini. Facade in stone with doric parasts, oculus and coat of arms of Bartolomeo and Aurelia Orsini; next to the main altar four sarcophagi of the ancestors De Capua, and in the tomb of Andrea rest also the remains of Queen Constance of Chiaromonte.
Info LIPU 0931 735026 (data of the regional guide of 2016, to be confirmed)
The dome of Schellino, the Cuneo Gaudí.
From the Apennines to the plain in seven salt.

The municipal territory, in the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, includes 12 villages on three valleys, from the basin of Filignano to the first buttresses of Monte Marrone, and the provincial road offers a panorama of the Mainarde. The paths in the woods are lined with dry stone walls, which also serve to terrace and protect the slopes, and votive newsstands decorated with majolica of Neapolitan school; in the woods remain the straws, ancient pastoral shelters in dry stone that recall the Greek tholos. From the village of Cerasuolo passes the Via Francigena del Sud coming from San Biagio Saracinisco.

Hellenistic-Roman city rebuilt on Mount Catalfano after Dionisio of Syracuse, at the beginning of the fourth century BC, destroyed the oldest center on the coast; a dedication to Fulvia Plautilla, wife of Caracalla (202-205 A.D.), marks the traditional end of the city. You walk along a regular road system with blocks, peristyle houses with cisterns, shops on the main street, the agora portico, the spas and, higher up, theater, bouleuterion, the so-called Ginnasio, the House of Arpocrate and a sacred area with terraces. The Antiquarium exhibits amphorae, remains of statues, marine finds, architectural elements and parietal paintings.
Complex outside the walls essential to understand the conversion of Francis: it was the convent of Saint Clare, where the saint died.
Fortezza dei da Varano in the hamlet of Sfercia, now home to an exhibition center of artistic crafts.

The centre has grown around the Palazzo dei Principi di Trabia, lords of the territory since the mid-sixteenth century; the building, recently renovated and with free access, preserves volumes and books. Around the Civic Tower with Art Nouveau clock of 1848, the church of Santa Margherita with the wooden statue of Our Lady Odigitria dated 1500, Belvedere Square and the Climb Lampasona, panoramic view requalified with street art.
The medieval district of colorful houses on the Serravalle hill, with alleys linked by steps in trachyte and cellars where you taste the Malvasia; there you will find funtana manna in red trachyte.
The baroque living room was born around a mythical source.

Collection set up since 1974 in the cellars of the fortress: about twenty tanks with the fishes of the Po, dioramas with reptiles, mammals and birds, instruments of river crafts and a prehistoric pirogue of about 4,000 years ago, then ethnographic sections on the rural life of Padana and archaeological with paleontological finds of 15-20 thousand years ago. Open on Sunday afternoon, except January, July, August and December.
Cathedral on Piazza Risorgimento, the central square of the city, known for its mosaics.
The most collectible square in the city.
The megalithic door that enchanted the Grand Tour.

In the Osteria dei Pellegrini built in 1607-1616 by Ferdinando de' Medici, on a project by Mechini, to welcome the pilgrims of the sanctuary: it tells the Valdinievole and the reclamation of the Padule di Fucecchio.
The Baschenis frescoes.

About 7 km from the village, on the banks of the Esino, it was founded by Saint Romualdo and in 1180 entered the Camaldolese congregation. Romanesque-Gothic and compact as a church-fortress, it has sailing bell tower, decorated Romanesque portal, three naves with figurative capitals and a crypt under the presbytery; only the church can be visited.

Founded on 5 March 1997 by Bishop Antonio Pagano, the section of sacred art is divided into five nuclei (marbles, sculptures, paintings, silvers, various objects) and preserves a cover of early Christian sarcophagus from the IV-V century. The archaeological section, of about 1,000 m2 with the furnaces and necropolis of Pithecusae, is located instead at the complex of Santa Restituta in Lacco Ameno.
The largest Punic necropolis in the Mediterranean, with thousands of tombs on the Tuvixeddu hill overlooking the port, along with the Viper Cave.

Defined the only historic center of Puglia where you can miss it completely, it is made of narrow streets and few, tiny squares. The heart is Piazza Plebiscito, surrounded by important buildings, including the Palazzo del Balì and, in front, the Sedile, once the seat of the University.
Paths with views of the countryside; along the way you will encounter the chestnut millennial, symbol of the history and nature of the place.
The hairpin road in the gallery.

Of the fortress erected by Gentile da Mogliano in the fourteenth century remain the bastions, excellent panoramic point; inside the deconsecrated church of Santa Maria del Suffragio (1698). From the fortress you can see the former hospital of San Michele (1782) and the Autopalace liberty, a former garage restored as an exhibition space.
The fifteenth-century church in the locality of Acquebone dedicated to San Rocco, invoked against pestilences and epidemics; inside paintings on the life of the saint.

In Palazzo Eccheli Baisi, a noble residence between the Five and the seventeenth century next to the archpriest's church, preserves more than 1,000 fossils collected on Mount Baldo northern (collezione Osvaldo Giovanazzi), which document the marine animals that succeeded in 150-180 million years after the Triassic, from protozoa to crustaceans; outstanding for the gasteropods of the Sorne field, with 134 classified species. The palace is also linked to the mines of Baldo's Claudonite, from which the Brentonic Green pigment.
An intact village overlooking the lake.
€5, students €2, free up to 7 years

A rural church erected in the 16th century about 3 km from the village among secular trees, with a modified facade in the 18th century; there are the Nativity of the Virgin on 8 September and St. John the Baptist at the end of August.

Along the road to Carpegna, the 11th century Romanesque parish church preserves a marble statue of San Sebastiano from the 15th century; excavations conducted between 1990 and 1997 brought to light a medieval necropolis and a Roman area of republican age, with remains of an ancient Roman road.

Fortified building with thick walls and a 12-metre tower; the paved courtyard ends in a Renaissance loggia with a wide view of the countryside. Perhaps of the ninth century, it was used by Frederick II as a hunting lodge and meeting place of the poets of the Sicilian School; in the sixteenth century there held dinners the humanist Giovan Battista Manso, with Torquato Tasso host, and in the eighteenth century became residence of the Duke Ascanio Pignatelli.
The Roman Assisi.
In the Comacchio Museum Pass (€17 full, €14 reduced, with boat tour in the valleys); free on the first Sunday of the month
Remains of the castle of the 11th century on the edge of the cliff, remodelled in the 16th century, reachable from the piazza del Baglio.
16th century cloister and baroque bell tower in the heart of Oreno.
Ancient irrigation channel along which run mountain bike routes.
Alleys and Lecce stone around the castle.

The church, built in the fourteenth century and renovated in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, has a Gothic portal and fifteenth-century frescoes; in the former convent is set up the Museum of the radio of epoch, according to the regional portal the second public museum of this type in Italy.
Sanctuary in Doric style in the hamlet of Quattropani, overlooking the sea.

The town of Cilento overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea at the mouth of the Alento, where the ruins of Elea-Velia rise, founded around 540 BC by the Focei and home of the philosophical school of Parmenide and Zenone; along the coast the Path of the Lovers climbs from the cliff of Ascea Marina to the Telegrafo Tower; the beaches of Torre del Telegrafo, Piana di Velia and Marina di Ascea are Blue Flag 2026.
The castle that named Tyrol.

The pre-Romanesque church of the 7th century has been modified several times, preserving fragments of ancient architecture, altarpieces of various eras and finds of the excavations of the 20th century.

Small hamlet on the high hill, part of the territory of Valencia since the 14th century, developed along a single road: the church of Sant'Eusebio, the church of the Convent and the bell tower. From the village you can see the Po plain with the centers along the Po and, on clear days, Mount Rosa.
The sanctuary of Athena di Lagaria.
Palaces and squares of a noble village in Lucano.
A 16th century church on the outskirts of the village, with Gothic-Aragonese elements, Renaissance decorations and a wooden statue of the Virgin.

Beach of soft white sand on a semicircle coast, behind dunes covered with Mediterranean maquis, with sandy stretches alternated with rocks. Crystal clear and turquoise water and sandy bottom; free stretches and establishments with sun loungers, umbrellas, showers and bars. The Romans already built their villas there.
The chestnut of the Prenestini Mountains.
Visit on request to the Tourist Office of the Municipality

Village of the Diano Valley at 501 meters, founded on November 2, 1333 by Guglielmo Sanseverino, with a historic center of buildings of the Three-Fourteenth century, frescoed churches and the Museum of the ancient knowledge in the Baronial Palace Picinni-Leopardi.
One of the locations of the National Roman Museum in the area of Piazza Navona.
A red stone village on the lake.
About six kilometers of shady trails to Torre del Lago, with Viale dei Tigli and the bike path, kiosks and Villa Borbone.

In the premises under the complex of San Francesco is exposed the life-size copy, made by the School of Art of Manzù after the Year of the Etruscans (1985), of the parade biga of the middle of the 6th century BC in walnut wood covered with golden bronze with scenes of the life of Achilles. The original, found by chance in 1902 in a mound of the Colle del Capitano, was purchased in 1903 by the Metropolitan Museum of New York; two rooms document discovery, fugitive activity and funeral equipment, with an archaeological map of the territory.
The art returned.

Romanesque church of the 12th century, then Benedictine monastery mentioned in the Bull of Anastasius IV of 1153; of the monastery, ruined by the earthquake, only the church remains, reopened in 1703 and declared a national monument in 1889. The salient façade has a protire with two dragons that devour and regurgitate two men, a rosette with twelve arches, peacocks, knights, hunting scenes and a northern portal with Alexander the Great kidnapped by the griffons; the bell tower is detached. The interior with three naves, freed from the baroque additions, houses a Madonna with the wooden Child, a wooden Crucifix, a fifteenth century holy waterworks and the fourteenth-century Gothic sarcophagus of Blessed Berardo d'Aquino; part of the materials comes from a Roman villa found near the church. Next to it is a picnic area.
One of the Macabre Dances of the Baschenis, on a cliff above the river.
The sacred art of oriental rite.
Arches and a 17th century noble palace.
Built at the beginning of the 13th century on the edge of Gravina, with baroque portals, 17th century bell tower, 18th century wooden altar and a 16th century polyptych.
Theatre of 1845 with ceramic medallions of the great composers on the façade.
An illusionistic baroque with the Shroud among angels.
History and panorama in the same place.

Centre of the Conca of Bari, about 10 km from the capital, with the church of Santa Maria Veterana, its most important monumental testimony, the Baroque Santa Maria della Croce and the Convent of the Capuchins of 1616; the territory is crossed by the Lama San Giorgio.
A millenarian parish church with a fifteenth-century baptismal font.
Stars and paths in the woods of the Pineta Park.
The pharmacy plants on the lake.
Nature and Gothic frescoes on the same hill.
Industrial archaeology and art.
A thousand-year-old parish church in the historic centre, dedicated to the bishop and martyr St. Magnus, patron saint of the country, celebrated on August 19.
The medieval Ferla of alleys and caves.
Michelangelo's work was created in a room of the Baths of Diocletian, with the clementine sundial inlays of colored marbles on the floor.

Municipality of Alto Milanese near the Milan-Varese motorway that houses the Zucchi Collection, indicated as the largest collection in the world of blocks for hand printing on fabric, and part of the Park of Rugareto, crossed by the Way of Saint Augustine.

The limestone monolith is about 25 meters high at the beginning of the Mattei promenade, south of the centre, considered the symbol of the city; it is also admired from the top by via Bracco, in the historic center. According to legend he was a young man turned into stone by the jealousy of the Sirene, who prevented his love with Cristalda.

Founded in the 8th century; in the 9th century Bishop Rotaldo had the bodies of the saints Benigno and Caro laid there. He holds a Deposition by Girolamo Dai Libri and an eighteenth-century medallion on the ceiling; feast of the patron on 26 December.

Museum born from a private initiative that collects objects of everyday rural life, with reconstructions of ancient environments and a late medieval mill recovered in Pacentro; organizes exhibitions on local traditions. Contacts: 085 8285452, info@mutac.org.
Former Benedictine monastery in the hamlet of Villa Eucheria, with a still intact cryptoportico; it is part of the network of the Historical Residences of Lazio.
Marble, light and silence.
Visitable with free guided tours by reservation (villaaperte.info) at Ville Aperte in Brianza

Città del Novarese was born in the 12th century as a Franco village, which took the first name of Borgo San Leonardo from the oratory where the pilgrims of the Via Francisca stayed; to see the Oratory of San Leonardo, Villa Marazza with the park and library of the Foundation, and in the hamlet Santa Cristina the museum of peasant civilization "How we were." In September, Festival of Grapes and Palio degli Asini.
The ancient nucleus and the great Venetian painting of the plague.
Among the best preserved Gothic-Catalan works of Sardinia, it houses a 1560 retablo.
The peasant village at the foot of the Presolana.

Of Roman origin (Atranum), it retains the medieval structure considered the best preserved of the Coast: alleys, arches, courtyards, squares and stairs that go down to the sea. The little square on the sea was born as a shelter for boats in stormy days; under the arches where fishermen used to repair nets today there are some trattorias. On 22 July, St Mary Magdalene is celebrated.
Sacred architecture of the after Council signed Nervi.

Born at the will of the blacksmith Carlo Rizzarda and opened in 1938, it preserves over 400 wrought iron works made between 1910 and 1930, as well as ceramics, glass (also by Carlo Scarpa), painting and sculpture of the nineteenth century; in December 2018 it received as a gift the collection of glasses Nasci-Franzoia (738 pieces).

Discovered in 1931 by the Speleologist Zanchi and made accessible by the group "Grotte San Pellegrino" with an artificial gallery, catwalks, stairs and electric lighting; in 1941 a second tunnel was dug to drain the water into the flood. They are among the first caves discovered and equipped in Italy, even if of small size: a chasm covered with limestone concretions, stalactites, stalagmites, underground lakes and swallowholes.
The first rural church in the area, dating back to 1002; contains a marble epigraph of the fifth and sixth centuries with the letter of Jesus Christ sent from heaven.

Born from donations of the inhabitants, it is set up in the Ferrant Mill, former mill of the eighteenth century, and collects copper, sieves, wagon wheels, yokes and other tools, with photographs of the work in the fields.
The church on the hill.
To be checked: weekend visits or by reservation for groups
A stage for romantics.

House-museum close to the center that tells the peasant life between the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries: in the houses of earth and straw, called "earthed" , original tools, a frame, the fireplace and the "prete" , the bed warmer.
neither the Municipality nor the FAI indicate ordinary times or methods of visit; visitable at FAI openings

It rises between IX and XI century on the highest point of the country: an act of donation of 1092 attributed it to William of Caggiano, first lord of the place. It had a central body with three high towers, a tower and two forts; in the fifteenth century it became a noble residence. The walls had four gates and the eastern one, with the drawbridge, still gives the name to the area of ...Bocca del Ponte. Mostly municipal and restored, it hosts exhibitions and events.
Alleys, doors and buildings of the sixteenth century.
The portal of 1540 and the rosette of snakes.
The Baroque dome that marks the profile of the village.

Rural buildings in stone and wood along the ancient road to Feltre, with alleys (canisèle), stone fountains, about twenty murals on legends and nature, over one hundred inscriptions on the walls and about 400 gardens, the green heart of the country; themed routes on water, gardens, rural architecture and engravings. On the red chairs scattered around the village you ring the bell and arrives an inhabitant to tell stories and anecdotes of the village.
The pilgrim hospital.
It rises in a square with a panoramic view of the old town; the church of Carmel is among the few escapes to the destruction of the earthquake of 1908.
Fortress built around 1300, ancient entrance from the ground and south door of the center; once called Porta di Santa Maria, for a capital of the Madonna di Marina inside.
On the noble floor of Palazzo dei Diamanti, the great Ferrara painting of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

Church dedicated to St. Apollonius, the fourth bishop of Brescia, whose relics were then transferred to the New Cathedral. During maintenance work in 1958 under eighteenth-century layers of lime frescoes were discovered considered important for the Renaissance of Brescia.
A glimpse of a crib.
The heart of the ancient village.
On Via D'Aquino: Carmelitani from 1595, church of 1609 and facade of 1937; hosts the processions of Holy Week.
14th century frescoes in a small church.
The bottom of the ancient sea between Antola and Aveto.

The old town, called for its shape, arose around the 1000 against the Saracen pirates: alleys, steep climbs, the fourteenth-century Porta di Santo Stefano and the covered passage of the Rivolte di San Sebastiano.
Gothic church in the square of the Earth; the polygonal apse preserves fifteenth-century Umbrian school frescoes, influenced by Filippo Lippi, with a Crucifixion.

Tower of the fortress built in 1354 at the behest of the Gonzaga to fortify the village, transit point on the road between Reggio Emilia and Mantua; the French destroyed the fortress at the beginning of the eighteenth century leaving only the tower, several times restored.
The fortress with the panorama of 34 countries.
The fifteenth-century church on the square of the village; the altarpiece painted in 1625 by Enea Salmeggia shows at the lower part the Turrita Gromo of the time.
Historical seat of the palace of the Municipality, example of Venetian Gothic with the white-pink bichromy and the light porch.
A seventeenth-century theatre in a convent.
€7 (included in the Castle ticket)
The goal of the procession of the Virgins.

Church of the eighth century, with bell tower probably added in the twelfth century; the Carolingian frescoes are among the oldest mural paintings of central Europe, with portraits of the founders, the bishop of Chur and a French gentleman in costume, without comparisons in Europe. In summer visits Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, guided (German or Italian) Monday, Wednesday and Friday; closed Sunday and holidays.

Small church in a natural cave against the wall of the Colle della Tagliata on Monte Autore, about 1,337 m above the springs of the Simbrovio; you go down a staircase in the rock, arriving from Vallepietra on asphalted road or on foot on the paths (including 652 and 683a). On the west wall the fresco of the Trinity of the twelfth century, with three identical figures sitting to the Greek, and under the remains of a cycle of agricultural works; on the east wall frescoes of Byzantine taste with Annunciation, Nativity, Adoration of the Magi and Presentation, plus Madonnas of the fifteenth century. The origins are uncertain, between Eastern monks and Saint Dominic of Sora (X-XII century). The festive cliffs on Sunday after Pentecost, with the "compagnie" of the Valle dell'Aniene on the way and the Pianto delle Zitelle.
The high medieval origins of the country.

Neoclassical villa of the early nineteenth century, designed by L. Pollak, built on the convent of the Reformed Fathers: their church, partly incorporated into the villa, preserves a marble pulpit of the fifteenth century and frescoes, including a Crucifixion of students by Bernardino Luini. Parini, Stendhal, Monti and Foscolo stayed there; the park has neoclassical statues and architecture.
Contemporary art exhibitions in the barn of the villa.
Bathrooms in Lake Maggiore with views of the Borromean Islands.
The peasant village of the Bassa remained intact.
The serene stone living room of the village of the stone chisels.
A palace of the Roman Renaissance.
Pedal through Kerouac's pages.

Considered the most beautiful of the village: Baroque façade with rococo touches, bell towers (the left collapsed with the earthquake of 1908) and Greek cross plan with arms of 33 meters, unique in the south-east of Sicily. The octagonal dome is frescoed by Credadoro with the Triumph of St. Anthony; fourteen stucco statues depict the cardinal and theological virtues.

The "belvedere del Piceno" (Piceno), high on the hill between the valleys of Menocchia and Tesino: walls of more than two kilometers with medieval doors, the narrowest alley in Italy (43 cm), the cathedral of Saints Gregorio and Margherita, the Palazzo del Podestà with the Mercantini Theatre and the civic museums.
In the Upper City, it tells the ancient history of the territory from prehistory to the Roman age with finds, mosaics, coins and objects of daily use.
Inaugurated in 2009 at Palazzo Piacentini in the ancient center, it is part of the Museum of the Sea.
The tower of the gentlemen of Camerino.

Born in 1978 after the recovery of fossils found in Endenna di Zogno, since 1996 it is located in Villa Speranza and since 2007 it is part of the TRIASSICO.IT museum system. It exhibits about 1,500 palaeontological finds on the geology of the Brembana Valley, the most complete documentation of the lepidopterans in the valley (over 700 species, donation Attilio Torriani), the vegetation bands and endemic plants, a room on fauna and a diorama of the Calvi basin of the German artist Grapes Thuernau. Hours: in winter Saturday 10-12, in summer Tuesday 10-12 and Thursday 15-18; guided tours by reservation, audioguide in Italian and English.

Cited in a document of 1149, it is a late-Gothic building with trilobed windows and portal with acute sixth, Renaissance portico and Romanesque bell tower; inside remains of frescoes and a wooden Calvary of the eighteenth century. Next to it stands the new parish church, also dedicated to San Biagio and consecrated in 1935.

16th century coastal tower, today panoramic terrace on the Tyrrhenian Sea and on the cliff of the Ajnella; in the caves of Torre Talao were found stone and bone artifacts of the Paleolithic, with traces of the Musterian phase.
Plant open from June to the end of September, with three large swimming pools, one for children, fed by sulphuric thermal sources.
A curiosity for sportsmen.

Norman fortress of the XII-XIII centuries on the summit, on the remains of the temple of Venus Ericina of which the materials were re-used: mighty walls joined by a drawbridge to the Towers of the Balio and, above the door, a plumbing place with the coat of arms of Charles V and a bifora.

The stream was born at the Pizzo di Lago (3,050 m) and descends through two glacial suspended valleys; the name derives from the fracta-water, water continuously interrupted by waterfalls, and the lowest jumps, double jumping, are the most beautiful. You can walk from Borgonuovo leaving the car at the entrance of the park; a panoramic path climbs the side with views of the waterfalls, the valley and Chiavenna. In summer meadows and pools at the foot of the waterfalls are frequented for the bathroom, with caution for current and slippery rocks.
The most precious place of art in the municipality.
A thousand-year-old abbey lost in the forest.
The main church of the village contains an eighteenth-century organ attributed to the Faithful and the relics of St. Servilian and St. Gualtiero.
The theater hidden between the buildings.

The Great Orange Bench n. 155 of the Big Bench Community Project of Chris Bangle, at the Alpe Pinalba at 1584 meters: views of the Piedmont Alps, the Monviso, Turin, the Monferrato, the rice fields between Vercellese and Biellese, the Moorish amphitheatre and the Serra d'Ivrea. You come in part by car and partly on foot: from San Giacomo, on the road Ivrea-Mombarone, about 30 minutes on an agro-silvo-pastoral road closed to the cars. Passport stamps in some country exercises.
Catalan Gothic in the heart of Barbagia.
Ibla's fifth stage.
Ring path of about 5 hours, traced in 1996 by the CAI of Bolzanoto, between the artificial basins of the Gorzente at the border with the Park of the Capanne of Marcarolo; bathing is not allowed.
On the old bulwarks of the village, with views of Barbaresco, Alba and the Alps.

Valtenesi municipality on the Lombard shore of Garda, made of hamlets on a small peninsula among olive trees, vines and cypresses; the Fortress of Manerba, with the remains of the castle destroyed in the sixteenth century and the natural archaeological park, looks to the Island of San Biagio, while under the waters of San Sivino there is a village of the Bronze World Heritage.

The municipality of the Stura Valley in a narrow valley, linked to partisan history: a popular museum combines the museum of war and resistance, the chestnut museum and the path marked towards Paraloup; on the rocky hill overlooks the parish church of San Michele, of Romanesque-Gothic origin.

Probably sixteenth-century tower with a square plan of about 9 meters on the side and 15 meters high, with three floors and terrace; in the eighteenth century belonged to the Marquis of Villabianca, whose marble coat of arms is on the south facade. The name comes from the ancient production of coal.
Reventino wool from thread to fabric.
The lower district, with narrow alleys.
The retablo of St. Christopher.
1,200 devices, from Marconi to digital.
The village of peperino degli Orsini and the Sacro Bosco 16th century populated with stone monsters, which inspired artists like Salvador Dalí.

Considered one of the most beautiful and important Baroque monuments of Trentino, imposing church of the center of which the Counts Lodron had the patronage, symbol of their political and religious power; its furnishings are now exhibited in the nearby Diocesan Museum, which organizes guided tours also to the church.
The Arab maze at the foot of Etna.
Contemporary art in a mountain village.
Alleys, arches and churches around the Farnesian fortress.
The Caetani's palace on the square.
Bacci Chapel by reservation only, contingent groups
The Colonna's home where Caravaggio hid.
A guard castle on the Candigliano valley.
The nature of the Madonie collected by a naturalist of the nineteenth century.
The symbol of the country's history.

Established in 1978, it protects about 900 hectares long almost 8 km of Sesia between the provinces of Vercelli and Novara: blades (mirrors of water born from abandoned branches of the river), gerbids on gravel and edges of the last woods of the plain, in the middle of the rice mill. In the special reserve of the Isolone di Oldenico nest egrets, herons ashes, cormorants and herons, observed from the perimeter and the huts; self-guided paths on foot and by bike all year round, with mountain bike rental at the Locanda delle Lama.
The unfinished baroque over the country.
€3 whole, €2 reduced
Rebuilt several times, it preserves the Romanesque structure of the façade; inside the Assunta by Lorenzo Lotto (1506) and an Assunta by Jacopo da Bassano.
The sea of the first pearl of the coast.
The Franciscan silence among the holm oaks.
The river of Rome begins here.
Architecture of the Renaissance in the middle of the lake.

Built in the second half of the sixteenth century for the Fieschi family, who lived there until 1856; it became a hydrotherapy plant that exploited an internal source. Restored in the late 1990s, it is now a historic residence used as a hotel, meetings, banquets and ceremonies. Info: Municipality, Service culture and tourism, tel. 010 9360103.
The Soratte explained in a Vignola palace.
The two triptychs.

A small town on the Gulf of Garda, with a pedestrian promenade of about 3 km, the late Dogotic Cathedral of Santa Maria Annunziata with works by Moretto, Romanino and Paolo Veneziano, the Palazzo della Magnifica Patria and the MuSa museum in the complex of Santa Giustina.

Complex of the Volpi district, on the right bank of the Solfrana stream: the nineteenth-century church reconstructs a building already incorporated in 1758 in the monastery wanted by the canon Nicola Petrone; damaged by the 1980 earthquake, it was reopened to worship in 2008. Impressive facade with large arched window between pilasters.

It is the most evocative part of the old town, with an octagonal well, next to the complex of the ancient Hospital managed by the Hospital Order of the Friars of San Jacopo, known from the second half of the 11th century as Knights of the Tau. Here the welcome to the pilgrims of the Via Francigena became a real medical hospitality with doctors and lay surgeons. In the square there is also the Sala Peregrinatio, exhibition space for contemporary art exhibitions.

Municipality of the lower Tronto valley along the Salaria, which takes its name from the Lama stream and the ancient castle; it preserves the nineteenth-century gardens of Villa Seghetti Panichi designed by Ludwig Winter, the eighteenth-century Villas of the Lama, Roman traces such as the cistern and the milestones and the collection of contemporary art            .
A city designed at a coffee table around the salt.
Church of the hamlet of Corona (Graun) in a late-Gothic style; on the bell tower a restored fresco of San Cristoforo. Patronage party on April 23rd.
A hiking destination among the larch trees.
The castle symbol of the Oltradige, with a view that reaches the Dolomites.
Nature and music on the lake.
Room with about 200 ancient musical instruments.
The medieval gate to the ancient city port, stop of the itineraries on the Rimini of the leaders and merchants.
Smile at the museum.
Nature and agricultural memory in an oasis cared for by volunteers.
Romanesque parish with the original Gothic arches, erected by Oderisius II around 1200.

Country of citrus groves at the foot of Montiferru, with the Romanesque Saint Paul, the parish church of San Sebastiano and the neoclassical Palazzo Boyl, seat of the Jewel Museum and Sardinian costume.

Ring of 8.4 km, about 3 hours and 300 meters of difference in altitude, easy/medium, from the parking lot of Camposilvano: touches the Valle delle Sfingi, the Buse di Sotto and Buse di Sopra alpine pastures, the Cross of the North, the Lausen refuge and the Gal Cross, to return next to the Covolo and the museum.
Partisan memory on the site of events.
The fortress that dominates the Lunigiana.
The city museum in a Longobard monastery.

Borgo della Barbagia at the foot of Monte Corrasi, the highest peak of the Supramonte, Orange Flag of Touring: historic center with the district of sa Maddalena and the church of Sant'Ignazio, the source of Su Gologone and the valley of Lanaittu with the village-sanctuary of Sa Sedda 'e sos Carros and the caves Sa Oche, Su Bentu and Corbeddu.

Until the 1940s, the most important solviferous center, today told in the museum of the zolfara of Villa Rose, the Victorian villa of English entrepreneurs; in the village the Mother Church of Santa Maria della Snow and the seventeenth-century church of San Matteo, in the territory the Sican settlement of Colle Madore.
The neoclassical lounge of the village.
Built by the Templars, it has a bell tower that originally was a military tower; two stone slabs bear the coat of arms of the Knights of Malta.
The 18th century processional statues.
The chapel of Francis inside the basilica.

Parish since the middle of the fifteenth century, several times renovated and consecrated in 1720; inside basilica with altar greater of 1785 and six altars in polychrome marble. On the main altar the canvas of 1606 by Felice Guarini, Grandpa of Francis, with the patron saint and the Madonna of Montevergine; by Francesco Guarini is the Madonna of Carmine. Open during the functions, open by reservation.
Hot sulphurous waters in the upper valley.
An intact Romanesque setting, with traces of the Roman temple on which it stands.
Old school.
A walk between castle and palaces.
Via Dante, Via Alberica and the streets and squares of the center, perfect for architecture, shops and aperitif.

Borgo sul Lago di Como known for the stone \"moltrasina" with the Romanesque Sant'Agata of the 11th century, the parish church of Saints Martin and Agata and historic villas like Villa Passalacqua, where Vincenzo Bellini stayed; four thematic routes (water, stone, history, panorama) cross the village.
Medieval village of Cilento perched on the Calore river, closed by walls with thirteen towers and a medieval bridge, entrance to the Gorges of the Calore, oasis of the otter.
The spa of the hamlet of Fratta Terme, about 5 km from Bertinoro.
Cumulation system museum €6, reduced €4,50
A painting of the Zoppo di Gangi.

Opened in 1931, in the fourth centenary, in the former Casa Battistini, on whose threshold according to the tradition Francesco Ferrucci was killed by Fabrizio Maramaldo at the Battle of Gavinana on August 3, 1530; re-established in 1957. It has 32 armored loans from the Bargello, 156 coins, documents and relics, a diorama of the battle, two paintings by Massimo d'Azeglio from the Brera Academy and costumes and flags of the historic Florentine Calcio; the Capanna di Ferrucci is part of it. In the square the equestrian statue of Ferrucci by Emilio Gallori; the Feruccian celebrations are held in the first ten days of August.
The star of Venice.
A hot outdoor bath under the village.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione between Langhe and Monferrato, with the porticoed street painted by Vincenzo Piccato and the panoramic tower of the Park of the Remembrance.
Panorama on the valley of the river Posada and on the beaches of San Giovanni.
The Romanesque of the fourteenth century in the high valley.

Former Franciscan monastery with frescoes from the middle of the seventeenth century attributed to Vincenzo Manenti and decorations in baroque stucco; VisitLazio indicates it as the stage not to be missed.

Built between 1674 and 1772 on the headland of the Guardia, it takes its name from an ancient tower of signaling today bell tower: remained unfinished, it is considered the most important baroque testimony of the area and has a remarkable major altar in black marble.
The 18th century bust of San Biagio.

In the abbey complex, dedicated to the history of the Via Francigena in Lunigiana: it houses a medieval pilgrim mannequin and a 14th-century column in local stone on the remains of a bell furnace of the 12th century. The route touches church, capitular hall, room of the sculptures of Oberto Ferlendi and cloister-garden, with coins, ceramics, capitals and a portal from the excavations of 2003 and the  "Gospel of stone" , capitals with winged dragons of Ferlendi.
Ovo Pinto's artist's eggs.
A Roman senatorial villa next to the highway.
The hall of the audience of the Mercanzia College, one of the two great medieval guilds housed in the Palazzo dei Priori.
Nineteenth-century church of the cimbrian village, next to the Trombone Museum.
The oldest church in the village, with frescoes.
Ruins and summer shows with views of the Vallagarina.
A baroque building of the 16th century; in the chapel of the Virgin there is a altarpiece painted in 1621 by Cristoforo Martinolio.
One of the most important medieval monuments in Abruzzo.

Country on the eastern shore of Lake Como, on a peninsula shaped like a cone, with lakefront, small beaches and the tower of the castle of Orezia; in the hamlet of Corenno Plinio, among the most beautiful villages of Italy, the castle-quench fourteenth century, the church of San Tommaso di Canterbury and the arches of the counts Andreani.
On the trail of Santa Rita's life.

The Bishop's Palace (1560) has a late Renaissance façade with the coat of arms of the Baron bishop; the Governor's Palace (16th century) has three balconies and Renaissance decorations; in the village also the houses of the Pepe and Cenci families and Lagravinese palace.
Lunch at the market like the Modenas.
14th century church with important frescoes and a marble tabernacle of the 16th century.
The village rises on a high ridge at about 900 meters that dominates the territory and marks the northern limit of the Calanchi; from here start excursions to the nearby woods.
In Prabanta, two neolithic domus de Janas (3200-2800 BC) related to the popular character of Luxia Arrabiosa and the menhir Su Furconi.

Two lakes north of the city: the Great Alimini, brackish and once connected to the Adriatic, with Mediterranean maquis and sand, and the Small Alimini or Fontanelle, fed by fresh water sources, with marsh vegetation and rare plants such as the water chestnut and swamp orchids; the bay of Alimini has low and transparent seabeds.
Eight mills in chain between Brengon and Clou, fed by a small stream and connected by a path.

It rises on the top of the upper torrent Terdobbio, a place of worship with Celtic, Roman (are and epigraph) and Christian traces. The Romanesque system was modified in the Baroque age in the seventeenth century; it houses canvases by B. Fields and G.B. Tassinari, the cantoria del Fiammenghino, other paintings of the Pavese school and two side chapels baroque frescoes.
One of the bastions of the walls, built during the Sienese rule and completed in 1345.
Trecentesque and sixteenth century frescoes dedicated to the Virgin.

Built in 1317 by Castruccio Castracani in stone and river pebbles instead of a Romanesque bridge on the border between Pistoia and Lucca, he climbs over the Lima with a single arch with a donkey back without batteries, from which the name of Ponte del Deavolo. On the banks of the Bell Mill (XVIII-XIX century) and on the other side the Old Customs between Pistoia and Lucca; you can reach from Lolle or Popiglio.
Paolo da Visso and Boccati in a country church.
The museum of the city museums.
The ruins of a forgotten palace.

Museum of art in nature a few kilometers from the Terme di Comano: a ring path signposted in the woods, with works on the theme of the refuge made of natural materials, from traditional wood carvings to avant-garde installations. The path is easy, accessible to all (OPEN mark for accessible tourism), with benches and fountains, and has a children's path, the Path of the little Walkers.
accessible only the ground floor according to the Municipality

Città dei Gonzaga surrounded by the lakes of Mincio, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Sabbioneta: the Doge's Palace with the Chamber of the Spouses of Mantegna, Palazzo Te di Giulio Romano, the Basilica of Sant'Andrea di Leon Battista Alberti, the Round of San Lorenzo and the Theatre Bibiena where young Mozart played.

The center is dominated by the Arch of Porta Nuova. The Palazzo Comunale, historically Palazzo della Ragione (1502), has a porch and tower and is the work of Pietro Antonio Maggi, who also designed the nearby Palazzo dell'ex Monte di Pietà.

Inaugurated in 2003, it collects objects, documents and photographs of the First World War on the Ortles-Cevedale front, recovered at altitude or donated by private: weapons, uniforms, a kitchen, a first aid place, a trenches tabernacle with portable altar and the cart of the cable car recovered in Punta Linke; with the Stelvio Park organizes evenings and excursions on the places of war.

The village, on a rocky spur above the river Aulella near the river Tassonaro, developed in the fifteenth century around a castle of which remain a cylindrical tower and few sections of walls.
