The name derives from the Roman term "Casuli" (Casuli), which was linked to Fivizzano from the fifteenth century to the nineteenth century, passed to the Duchy of Modena in 1841 and to the province of Massa and Carrara in 1859.
part of the signs damaged by vandalism: bring a map
Fortress with pentagonal plan, today preserved only in remains, in the citadel on the hill overlooking the historic center; in the courtyard stands the church of Sant'Aldebrando.
A fresco from the early sixteenth century in a Romanesque church.
The highest point, with a view up to the Tiber springs.

The Romanesque-Norman cathedral commissioned by Robert Guiscardo on a early Christian church built on a Roman temple, consecrated by Gregory VII; in the baroque crypt the relics of St. Matthew, patron saint celebrated on September 21.

A castle in lava stone documented from the IX century, already Benedictine abbey, Farnese, Luciano Bonaparte and Torlonia; the museum tells the Etruscan-Roman city with the findings of the necropolis.
From Stafal start the ski tours to Punta Gnifetti (4459 m) and Capanna Regina Margherita; in summer excursions to lakes, huts and panoramic points such as Sant'Anna.
Cemetery church on a hill outside the center, built on the ruins of a pagan temple and cited in a document by Frederick I of 1163.
Former vote after the outbreak of 1630, dedicated to the saints Fabiano, Sebastiano and Rocco.

The hilly village of the Nebrodi overlooking the valley and the sea, with the seaside hamlet of Castel di Tusa; in the territory there are the ancient Sicilian-Greek town of Halaesa Arconidea and the first work of the Fiumara d'arte, "La materia potre non essere" by Pietro Consagra.
The first Valdostana dairy.
Nature and birds along a sesia bend.
The treasure of the Collegiate House between English alabasters and Neapolitan silvers.
The deepest cave in Puglia.
The hidden village and the altar of Juvarra.
Traditional customs and sacred art of the parish.
A village with a Ligurian air in Piedmont.
Fortilizio dei Nicelli with loggia in Bramaino, 440 meters; it is believed to be of the tenth century, but the first written documents date back to the fifteenth century.
The oldest Romanesque church in the country.

After the demolition of the walls, since 1887, new blocks and avenues arose: Piazza Garibaldi was prolonged during the Vittoria and in 1925 was completed Viale dei Tigli, with Liberty style villas, the former National Opera Balilla and public baths of 1924; the former racetrack of 1895 became an urban park with the monument to Vittorio Emanuele II.
The cycle of frescoes of the thirteenth century.

The castle on a fortification of the 10th century, the Falletti since 1325 and purchased by the municipality in 1970, hosts since 2010 WiMu, one of the most innovative wine museums in the world, and the Regional Winery.

Posada is one of the four municipalities of the park, recognized by UNESCO as a Biosphere Reserve, with paths between forests, springs, lagoons and dunes for trekking, mountain biking and horse riding; the final stretch of the Posada river, can be traced back in kayak, forms canals and ponds like that of San Giovanni, frequented by Italian knights and pink flamingos.
The seaside village with the port with the eyes of a cat.

The centre is surrounded by medieval houses, Renaissance palaces and stone portals with Latin coats of arms and mottos; the square is surrounded by buildings from the 15th and 16th centuries, including Palazzo dei Priori, Palazzo dei Governatori (XIII century) and Palazzo Varano (1516).

From the right side, for Frais, the paths go up to the Gran Serin, military fortress of 1897 at 2589 meters overlooking a glacial lake, and to the Ciantiplagna (2849 m), highest point of the municipality, along a panoramic former military road towards the Colle delle Finestre and the Testa dell'Assietta. In summer, in the Rhododendrons, alpine stars, gentian, arnica and genepì; among the fauna of chamois, deer, roe deer and marmots.
The medieval heart of hospitality on the Via Francigena.
Rooms where the good pope grew.

The historic beach vecia is located in the western part of the island between port and lagoon, among the first stretches used for bathrooms: it alternates free stretches and establishments (Tivoli, Piper, Keywest, Côte d'Azur), with backdrops that descend faster and a seafront of locals overlooking the lagoon.
Barbagia's most enigmatic hysteriad menhir.
The country of the Serchio Valley is famous for the Devil's Bridge and the Halloween Festival.
Fortified town founded in 1564 for Cosimo I de' Medici, with a belt of over 2 km and the large gun square.
Church of the historic center with facade and stone bell tower.
The highest point of Squillace, with a wide view of the gulf.
Arbëreshë costumes and golds.
Paths and fishing in the woods.
Two walled villages of the Maremma.
Bluefin tuna at the source.
River nature and a medieval village in one walk.
The mountain wine of Val Venosta, on foot among the rows.
A few kilometres from the capital, the village where Giovannino Guareschi was born, with his birthplace, the sixteenth-century church of San Martino and the Circolo Giovannino Guareschi.

Discovered in the 1930s and excavated since 2002 by the mission of the University of Tokyo, the villa was buried by the eruption of 472 A.D. (Pollena's) The believed statue of Augustus is a Dionysus with a puppy of panther; monolithic columns in marble of Asia Minor, white mosaics, apses with tritons and nereids and a wine cell with over thirty dolias. On site there are copies: the originals are at the Archaeological Museum of Nola.
The parish church reborn after the earthquake.
The small church of the valley consecrated by Cusano.
The highest village of Procida, overlooking the Gulf of Naples.
€1 symbolic offer

The municipality of Val Maremola is about three kilometers from the sea of Pietra Ligure, with the hamlets of Bardino Vecchio and Bardino Nuovo, aggregate in 1928; in Bardino Nuovo the Museum of Tower Clock G.B. Bergallo, the first museum of the kind in Italy, and around six-seventeenth-century churches, the ruins of the castle of the Folchi and a network of paths between olive groves and woods.
The town hall, by Ernesto Basile in Art Nouveau style.

Medieval castle fortified with walls and towers, whose remains are embedded in the houses of the center. In 1564 the fief was entrusted to Giulio Vitelli, who became a Marquis; the name derives from "bucina" (a fishing net or hunting net that appears in the coat of arms). The village, of the counts Guidi di Modigliana, was placed in 1225 under the protection of Arezzo and was taken by force by the Tarlati around 1325.

Forca di Presta, at 1,550 m at the foot of Monte Vettore on the border between Marche and Umbria, offers in winter 25 km of cross-country skiing and ski touring slopes and ski lifts; in Forca Canapine, at 1,541 m, there are other skiing facilities on the border between the two regions.
The Gran Sasso above the village.
The hamlet of the extaturation is grossetana.

Reserve of about 257 hectares established in 1987 between Predosa, Bosco Marengo, Capriata d'Orba and Casal Cermelli, also ZSC and SPA: riparian woods of willows and poplars, oaks, small grets and arid prairies on the first terraces, between fields and poplars. There are reported more than 200 species of birds, blooms protected as snowshoe and orchids, the dragonfly Oxygastra curtisii and the return of the wolf; the visitor center with ornithological museum is in the municipal mill of Bosco Marengo. Dogs only on a leash.

Villa of the late seventeenth century attributed to the architect Frigimelica Roberti; it houses the civic library and the interiors are open to visitors. Here the Dal Lago Museum opened to the public in 1995, before the transfer to Palazzo Festari.
€2, reduced €1,50

Country of Irpinia at 742 meters, overlooking the valley of the Ufita and crossed by the Tratturo Pescasseroli-Candela, destroyed and rebuilt several times after the earthquakes of 1694 and 1930; to visit the multimedia museum of transhumance, the Municipal Museum and the church of Santa Maria Assunta. On August 27, for St. John the Baptist, the Giglio drags along the streets with ropes, obelisk of straw woven about 28 meters high.
A fifteenth-century church on the banks of the Musestre.

Probably built between the 8th and the 10th century, rebuilt around 1536 and in 1906 by the will of the archpriest Antonio Gardin; it is reached on foot from the last stretch of Via San Vettore or from Forcella Mostaccin, along the path of the two Rocks.
In front of Palazzo Chigi on Piazza di Corte, with its large dome, it is one of the last masterpieces of Gian Lorenzo Bernini, who drew every detail, including furnishings.

In the middle of the Gulf of Poets, the city chosen by Cavour for the Arsenale della Marina: the Castle of San Giorgio with the stele statues, the Via del Prione and its museums, the Morin promenade on the sea and the rationalist cathedral of Adalberto Libera, with the Sunsets and Monesteroli on the hills towards the Cinque Terre.
Didactic route with sixteen thematic islands to discover the nature of the territory.
Bozen from the top between palm trees and olive trees.
One of the oldest churches in the valley.
The oldest Romanesque.
The Navy story.
The parish church commissioned by San Carlo, with works from San Lucio.
One of the most significant monuments in Val Trebbia.

One of the locations of the Museo Territorio (Territoir Museum) .The Faces of the Ubagu della Valle Arroscia. The museum in the village, in six sections with panels, photos, maps and reconstructions, tells the history and traditions of chestnut in the communities of the Ligurian hinterland: tree botany, ethnographic uses, techniques of processing and conservation; it closes with the real section of a millennial trunk and a video. The open-air path continues with the restored stone dryer ('canissu', used in Valle Arroscia from the eighteenth century to the mid-Twentieth century), two rebuilt charcoals (one whole, one sectioned) with the coal barn, and ends in a chestnut grove.

In the Centre \"Aldo Gorfer" , in rooms with stone vaults: tools for fields, viticulture, breeding and processing of milk , lumberjack , carpenter and barrel , with the reconstruction of stable , cave and open kitchen of a farmhouse .
Remains of the Capitolium foundations under Piazza delle Erbe (civic 38) and the curia with a cult complex in alley Corticella San Marco 3, preserved inside private premises.

The heart of the center, overlooking the Cathedral and the Municipal Palace with the Venetian Loggia erected in 1610 on a project by the architect Lantana. The fountain with Hercules that crushes the Hydra is a marble copy of the work of Antonio Carra and Cesare Vischietti (1593-1595); the original restored is on the staircase of the Town Hall. In the square also the Grand Caffè Liberty, and in the city numerous Liberty residences.

City of Lombard textiles: the Renaissance shrine of Santa Maria di Piazza with the polyptych of Gaudenzio Ferrari, the basilicas of San Giovanni and San Michele, Palazzo Marliani Cicogna, the Social Theatre on the model of the Scala and the liberty villas of the industrial age.

It develops among the narrow streets of the hamlet Vernetti, at the Locanda Ceaglio: photographs and tools of the past tell the peasant life and the labors of the ancestors. Always visitable, but it is better to check first (tel. +39 0171 998117).
Routes in the underground of the city with guided tours reported by the Ministry of Culture.
Founded after the earthquake destroyed the old center of Briatico Vecchia, it preserves remains of other churches lost.
Along the main street of the village.
The commercial lounge of the old town.

A cylindrical tower 23 meters high, with an external diameter of about 13 meters and walls of more than 3 meters at the base, dating from 1116 to 1122 thanks to a parchment of the treasure of the Cathedral of Troy; one of the few traces of the Byzantine walls and buildings. Restored, it houses cultural spaces and the small ethnographic museum; the municipality indicates free access.
The ancient neighborhood between two hills of the Treviso Alps, with the cathedral of Santa Maria Nova surrounded by medieval alleys and buildings.

A plain park created to safeguard the network of fountains and springs of the Tormo, which was born from the Roggia Murata in Arzago d'Adda and flows into the Adda in Abbadia Cerreto, in a landscape marked by the ancient morphological escarpments of the river Adda.
Ring path in the park on the life of the community: hydraulic mill, former school, municipal oven of the village Oulme, charcoal, lime furnace, nineteenth century ice-cakehouse and smoked sauna.
Picnic and views to Segesta.

Country of the Biellese that rises from 600 to more than 2000 meters up to the Mombarone, to the borders with Canavese and Valle d'Aosta; it is known for the seventeenth-century Sanctuary of the Madonna of Loreto, with the octagonal dome 38 meters high and the perspectives of Fabrizio Galliari, and for the churches of the center such as the parish church of Santa Fede and the confraternity of Santa Croce.
The first residence of the Este.

Maybe from the Angevin era, enlarged by various feudal lords and summer residence of the Marquises De Marinis; after the earthquake of 1893 it was remodeled on three floors and, damaged by the earthquake of 1980, restored between 1987 and 1990. Since 1995 it has again hosted municipal offices.
The view of the entire coast of Chia.

Ancient seaport of Alessano, where the ruins of a watchtower remain; Torre Novaglie is still known on the Rio Canal. Near Punta Rossa there is the Blue Grotto, while south of Novaglie the Cipollian and Prazziche caves, neolithic stations, are reachable only from the sea.
Another stop in the footsteps of Mattia Preti.
The artificial lake of Mugello, where you can swim and there are restaurants with views at sunset.
Aversa's last noble seat.
In the Hospital of the Infirms of the eighteenth century, the story of the delta from prehistory to the Middle Ages and the entire cargo of a Roman ship found near Comacchio.
€5, reduced €3,50; guided tour €7
A place of the memory of the high Valmarecchia.
A ridge castle with over a thousand years of history.
Megalithic tombs in the Murgia landscape.
The Fortress of Ariosto and the Orlando Furious multimedia.
The pulpit outside the corner of the facade, carved by Donatello and Michelozzo in 1433-1438 for the exhibition of the Sacred Cingolo; the original reliefs are in the Museum of the Opera.
Byzantine frescoes in the open air.

The water village in Valle Antigorio: the cold sources from which the Crodino was born, the national museum of mineral waters at the Parco delle Terme, the central of Verampi designed by Piero Portaluppi, the parish church of Santo Stefano with the bell tower of 1026 and the stone churches of Cravegna and Salera among the woods.
The fort against the city.
Sanctuary of the Filippini Fathers built in 1586.
Where the Parmesan was born.

Marine education center with 22 tanks for about 20,000 liters that recreate the habitats of the protected sea: posidonia, starfish, hedgehogs, octopus, groupers, moray eels and jellyfish, with tactile tub, children's workshop and multimedia room.
Elegant Walser resort of the Lys Valley, Orange Flag since 2017, vacation of Queen Margherita at the foot of Mount Rosa.
The Mothers of Capua.

Valley of the Toscolano stream where it is made paper from the Middle Ages: in the Quattro-Cinquecento it was the main paper centre of the Republic of Venice and the last paper mill closed in 1962. The paths pass through the ruins of the paper mills and descend to the Greto; the most spectacular point is the walkway on the gorge of the Covoli.
The place of prayer of the poet.
From the thirteenth century, the oldest church in the city, on the square with Palazzo Gromo di Ternengo.
The oldest sanctuary in Selinunte.
A path through boulders of the main rock types of the Valdostane mountains, surrounded by shrubs and tall trees, accessible by the stroller.
It takes its name from an ancient church dedicated to San Michele Arcangelo, where the ancient Palazzo Caracciolo is still visible.
A craft of art handed down.

Borgo dei Monti Lepini on a hill among the woods, Flag Arancione, home of Aldo Manuzio: the walls of the Caetani, the Museum of Scriptures in the Palazzo Caetani, the Collegiate Church of Sant'Erasmo and the Cave of Selvascura.
The largest beach in Calasetta, suitable for children.
A dirt track follows the river southwards: the first about 3 km you can drive or mountain bike, the rest on foot on the gravel bed, between poplars and willows, with blackbirds and fishermen martins.
Documented from 1224 and renovated in the sixteenth century, with hanging gardens.

The palace extended in 1634 on a project by Bartolomeo Avanzani, today seat of the Military Academy, with the Courtyard of Honor and the State apartments. The guided tour includes the Military Academy Museum, with weapons, relics, flags, uniforms and drums.
Giant bench built in 2024 to admire the surrounding landscape.
discordant times: the MiC tab indicates closed every day with extraordinary openings on request (tel. 0721 723263) and ticket office 8-18

Church built before the year 1000 in panoramic position on the lake and the valley, on top of Mount San Zeno; collapsed in 1956 for a lightning, it has been rebuilt since 1996. The ascent is marked by the stations of the Via Crucis made by the Alps with railway sleepers; inside a copy of the Corona Ferrea.
An entire country transformed into an art gallery.

The first nucleus dates back to the 11th century; it preserves works of art, a library of the 16th century, a permanent nativity scene and a necropolis ossuary. Under the abbey a museum complex is spread over three floors.

Borgo della Val Vibrata among hills and olive groves, Città dell'Olio and land of DOC and DOCG wines celebrated by the Wine Festival. The historic centre is dominated by the brick tower of 1370, the only trace of the castle of Corata, next to the Doge's Palace; outside the walls the church of the Madonna delle Grazie and the chapel of the Icon, and in Via San Giuseppe the Museum of peasant civilization in Val Vibrata.
An ancient church with a Baroque face.

The city of Quintana in the Umbra Valley, in plain and straight streets: Palazzo Trinci with the frescoes of Gentile da Fabriano, the Cathedral of San Feliciano and, in the mountains, the plateau and the marsh of Colfiorito and the abbey of Sassovivo.
Walk on the Appia between holes, theater and statues of a Roman city.
The last district of Rome (1921), with Piazza Cavour, the Palazzo di Giustizia called "Palazzaccio," the Valdese Temple of 1914 and the shopping of Via Cola di Rienzo.
The Mediterranean scrub on the sea.

Rococo church of 1740 with late Baroque façade and two symmetrical bell towers, with a Greek cross plan; it houses an Assumption attributed to Niccolò di Liberatore called the pupil or to his school and the "Madonna del Perugino" commissioned in the seventeenth century by the Perugino Francesco Caffarelli.
Sicilian capital in the Golden Conca, with the Arab-Norman UNESCO Heritage itinerary, the baroque of the popular districts and the historical markets of Ballarò and Vucciria.
Green basin of meadows and orchards at 960 meters, home of the Fontina DOP seasoned in the rock of an ancient copper mine.

Rebuilt several times, the current church was designed by Domenico Spotorno and consecrated in 1688, on the remains of a church wanted by woman Violante Carroz, Marquis of Quirra. Baroque façade between two twin bell towers united by a balaustrate porch and 36 meters high dome; inside a Latin cross painted with the stories of Saints Peter and Paul, a rare crucifix of the fourteenth century and an organ \"ad ala Â" of Roman school, the oldest preserved in Sardinia.
A Sunday market with almost six centuries of history.
The villa-jewel of the FAI overlooking the lake.
Inaugurated in 1923 as the Park of Remembrance and requalified in 2019, they are a place of memory and recreation.
The Renaissance along the course.
Remains of the watchtower along the coast, known as the tower of Capo Spulico or Torre Spaccata.
The ancient rural village.
Church with graceful shapes in the upper part of the city; from the square the look ranges over the city, the plain of Pinerol and the Valdesi Valleys.
the Municipality lists it among the accommodation facilities (B&B and venue of events): visitable only on special occasions

The public park Teresio Oleveli, in front of Villa Mainona, has a panoramic terrace-darsena. Not far from the municipal park of Villa Mayer, a 19th century villa damaged by a fire in 1919 and renovated by the rationalist architect Pietro Lingeri, recreates the Italian garden of Villa Colonna in Rome.
A washroom still in operation.
It collects ethnographic material on traditions, superstitions and arts of Matese's agro-pastoral culture, with attention to the different models of the traditional women's costume of Letino.
In the hall of the Town Hall there is the bust of André Massena, appointed by Napoleon Duke of Rivoli, donated to the community in 1902 by the grandson of the general.
The most romantic garden in Vomero.
The caves inhabited by the ancient Ligurians.

Built between 1471 and 1480 on a design by Giovanni Battagio, with neo-Gothic façade by Edoardo Arborio Mella built in 1877; it houses canvases by Malosso (S. Lucia, 1585), the chapel of the Rosary with a table by Altobello Melone and frescoes rediscovered in 1975 attributed to Agostino Pesenti, the presbytery with frescoes by Robert De Longe on the life of San Lorenzo and a Crucifix of the Chiaveghino (1594).

What remains of the complex of the Oratorians in Borgo Vecchio, rebuilt between 1706 and 1713; Baroque interior with stuccoes, polychrome wooden statues and illusionistic frescoes of the brothers Pozzo and Milocco, the canvas of the Visitation of Sebastiano Taricco (1682), Crucifix and Immaculate of the Luganese sculptor Carlo Giuseppe Plura. Guided tours by reservation at the Tourist Office.

The main church of the village, decorated with mural paintings.
The bridges of the ancient marble railway that carried the blocks from the quarries to the port, along the road that goes up to the basins.
The frescoes of Ottaviano Nelli.
Etruscan tombs carved in a fossil bottom.
A descent through flowery meadows and farms with the Dolomites around.
Small museum with an atmosphere of the late nineteenth century in the heart of Villa Borghese.

Documented since 1006, when Count Pietro Attone of Todi founded a monastery there: walls, ogival gate, well, triangular mast and remains of dwellings, fortifications strengthened by Perugia in 1310 against Henry VII. Nearby the fifteenth-century remains of the emissary built by Braccio Fortebraccio da Montone (Lord of Perugia 1416-1424) to regulate the lake, renovated in 1896.

In the old church of San Bortolo is exhibited the collection of trombini, heavy firearms derived from the archibugi of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, born as weapons of defense and become a festive instrument for celebrations, commemorations and festivals; St. Bortolo keeps alive the tradition of shooting. Ancient specimens, decorated and carved, with films and projections. Open from 1 April to 30 September on Sundays and holidays 10-12 and 15-18.30; from October to March and in weekdays only by appointment for groups of at least 10 people.

The village preserves houses in red trachite with Aragonese-style windows and basalt ornaments, and artisan workshops of cork carving, leather processing and blacksmiths. At Carnival the masks sos Corriolos animate the rites with a bonfire in the central square; at the end of September the festival Licanias is dedicated to rural landscapes.
The tower of the Rangons in the heart of the country.

Nuraghe of mixed type, to corridor and tholos, probably a protonuraghe transformed in successive phases: the central tower leans on a trilobed bastion and a staircase leads directly to the second level, from which you go up to the main hall to the third. Around the remains of a village of circular huts and, about 100 meters, a tomb of the giants and another tomb with a small dolmen.
Agricultural and industrial center about 8 km north of Reggio Emilia, with the fourteenth-century Torrazzo dei Gonzaga, the Art Nouveau theatre in Piazza Garibaldi and the Romanesque Pieve Rossa.
The Cimini Lake.
Memory patch.
The bay under Monte Monaco.
A fine sand and a walk on the dam.

Open-air jasper mine discovered in 1987 and excavated by the Superintendence between 1988 and 1995, exploited between the 4th and 2nd millennium B.C. (Radiocarbon indicates about 2920-1890 B.C.): the quarryers were made semi-finished for tools in splintered stone, especially arrowheads. The archaeological and naturalistic path shows the extraction surfaces as they were left, two quarry areas and two shelters with splinters, percussors and fragments of ceramic. Tel. 0187 845617.
In the old town, it houses a wooden statue of the Madonna and Child of about 1700; heir of a parish church of the same name of Byzantine age, in use until the late 18th century.
Parish church built in the mid-18th century, inspired by the church of San Fedele in Milan.

The ancient Capua, one of the most powerful cities of the peninsula from the Osci to the Middle Ages: the Amphitheatre of Campania, second in size to the Colosseum, the Frescoed Mitreus and the museum of the ancient Capua.
The shrine of the village.
€16 full day, €19 with reservation; €22 with Boboli and Bardini; €2 from 18 to 25 years EU; free under 18

Documented since 1406, renovated in Baroque forms in 1670 and set on fire by French troops in 1793; three times cruising on pillars, the patron's altarpiece between the statues of Saints George, Florian and two bishops, and the Fourteen Saints Helpers in small niches.
The place to understand one of the most atrocious Nazi massacres in Italy.
The largest rose collection in the world in private hands.
The convent in the woods above the village.
Oratory of the hamlet Penicina dedicated to the Madonna di Caravaggio, with a Pisan-style facade with alternating bands of bricks and sandstone; the pillars date back to the 16th century.
The ascent to the hill.

The cultural association Castrum Saliceti accompanies, only by reservation (season 2026, Sunday at 15), the Church of San Lorenzo, the Confraternita di Sant'Agostino and the Church of San Martino in the village Lignera.
The Romanesque church of the village; in the village also the parish church of Saints Quirico and Julitta with three aisles, the Madonna of Loreto and San Rocco.
A story of prisons and Garibaldi.
The prologue to the Sacred Mount.
Wellness in the hills.

Ossario inaugurated in 1951 that preserves over 900 corpses: the soldiers of the renewed Italian army fallen in the first battle against the Germans (8-16 December 1943) between the gorges of Mignano and the slopes of Mount Long, and the fallen of the war of Liberation (1943-1945) collected by war cemeteries of the peninsula; it is the only military shrine dedicated to this war. The attached museum reconstructs the phases of the battle and the Italian participation in Liberation with weapons, allied and German relics and photographs. Summer time 8:30-17:15, winter 8:30-15:45.
The frescoes by Bernardino Campi saved from the oratory of the castle.
The merchants' street.
Romanesque church, the only surviving structure of the ancient Benedictine complex; the ancient watchtower has become bell tower.

The Old Prisons district is the only medieval remnant that survived the earthquake of 1693, with narrow alleys, ancient houses and caves; from a Byzantine church starts a path of tombs and caves. Here and in the popular districts of Castelverde and Calanconi the doors preserve the "iattaruala" , hole for cats, and the "justieddu" , peephole to see without being seen.

Born from the initiative of a group of young people with the support of the Superintendence of the Antiquities of Turin and the Municipality, it exhibits in chronological order finds of the area: from the culture of Golasecca of the Iron Age (cinerary urns, bronze fibulas, funeral kits; the first showcase shows the evolution of the urn from biconic to ovoid) to the first Roman finds. It is located on the first floor of Villa Soranzo, with entrance from the municipal seat. Not indicated hours: information to the Municipality, tel. 0321 95355.
Walk through the oasis.
The door of the alchemists.
The suspended village, postcard of the Maira Valley.
Where the oldest flying reptile in the world was found.

Built between 1597 and 1623 according to design by Giovanni Guerra, with bell tower erected between 1884 and 1902 on a project by Francesco Vespignani and surmounted by a copper Redeemer; organ of Gaetano Callido (1783) and crypt of bishops.
The tower has been integrated since the year about 1000, built by Abbot Ugo I to defend the Abbey of Farfa; it offers views of the surrounding countries.

It is a ring of 6.8 km, about 3 hours and 290 meters of difference in altitude, suitable for families: from the Vuseum the path 18 climbs to the archaeological site of Ganglegg, with settlements of the Bronze and Iron Age; then the path 17 along the Leitenwaal Roggia to the gorge and the descent on the Berkwaal (17A) passing under Castel Coira, to the station. Water has been flowing in the streams since April.
Small lake at 2583 meters next to the refuge Green Lake, reachable in about 2 hours and 20 minutes from Bout du Col or 3 hours and 20 minutes from Ghigo.
About 500 metres from the village, the site preserves the graptolites, rare fossils of the Paleozoic.
Here in February 1797 the Treaty of Tolentino was signed between Napoleon Bonaparte and the Papal State.

An unknown castle, with damage and destruction documented in the 13th century; the Marazzani bought it in 1453. Today of the Petrelli family, it is an organic farm with educational farm, orchard and vegetable garden; the visit includes the square tower, the tower in the Water, the courtyards, the church of Santa Maria (cappella of the IX century), the peasant museum and the moat. In May and October it hosts the exhibition "Frutti del Castello" on ancient varieties. It is part of the Castles of the Duchy of Parma, Piacenza and Pontremoli.
18th century palace in front of the Duomo, with Roman epigraphs along the wall of the staircase of honour.
One of the oldest known prints on paper.
The Greek walls best preserved.
The book house.
In the footsteps of merchants between Italy and Switzerland.

The highest municipality in the Stura Valley (1,650 m), on the border with France: in Ferriere the house-museum of smuggler, in Bersezio the medieval church of San Lorenzo, and in altitude the lakes of Roburent and the Lake of Maddalena on the homonymous hill.

The medieval and sixteenth-century walls preserve three towers and the only surviving door, the Door of Fossato or Water. The castle is a sixteenth-century fortress with circular tower and walls on a hill south of the village, behind Sant'Andrea; it is privately owned and can be seen from the outside. Tradition has it that underground passages to the beach and the Annunziata depart from here.
The women of Valcellina and their mountain.
The central square where seven streets converge, with Palazzo Grimaldi-Serra seat of the town hall; you arrive there from the Baroque Porta del Sole.
Natural terrace between the Trasimeno and the valley of the Nestore: the village walled on three squares, with the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano del Perugino and the tradition of embroidery on tulle.

Built from the end of the 12th century on the side of Mount Taleo in custody of the cave where St. Benedict lived as a hermit for three years: two churches entirely painted over, the statue of the saint in prayer by Antonio Raggi, pupil of Bernini (1657), and in the chapel of St. Gregory the oldest known portrait of St. Francis, painted when he was still alive, without aureole or stigmata. Petrarch called it the threshold of Paradise.
The Catalan Gothic of Marmilla.

Borgo Irpino del grano e della pietra, Fontanarosa is famous for the 28-metre straw obelisk pulled every 14 August in honor of Our Lady of Mercy: the cart is told in the Civic Museum of Popular Craftsmanship, next to the Shrine of Mercy and the Church of St. Nicholas.
Traditional accessories, costumes and amulets.
18th-century bridge over the Varaita stream, overlooking the village.
The arch that opens via Crociferi and joins the two sectors of the homonymous female monastery: according to legend it was built in one night.

Protected area since 1996 on the Umbrian-Marche Apennines, includes the municipalities of Costacciaro, Scheggia and Pascelupo, Fossato di Vico and Sigillo: meadows, woods, beech woods, gorges like that of the Rio Freddo towards Pascelupo, high springs and a large reservoir of water fed by rains. The summit of Monte Cucco can be reached by car or on foot on marked paths; excursions suitable for everyone, even for children, as well as caving and hang gliding.
The lounge of the knife town.
The cradle of the Renaissance, UNESCO's historic heritage center since 1982. With the Firenze Card you enter almost all the museums of the city and the Metropolitan City.
in July and August quota access, only with guide and reservation at the Park offices (dates indicated by the source referring to 2016)
The Roman temple overlooking the Pontina plain, beautiful at sunset.
The little church of the pilgrims on the Francigena.

The municipality of Soveratese sullo Ionio, with a hilly historical centre born in the IX century to escape the Saracen pirates and the hamlet of Isca Marina, where stretching 4 km of fine sand; in the village the Museum of the instruments of the popular music of Calabria preserves over 60 traditional instruments.
The wild side of the peninsula.
The medieval maze dug into the tuff.
Twenty-one Roman arches.
The hilly side of Castiglione.

The restoration of 2000 brought to light an oculus of an earlier 11th century Romanesque church; in the 17th century the building was completely renovated. The painting with the martyrdom of the saint is by Rocco Pittaco.
The place of a page of the Risorgimento.
16th century castle, indicated as one of the best preserved in the area, which preserves furnishings from different eras.
Cambiaso and the polyptychs.
Get into the mine on the miners' train.

Called in a provocative way to a multifaceted figure lived in Scordia in the first half of the nineteenth century, it presents a material documentation of the history of the place and its inhabitants. Open from Monday to Friday 8.30-12.30, Wednesday also 14.30-19.30; closed Saturday and Sunday (tel. +39 095 7935921).

The South Milan Agricultural Park protects about 6.3 km2, more than half of the municipal territory: the whole area south of the Tangenziale is agricultural, dotted with farmsteads and crossed by rogge. Buccinasco is entirely in the area of the fountains and is among the municipalities of the province with several active fountains (Bazzanella, Carchena, Nosotto, Molinetto, Campociocco, Melzi, Marozzi, Visconti and the wet area of the Castle); south of the Tangenziale there is also Lake Santa Maria, excavated in 1966 for the West Tangenziale and stop of migratory birds.
The hand of the "Pacem" in Terris in the cast of Manzù.
The 360 degree view of Lake Iseo.

Recognizable for the large drum dome and the pyramidal bell tower, the sanctuary was almost entirely rebuilt in the twentieth century on the site of a more ancient church dedicated to the Saint from the seventeenth century, when he became patron saint of Cocullo. Here the most heard rituals of the feast take place: the faithful take stone from behind the altar to spread around houses and fields and pull with their teeth the rope of the bell against the toothache; after the mass the statue is decorated with live golds and snakes and carried in procession.
The civil genius construction site on the river.
The village of Gian Domenico Cassini, Orange Flag, with the municipal astronomical observatory, the museum dedicated to the astronomer and the sanctuary oriented on the Ligurian .
The Romanesque angels of the highest abbey in Europe.
Among the alleys of the old town women still prepare by hand orecchiette, the typical Apulian pasta, one of the traditions to be observed walking.
The church of the family of Sixtus V.
Park in the direction of Riesi with hiking, running and tennis and a kiosk.
Up the Varrone towards the Pizzo Tre Signori.
Marian Shrine of Our Lady of Reggio, Virgin of Adoration, dedicated in 1946.

15th century mill, restored (last intervention in 2004) and part of the Ecomuseum of the Friulian Dolomites Lis Aganis: on the ground floor a small forge-falegnameria for repairs and the hall with Hungarian millstones and roller mills, on the upper floor the machines to work cereals and the turret with sieves to separate the flours. It housed the Madonna della Misericordia del Pordenone (1524-1527), since 1957 at the Civic Museum of Conegliano; today there is a work by Vittorio Basaglia. Visits on request with reservation required (tel. 0434 749622).
On the trail of Renzo and Lucia.
The noble villa from which the village was born.

Founded in 1987 at about 1,300 meters in the Upper Sestaione Valley, it preserves the flora of the northern Apennines: the cold microclimate hosts alpine species at the southern limit, such as spruce and rhododendron, and two endemic species, the Globularia incanescens and the carnivorous Pinguicula christinae. The route crosses beech, abetina, rocky garden, blueberry moor, peat bog and a pond; it is part of the Ecomuseum of the Pistoiese Mountain. Seasonal opening.

Private collection of Nello Salsapariglia in the hamlet of Pieve Rossa, with motorcycles, bicycles, tractors, engines, radio and gramophones from the end of the nineteenth century to the twentieth century.
Villa of the second half of the eighteenth century, with park.
The best view of Arezzo.
The fortress of the Este in the Lower.
church deconsecrated in 1920 due to risk collapse, stabilization work in progress since 1988

Remains of a large Roman building from the beginning of the fourth century, in the residence of the Emperor Maxentius: a two-level nymph, square outside and circular inside, with a circular exedra in each of the four lower corners, vaulted with octagonal coffers and walls once covered with polychrome marbles.
The walk of Cortina among frescoed houses and showcases.
The symbol square of the Baroque Rome on the path of the Stadio di Domitiano, with the Fountain of the Four Rivers and the church of Sant'Agnese in Agone.

Romanesque church of the year about 1000 on a rocky spur overlooking the Morenic Amphitheatre: it is the only survivor of the village of Sessano, destroyed by a landslide in the 13th century. It preserves frescoes from the middle of the 11th century with the twelve apostles and St. Stephen, restored in 1999; reopened to the public in 1996 after the restorations of the seventies. Next to it, a medieval garden with six parcels of ancient plants, a pergola of Canavesian vines and a collection of rosemary trees, recognized by the Piedmont Region as Public Botanical Garden since 2009.
The 17th-century parish church next to the shelter.
Public gardens with the statue of Pietro d'Abano, the doctor and philosopher born in 1257 who taught in Paris and from 1306 in Padua, and the fountain of the Harlequin of Hamlet Sartori.
The point of view that made Taormina famous.
Masolino and Tuscany of the first Renaissance in Lombardy.
The Arabic jug of St. Ugo.
Carved woods and cantons of stone houses.

Between Treviso and Venice, Mogliano Veneto houses at Villa La Marignana the museum of the sculptor Toni Benetton, with iron works in the cellars of the villa and a park of over 20,000 m2 with its macrosculptures outdoors; in the center the church of Santa Maria Assunta, completed in the 11th century and consecrated in 1570.
Long loggia built in 1600 by the Arte della Lana, where it stretched to dry the wool just woven.
An icon of comasca abstract art.
At the corner of via Craveri and via Barbacana, the greatest monument of Piedmontese baroque, designed by Bernardo Antonio Vittone, with frescoes by Pietro Paolo Operti.
The hidden bell tower.

In the Borgo dei Nobili there are the Villaggio Giovanni Agnelli, called Ruata del Pozzo, built in 1915-1916 with fan-shaped structure and completed in 1931 by the Rotonda, the houses of the managers of Viale Agnelli (1935-1936) and the Villaggio Edoardo Agnelli of the early 1940s, with eleven small villas around the octagonal square. Around the building remains the social buildings desired by the factory: boarding house (1909), refectory (1910), tram station (1918-1919) and the church of Sant'Aniceto, erected in 1928 by Giovanni Agnelli in memory of his mother.
Remains of a fifteenth-century palace, home of the leader Francesco Salamone (1478-1569).
The literary landscape of the moon and the bonfires.

The village has been documented since the 13th century, but some historians assume its Etruscan origin. The parish church of San Giovanni (Baptist according to Visit Tuscany, Decollato according to Terre di Pisa) is of Romanesque origin and according to tradition stands on the foundations of a more ancient temple; the ruins of the ancient fortress remain.

Monastery complex documented in 1014 and rebuilt in the fourteenth century, with frescoes from the fifteenth century by Paolo Schiavo, Bicci di Lorenzo and an Annunciation of the Scheggia, brother of Masaccio.
The city of shoes.

Dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Immaculate, cited in a status of Padua of 1276 with its ancient bell tower and consecrated in September 1488 by the bishop of Padua Pietro Barbarigo; frescoes at the high altar are documented in 1572.
The heart of the town, with the Town Hall of thirteenth century origin rebuilt in the twentieth century, and the narrow streets of the center.

Promontory between the Gulf of Velia and the Gulf of Policastro, with walls peaking up to 50 meters and 32 caves above and below sea level. The Blue Grotto, the largest, has a triangular entrance of about 6 by 10 meters and lights up blue for an underwater siphon, with sulphurous springs, stalactites and stalagmites; then the Blood Grotto with reddish walls, the Monks Grotto, the Silver Grotto and the Fetente Cala with the smell of sulphur. The Bay of Buondormire can only be reached by boat.
Four floors of karst tunnels.
Minor basilica on the Gianicolo with catacombs.
The hamlet of the legend of the Fairies of the Carrier.

The northernmost valley of the municipality, reached by Gramolazzo, has the basin at 1050 m and the Refuge Orto di Donna, about 7 km from Minucciano: from the parking lot you climb with the path CAI 180 and from the refuge starts a ring on the paths 179, 167 (Passo della Focolaccia), 168 and 186. From Val Serenaia starts the normal route to Monte Pisanino, long and tiring, for the Foce di Cardeto (path 178), the Buca della Neve, the Pizzi Altare and Maggiore and the Canale delle Rose. Passo della Focolaccia and Foce di Cardeto are among the panoramic points of the municipality; the numerous caves require speleological preparation.

Medieval village of Massa Trabaria surrounded by thirteenth-century walls along the Metauro, with the Collegiate Church of Saints Peter and Paul, the church-museum of Saint Francis with the Crucifix of John of Rimini and the Romanesque bridge with three arches.
The castle of bishop princes and the peoples of the mountains of the world.
A Gothic Line cornerstone on the ridge.
The open spaces overlooking the landscape that gave Cingoli the nickname of "Balcony of the Marches."

Established by the Cultural Association Riofreddo Together to preserve the memory of a hard and modest life, it collects about 2000 objects from the eighteenth to the first half of the twentieth century: documents of a Ferriera, a weight of Elban origin, Albisola ceramics, nineteenth century furnishings and early twentieth century clothes, sacred objects, banners and clothes of fraternities, materials on crafts, domestic life and leisure. Open on Sunday 14-18, without reservation.
Birdwatching between the reclamation channels.

Comune Behind Menaggio, in the Val Sanagra: in Codogna the eighteenth-century Villa Camozzi houses the town hall and the Ethnographic and Naturalistic Museum Val Sanagra, from which starts the path to the Rogolone, monumental oak protected since 1922 and symbol of the Val Sanagra Park.
Romanesque, frescoes and cloisters.
The view over four historical regions of Sardinia.
Walk in the green liberty.

Along the itinerary, which can be walked on foot, on horseback and mostly by mountain bike, can be divided into two sections: it starts from the Shrine of Piancastagna and touches Cascina Tiole, Bricco, Batresca, Pessina, a chestnut dryer, the ruins of Sodovi, the carbonaias and the rock shelters of the Pianazzi, Pian Siriti and Siriti, returning to Moretti on asphalt. From the top of the Pianazzi the panorama is 360°. The Municipality also offers the ring Piancastagna, Abasse, Cascina Gorello, Cascina Viazzi, Moretti, with ford of the river Miseria.
Climb on the third bell tower of Veneto during the Premiere del Torcolato.

The oldest nucleus of Roseto, on a hill north of the mouth of the Vomano overlooking the sea: of medieval origin, the inhabitants of the coast would have taken refuge to escape the Turkish raids; the name comes from the Latin "mons" and "pagus" . There are still parts of the fourteenth-century walls with the Door of Feet, unique arched with sharp sixth and overlooking Roseto, and the Door of Borea, where the duties were collected, with the coat of arms of Acquaviva di Atri.
The wall of lovers.
At the intersection of Via Operai and Via Roma, one of the main nodes of the city, it is the only survivor of the series of villas built in those years along Via Roma.
The path along the ancient canal of the aqueduct and the routes from Arziglia to Monte Nero, ancient volcanic crater; from Cian d'Innamurai you can see Menton, Monaco and Nice.
An enigma of stone between peasant use and ancient worship.
A Romanesque church among the farmhouses, with frescoes from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century.

The Ladin municipality of Sèn Jan brings together Vigo and Pozza di Fassa under Catinaccio and Latemar: the late Dogotic parish church of San Giovanni with the 67-metre bell tower, Santa Giuliana with the Georg Artzt triptych, the Ladin de Fascia Museum with its sections on the territory, the Ciampedìe terrace and the thermal baths of the only sulphur spring in Trentino.
One of the oldest cultural institutions in Siena, born in 1758 from the donation of the archdeacon Bandini: about 500,000 volumes and important ancient manuscripts.
The museum dedicated entirely to accordion.
The widest view of the valley.
With nineteenth century frescoes.
The walls of Aristanis.
The life of the fishermen of Garda.
open normally only during calendar events
Nine kilometers under the feet.

The medieval village founded in 1160 by Bishop Uguccione on the hill, reachable with the panoramic funicular: low porticos, cobbled streets and houses decorated in terracotta; since 2025 among the most beautiful villages in Italy.
The church on the ancient abbey of St. Peter.
The thermal lake of prehistoric stilts.

Neoclassical palace renovated in the last decade of the eighteenth century by the architect Stefano Ignazio Melchioni, with colonnade porch, staircase with stone balustrades and frescoes of classical statues; the salon has faux marble walls and the round of Nesso that kidnaps Deianira, a small room four rounds with the myth of Enea and Didone. Split between private and municipality, which organizes exhibitions and events.
Yellow church of the 11th century rebuilt in the Baroque era, on the first slopes of the Castellaro hill.
The Lombard cathedral reborn after the war.
The slopes just outside the center, reachable by cable car, with walks and sea views.
The city's cathedral.
The Sistine Chapel of Val Trompia.
Long Christ and Renaissance marbles.

Borgo almost a thousand meters on the Valley of Sagittarius, founded in the 11th century by Benedictine monks, with a historic center with amphitheatre of stairs, arches and carved portals; under the village the lake of San Domenico with the hermitage where the saint lived around the year 1000 and, little beyond, the lake Pio, regional nature reserve.

Built between 1749 and 1758 by Silvestro Gugliara, it conserves the stones of the discovery of 1599 and a copy of the painting of Our Lady, whose original was lost in a fire of 1769; four paintings of 1927 and a painting of 1929 are by Giuseppe Barone. In the crypt the Chapel of Holy Water, baptistery since 1998.

Church of Byzantine origin was built where in the Middle Ages it was the gate of Santa Maria degli Angeli, next to the former monastery of the Observing Fathers of 1620. It houses three marble sculptures (two of Saint Anne with the Madonna of the Angels and one Madonna of the Help), altarpieces and five altars.
The monumental heart of Bisacquino.
A Renaissance cross from the Marche school.

Marinar village at the northern end of the island of Sant'Antioco, founded by Ligurian families arrived from Tabarka in 1769, with white or pastel-coloured houses: the Sabauda tower with the archaeological museum, the MACC of contemporary art in the former slaughterhouse, the Spiaggia Grande and the cliffs of Mangiabarche.
Murales di Sciola and view of the Flumendosa.
Openings only for guided tours on some Sundays and for groups by reservation; the MiC card (2021) indicated the closed museums until the date to be dedicated
For those who love to walk.

The town of Chietino is located a few kilometres from Pescara, of which is the village of Sambuceto, where stands the church of San Rocco designed by Mario Botta; in the capital there is a small civic museum of natural sciences.
Nine jumps of water in the heart of the Nebrodi.
after the earthquake 2016 historic center, monuments and museums of Ussita are only partially usable (Tourism Marche)

Complex started in 1808 on a project by Carillo Rougier for the collector Ambrogio Uboldo, who conceived it as a museum house; the collections were largely dispersed since 1867 to support the shelter for elderly people he wanted, opened in 1877. The south façade recalls Piermarini and Prunek; on the ground floor three rooms with neoclassical frescoes restored in 1971 and 2014. The English garden is today a public park.

Built around 1130 for Count Ulrico II on a rock spur above Missiano, at 636 meters, it is considered one of the most important fortifications in South Tyrol, with views of the Adige Valley, Bolzano and the Dolomites. It has a pentagonal mastic 23 meters high, the "Wolfsgrube" and the "Kreidenturm" , an educational itinerary of 11 panels and the "Conte Egno" room dedicated to Count Egno of Appiano; there is a tavern of the castle and you can try the archery. Season 2026 from 28 March to 8 November, closed on Wednesdays (in June and July also on Thursdays); guided tours of castle and chapel every half hour from 11 to 16.
Tastings in the vineyards with sea view.
Where the genius of the opera was born.
The underground tombs of the Dauni.
The crypt of the emperors.
In the hamlet of San Gregorio the valley of Rio Lungo preserves historic villas, estates, gardens and gardens; near, the nuraghi Cucuru Gravello and Santo Gregorio with nuragic and Roman testimonies.
the MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day; times to be checked with the tourist office of the Municipality
A young Michelangelo.
The memory of the plague of 1630.
The village of pilgrims.
The Gothic palace is crisp.
The ferrata of the Lanzo Valleys.
Baroque and Gaginian sculptures in the old quarter.
One of the main examples of medieval art in Lombardy.
Small lake at the foot of Monte Castelli, surrounded by beech woods, in the Nebrodi area around Mistretta.

Church started in 1257 and rebuilt between 1761 and 1766 in baroque and rococo forms, with stuccoes of the Rusca, the choir of Ludovico Paci (1771), paintings by Bernardino Santini and the altarpiece of the Circumcision (1506).
The baroque ballroom where the Archduke used to go.

Walk in the center of the village between the neoclassical Palazzo Auriti, built with pebbles and sandstone, and the nineteenth century Palazzo Finamore in Piazza Monteclo, with Italian garden and back garden. At the end of the path the brick wall fountain with two beccucci, from the late nineteenth century, celebrated in the poems of De Titta.

It was mentioned as early as 1296, it was reconsecrated in 1447 and declared "insigne" by Paul III in 1535; after a fire it was rebuilt and consecrated in 1705, with a baroque façade joined to the bell tower and apse decorated in the early eighteenth century by Francesco Alippi and Luca Rubini. Inside a pulpit in unfinished walnut by Matteo Siler (dead in 1678). The museum of sacred art, opened in 1979 in the sacristy, preserves a cycle of Renaissance frescoes of the Passion, fifteen eighteenth-century tables, vestments, ex-vote and a liturgical set donated by Cardinal Ferrata.
The Gothic entrance door to the village.
Ring of 13 km in which at each stage you meet a story, characters and legends of the place; ends at the Map Rubbettino Museum.

Mother church with fourteenth-century façade crowned with hanging arches and portal without comparison in the region, with a small bezel between sun and moon; a single nave interior of the eighteenth century, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1694.
The most beautiful Renaissance court in Valtellina.
The Ascola ceramic tradition.
Between the villages of Pontignano and Geggiano.
The little ancient world.
Gothic frescoes on the hill.

Modern Museum with ethnographic collections of the Ladin Cultural Institute, with multimedia supports and tables by the designer Milo Manara; Mobicult audioguide in six languages (including Ladin) and experience in virtual reality Pigui Experience (€2 more, by reservation).
An unexpected nineteenth-century painting.

Alta Val di Susa railway station in the Milky Way ski area, with the sixteenth-century parish church of San Giovanni Battista, the chalet of Carlo Mollino al Lago Nero (1946-47) and access to the Gran Bosco Natural Park of Salbertrand.
Skiing on the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines.

Country of Alta Pusteria in the Dolomites Region Three Peaks, formerly seat of the Court of Auditors of Gorizia: in Piazza Von Kurz the late Baroque parish church of Santo Stefano and Casa Wassermann with the Museum of Tourism of Alta Pusteria, just outside the village the church of Santa Maddalena in Moos (1490).
A frescoed noble palace that houses contemporary art.
The church of the patrons next to the Sovereign Trullo.

The residence of the popes fleeing the sieges of Rome and the pontifical rectors of Tuscia; the garden, created in 1736 by Cardinal Aldrovandi paving a hill, looks together at the lake, the Tyrrhenian and the Apennines.

Designed in 1939 by the agronomist Igino Ambrosini (1883-1955), already among the creators of the Alpine Garden, it had its first seat in the school building; since 1976 it has been in the seat built on purpose, promoted by the Association Friends of the Museum under the patronage of the Municipality. It tells of a trade that the craftsmen of Gignese successfully brought around the world: over a thousand umbrellas, parasols and handles, including those belonging to Queen Margherita of Savoia and Giuseppe Mazzini, with photos of the first umbrellas, tools and a work bench. Seasonal opening from Tuesday to Sunday 10-12 and 15-18 (date 2024), in other periods for groups by reservation.
The Medici passion for botany.
Exhibits, rocks, minerals and reconstructions of the Maremma environments.

About 3,800 hectares on the north side of the high Val di Susa, established by the Piedmont Region in 1980: woods of spruce and red, silvestre pine, cembrus and larch, with marmots, chamois, deer and wolves.

Sant'Arpino was founded in the territory of ancient Atella, the Oscian city cradle of the Fabulae Atellane, and it was named after Sant'Elpidio and was a fief of the Sanchez de Luna, which built the Doge's Palace in front of the mother church of Sant'Elpidio between 1573 and 1592.
The park on the Po.
The sweet of the village, created in 1725 by Sister Virginia Casale of the College of Mary on commission of the Marquise of Sambuca, inspired by the hills seen from the window.
The delightful villa of Piermarini and its park.
Birdwatching in the fishing valley.
With the tower of Mariano, the most significant testimony of the walls of the judicial capital.

The fourteenth-century castle on the cliff of Corenno, with walls and two towers where the population took refuge in case of danger; it is considered one of the best examples of fortification of the Lario. Next to it, the natural viewpoint looks at the lake and the villages of the opposite shore.
Church with façade decorated with ceramics; inside the fresco of the Crib by Giovanni Andrea De Magistris, dated 1560.

The MUSAC, Museum of Street Art of the Castles, collects works by urban artists; in the hamlet of Pavona, between Albano and Castel Gandolfo, the project    \ Art in Station and Color City of the Railways brought murals of Krayon, Alessandra Carloni and Diego Poggioni.
Private residence of the Marquis Malvezzi Campsites, the rooms are rented for ceremonies
The square in front of Castel Sismondo, open-air seat of the Fellini Museum, with the veil of water that evokes the ancient moat and the circular golden bench as a circus track.
A small historical theatre in the heart of the village.
It is a site with medieval finds on Monte San Michele, where there was a fortified settlement on two terraces, probably a destination for pilgrimages.
Two centuries of astronomy.
A quiet glacial lake with pirouettes from 3,500 years ago.
Village among the olive groves of the Argentina-Armea valley, divided into small villages on the hill overlooking the sea, with the watchtower of the Panei as symbol.
The convent church that dominates the village.

Near the historic centre, on the hill towards Riscone, it preserves the graves of the fallen of the Great War and is one of the most important memorial of the First World War in South Tyrol; it is reached by path no. 22, along which is also the Fountain of tears.

Pieve documented since 1029, rebuilt in 1303 inside the walls, then demolished and rebuilt between 1744 and 1758 and enlarged in 1884 on a project by Angelo Gottardi. Neoclassical façade with ionic columns and steps in red of Verona; altarpiece of Francesco Morone, paintings of Domenico Morone, Farinati and Cignaroli, statue of the Redeemer of 1553, baptismal font of 1430 and organ of George Trice of 1889.
The monument of Arnaldo Pomodoro at the entrance of the city cemetery, where Frederick Fellini, Juliet Masina and his son Pierfederico rest.
View of the Camastra Valley.
The graffiti of transhumance shepherds.

Ethnographic-agricultural museum established in 1976 on the ground floor of the former convent of Sant'Agostino: 14 sections on 750 square meters with rebuilt environments (granary, cellar, workshop of the workshop and shoemaker, kitchen, room, school, tavern, weaving room), carts, large agricultural tools and tools for pastoral and hunting. The route has been renovated and includes immersive experiences.
The old town, the lakefront and the ancient port dug into the rock.
A few minutes from Boccheggiano, it houses the installations of the artist Paul Fuchs: very tall structures that move and emit sounds with the wind, a place particularly loved by children.
15th-century Basilica overlooking the Piazza I Maggio.

The Contrada Granda, the main street in the historic center between Via XX Settembre, Piazza Cima and Via Beato Marco Ongaro, is almost all porticoed and line Casa Piutti, the Town Hall, Palazzo Sarcinelli, the Montalban palaces and the Monte di Pietà with the frescoed façade, between Porta Dante and Porta del Monticano with the Leone di San Marco. Piazza Cima, slightly sloping on the hill of Giano, is closed by the eighteenth-century Town Hall of Ottavio Scotti and the neoclassical Teatro Accademia by Andrea Scala (1859-1869); here Pietro Germi shot scenes by "Lord & Lords" (1966).
The large hilly park next to the circuit, with paths and pond.
The Gothic church built between 1339 and 1343 thanks to Gualtiero Galeota, outside the ancient walls, with scenic access staircase and frescoed noble chapels.
Church built on the ruins of a early Christian building and enlarged in the 14th century.
Promontory of Aspromonte with the shape of a crouched lion, reachable on foot; from the viewpoint of the Tre Croci the view reaches Sicily and the Aeolian Islands.

The hillside municipality of Friuli, where, on the hill of Susans, stands the seventeenth-century castle of Colloredo, a Tuscan villa in Medici style with four corner towers reached by a avenue of cypresses; in the hamlet of San Tomaso the church of San Giovanni dei Templari preserves frescoes from the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
The story of black pens.
Built probably in the second century AD in lava stone covered with marble, elliptic of 125 for 105 meters, it could accommodate 15,000 spectators: today we see a section in Piazza Stesicoro.

The theater was born in 1827 from the transformation of the oratory annexed to the Franciscan Tertiary monastery, after in 1822 the City Council had asked Maria Luigia of Austria for the hall; at the beginning of the twentieth century it was named after Eleonora Duse, who had recited it at the age of ten. The neoclassical façade has three doors, three windows between pilasters and a tympanum with the city coat of arms; you visit during the theater season and events.

It rises on a ground taken from organized crime, today a garrison of legality and culture: under a dome of more than three meters a professional telescope for photographs and educational activities, with filters to observe the Sun safely.

Of fourteenth-century origin and rebuilt in the seventeenth century, it is linked to the Compagnia della Madonna del Giglio, founded on 1 November 1300; on the main altar a fresco of the 15th century Madonna del Giglio with the Child.
€13 (path A), €15 (path B)
Eight hundred varieties of roses on a ridge.
The Campedèl, the heart of the city and the traditional meeting place of the Bellunesi, with porticos, cafes, the walk of the "listòn" and the gardens.

Discovered by chance in November 2000 during the work for a sarno purifier, it was a river settlement on artificial islets separated by canals, inhabited by the middle age of the Bronze Age to the sixth century B.C., with huts of perishable materials and workshops that worked metal, bone, glass paste and amber; there were found a landing place and three pirogues. The humid environment has conserved many perishable materials; the site is managed by the Municipality under the Archaeological Park of Pompeii, with educational room, captions, marked routes and cafeteria.

Fortress of about 1450-1470 with a quadrangular plan, overlooking the sea in front of the Costa dei Trabocchi; damaged by the bombings of 1943 and by a landslide in 1946, restored in the 2000s, houses in a tower a small museum.
The port of Oneglia.

Where tradition places the martyrdom of Efisio (303 A.D.): a high-medieval sanctuary rebuilt in Romanesque style by the victorious monks of Marseilles at the end of the XI century with stones of Nora, portico and atrium of the seventeenth century. The destination of the great procession that starts from Cagliari on May 1st, with rites on the beach on May 3.
400 million years of Carnic Alps in a museum.
The origins of Bari.

Opened on 12 August 1997 in the ancient bishop's palace, before the sixteenth century, where San Gerardo Maiella lived from 1741 to 1744 at the service of Bishop Albini. It has a lapidary section (stemmi, acquasantiere, architectural elements from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century) with the well of the miracle of Gerardiello, an archaeological section with Roman and Sanniti artifacts, including inscriptions in Osco and Latin, and an ethnographic section with a wine press of the fifteenth century.
A curious collection.
Artificial basin in the Regional Park of the Lakes of Suviana and Brasimone, with canoes, pedalos and trails.
The father's home in experimental biology.
15th century frescoes just a stone's throw from fossils.
To be checked (for a fee)

Until 1915 on Mount Rive stood the Torre dei Sicconi, last rest of the castle infeudato in 1201 to the lords of Caldonazzo and linked to Siccone II, attacked in 1385 by Vicentini and Veronesi; the tower still appears in the municipal coat of arms. The excavations of 2006-2008 have brought to light the tower, sections of walls and a probable palace, with materials of the 13th-XV century; since 2005 the Municipality has started a thematic garden. Walk up from the Town Hall Square in about 50 minutes.
Prehistoric finds and Hellenistic-Roman age.

Educational museum that traces in chronological order the history of Gradisca: fossils and geological evolution, Roman stone fragments, medieval and Renaissance weapons, coins, seventeenth-century paintings and Baroque frescoes from the Cathedral of the SS. Peter and Paul, with a section on the Jewish community present since the sixteenth century.
In the village with its almost intact medieval structure, the parish church of San Quintino and the Palazzo Civico, seat of the tourist information office.
Walk through buildings of various eras.

Overhanging promontory on the westernmost tip of the island, dominated by a lighthouse of 1864 whose summit is 138 meters above the sea, with a lantern visible up to 28 miles. On the cliffs he nidifies the queen's hawk; in front is the island of the Horn. You go down to the sea with steep paths: the source recommends the boat trip.
The city's art museum.

In the sixteenth-century convent of Santa Maria del Soccorso, called "Badia" (Badia), enlarged between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, exhibits around the cloister porched finds from the ancient Neolithic (VI millennium BC) to the late antiquity: the sanctuaries of Demeter and Kore of Mollarella and Casalicchio, the settlements of Poggio Marcato d'Agnone and Monte Sole and an entire hall on Finziade, founded in 282 BC by the tyrant agrigentino Finzia, with the House 1 and the treasure found inside. Since 2025 the medieval and modern section exhibits the fifteenth-century triptych attributed to the Master of San Martino, the Madonna del Soccorso attributed to Domenico Gagini (1470) and a sixteenth-century sarcophagus with knight. Open Monday-Friday 9-13.
The oldest village, overlooking the village.
Two towers of the late nineteenth century at the entrance of the ancient nucleus.
The oldest baptistery in Calabria.
Consecrated in 1841, of classical lines, with cuspidate bell tower.
Four centuries of Massimo history.
Excursions between woods and peaks over 1,800 m.
The Temple Theatre of the Sanniti, overlooking the valley of the Trigno.

Country on the eastern branch of Lake Como at the foot of the Grigne, historical seat of the Moto Guzzi founded in 1921, with the museum in the historical factory; in the village the archpriest church of San Lorenzo with the Museum of Sacred Art, the sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the River and, in Maggiana, the Tower of Barbarossa, while above the village passes the Path of the Wanderer with the frescoed church of San Giorgio.
The minerals of the hills in a medieval palace.
Top of the South Tyrol centre.
A country left empty.

The modern center was built in the eighteenth century by Antonio Winspeare and Francesco Carpi, with piazza del Comune (Piazza Castello), the church of Santa Candida and Piazza De Gasperi. Spinelli, Rossi and Colorni wrote the Ventotene Manifesto in 1941-42; in 2022 the island received the European Heritage Mark.
A hidden jewel.

Also known as the parish church of San Daniele and dedicated to the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary and to San Daniele Prophet, it is an eighteenth-century church that combines baroque and neoclassical elements; it preserves paintings by Nicola Grassi (1725) and a Baroque altar by Giovanni Saidero da Venzone (1641).

Giurdignano is considered the largest and most diverse megalithic site in Italy, with seven dolmen still intact. The Dolmen Stable, along the road to Giuggianello between olive trees and dry stone walls on a plateau at 102 meters, dates back to the beginning of the II millennium BC: it has a rectangular plan with a covering plate resting on a series of blocks, and for many scholars it was part of a wider megalithic structure. Other imposing dolmens, perhaps used as altars, are Orfine, Chiancuse, Peschio Gravasce, Santa Barbara, Sferracavalli, Paolo Niuri and Grassi.
Walk through medieval walls and towers in a garden of centuries-old plants.
The workshop of the valley painters.
An italic sanctuary on the valley.
The work of Giovanni Angelo Montorsoli with Martino Montanini (1547-1551), celebrates the first city aqueduct with the rivers Nile, Tiber, Ebro and Camaro.
At the foot of the rose.
A rare example of rural archaeology around a Romanesque abbey.

Borgo del Goceano, about 600 meters, founded in 1337 by Mariano IV d'Arborea at the foot of the castle of the Gocean, a judicial fortress of 1134 on a granite cliff; in the village the Museo dei Castelli di Sardegna and, in the hamlet of Foresta Burgos, the horse breeding centre, the church of San Salvatore and the nuraghe Costa.
An entire village as an art gallery.
Urban art in the city: in the Alley of the Waters the white gorilla of Davide Toffolo, homage to Copito de Nieve, and in the district of Torre large animal figures on the facades.
The historic city theatre, among the places of the culture of the country.
Portals and mullioned windows of an award-winning village.
Industrial archaeology.
The theatre of the city's opera.
The sharecropper of Tuscan farms.
The fossil marine reptile of the Marches.

The Oratory of the Dead (or Disciplini), a national monument of the 14th century, preserves remarkable coeve paintings. Not far away is the arched bridge designed by Francesco Cifrondi of Clusone, completed in 1686.
The art of Alberto Martini.
The church of the patrons.
The main church of Caldarola, inaugurated in 1590 with the bubble of Sixto V and then elevated to Collegiata distinguished; overlooking the square next to Pallotta Palace.
closed for the winter break from 9 November 2026 to 31 March 2027 (weinmuseum.it)
Freshwater birdwatching.
A village of authorship signed by Gorni.

Court documented already in the twelfth century as Villa dei Reatini, which hosted the Franciscan preacher Saint Bernardino da Siena; the palace of Matildica period, renovated in the fifteenth century, includes the manor house to the west, a dovecote tower to the north and a fifteenth-century oratory dedicated to the saint.

Works mainly local from the churches, with the hat reconstructed of the Stories of St. John the Baptist of the Salimbeni brothers and works of Pinturicchio, Niccolò Alunno, Vittore Crivelli, Paolo Veneziano, Lorenzo d'Alessandro and Bernardino di Mariotto.
The sculptures of Achtermann in a 17th century church.
The largest wetland bell.

Canyon between Celano, Aielli and Ovindoli with walls up to 200 meters high and distant in some points just 2 meters, dug by water; along the path the Fonte degli Innamorati and the ruins of the Celestian monastery of San Marco alle Foci, with griffons, royal owls and pilgrim falcons. The crossing (difficulty E+, white-red CAI trail, 3-3,5 hours) starts from the parking lot in Foci and arrives in Valle d'Arano, on the plateau of Ovindoli; the municipality recommends late spring and summer, avoiding the rainy and snowy seasons for the floods.
Strong and lakes above the Valley of Susa.
The beaches are the second great attraction of the village, summer seaside resort with clubs and shops; San Felice has the Green Flag of pediatricians for baby-friendly beaches.
The Alpine memory of the Camonica Valley.

White wine from an ancient native grape, produced in a sweet (passed) or dry version; among the wineries of the village Tenuta Cecolo IX in Vicenne, which also produces Montepulciano and Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo, Pecorino and sweets Moscatello (tel. 085 7998193; visits and tastings to verify).
A collection of decorative arts in the village.

Ring of 5.1 km (373 m of difference in altitude, about 1 hour and 45) that from the center follows path 12 towards Missiano, passes the Gothic tower of São Paulo and Castel Korb (of Roman origin, today hotel), climbs to Castel d'Appiano and, after 60 meters of metal steps a gorge in the porphyry, reaches the ruins of Castel Boymont; return between orchards and vineyards with views of Bolzano and the Dolomites.
The headless Roman statues.

Built by the Normans on the remains of a Roman fortress, with the cylindrical Norman tower of the 11th century attributed to Count Drogo; expanded by Frederick II and transformed into a residence in the 17th century by the dukes of Guevara, whose descendants lived there until 1961. Coffered ceilings, courtyard with clock tower and hanging garden; Torquato Tasso and Pope Benedict XIII stayed there.
The medieval village perched in the Roman Castles.

The main square, the heart of the village life, with historic buildings, cafes and shops. Nearby, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Sartoretti with a decorated lounge and views of the park, and the church of Santa Maria Assunta with a Corinthian façade.

Opened in 1810 after the Napoleonic edict, it has a row of family chapels on the street side, wrought iron crosses of local craftsmen and silhouettes of angels in sheet metal, once painted, on the children's graves.
High-altitude lakes.
The red trachyte symbol of the country.
End sand just a few steps from Ischia Ponte.

Romanesque church of the fourteenth century with portal with pillars and bell tower with double windows; the interior with a single nave is rich in Umbrian frescoes, some attributed to Paolo Bontulli from Percanestro, and the main altar is under an ogival canopy.

In the second half of the nineteenth century the architecture of the town was renewed along Via XX Settembre; from the early twentieth century to the post-war period facades in Art Nouveau style arose with stone decorations of local stone chisels. Between 1880 and 1925 the Villa municipale, the new cemetery and the sports field were built. From the village the view extends over Mount Etna, the Climate Mountains and the Ionian Sea.
The forts above the city.
With 1019 meters it is the highest peak of Elba and the province of Livorno; you walk up the CAI trails or in a few minutes with the cable car near the village, active in summer.
A hot bath after a hike in the park.

Città dei Castelli Romani on a spur of pepper next to the Bosco Ferentano, overlooking the lake Albano 23 km from Rome: under the village there is the net of caves of Marino Underground, with the mitreus frescoed of the second century; on the surface Palazzo Colonna, the basilica of San Barnaba, the Fontana dei Quattro Mori and the Civic Museum "Umberto Mastroianni" in the former church of Santa Lucia.
Contemporary art a stone's throw from the sea.
Church founded in 1257 in Borgo Pinti, which houses the famous fresco of Perugino in the capitular hall.
Baroque Monrealist and Barge stone.
With the Archaeological Museum €13; with the Fortress of San Leo €14,50
The earthly paradise under your feet.
15th century frescoes in a country tower.
The Northern Cross is one of the largest radio telescopes in the world.

The village of medieval white houses on the cliff, inhabited since the Neolithic, with traces of Arabs, Byzantine, Spanish and Norman and the remains of four defensive towers. You enter it from the Arch of Marchesale (Porta Grande), of the sixteenth century, until 1780 only access to the village surrounded by a moat with drawbridge, today covered by Piazza Garibaldi. In the alleys: the Palazzo Marchesale dei feudatari, via Giudea (the ancient Jewish ghetto) with the churches of Purgatory and Santo Stefano, the verses painted by the street artist Guido Lupori (the "Guido il Flâneur") and the belvedere on the sea, like wide Cave Ardito at sunset.

The Accademia Valdarnese del Poggio, in the Franciscan monastery of San Lodovico, exhibits thousands of fossils of the Upper Valdarno of the Pliocene and Pleistocene: the Mammuthus sudridis, giant hyenas, jaguars and the skull of Canis etruscus, the oldest known testimony of the species; an archaeological section with Etruscan and Roman finds.
Ancient statues among the turbines.
The memory of the mill that made the history of the country.

Pre-Hellenic necropolis discovered by chance in 1953 during road work, in an artificial canal made in the shell limestone: artificial grutticella tombs, or "forno" (a furnace), largely closed by squared stone slabs, with overlapping burials and skeletons in fetal position, dated from the MiC to the XIII-VII centuries B.C. (XI-X B.C. according to the Municipality). The equipment is at the National Museum of Magna Grecia in Reggio Calabria. The area, redeveloped in 2009, has playground and picnic area and looks at Calvary on the historic center. Open Monday-Thursday 9-12 only by reservation (tel. 0965 742012).
Salami and Black Rooster under the arcades.

A nuragic sacred area of about seven hectares in the Pratobello valley, about 1000 meters in a wood of roverelle: a fence of 70 meters with circular temple, a megaron temple of eleven meters and apsed environment, about one hundred huts and the only nuragic aqueduct so far known, with the springs closed by a semicircular curtain and a pool perhaps ritual. Facilities of the recent Bronze (XIII-XII century B.C.), finds up to the final Bronze.
At 2656 meters above Saint-Barthélemy, reachable on foot, dates back to 1659 and is dedicated to the Madonna of the Snows; the current building was rebuilt in 1861.

At Casarinaccio, rediscovered in the mid-Twentieth century, the forum of the ancient Ardea with a large temple of the fifth century BC and a basilica of republican age; at Colle della Noce the remains of the temple of the Mount of Noce, in the sixth century BC among the major sanctuaries of the Latium Vetus, discovered in 1981; near, a Christian hypogeus oratory found in 1964, born as a nymph in the second century BC, used by Christians from the fifth century and frescoed in the twelfth century.
18th century building used as a pasta factory from 1890 to 1949, today a museum of itself with the twentieth century machinery on display.

Ancient Maremma Stone, on a rock above the river Ombrone: the castle, attested since 988, controlled the Traversa dei Monti, via del sale between Grosseto and Montalcino, and passed to Siena in 1403 and to the Medici in 1559. There are still alleys, access arch and stretches of walls, the remains of the ancient bridge over the Ombrone, the Antiche Fonti del Sasso along the path towards the river and the municipal terraced park of Bellacosta.
The young reader's attic stele.
The Great Synagogue.
