Small village on a rocky spur at more than 800 meters, probably founded in the IX century, with the remains of the walls and medieval fortress of the ancient Castrum Smerilli; on clear days the view arrives to the Sibillini, the Gran Sasso, the Conero and the Adriatic.

Approximately 13 hectares of wetlands, hygrophilous forests and humid meadows that host one of the largest gauzes of Emilia-Romagna; the most common species is the heron, now sedentary. The best time to visit is spring or autumn.
The sea of the Ionian Sea with a thousand shades.

On the western side of Mount Orlando, overlooking the sea, the 11th century sanctuary takes its name from three cracks of the rock that tradition binds to the earthquake at the death of Christ. Baroque interior with a single nave with a canvas by Raimondo Bruno (1850) on the main altar and the bed of San Filippo Neri, a stairway in the slit descends to the Chapel of the Crucifix (16th century), built on the fallen stone in 1434, and along the wall you can see the "Mano del Turco" (Turco's Hand). Freely visitable, entrusted to PIME missionaries; not accessible to disabled people.
A 15th century church isolated in the woods.

Natural monument at 635 meters along the ascent to Tuttavista: a rocky wall with a large natural hole of about 10 meters in diameter, overlooking the valley and the Supramonte, reachable by a short path from the main road.

In the Bishop's Palace, part of a path that includes Duomo, churches of St. Francis and St. Stephen and Ducal Palace; the first section is in the sacristy of the Cathedral, with altar, bishop's throne, choir stalls, sacristy furnishings, liturgical silvers from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century and two wooden panels from the fifteenth century. On the first floor the paintings of the Molisano Paolo Gamba, a pupil of Francesco Solimena; among the notable pieces the homeral veil of Bishop Belisario Baldevino (1555-1591), who in 1564 founded the first seminary of Christendom. Hours indicated by italia.it: every day 9-12.30 and 17-19.30.
The biggest times of the Forum.
The medieval watchman at the entrance of the village.
The public fountain with the Latin motto.
The Bosco di Maglie, called Bosco dei Signi, stretches in the plain not far from the museum to the shores of Lake Pertusillo, with picnic areas suitable for family trips.
The university music house.
Along the ascent to Piazza Grande.
Among the most important international opera theatres, rebuilt by Carlo Mollino after the fire of 1936, with a violet ceiling, color usually banned by the theatres.
A work of unique dramatic force, a stone's throw from the square.
A thousand years of history and the view of Lake Viverone.
The stone bridge of Istria started by Augustus and ended by Tiberius (14-21 AD), still accessible today, with the village San Giuliano on the other bank.
times not indicated by sources; MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day: contact the Ecomuseum of Biellese
In the footsteps of Saint Francis.

A baroque church dating back to the 16th century that houses the parish museum with sacred furnishings, wooden reliquaries, a Madonna Odigitria in polychrome wood, a 17th century wooden Mary Magdalene and a 18th century Deposition.

The academy founded in 1580 by Count Gaspare Campo, in the palace completed in 1814: a library of about 300,000 volumes and incunabula and part of the art gallery with Tiepolo, Bellini and Palma il Vecchio.

The village stands almost 800 meters between the peaks of three mountains; the view ranges over Barbagia, Baronia, Logudoro and Gallura, on a territory of granite reliefs and deep valleys, holm oak and cork forests and numerous springs.
The traditional Christmas market that animates the squares of the center in winter, when Trento lights up like a crib in the background of the mountains.
The castle of the Anguissola, from outside.
Panorama of the Santerno valley.
12th century basilica with double ionic façade, overlooking the port.

From the valley station of the Rasciesa funicular, north of the village, the path no. 10 climbs in the woods up to the Rasciesa refuge (2,170 m) and the summit cross (2,125 m): 4.9 km, about 2 hours and 40 and 857 m of altitude difference, medium difficulty; alternatively you climb up by funicular. From the top, the view spans Odle, Sella, Sassolungo, Sciliar and Valle Isarco.
In the Cittadella dei Musei in the district of Castello, the museum that houses the finds of the ancient nuragic communities of Sardinia.
Prehistoric signs in the rock of the Bracco.
The castle overlooking the centre, among noble stuccoes.
visits only by reservation required through the Literary Park

Built between 1734 and 1750 on a project by Domenico Antonio Vaccaro and Michelangelo Di Blasio after the earthquake of 1732, example of Neapolitan Baroque with octagonal plan with frescoed rooms and stuccoes; national monument since 1868, houses the state library with almost 200,000 volumes, 24 codes and 38 incunabula.

Founded in 1994 in the premises next to the parish church of San Vincenzo Martire, on an ancient place of worship overlooking the Valley of Susa, it was born from the exhibition  "Valle di Susa": art and history from the 11th to the 18th century in 1977; since 2001 it is part of the diocesan museum system. It collects works from the numerous chapels of the territory: above all wooden statuary from the 15th to the 20th century, with seventeenth-century pieces of the Moriana carving schools (Clappier of Bessan, Claude Simon of Bramans), goldsmiths and sacred vestments. The visit also includes the church; openings on dates indicated by the Diocesan Cultural Centre.

On the sides of the mountain, at 330-340 m, a circuit of polygonal walls encloses about 150 hectares in the upper part of the relief; the walls are made of large limestone blocks arranged without regular order within an artificial cut in the rock.

Country of Sibaritide linked to the ancient Lagaria: the sanctuary of Athena on the Timpone della Motta, the necropolis of Macchiabate with almost two hundred mounds, the archaeological civic museum of Palazzo De Santis and the museum of rural art.
Oratory of the fifteenth century set in the serpentinous rock of the Stone Perduca, reachable by a path following the sign for Bobbiano.

Outside the centre, surrounded by greenery and overlooking the Vallone dell'Arenaccia, it preserves a cycle of Marian frescoes from 1713 by Anselmo Palmieri di Polla and an altar by Andrea Carrara di Padula; the festival is July 2. It is the starting point of a walk in nature.

Center of the Tiber Valley dominated by the fifteenth-century castle of the Orsini, with the parish church of Santo Stefano; in the territory, along Via Tiberina, the Roman villa of the Volusii Saturnini, discovered in 1961 during the work of the Autostrada del Sole.

In the crypts of the Mother Church, set up on a project by Giuseppe Pannano, he exhibits the treasure of the church: a Christ died in limestone of the fifteenth century, silvers of the eighteenth century, vestments, prints and paintings, and a chess book of 1617 considered the first to describe the Sicilian  "defense."
Village of the national park for walks in the unspoilt nature, with an itinerary of valley bottom easy even with stroller.

Designed in 1965 as an innovative environmental space, on the model of the Maeght Foundation of Saint-Paul-de-Vence and the Louisiana Museum of Humlebamycin, with hexagonal building; the founder's idea was to bring the works of art out in the open. Hundreds of sculptures and mosaics by Italian and foreign artists in marble, stone, bronze, iron, steel, wood and glass, from the second half of the twentieth century, including works by Jean Arp and Alexander Archipenko, are exhibited on a large area.
The heart of the Medici city.
private property, not visitable: you can see it from the alleys or at events
Solimena and Guarini in a hamlet church.

New Renaissance villa built between 1852 and 1865 for Count Francesco Revedin on a project by Giambattista Meduna, donated in 1984 to the University of Padua and restored in 2015. The English garden, one of the most important in Veneto, covers more than 8 hectares with more than a thousand trees, a lake with two islands fed by the Avenale, the Cavallerizza with semicircle statues, a Moorish greenhouse and two towers. Access by reservation on weekends and holidays (049 827 3939).
Today it is the most beautiful view of the center, with the Tower Asinelli closed.

House of a family perhaps descended from Catalan knights arrived in the Spanish age, inhabited until the mid-Twentieth century and transformed by the Municipality into a cultural center after 1980: portal eighteenth century in rustic, three bronze bells from destroyed churches, exhibition on emigration, historical cuisine, historical municipal archive, art museum with works collected by Enrico Crispolti in the eighties and archaeological finds. In the garden an outdoor theater for summer events.

Romanesque, from the XI-XIII centuries, restored after an earthquake of the eighteenth century: inside three naves with semi-colons, truss cover, matroneo with triphor and carved wooden choir; the façade unites Romanesque portal and baroque window.
A stone pastoral village at 721 meters.
The oldest towers in the mining village.
Built by the Templars in the 12th century, it preserves over the arch of a portal a plaque with the symbol of the cross at TAU.
The cathedral on Piazza Duomo, the point of arrival of the walk under the arcades.
Country of ceramics on the Riviera del Beigua, open-air museum with the promenade of the Artists of 1963, the furnaces of Pozzo Garitta and the eighteenth-century Villa Faraggiana.
From the Middle Ages to the twentieth century in a Jesuit college.
Born as a house-tower of the thirteenth century, prison from the Napoleonic age until 1973, restored and opened to the public in 2016 as the venue of exhibitions and events.

Started by the Savelli in the second half of the sixteenth century, it was transformed by the Chigi between 1664 and 1672 into a sumptuous baroque residence designed by Gian Lorenzo Bernini and the young pupil Carlo Fontana, and retains largely original environments and furnishings; Prince Agostino Chigi Albani of the Rovere gave it to the Municipality on December 29, 1988. It houses a collection of paintings, sculptures and furnishings, especially of the seventeenth century; you can visit the Rooms of Cardinal Flavio Chigi, the noble floor and the Museum of the Roman Baroque, all without barriers. This is where Luchino Visconti shot many scenes of the "Cattopardo" (Cattopardo).
can be visited with the guided tour of the country on Wednesday at 16.30 from May to October; groups on request
Walser culture.
Prehistoric finds under a cycle of 16th century frescoes.

Borgo on a tuff cliff at the confluence of two streams, linked to the Farnese: the Farnese Rocca renovated by Antonio da Sangallo il Giovane, the archaeological museum "Pietro e Turiddo Lotti" and, in the wood, the ruins of Castro, capital of the Farnesian Duchy razed to the ground in 1649.
The peak of the village, between castle and devotion.

Gothic church of the fourteenth century on the side of Piazza Masaccio, which incorporated a smaller church as a right aisle; sandstone and brick facade. The restoration of 1903 brought to light the frescoes of Scheggia, the brother of Masaccio, including the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano; in the presbytery the triptych of the Coronation of the Virgin of Giovanni del Biondo (about 1374). In 1780 a mummified body was found in a pillar of the counterfaçade, still visible in a niche.
Square of the historic centre, between Corso Garibaldi and the castle, the heart of the summer evening life.

Interactive museum in the historic Villa Wachtler on the birth and evolution of the Dolomites: myths and legends, ancient fauna such as the Megachirella wachtleri, ancestor of snakes and lizards, evolution of plants, cave bears and a section with original dioramas and skeletons of dinosaurs. All year round you can try to look for gold, crystals and fossils; activities for children and boys.
Polar expeditions of Norge and Italy.

The Scaligera fortress built between 1354 and 1356 on the Adige, civic museum since 1926 with the setting of Carlo Scarpa: sculptures of the fourteenth century, scaligere goldsmiths and works of Pisanello, Bellini, Mantegna and Veronese.
Three water jumps between rocky gorges and woods, fed by the Rutor glacier, observed by wooden and metal bridges.
Two thousand five hundred years of walls.

Spa and sports center near the old town, fed by the Cinglaccia spring: indoor and outdoor pools, 60 meters slide, thermorium with saunas, Turkish bath and whirlpool, treatments with mud and inhalations and wellness treatments.
The great prehistoric enclosure of the plain.
For sea fans.
Fishing boats under the castle.

In Piazza Vittorio Veneto, one of the most important museums of the twentieth century in Italy, with futurists such as Boccioni, Balla, Depero and Pannaggi (Treno in corsa, 1922) and works by Donghi, Scipione, Mafai and Fausto Pirandello.
The white cliff where the Apennines ends.
Terrecottas of taste robbiano inside one of the castles of Arcevia.
Eight centuries of paper.
Side valley frequented by ungulates and gipeto, reachable on foot or by bike from Niblogo along the road to the bridge of Peceneccia.
The oldest Romanesque in Centemilia.
The Langhe sentry.

At about 1 km from the village, underground burials of Christian age obtained in caverns already used in the Bronze Age: the "Grotta di Dionisio" owes the name to the inscription of a local priest, the "Grotta di Sant'Anna" preserves a medieval fresco of the saint.

In an underground environment excavated in the historic center, he tells the town with coins from the end of the 16th to the end of the 17th century, documenting the mint shop and the guys from Piombino.
Woods and river shores a stone's throw from the village.

Franciscan Church was completed in 1307 and has a fourteenth-century portal of the mystical lamb, a holy waterworks held by the ancient synagogue, an eighteenth-century wooden pulpit and a guazzo-painted ceiling of 1745 by Francesco De Martino. Closed on Monday.
A destination of pilgrimage built in memory of the tearing of an effigy of Our Lady in 1953.
The miraculous image painted on the tuff.
Built between 1792 and 1797, with a Romanesque portal in serpentine, frescoes by Lorenzo Peretti and in the chapel of San Carlo a painting by Tanzio da Varallo (1615).

Born in 1986 thanks to the scholar Fiorenzo Amiconi in the former convent of the Augustinians Scalzi, in 1990 he enriched himself with the ethnographic collection: about 1,500 objects of peasant civilization and the trades donated by families, in four rooms and in the cloister (weights and sizes, spinning, domestic life, babes in rags and firework of the parties, tools of carpenters, crotch, shoemaker and blacksmith). In the basement sacred art from the fifteenth to the twentieth century from the churches of the village, with a processional cross of Sulmonese school, a Nativity of 1571 and a Holy Family of the eighteenth century. MiC timetable: Monday-Saturday 10-18, Sunday 9-19.
The fortress above Taormina.
The view of the Aeolian cliffs.

Green area of over 9,500 m2 on the Via Francigena, between the centre of Rivera and the industrial area, with picnic tables, children's games, fountain and pond; in summer it hosts concerts and tastings.
An eighteenth-century library still alive.
The mother church combines Romanesque and Gothic elements; in front of it an arch gives access to the ancient Jewish ghetto.

The Clock Tower, about 20 meters high, was built from 1859 and inaugurated on March 6, 1877, with original mechanism of the Solari brothers of Pesariis replaced in 1975; in Piazza Garibaldi, from the balcony of Palazzo Accardi, Garibaldi spoke to the crowd on July 22, 1862.

It rises 2373 meters to the border with Canavese and Valle d'Aosta, dominated by the monument to the Redeemer, 13 meters high and surmounted by a bronze statue of Christ, next to the Rifugio del Mombardo. From Graglia there are marked paths.
The elegant face of the country.

Church of the early thirteenth century, with three naves, built on a rocky spur overlooking the valley; it is called of Saint Lucia because it guards the statue of the patroness. It was Michael's and Apollonia's wedding set in the "The Godfather."

Opened in 1969 next to the archaeological park, it exhibits the finds of the Greek cities of Siris and Herakleia and of the indigenous centers of the interior: votive statues and accessories of Siris with some of the oldest figurative ceramics of Magna Grecia (VII-VI century B.C.), matrixes, votive objects and accessories of Herakleia with red-figure ceramics and gold jewels in filigree, bronze armour, silver jewels, gold and amber. Closed on Tuesdays.

Educational garden on the history of beekeeping, biodiversity and sustainability, which recovers ancient practices of nourishment of bees and hosts over one hundred species of herbs, shrubs and honeycombs. It offers sensory activities: recognizing the fragrances of plants, tasting different honeys, discovering how bees communicate with smells; designed for schools, enthusiasts and families.
From the square on top of the village a spectacular view of the hills of the Langhe and the Alps.
The typography told.
Ass-back bridge of 1499 on Santerno, with a single high arch.

Municipality on the Sile at the edge of the Venetian lagoon, in whose territory stood the Roman city of Altinum, on the Via Annia: today the National Museum and the archaeological areas of Altino, part of the UNESCO site  "Venice and its lagoon," the seventeenth-century basin of Portegrandi and the naturalistic itineraries of the Sile Park.
The city theatre with the Sala Maggiore and the Sala del Ridotto, home to the seasons of concerts and shows.
The rebuilt cathedral.

A sandy strip between the lagoon and the sea with reeds, Mediterranean maquis, lagoon basins and jockeys of the Lipu Oasis, which can also be crossed by mountain bike; from the Visitor Centre there are guided tours of about an hour on the educational path on the catwalk (€2) and catamaran excursions to the Acquarotta Canal (€5).
Probably risen in the 13th century and transformed in the 17th century into a Doge's Palace, it dominates the village from above.

Historic plant named after the La Salute spring, inaugurated on 4 August 1901 after the first rudimentary baths of 1836; sulphurous waters rich in bromine salts and iodine (sources La Salute, Gisella, Pisciarello and Zolfanina, described already in 1576). It offers spa and wellness area with thermal pool, sauna and Turkish bath.
The fortress on the lake.
€5 unique ticket of the museum route; reduced €4, €3,50, €1
The ancient capital of the Monferrato dei Paleologi sul Po, with the castle, the cathedral of Sant'Evasio and one of the most beautiful synagogues in Europe.
Walking or mountain biking path along the Fersina which leads to the old sawmills, mills and one of the oldest mines in the valley, with the feeling, writes the portal, of an open-air museum.

The first giant bench, from which the designer Chris Bangle started, installed in 2010 just a few meters from the home of his creator. Red and accessible to all, look over the mountain arch of the Cuneo mountains.

Free entrance spa park with tour guide service, where you will find the Earth Cinema of Anish Kapoor, a large excavation in the ground that resounds of the sounds of the earth, and the Terzo Paradiso by Michelangelo Pistoletto; from May to October the Lucane Thermal Baths offer saunas, Turkish bath and emotional showers.
The noble palace that houses the municipality.
The life of the Bergamo fields between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, object by object.
An unusual medieval pillory.

In the Lariano Triangle, 754 m between the two branches of Lake Como, Magreglio is the village of Ghisallo: the sanctuary of Our Lady proclaimed patron of cyclists in 1949 and, next to, the Museum of Cycling; from the village a path in chestnut trees leads to Menaresta, source of Lambro.
The residence of the Marquis on the foundations of the castle.

In the "Baraccone" , rural building nineteenth century bought by the Municipality in 1996, panels and an audiovisual tell the transhumance: life and work of the shepherds, wool and cheese, temporary equipment and shelters; educational area and workshop of products related to transhumance, laboratory by reservation.

The cathedral on the piazza del Duomo, dedicated to the patron saint: since 1876 it houses the remains of Vincenzo Bellini in a funeral monument near a pillar of the right aisle and is home to the concerts of the Bellini Festival.

Inaugurated by the municipal administration in 1893 in the old district of Frontera de sa Mitza, it is a liberty structure similar to a temple in black trachyte of Serrenti, wrought iron and cast iron: cast iron columns hold the sheet metal cover over 36 masonry tanks covered with trachyte, with a fountain still active decorated with lion, lioness, siren and angel faces. The only survivor of a complex that included a slaughterhouse, loggia and watering trough, abandoned since the 1960s, was restored in the 1980s; it is located in the center, near the mill Cadoni and the church of Santa Barbara.
White alleys to the sea.
The story of a village hospital.
The face of the Gonzaga town in a few steps.

Small medieval village gathered around a castle of the year 1000 on Roman ruins, on the hills north of Orvieto; under the village the karst gorge of the Devil's Tane, with prehistoric finds, and the thermal waters of the Devil's Bath.
The Roman temple became Cosmatesque church.

Small village a few kilometers south with a fishing boat port and the typical bisse; there flows the Aril, referred to as the shortest river in the world (175 meters), which passes under three bridges, forms a waterfall and flows into the lake. On the port the Museum of the Lake exhibits fishing gear, objects of use and photos of ancient sailing boats.
The cork of Gallura, machine for machine.
The medieval origins of Franciacorta, among vineyards and hills.
The art of Emblem in the house and garden where it was born.
A green stop next to the abbey.
Water sweats and the history of the Ora of the Soana Valley.
In the square, the fountain "Arca di Noè" is carved by Arturo Martini, who lived in Anticoli for three years.
Caravaggio and Arcimboldi in Cremona.

Easy walk of 6 km round trip (1 h 45 min) from Roda towards Predazzo along the Avisio, in a protected area of the Reserve Network: panoramic walkway, two wooden bridges on the tributaries of the Lagorai, a birdwatching tower halfway and an observation point on the Greto. Symbol of the reserve is the alpine tamarisk, which grows almost only in this part of Trentino.
Church considered of the seventeenth century, dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, devotion very widespread in the village with celebrations every year.
MiC sources indicate openings only with guided tours on event dates, site closed on other days
The market is just a stone's throw from the Temple of Malatestano, with over 100 counters and the largest fish market in Emilia-Romagna, supplied daily by fishing boats.

The parish church of San Dalmazzo, whose current structure dates back to the 11th century, is an important place of worship of the Maritime Alps; the path, in three sections (museum, archaeological and parish), exhibits excavation finds and panels on the evolution of the building, with remains of Roman times and overlapping churches, and ends in the Romanesque crypt with elements of Lombard taste. Open on Sunday afternoon (June-October 15-19, November-May 14-18) with guided tours at every hour; better check it out first.

One of Gargano's largest historic centers: the Civita, the oldest nucleus that around 970 took the name of Vicus, and the Earth inside a walls with fourteen towers; below, the 17th century farmhouse. Fishbone alleys with arches, fireplaces of various shapes, houses with coats of arms and access ladders, stone portals.

2,190 hectares along the bed of the Stirone, almost dry in summer, where the entire series of marine clays of the Pliocene and the Lower Pleistocene emerges: rich in fossils, it is an open-air museum.
Art of the twentieth century in a private foundation.

On the south-west coast of Cagliari, Pula preserves the ancient city of Nora, founded by the Phoenicians and became Roman town hall, with spas, forum, mosaics and amphitheatre on the promontory; in the village the Patron Museum with excavations finds, on the bay the church of Sant'Efisio and along the coast the coves of Santa Margherita.
Ten minutes of steep climbing above the valley, on a Belle Époque plant.
Palace with Baroque garden and refined interiors, which tells the aristocratic life between the Seven and the Nineteenth Century; the garden is also seen from the walls.
Parish Church that houses ancient paintings (of the seventeenth century for VisitModena, of the eighteenth for Emilia-Romagna Tourism) and an organ of Agostino Traeri.
The large white building of Pio Piacentini on Via Nazionale, now home to exhibitions and culture.
The Etruscans in Rome.
On the trail of Montalbano.

Founded in 856, with quadriportico of the 11th century and basilica with three naves on 24 granite columns of 1120; destroyed by the bombings of 1943 and rebuilt by 1958. In the eighteenth-century crypt a Christ by Matteo Bottiglieri; the Lombard bell tower, rebuilt in Norman age, rests on Roman blocks.

City rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783 by the inhabitants of Castelmonardo on the model of the Philadelphia of William Penn: orthogonal plant in four quadrants, each with its own church, and a large central square; outside the village the Fontana Ficarazza and the ruins of the disappeared city.
The 17th-century mother church of the country.

Built in the early seventeenth century with irregular Greek plan, with bell tower in polychrome cones; it preserves a sixteenth-century wooden statue of Saint Stephen and a painting attributed to Giuseppe Salerno, the
The birdwatching paradise in Tuscany, just a stone's throw from the village.
The Caravaggio attributed and the treasure of Saint Agapito.
the MiC card indicates it closed every day and the abbey is under restoration after the earthquake

The town of Feltrino at the foot of the Dolomiti Bellunesi National Park, the gateway to Val Canzoi, the glacial valley of the Caorame stream with the gorges of Ponte Umin, the Stua lake and the ancient calchere; in Seravella the ethnographic museum of the Dolomites in a nineteenth-century villa, and in the village the historical museum of the bicycle.
Aversa is home to musicians Domenico Cimarosa, with his birthplace in the street of the same name and a monument in front of the station, and Niccolò Jommelli, born in via Constantinople.
The tradition of nets, the historical craft of the island.
The story of the chimney sweeps of the Orco Valley.
The Palladian Palace, the heart of the city.
The view of the sea and the valley.
Trento view from above in a few minutes.
Evening walk between yachts and docks.
A climb through the woods of the national park.
The church of the patron in the heart of the ancient village.
The oldest nucleus of the city with late-Gothic buildings, arches and courtyards, the shopping street that houses the Old Town Hall with the Historical Archives and the Mercantile Palace.

One of the largest and most important wetlands in northern Italy, in the Mincio Regional Park and in the Natura 2000 site and Valli del Mincio , which surrounds the village of Grazie; in 2009 it was among the five Italian towns awarded with the European recognition EDEN.

City with a chessboard plan with a Liberty centre around Via Cavour and Piazza del Popolo, where stands the neoclassical theatre named after the founder Vittoria Colonna; home of the Cerasuolo di Vittoria, the only Sicilian DOCG, and the door of the reserve of Pino d'Aleppo.

Municipality of the Livorno hills crossed in ancient by the Via Aemilia Scauri, then Medici villa and center of the Grand Duke's Farm; to see the Villa Medicea, the Pinacoteca Carlo Servolini, the Roman Mansio of Torretta Vecchia, the Aquedotto Leopoldino da Colognole and, in nature, the Park of the Livornese Mountains and the Oasis of the Countess.
A neighborhood church over the door.
The symbol of Manchester d'Italia.
Art on the roof of the Lingotto.
Vittone's masterpiece.

The seventeenth-century Palazzo D'Avalos with the chapel of Our Lady of Purity and St. Leo the Great (today the parish) and the church of the Annunziata of the seventeenth century, with on the main altar a canvas donated by Cardinal Orsini, then Pope Benedict XIII; in the center the monumental fountain "Munt Ercole" built after the Unity.
Today, the municipal auditorium preserves frescoes with the Madonna and Child attributed to Giovanni Santi, father of Raffaello.
Palms, Liberty and fine sand.
The only city of foundation recognized art city, according to Emilia Romagna Turismo.

Borgo dei Monti del Trasimeno overlooking the Nestor, between the lake and Città della Pieve, linked from the end of the thirteenth century to the art of glass brought by Venetian craftsmen, today told in the Glass Museum; in the territory the castles of Castiglion Fosco, Cibotola and Gaiche and, in Pietrafitta, one of the richest collections of fossil vertebrates in Italy.

Megalithic shrine and ceremonial area of the Copper Age (III millennium BC) on the plateau of Ossimo-Borno, on the hill of Anvòia, in a dense forest about 850 meters between two torrential valleys. Nine excavation campaigns, conducted between 1988 and 2002 by Professor Francesco Fedele with an international team, revealed four boulders lined with stylized faces engraved and, on the M3 mass, Remedello daggers; the originals were removed for preservation and replaced by resin reproductions. Free entrance and always visitable, with solutions for access to people with disabilities.
Asti's art.
Remains of a Roman domus between the 1st century BC and the 2nd A.D., which can be visited as a section of the civic museum.
The port where the fishing fleet disembarks: every morning, in the space near the port, the fish auction is held with the auctioneer by voice.
The medieval mother church.
The oldest defenses in the city.
Mountain fraction known for the springs and canals that cross it; buildings and machines for the weaving and grinding of wheat have been restored.
The monumental church of the Servants of the historic center, inserted in the itineraries of the churches of the city.
The shrine built by sinners.

Opened in 2007 in the house-study of the neoclassical painter Giuseppe Diotti (1779-1846), director and professor of the Carrara Academy of Bergamo, is the main headquarters of the Civic Collections of Art, with works from the late eighteenth century to today of the main local artists and temporary exhibitions.

Built between 1532 and 1622 on the previous Rocca degli Orsini on a project by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, from the early twentieth century it is the seat of the Town Hall; it can be visited underground caves.
A Barocci in the heart of the village.
The covered market of Via Flaminia in the structure of the early twentieth century belonged to the Ruffo family.

Industrial complex of 1874, built by Swiss entrepreneurs from which it takes its name (today Texcene SpA): the factory and the workers' houses are divided by the Serio, of which it exploited the waters, and connected by a stone bridge. From the second half of the twentieth century it is divided into small artisan activities, but the original structure is still well readable.

Set up in the rooms of the former restored prison, it exhibits objects of vinification and peasant life of a time in a path in four sections: environment, grape, cleft and religious rituals; woman and machines; in the cell of isolation the cholera revolt is linked to the epidemics of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; the house. A video shows the ancient traditions. Booking not required; MiC (2020) does not report up-to-date times.
The memorial of the fallen of 1867.
The octagonal tower of the emperor.

It is the main and oldest church of Casoria, attested by 1092; the present building, Baroque, was built between 1606 and 1621 and completed in the seventeenth century, and the Municipality is patron and owner of it. It houses works by Pietro di Martino and Giovan Vincenzo d'Onofrio called Forlì, including the altarpiece of the Madonna di Monserrato (1599), the last paintings by Domenico Antonio Vaccaro, a pipe organ of the eighteenth century and a ceiling with golden drawers of local carvers.
The lookout on the Strait.
Sanctuary dedicated to the Loverese saints Captain and Gerosa, a pilgrimage destination from all over northern Italy.
Rossini's life in ten rooms.

The Val del Riso mine is safely and open to the public recently and can be reached by a walk of about 10 minutes from Plassa. From the mountains of the valley were extracted blend, galena and calamine to obtain zinc, lead and sulfuric acid; the mines were opened by the Romans over two thousand years ago and exploited also by the condemned to forced labor.
Remains of a medieval signaling tower in the hamlet of Christ, reachable beyond the bridge of the dam of Piedilago.

It ruins in the coniferous forest of which only the massive mast remains standing, with walls about two meters thick; it is reached with the ring of 6.5 km from Stanghe that crosses the Gilfenklamm to Ponte Giovo and returns to the path 11A passing from the ruins.

Municipality of the Upper Germanasca Valley linked to the Waldensian history: at Balsiglia a small museum in the former school recalls the siege of 1690 after the Glorious Repatriation, and from here passes the hiking path that traces the last stages of the return of the Valdesi from exile.

Lake of mountain, the ancient Lacus Velinus, frequented for rowing and canoeing and with boat trips; on the shores the medieval village of alleys, stairs and arches, which between late June and early July hosts the Festa delle Acque.
The Romanesque bell tower just outside the walls.

Mother Church of Baselice, dated to the fourteenth century, near the Gate of Feet; it preserves an engraving dedicated to the Virgin of 23 March 1948 and, after the Second Vatican Council, the marble altar was brought to the center of the nave.
A mountain lake with the remains of an ancient customs.
A castle just a stone's throw from the hermitage.

Village of Etruscan origin, with narrow and paved alleys, medieval squares and exposed brick houses; the Arch of Bacchus has signs attributed to the temple presence. In the center the medieval palace of the Old Town, with the archive of local history, and the ancient fortress, former residence of the noble family. Guided walks by reservation with the Proloco.

An ancient mountain village on the southeastern slopes of Gennargentu, the bishop's seat of Ogliastra and the station of the Green Train: in the center the cathedral with the frescoes of Mario Delitala and the diocesan Museum, on the plateau of Selene the Nuragic archaeological park and, on Mount Armidda, the astronomical observatory.
The house of the witch is the historic house of the village that tells the witchcraft and the Inquisition in Sardinia.
Village of houses-towers and, near, the abbey of Santa Lucia di Roffeno.
Sandy beach about four kilometers long, part of the coast Blue Flag of Lavagna, indicated among the most beautiful seaside destinations of Liguria; also the marina has the Blue Flag.

It was mentioned for the first time in a document of 911, it was a fortified fence that in Baroque times became a noble country residence; it took its present form in the eighteenth century. From the medieval phase remain the corner tower of the thirteenth century, used as a lookout and last shelter, and the imposing walled wall; in the inner courtyard the cistern that would give the name to the village. You enter from an ancient arch with the coat of arms of Pope Innocent XII, memory of the lordship of the Church.

About 44 hectares of coast between Anzio and Lavinio, established regional reserve in 1988, with fossil dunes frequented by the grunts and Mediterranean maquis, rare rest of the ancient coastal forests of southern Lazio. The 16th century circular tower, built with materials of Roman buildings and arranged around 1565 by Marc'Antonio Colonna, defended from pirates; from the 16th century a sulphuratara was active, and on the promontory were emerged in 1999 remains of a Roman maritime villa of the I-III century AD. You can walk the Path of the Tower.
The water village.

The Town Loggia in Piazza del Popolo, dating back to the 13th century, is one of the few late medieval loggias that survived in Liguria and preserves a fifteenth-century fresco of the Annunciation. Around, via Guani with the Renaissance palaces (including the Palazzo delle Sirene at no. 37), via Garibaldi with painted facades and nine frescoed caricatures called "Grottesche" (Grottesche), the large medieval arches of Piazza da Passano and, between Via della Compera and the nearby alleys, the remains of the medieval port with a dock over 50 meters long. Cavour Square with arcades is the heart of the city.
A romantic park among statues, lake and islands.

Residence with two towers with rustic cantonals that recall the ancient strong houses, renovated in the eighteenth century with frescoes and period decorations. It is one of the stages of the Fontanile Cyclable.
19th-century building built on the beach for thalassotherapy, now home to exhibitions and events.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 5 of the 12 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

A common place at the foot of Monte Barro, a panoramic terrace overlooking the Brianza and the lakes of Como, Annone and Garlate protected by a regional park; the Hermitage the archeological area of Gothic age and the Archaeological Museum of Barro, in the medieval village of Camporeso the Ethnographic Museum of Alta Brianza, in Galbiate the eighteenth-century Villa Bertarelli with its historical gardens.

Among the first pedestrian areas of Milan's hinterland (eighties), the center has a path dedicated to silk: Piazza Gavazzi, where the spinning mill stood, with the statue of a baco; Piazza Repubblica with the sculpture of Nado Canuti on the metamorphosis of the baco; Piazza Matteotti with the fountain and a mulberry of about 130 years; Piazza Padre Giuliani with the row of mulberry trees; Piazza Unità d'Italia with the "Tuba Mirum" by Arman.
A miniature ladder.

With Palazzo La Marmora they form the Cultural Polo del Piazzo, seat of exhibitions; the octagonal tower of Palazzo Ferrero is one of the symbols of the city and from its gardens you can admire Biella.

Specialties of the village are the mostarda of figidindia, celebrated in October with the Festival of Mostarda and Ficodendia (edition 2026: 9-11 and 16-18 October), the cassatelle of the aunt nun and the driven out with wild vegetables and red oranges.

In the Palazzo della Cultura, a former Carmelite convent renovated in 2001 and became a cultural centre accessible to all: paintings and sculptures by many local artists, the Nojani Arts Hall, the studio room (Sala Pende) dedicated to Professor Pende, a Nojan scientist and a room with permanent exhibition on the painter Dyalma Stultus. An archaeological section tells of the findings of the sixth century BC. (vases, bronze armor, worked sheets, goldsmiths) of the peucet necropolis of the districts Cipierno, Trisorio and Calcàro, including a bronze belt with a quadriga in running; according to the Municipality and the MiC these finds are kept or exhibited in the archaeological museums of Bari and Taranto. Booking not necessary.
The smallest and worldly island of the Aeolian Islands.

Five winged lions in white marble, symbol of the Serenissima, which adorned the gates and walls of the fortress rebuilt at the beginning of the sixteenth century; today one is walled in the ramp of the bridge on the side of Porto, others are at the gymnasium of the Cotta High School and in the gardens of Via XX Settembre, and one in the courtyard of the Fondazione Fioroni. Always visitable.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Gabrielli the finds of the necropolis of the territory, from the bronze age to the late empire, with canopies, buccheri, fetid stone statues and the real-size reproduction of the Tomb of the Infernal Quadriga.
The most famous footpath in Garda.
The pure Renaissance, next to the market.
The costume of Letino's women.

Fort built in 1891 at over 700 meters above sea level against possible attacks from the Moncenisio, in control of the Val Cenischia and the Dora valley; perhaps remaking of a fourteenth-century fortification called "Castelluzzo" (Castelluzzo). Of almost triangular plant, it could accommodate 150 men and had a metal sliding caponier with machine gun, a unique in the Valley of Susa. After the Great War, it was a deposit of bullets, then abandoned around the mid-Twentieth century and sold by the State to private individuals.

The ancient capital of Sabauda at the foot of the Alps, the cradle of the Risorgimento: the Egyptian Museum, the Mole Antonelliana with the Cinema Museum, the Royal Museums and the Palazzo Madama in Piazza Castello, the Basilica of Superga.

Wanted by Teodoro Trivulzio on a project by Marco Antonio Barattieri (1620), a single nave, it is reached from a quadriportico with the chapels of the Via Crucis (Pietro Antonio Magatti, 1725). It preserves seventeenth-century wooden bas-reliefs by Antonio and Francesco da Sirone, a wooden altar painted by Luigi Miradoro (1652), a San Luigi by Daniele Crespi and wooden statues from 1584; the eighteenth-century cloister is by Carlo Francesco Monticelli. The convent, suppressed in 1780, was purchased by Mother Cabrini for the first house of the Missionaries.
Massa's living room.
