Founded in 1568 by Ulisse Aldrovandi, one of the oldest in Italy: about 2 hectares in the university area up to the ancient walls, with greenhouses and monumental trees.

Small church built in the Lombard period, probably on a Roman cemetery area, already owned by the bishop of Padua in 874. Rectangular plant with semicircular apse and a single nave with wooden trusses; it was parish until 1872. The next tower, of Carolingian origin, became bell tower; the municipal restoration ended in 1984.

Hiking ring (difficulty E, about 500 m of difference in altitude, from 2 to 3 and a half hours, recommended from April to October) that from Balmarossa climbs to Crestet, Varda and Maison to the church of San Luigi (1582 m), then to Mola, Cappelle and Potes, from which you can admire the waterfall of the Roc stream; beyond the bridge, Borgo Vecchio with the church of Sant'Antonio (1534 m), then the descent to the ruined villages of Ertà and Fregai up to Pianchette. Since 2000 the Park Authority has started the rehabilitation of the hamlets, rebuilding scenes of daily life like the school of Maison; around chestnuts, cherry trees, birch trees and a beech wood.
The thirteenth-century remains of the castle of the local lords, visible from the parish square.
The mother church next to the remains of the Dominican monastery.
Built in 1824 at the behest of Margherita Branciforte, Duchess of Mondragone, is the oldest preserved civil building in the country.

Fraction at about 180 meters above sea level, referred to as "Mons arduus" along the route of the Via Traiana; in the Middle Ages it was home to important schools of mathematics and music. It preserves the castle of the XV-XVI century and messapic remains: a walls of the fourth century BC, graves and foundations of buildings.

Medieval stone village on a spur overlooking Lake Turano, in the Natural Reserve Monte Navegna and Monte Cervia, dominated by the polygonal tower of the 11th century; in front, on Mount Antuni, the abandoned village with Palazzo del Drago and the Hermitage of San Salvatore.
Contemporary art and silk memory in five squares.
The medieval core at the top of the village.
The riding hall leaves its mouth open.
Protected natural area along the provincial Sefro-Sorti, with dense woods, undergrowth and the Scarzito stream, suitable for walks and bikes.

It was built by Filippo I d'Acaja between 1324 and 1332 as a fortress and was then transformed by the Savoys into a residence: Bona di Savoia and Cristina di Francia stayed there and in November 1562 Emanuele Filiberto signed the Treaty of Fossano; later it was the prison of the Waldenses and barracks. Four corner towers joined by crenellated walls, courtyard with loggia with fifteenth-century columns, the Room of the Grotesques frescoed by the Flemish Giovanni Caracca and a panoramic tower with views of the Monviso; in the sixteenth-century loggias the civic library (over 150,000 volumes). Guided tours only, from Wednesday to Sunday at 11 am and at 3 pm (reservation recommended); the route has about one hundred steep steps to spiral without handrail.

Country of the hinterland of the Costa degli Dei known for the rocky settlement of the Grotte degli Sbariati, the small Petra Calabrian , with dozens of environments dug into the rock from the 8th to the 11th century; complete the visit the Museum of the rocky and peasant civilization, the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Snow, the Grotto Trisulina and the abandoned village of Papaglioni.
Church of the fourteenth century with facade rebuilt in the sixteenth century, today seat of a small auditorium.
Paths between stain, prehistory and lake view.
Piacenza's living room.
The 18th century of the town hall.

At the entrance of the complex, reopened in summer 2004 after a large restoration: a centuries-old sequoia dominates the bottom of the garden, in front of old ginkgo; in the middle a baroque garden with flowers, medicinal herbs and a fountain. Open Monday to Saturday 10-17.
A Roman portal and Renaissance frescoes.
Late-gothic frescoes in a collected chest.
From 3 November to 28 February every day 8-17. In summer longer hours.
Mercantile Ferrara, perfect by bike.
A complete Etruscan town, from huts to graves, surrounded by greenery.
Wooden furnishings and a Madonna dei Del Maino.

Built in the second half of the sixteenth century by the Orsini di Gravina, feudal lords of Solofra, on a project by Flora Campanile and with decorations of cave workers; damaged by the 1980 earthquake and rebuilt in the original form, since 1993 it is the seat of the municipality. It has a corner turret at the viewpoint, a square courtyard with garden and well, a Renaissance staircase and frescoed rooms with the feuds of the Orsini.
Sicilian defense chess book.
The context before visiting the nuragic sites.
A high medieval church over a Roman station.
Eight centuries of history in a baroque mountain church.
Two floors with balconies at the top and wrought iron bras, garden with secular trees, neoclassical statues and master chapel; of the Murmura family since 1893.

Of Romanesque origin, it was rebuilt in the 15th century (the Gothic portal of the facade dates back to 1425) and then enlarged: the lateral aisles were extended east to the mid-19th century and the presbytery enlarged at the beginning of the 20th century.

The collegiate church of San Francesco dates back to 1265, renovated in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries; the church of Suffragio, reopened in 1779, preserves a painting by Claudio Ridolfi; the Addolorata, consecrated in 1755, has an organ of Callido above the entrance.
The terracotta houses and Bandello's house.
A Madonna by Francesco Laurana.
On the Piazzale del Castello the church of Santa Maria Assunta with panoramic views, and in the village the Santissima Annunziata.

A hilly area to the south-east of the Bazzanese state road with large oaks; there pass itineraries on foot or by bike like that of the Mostino and that from Monticelli to Montebudello and Acqua Fredda.
The two lakes of the Castles in one glance.
Conventual complex near the abbey, reachable on foot (XVI century second italia.it, XVII second Basilicata Touristica).
Church of fourteenth century origin with works by Calvart.
The grave of King Murat.

The Roman citadel, the medieval castle besieged by Barbarossa in 1155 and the fortress rebuilt in 1773 by Bernardino Pinto, razed to the ground by Napoleon in 1801; remains fragments of walls and the tower. The Torrione, 34 metres high and visible from the motorway, combines Art Nouveau and Medieval style.

Palazzo Gentilizio 19th century, house of the literary Marciano De Leo, today House of Culture with the Civic Library and the FriMact Museum, which combines an archaeological section on the history of the village with a collection of contemporary art among the three most important in Southern Italy.
The house of a doctor of the third century with mosaics and the richest surgical equipment of antiquity ever found, museumized where it was excavated.
A baroque residence of the Alfieri overlooking Langhe and Roero.
A fourteenth-century square-plan complex with shops on the ground floor and houses above, opened by three arches with the inscription of owner Nicola De Rubeis.
The village seen from below.
In the former Jesuit College built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, more than four hundred works from the Middle Ages to the end of the twentieth century.
Summer river baths.
Late-Medieval church that preserves a cycle of frescoes of the sixteenth century by Pietro Guido da Ranzo; it is the starting point of the ring of the waterfalls of the Arroscia.
The tomb between the cliff of São Paulo and a loop of the Tiber with the Roman funeral rites of the II-III century A.D.
The peasant life of Lunigiana inside a real watermill.
The most famous karst abyss on the plateau.
The seventeenth-century convent and its organ.
An ancient village at the gates of the Val Monastero.

Two routes of the reserve between canyons, gorges and monoliths: Petra Aggiallu (1.6 km, about 2 hours and a half, difficulty E, with the source of the Three Fountains) and Misorbo with the Campanaro stream (1.4 km, about 2 hours, difficulty E).

At the foot of the statue of the Redeemer, on Mount San Biagio, it preserves the relics of the patron saint; from here starts the procession of the feast of San Biagio, four days that close on the second Sunday of May.
The climb to the roof of the Pontine.
The heart of the country and the memory of July 1944.
Closed for transfer work at Forte Rivoli (comune page)
The 19th century theatre.
An enigmatic hypogeum of Roman age in the tuff.

At 1501 m, with a perimeter of 1,5 km, deep about 20 m and an area of about 58,000 m2, it is the largest of the Apennine lakes; it is reached by car and on foot and is starting point towards Mount Giovo (1991 m), which overlooks it with an overhang of 500 m, and the Rondinaio (1964 m).

Rebuilt between 1680 and 1715, perhaps by the same workers of the cathedral of Ales, on a Gothic-Aragonese church documented in 1524, of which remain the late dogotic apse with cruising vault and part of the sacristy; restored after the Second World War, it has eighteenth-century bell tower with dome of colored majolica. It preserves the retablo dell'Annunziata, signed and dated 1501 by Lorenzo Cavaro under the mantle of Our Lady, coming from the church of São Paulo di Serzela, and a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century.
Ruins overlooking the gulf.
A fountain with arches in the center.
From Villa San Giovanni the ferries and hydrofoils to Messina leave continuously; during the crossing you can see the Calabrian and Sicilian coasts and the reliefs of Aspromonte and Etna.
seasonal opening from the end of March to the beginning of November, in low season only some weekends (common calendar)
Camuni wooden altars and the Nativity palace.
The heart of the village and the traces of the power of the Centurione.
The history of the South Tyrolean apple in its common symbol.

Built in 1614 by Gianfranco Dagani with municipal funds and dedicated to the Madonna della Neve, it takes its name from the Adamino family owner of the land; bell tower, sacristy, vestibule and choir were added between 1670 and 1680.
A whole Roman city, with the inhabited theatre.
The hermit's cave.
The story of Piacenza in wax.
Pinturicchio and the Salimbeni.
The fortress in the throat.
Mountain contrasts and the head of the valley.

In the former Granatic Mountain of the mid-nineteenth century, exhibits ceramic, metal, vitreous and lithic finds of the territory from the fourth millennium BC to the third century AD, especially from the excavations of Su Mulinu, and illustrates the evolution of nuragic architecture. The strong piece is the life-size cast of the nuragic altar of the IX-VIII century B.C. in a scenic reconstruction; there is a section for the blind with captions in Braille and finds to touch. Admission fee, free for residents and children up to 6 years.

The medieval village was built in the early Middle Ages as a refuge from the Saracen incursions on the Roman Arce: the octagonal tower 25 meters high, commissioned in 1377 by Onorato I Caetani, is the only integral one of the twelve of the belt, destroyed by the bombings of 1943. A little below, the cavea of the Roman theatre of Augusta age rests on the hill facing the sea: today it is incorporated in over 70 houses, among which you can see columns, vaults and walls in cross-linked work.
A millennial church at the top of the promontory.
Renaissance in high altitude on the Sibillini.
The church of the patron.
The nuraghe of the fig tree and the baths of a Roman villa.
Fortress wanted by Cesare Borgia after the fall of Varano.

The country grows widely strawberries, blackberries, raspberries, black currants and blueberries: the small fruits "Sant'Orsola" are now sold all over Italy. In the local shops there are also honey millefiori of mountain, acacia and rhododendron, aromatized grappas and mixtures of herbal teas; two restaurants serve typical dishes.

Three itineraries between vineyards and woods in the places of the stories of Lajolo (the fortresses of Barbera, the green sea of the hills, the woods of the Saracens), starting from the cellar in San Pancrazio, on the border with Vaglio Serra, and from Piazza Vercelli. According to tradition on the Bricco dei Saraceni Aleramo defeated the Saracens in 935, and there was found a neolithic axe today at the Museum of Antiquity in Turin.

Rauscedo, the largest fraction, is called the world capital of barbatella for the wine-growing viticulture, largely cooperative, and is the birthplace of the painters Angiolo and Jacopo D'Andrea; the landscape is marked by the white stones of Meduna. The neoclassical parish church, built between 1845 and 1850 on a project by the Venetian Francesco Lazzari, houses a seventeenth-century altarpiece of the Coronation of the Virgin (property of the Academy of Fine Arts of Venice, attributed to Matteo Ingoli), the Nativity of Angiolo D'Andrea, a Transit of St. Joseph attributed to Michelangelo Grigoletti or Luigi Nono and a frescoed ceiling of the late nineteenth century with the Assumption.
The chestnut country.
Paleontological, mineralogical, zoological and botanical collections that illustrate the flora and fauna of the territory.
Adults full tour €14, short tour €12; children 3-10 years €9 / €7
An eighteenth-century theatre came back to life.

Borgo on the morainic hills of the lower Garda, dominated by the Visconti-Venetian Rocca of the Ugo Da Como Foundation with the House of the Podestà and its library of over 50,000 volumes; in the village the Civic Tower of 1555 and the Baroque Basilica, in the surroundings the Abbey of Maguzzano and the Roman Fornaci.

You enter from the Gate of St. John, in the walls presumably of the thirteenth century, between the Torrione and the Torre Grande. Along the Strada di Sotto the seventeenth-century Palazzo Rezza, partly leaning against the walls, and Palazzo Ianni; near Porta Maggiore Palazzo Fanelli (formerly De Vecchis, early seventeenth century) with a baroque balcony and frescoed andron, next to the church of San Nicola; near the Collegiata the complex of Palazzo Iacobelli (XVI-XVIII century) and far Morelli the massive Palazzo Boncompagni with buttresses, of the late sixteenth century.
Cassino's war seen by those who suffered it.
The town sanctuary full of stucco and marble.
open only on weekends from June to September with obligatory booking; in the other months visits by reservation (ValSeriana)
Calanchi, woods and balconies in the Maritime Alps.
The oratory of the feast of the sea.
Park with a panoramic terrace overlooking Lake Pieve.
The Sienese works of the sanctuary of Amiata.

Seaside town on the Ulysses Riviera, with the medieval district of Sant'Erasmo dominated by the Angevin-Aragonese castle, the Duomo with the Arab-Siculo bell tower and the complex of the SS. Annunziata; on the promontory of Monte Orlando the sanctuary of the Mountain Spaccata with the Grotta del Turco and the mausoleum of Lucio Munazio Planco, and about ten kilometers of beaches, including Serapo.

The old town preserves the medieval plant and numerous cavities dug in Renaissance age to extract the gray tuff, then transformed into cellars; the towers and cellars date back to the XIV-XV centuries. At the edge of the village stands the Angevin Tower, with a terrace.

In the noble house of the Lai family, it is dedicated to the cheese Fiore Sardo DOP: stone rooms with barrel vaults for sensory paths and tastings, traditional and modern tools of the cheesemaking with photographs of the Slovenian Žiga Koritnik, the documentary "Fiore Sardo" by Fabio Olmi and a plan for temporary exhibitions. A cumulative ticket with the Porcu Satta Museum House €7, reduced €5.

The present church, built in 1802 by Pietro Maggi, has a single nave decorated in the early twentieth century by Giuseppe Pauri and an organ by Carlo Carlo Carletti installed in 1884; reopened after the restoration concluded in 2002, it houses the Museo Sistino with the cup donated by Sisto V to his birthplace, a medal with the effigy of his sister Camilla Peretti, the Sacred Conversation of Vincenzo Pagani and two tables by Vittore Crivelli with San Rocco and San Sebastiano.
Walk along the Castellum Novum towers.
The itinerary of medieval churches with the alternation of white Carrara marble and green Prato.
The view of the village and the plain from the hill.

On a low hill at the first slopes of Gargano, Apricena links its name to a hunting legend of Frederick II, who often stayed here: in the historic center the Baronial Palace rises on the ruins of the castle federiciano, the clock Tower and the Civic Museum in the eighteenth century Palazzo Paolicelli; in the country the ruins of the monastery of St. John in Piano.
The eighteenth-century stuccoes of the village of San Bernardino.
Medieval ruins with outdoor frescoes.

Country of the Logudoro with the necropolis of Sant'Andrea Priu, about twenty domus de janas with the Tomb of the Cape transformed into a frescoed rock church, since 2025 among the seventeen Sardinian necropolis UNESCO Heritage; in the territory the almost abandoned village of Rebeccu, the nuragic source of Su Lumarzu, the Romanesque San Lorenzo and, in the village, the civic archaeological museum.
Around Monte Nerone there are trekking trails of various difficulty, and dirt and asphalt roads for the bike: Apecchio is a stop of the High Marche Apennines.
The antelamic façade of pilgrims.
Overlooking the vineyards of the Langhe with the Alps in the background.
A walk through white houses and churches, with traces of the Knights of Malta.
The ritual carnival of the Upper Monferrato.
Free access with offer

Water-based silk yarn with the rotating shaft still visible, rare testimony in Europe: at the beginning of the nineteenth century there were three torcoils on five floors, moved by a hydraulic wheel, and a canning machine.
The hooked pine forest.
The road in the rock.
The customs of the Albanian tradition of Calabria.
A promenade icon.
The young Cimabue to see closely.
Painted facades on the square.
The Madonie peasant life.
Area with the remains of the forensic complex and some patrician houses.
Città della Rocca sforzaesca e dell'Autodromo, with a historic centre full of buildings and civic museums.
Olive groves, vineyards on terraces and lemon groves covered by nets, with the sea visible almost everywhere.
The large cathedral next to the Round.
A Romanesque church with baroque furnishings in the village linked to Lucrezia Borgia.

400 hectares protected between Cinigiano and Arcidosso, between 800 and 1,000 meters, with views of Valle dell'Ombrone, Monte Amiata and Val d'Orcia; black pines, firs and centuries-old chestnuts alternate with meadows and shrubs, with species such as Linaria purpurea and Viola Etrusca.
A museum to listen to and touch on the life of the Lepini.

Città sul Po, known as the international jewelry centre, started around 1840 by Vincenzo Morosetti: in the centre the Cathedral of Santa Maria Maggiore, rebuilt in the seventeenth century, Palazzo Valentino and Palazzo Pellizzari; along the river the remains of the walls and the Garzaia, the historical nucleus of the river park.
Antonelli and Luca Giordano in the symbol church.
Medieval auctions on foot.
The hill of the Roman Tergeste.
Two churches one above another inside a tower.
The 16th century wooden altar.

Small church outside the walls of the castrum, the oldest building in Castelseprio and the only surviving destruction of 1287. The apse preserves a cycle of frescoes with the infancy of Christ also drawn from the apocryphal gospels, dated between the VII and X century, with techniques of Roman ancestry and oriental influences: one of the most important testimonies of the European early medieval mural painting. She's deconsecrated today.
A key place in the memory of the Friulian Resistance.
The fortress disguised as a church.

Marsicano village at the foot of the Velino massif, overlooking the Palentine Fields; in the hamlet of Rosciolo, fortified village in the fifteenth century, rises isolated among the oaks Santa Maria in Valle Porclaneta, one of the most important examples of Abruzzo Romanesque.

Country of the Canavese at the foot of the Serra d'Ivrea, dominated by the Castle of Masino, residence for over nine centuries of the Valperga and today well of the FAI, with park, 18th century labyrinth and museum of carriages.
Walk up from Greve among the olive trees.
The Doria Castle.
Rural park of over 5,000 hectares of olive groves, with pajare (ancient dry construction), canals, ponds and paths.

Village on the Veronese shore of Garda, with the historic center of fishing houses, the lakefront and the church of San Zeno, one of the most important Carolingian monuments in Italy; in Cisano the Romanesque parish church of Santa Maria and the Museo dell'Olio tell the landscape of olive groves and vineyards that surround the village.
The sixteenth-century stone portal.
The religious heart of the country.

The portal in travertine with concentric arches with the small figure of San Ginesio is of the 11th century; the upper part of the terracotta façade was built in 1421 by a German master. Inside the wooden Crucifix reported by the exiles in 1450, works by Federico Zuccari, Pomarancio and Simone De Magistris and the crypt frescoed by Lorenzo Salimbeni in 1406.
The country from above.
An intimate complement to the visit of the Morandi Museum.
17th century Cathedral of the diocese of Ogliastra, with frescoes by Mario Delitala on the life of Mary Magdalene and Christ.
At the municipal woods, it preserves the image of Our Lady of the Bosco, brought in procession to the Mother Church on Tuesday after Easter and accompanied back to the sanctuary in August.
Upstream the country the large artificial invades for electricity, the dams of the Plate and Chiotas at about 2000 meters.
Neoclassical building which is an exact copy of the Pantheon of Rome.

A city founded in 403 B.C. by Arconides, tyrant of Herbita, on a hill above the Tyrrhenian coast and the valley of Tusa; the first Sicilian city to take sides with Rome in the first Punic War, was one of the five  "civitates liberae et immunes" and was abandoned at the time of the Arab occupation. You can visit the walls of the fourth century BC with towers and two gates, the agora of the second century BC with colonnade portico, the cardo maximus, two houses peristilius, the bases of two temples on the acropolis (one perhaps dedicated to Apollo) and the church of Santa Maria delle Palate; the Antiquarium exhibits Greek and Latin sculptures and epigraphs from the second century BC to the third AD.
The Christ of Easter Rites.

The capital lies on a hill opposite Monte Ramaceto, which shelters it from the weather: it is a linear village, with the houses arranged in ribbon on the sides of the parish of Maria Annunciata. In church a shovel attributed to G. De Ferrari with the appearance of Christ to Saint Catherine and the statue of Saint Catherine of Genoa carved in 1860 by Paul Olivari; in May the feast of the saint involves the whole village.
The Franciscan cloister of the fifteenth century.
Roman epigraphs in a baroque palace.
Thousand trulli uphill, UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Renovated village, Alta Via stage n. 2.
Where tradition places the birth of the Third Order.

Borgo dei Castelli Romani at 680 meters, in the Regional Park of the Roman Castles, collected under the Pontifical Fortress mentioned already in 1181 and the Geodynamic Observatory that houses the Geoscience Museum; around, more than 1,400 hectares of wood with the Sacred Way towards Monte Cavo, the Campi di Annibale and the Pratoni del Vivaro.
Small hill near the village with the rock split in two, called "jacca" (crack, in dialect): tradition wants it to be opened when Jesus died on the cross.
A fifteenth-century mill with machinery still in place.
The art sent by post, in a unique museum in Italy.
The botanical garden of the University, in the city museum system reported by Terre di Siena.
The traces of the Lagorai front collected in a mountain hut.

It combines a high medieval baptistery with circular plan, the Round, and a rectangular nave probably added from the twelfth century; the baptismal font of the V-VI century, brought to light by the excavations of 2014, is one of the rare early Christian baptisteries of southern Italy. Inside frescoes from the 13th to the 1st 15th century, with the most important phase in the 14th century. According to the municipality the name of the city could derive from this building.

Country at the foot of the Alburni Mountains known for the Pertosa-Auletta Caves, karst complex crossed by the underground river Negro that is visited in part by boat, and for the integrated Museums of the environment (MIdA) dedicated to karstism, archeology of the caves and soil.

In a typical building with wooden loggia, on the ground floor reconstructs the workshops of bricksmiths, blacksmiths, roasters, slippers, slippers and carpenters with their tools; on the upper floors houses an entomological collection indicated among the five largest in the world. The route is connected to the Museum of Natural Sciences; visits to be agreed.

Ruin of a early Christian church, probably the oldest ruin of Tyrol's church. It is the final destination of the Path of Peace (about 3 hours, 100 m of difference in altitude, almost flat in the mixed woods), of which it is the seventh stage ("Amore"); Altenburg also arrives the High Path of Caldaro and other routes.

On the hill that dominates the city, with square plan with cylindrical towers at the corners; it bears the name of the fifteenth-century leader Nicola Monforte, count of the city after the earthquake of the mid fifteenth century. From the top the view reaches Majella and the Table-table; on the same hill remain ruins of a Sannitic fortification.
Quiet and sheltered bay, already seaside resorts in the Austro-Hungarian era, with marina, establishments and clean beaches between maquis and karst rocks.

Metalworking, from gold to wrought iron, was for a long time the economic engine of Agnone: a copper foundry existed already in 1754, moved by the waters of Verrino, the Statutes of 1456 regulated the trade and the Occiary Catasto of 1753 had more than 150 families of now. The Historical Museum of the Gerbasi copper shows the phases of processing and finishing with a cantilever; in the village there are still workshops of copper and wrought iron.
About 10 km of golden sand at the foot of the village, with clear water; Blue Flag in 2024 and one of the 10 beaches Green Flag of Lazio, suitable for children.
Historical trains of the lines of Lake Maggiore.

Church already existing in 1100, preserves pictorial evidence of different eras, including a Mercy, and two statues of San Domenico and San Giovanni Battista attributed to Giovan Battista Crespi called Cerano, a painter from Lombardy of the seventeenth century.
A 15th-century fresco with the knights.
Museum of the center, among the attractions indicated by the regional portal.
The villa is closed for restoration; the park is open to the public during the day all year round
The red pits of bauxite in the heart of the Murgia.
Green in 28 paintings inside a seventeenth-century court.
The symbol of the Turritan port.

Built between 1702 and 1721 with a Latin cross with three naves on the model of St. Matthew in Palermo, it has the high altar of 1765, the choir of the Cotton brothers (1910) and an organ of the Cimino brothers inaugurated in 2006. Among the works the SS. Trinity attributed to the Zoppo di Gangi, the Baptism of Jesus of Lo Cascio, the golden statue of the Madonna del Carmelo, patron saint of the zolfatari, and a Saint Francis of Paola carved in a trunk of pear; in the crypt a collection of nativity scenes visitable especially at Christmas.

In the rooms of Palazzo Beltrami once destined for servitude, he exhibits the traditional Marche farm wagons, known for their lively decorations, and tells the story of peasant life. Opening by reservation through Pro Loco or Tourist Office.

Medieval village on one of the highest hills of Monferrato, among the nine municipalities of the core zone In the center of the eighteenth century Palazzo Callori, seat of the Regional Winery of Monferrato; every summer the Vignale Monferrato Festival brings to the village the international dance.

Borgo documented from the Middle Ages, on three parallel roads (via Buonarroti, via Vergara, via Roma) joined by narrow and steep stairs, with two doors: the Porta Vecchia with round arches and "U Spurt" , incorporated in the Baronale Palace; remain drinking troughs, the wash-house of the Old Fountain and the cellars.
Romanesque, baroque and civic art gallery.
The castle of Dante and Urban VI.
Minor pontifical basilica that holds important works of art.

Medieval village of the Upper Tiber Valley closed by walls, with the sixteenth-century castle of the Bourbon del Monte, lords of an imperial marquisate from 1250 to 1815, today Palazzo Museo; near the parish church of Santa Maria with the chapel of the Marquis and, in the surroundings, the castle of Lippiano.
The architect of the Mole works in a lowland country.
The great Sardinian-American sculptor in his home country.
Common Orange Flag of the Upper Lake Maggiore formed by three villages, Trarego, Cheglio and Viggiona, in the green basin of Mount Carza with views of the lake.
From the lake to the ridge of Baldo in a few minutes.
In a 14th century palace, it recalls the famous challenge between Italian and French knights.
The historical halls of the books.

Permanent exhibition on the geomorphology of the Park: the natural forces that shape the environment, the composition and degradation of the rocks, the evolution of the Alps and the glacial landscape of the valley. Space also to the imprint of man (mines, stone in mountain architecture, water control) and to the bond with ibex, chamois, marmot and eagle; a plastic shows the rocks of the Park, a documentary project hall shot in the Park and a comic book path for children is guided by the Stamby ibex. Tel. 0124 901070.
The Norman portal of a church that was in ruins.
17th century church in the historic core of Busache's and Susu, with a 48 meters high bell tower and majolica dome. The patron saint is celebrated in mid-June.

Built in about two centuries above the Constantinian basilica of 320, with the dome of Michelangelo completed by Della Porta and Fontana and works by Bernini, Maderno, Borromini and Canova; below, the Vatican Caves and the tomb of Peter.
From the keep, hills and vineyards.

On the hills of Paradiso and Castellaccio, separated by the gorge of the Caurga, ancient Roman quarry of ollar stone, and connected by a suspended walkway; since 1955 it is part of the Museum of Valchiavenna, with rare flowers, walls and fortifications and an archaeological path in four sections from Prehistory to the Middle Ages. From Tuesday to Sunday 10-12 and 14-18 (17 in winter), Monday closed.
A new Florentine land with its walls.
Seriously damaged by the 2012 earthquake, not open to visitors: only seen from outside

Small rectangular church with semicircular apse and a nave on the right side; the apse and the walls of the left side, perhaps of the XI-XII century, are the oldest parts of the original Romanesque building, then very transformed.
Fossil fish, minerals and dinosaurs in a lime furnace.
On Piazza Sant'Eusebio, it preserves documents of great historical importance.
A walled village in the vineyards.
The front of the port of Oneglia between the commercial pier and the Long Pier, with the headlight and an atmosphere of sea.
The fourteenth-century church rebuilt in 1725 by Giovan Maria Ferraroni, next to the former convent today Palazzo dei Musei.

Brick church of the first thirteenth century in Certaldo Alto with the cenotaph of Boccaccio, the bust of the poet of Giovan Francesco Rustici (1503), two Robbiani tabernacles and a Romanesque cloister on two floors; in the canonical there is the Museum of Sacred Art.

Città dell'Oltrepò Pavese gathered around Piazza Duomo, with the collegiate church of San Lorenzo started in 1605, the neoclassical Palazzo Gounela and the Social Theatre of 1845; not far away the Visconti Castle of 1372 and, in the former Caserma of Cavalleria, the historical Museum Giuseppe Beccari and the Museum of Natural Sciences G. Orlandi.
the MiC card indicates it closed every day; check with the Municipality (0743 93781)
Renaissance marbles in fractions.
The municipal territory is entirely included in the Ticino Park.
Built at the beginning of the eighteenth century with the contribution of the Marquis Anna De Guevara, wife of the Prince of Avalos, to give hospitality to the pilgrims of the Via Francigena.

The old town has concentric streets around the main square, where the Palazzo dei Priori, rebuilt by Antonio Lombardo in 1467, with five-arch loggia and the large arch towards Palazzo Compagnucci, overlooks; in the Council Hall a Madonna in throne between saints and musical angels by Johannes Hispanus (1506).

The parish church was rebuilt after the earthquake of 1805 on a project by Berardino Musenga; Count Giuseppe Zurlo supported the works and donated a rich collection of paintings, much of the country's artistic heritage.
Visits by reservation through the I.A.T. Point.
The postcard of Tuscany.

Information and environmental education center dedicated to the hinterland of Garda, born to unite the coastal and the mountain belt: the route combines images, sounds, reconstructions of environments, naturalistic collections, old working tools, videos and interactive stations, with paths marked to the outside.

The castle, probably of Byzantine origin and devoid of decorations, became a military fortress under the Ventimiglia; the ruins remain on a difficult height to reach, chosen for its strategic and panoramic position, reached by the Via Biscucco paved in stone. Next to it, the little church of St. Anne was the chapel of the Ventimiglia: according to legend the skull of the saint was kept there from 1242 and then transferred to Castelbuono.
Casino built at the beginning of the twentieth century on the sea, set of "Amarcord" by Fellini and scenes of "Polvere di stelle" (Polvere of stars).
Cold water for the feet and a waterfall between the farms.
The church of Our Lady of the Heart.
Fresh water source that forms a small lake with papyrus, on the seafront of Ortigia; next to the Old 18th century wash-house, open for free.

The most evocative monument of the city and symbol of the local military architecture: the first fortifications on the two banks of the Adige go back to the 10th century, in defence of the river port; in 1475 the Venetians rebuilt the fortress with walls, moat and four round corner towers, one of which reached us. Visitable from the outside.
One of the oldest and most important cathedrals in Molise.
Carnival and barbaric life in a manor house.
The basilica of the sixth century was obtained from the Temple of Romulus on the Forum.

Borgo della Carnia at 560 meters in the valley of Tagliamento, already mentioned in 762 as \vicus Ampicio and in 1944 capital of the Free Zone of Carnia; Palazzo Unfer brings together the exhibition on the Resistance, the Geological Museum of Carnia and the Pinacoteca Marco Davanzo, in front of the cathedral of San Daniele and the seventeenth-century Palazzo Beorchia-Nigris.
The entrance to the ancient city.

Built in the fifteenth century by Count Giorgio Maffei next to the family palace and donated in 1499 to the Confraternita dei Disciplinati, it was enlarged and renewed in Baroque forms from the second half of the seventeenth century to 1779. It has a hut façade, a large hall with wooden trusses and, beyond the presbytery, the fifteenth-century vaulted building used as a meeting room, with frescoes restored in 2008. The marble main altar houses the altarpiece of Orazio Farinati with the Visitation of Our Lady to Saint Elizabeth and Saints Joseph and Zechariah.
Golden wooden altars of the seventeenth century.
17th century turret with a small museum.
The church of the Augustinian monastery.
The Etruscans of the lake, perhaps the ancient Sabbath.

Museo dell'Ecomuseo del Lago d'Orta e Mottarone dedicated to the relationship between man and water: it was born from the permanent exhibition "L'uomo e l'acqua" opened on April 15, 1995. About three hundred finds of industrial archaeology tell the evolution of the tap and craft techniques, with the copy of a faucet of about 25 AD from the villa of Tiberius in Capri; it also explains the birth of the industrial district of the tap and valve in the Cusio. Upstairs totem on the latest innovations; accessible with elevator.
The building where Murat slept.

Roman city buried in 79 A.D. by pyroclastic flows: are preserved upper floors, carbonized organic matter and everyday objects such as food and wood furniture; between the buildings the gym, two thermal complexes, the College of Augustals; along the ancient beach were found about 300 skeletons.
Built in the seventeenth century by the Moscow family, with Italian garden and water games; Casanova and Stendhal stayed there.
Natural starting point: from here the whole center turns on foot under the arcades.

Deconsecrated church built before the 14th century, called the "Sistina" of Bormio: the interior is decorated with frescoes of the Four-Fifteenth century dedicated above all to the Trinity and the Holy Spirit, with the Annunciation in the presbytery, saints wanted by private clients on the walls and once sixteenth century with Trinity, Apostles, Virgin, Evangelists, Fathers of the Church and Prophets.
A district of Norman times that preserves a gate and a stretch of walls; there is the Sanctuary of the SS. Trinity with the original statue depicting the mystery of the Trinity.

Emerald-coloured bay about 14 kilometers from the village, with golden sand with big grain, clear rocks on the sides and three large rocks reachable on foot on the bottom; behind the pond of sos Alinos, with reeds and agaves, where they nest water birds. A pine forest leads to Cala Ginepro and the small beaches of sas Linnas Siccas and sa Curcurica. In summer you can enjoy underwater fishing, surfing in winter; free entrance, parking, rental, refreshment and access for disabled people.
In the basement of the Town Hall: a Roman cryptoportico, inscriptions, capitals and sections of polygonal walls of the fourth century BC, with a reproduction of the Verolani Fasti.

The National Park of Peace, established in 2000, includes the hills around the village; a paved path beyond the museum rises to Col di Cava along the stations of the Way of the Cross, which bring the Passion of Christ to the scenes of the massacre. On top of the Ossuario, a stone tower 12 metres high with four arches designed by the architect Tito Salvatori and carved by Vincenzo Gasperetti, with a plaque bearing the names of the identified victims.
Towers and walls of the thirteenth century.
The path of pilgrims among the olive groves of the olive grove of Gaeta.

Opened on 4 November 2006 on the ground floor of the former Granaio Massimo, on the course of Borgo San Bartolomeo, it is dedicated to the musical culture of Arsoli and the Aniene Valley in four sections: pastoral instruments (flauts and clarinets of cane, flutes of bark, horns, bells), artisan instruments (organetto, putipù, triangle, tambourines), instruments of the rite (raganelle, battole, shells, with ample space to the Pilgrimage of the Holy Trinity) and band tradition, with nineteenth century brass and documents of the band of Arsoli, some of the eighteenth century. Many objects are gifts of the inhabitants and of the Maximus family. Opening hours: mon-ven 9.30-12.30, sab-dom 9.30-12.30 and 15.30-18.30, Tuesday closed.

First certain date on 778, when the Longobard Duke Ildebrando of Spoleto gave the church to the abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno; in the eighteenth century Gaspare Capricci frescoed it with stories of the saint and on the counterfaced the Hunting of merchants from the temple. Keep a collection of ex-vote and the simulacrum of the saint; you climb there with steep stairs up to Largo San Donato.
Visit by arrangement by reservation
In a 16th-century building in the historic centre, with the Galleria d'arte moderna e contemporanea.
The green along the Soča.
The heart-shaped lake.
It is part of a neoclassical itinerary that includes the Masini Theatre and the Laderchi Palace.

Church with original structure of 1494, transformed at the end of the nineteenth century, which preserves Gothic traits in the central nave and the pentagonal apse. Outside there is a fresco of the 15th century of the Virgin with the Child in terracotta arches; inside there are nineteenth-century frescoes by Netu Borgna, eighteenth-century wooden sculptures and a white stone stove from 1563.

He collects paintings of Italian and foreign artists of the twentieth century, acquired over time by Pro Loco, with donations of Amadio, Carma, Casals, Eolo and Raffaele Costi, Fiore, Le Donne, Marconi, Ragionieri and Sernia.
The "Salotto dei Sassaresi" (Saints Hall), with the monument to Vittorio Emanuele II in the center; with the Fountain of Rosello is the symbol of the city.
open Saturday and Sunday 10-19, on weekdays only by appointment (MiC)

Probably born at the end of the 11th century as a Romanesque church with a single nave, of which traces remain as the bell tower, older than the church; enlarged and reduced in Baroque forms, it was reconsecrated on July 30, 1758. At the altar of St. Anne one of the first works of Carlo Francesco Nuvolone (the canvas of 1645) with the Madonna and Child between St. Anne, St. Joseph and St. Vincent; on the left entering a fresco of St. Defender of the Gagnolesque school. Open 8-12 and 15-19.
The artist's house of Alessandro Morani.
A green stop on the Francigena.
Next to the Fortress.
Large red bench in the Roncogennaro area.

A sea town born around the Swabian Castle, wanted in 1229 by Federico II as port of Recanati and defended by pirates, which today houses the Moroni Art Gallery, the archaeological exhibition     . Divi & Dei , and the Arena Beniamino Gigli; to the south the remains of the Roman city of Potentia and the abbey of Santa Maria in Potenza.
Where the first country was born.
The museum on the acropolis of ancient Teate.
The art on the walls.
The village of the Cesi at slow pace.
Our Lady who named Buenos Aires.

The hills between Vulture and Murge, which grew up around the castle that Frederick II used as a hunting lodge; along Corso Manfredi, the Palazzo d'Errico houses the Pinacoteca with almost three hundred paintings collected by the patron Camillo d'Errico.
The theatre of the first century B.C. just outside the center.
The heart of the protected marine area, between coves and dives.

An ancient statue of the Madonna from the Cistercian monastery is on display on the altar, which gave its name to Villa Monastero. In Varenna, Cardinal John Henry Newman, canonized in 2019, wrote the litany of our Lady, published in the book Il pilgrimo (London, 1853).

Built in 1730 and consecrated in 1739 for the Confraternita dei Battuti Rossi, it is the work of Monregalese Francesco Gallo, who had also built the adjoining hospital; Greek cross plan, squares of the brothers Pozzo, frescoes by Michele Antonio Milocco, stuccos by Beltramelli and Barelli and twelve wooden lacquered matrons from which the sheltered follow the functions. Open on Sundays from 15 to 18.30.
The most photographed port of Desenzano.
In the ancient monastery of Santa Scolastica, in the historical and archaeological core of the old town, the archaeological museum with more than 30,000 finds and a medieval church with necropolis.
Works of 1,400 years of history, from the treasure of the Longobard kings to the gifts of Napoleon.
Cloister of the fourteenth century, today seat of the Town Hall.
In the first half of the fifteenth century, it replaced the church of San Pietro alla Rocca and was renovated in 1731; it preserves the plaque of Bishop Leone (VIII-IX century).
Green and views of the Comino Valley.
Where the Verdi musician was born.

Parish church on the ridge of the hill of the medieval village, on the site of a Norman fortified garrison: built in Renaissance forms in the sixteenth century after the earthquake of 1456, with the eastern tower transformed into a circular bell tower with spiral staircase. It was collapsed in the earthquake of July 26, 1805, which killed 136 people, and was rebuilt in 1806-1808 with the help of the emigrants; the façade, collapsed for the war, was rebuilt in 1945-1949. It preserves a baptismal font of 1552, early seventeenth-century saintshop and a wooden statue of Our Lady with the Child of Paolo Antonio di Zinno (1755).

Established in 2001, it covers 3,626,94 hectares between Acqualagna, Cagli, Fermignano, Fossombrone and Urbino: a limestone gorge excavated by Candigliano between Monte Pietralata and Monte Paganuccio, with jurassic layers and clay rich in ammonites. Leccete, oaks, a beech forest on the Paganuccio and highland meadows; a couple of royal eagles have been nesting there for years, along with the pilgrim hawk, and in the woods live wolf, roe deer and deer.
In the center of Montaione the civic museum, which preserves the fossil of a whale of the Pliocene, the Palazzo Pretorio and the parish church of San Regolo.
Border village on the hill above the Valtiberina, where Piero della Francesca painted the Madonna del Parto.
The oldest building in Grazzano, with its current appearance due to a 17th century redecoration; inside the chapel of Our Lady of Lourdes with numerous ex-vote.

In the Nuraghe Talia a fig tree grown inside has helped to preserve seven rows of stones; near a small thermal plant of imperial age, part of a villa, with four rooms, marble coverings and traces of mosaics.

Gothic church at the top of the hill, mentioned in a papal bull of 1058 and renewed in the fourteenth century, with frescoes of Umbrian and Perugia school; next to the few remains of the fortress destroyed by Pope Leo X in 1517.
Walk between the ancient village and the lake.

Country of the chamois in the Majella National Park, between the river Aventino and the slopes of the Monte Amaro: at the Visit Center there are the Archaeological Naturalistic Museum "Maurizio Locati" , the botanical garden "Michele Tenor" and the fauna area of the chamois; above the village there are the Cavallone Cave, between the highest visitable caves in Europe, and the Cave of Sant'Angelo.
Donkeys closed from end 2023 for Garisenda's safety work. The reopening does not have a certain date: the local press indicates as hypothesis the 2028. Alternative: Clock Tower.

In a typical campidano house, it tells the wild horses of the Giara, the last survivors of a species once diffused throughout the island and considered introduced by the Phoenicians: photo gallery on the life cycle, the environment of the plateau, the tools for tamination, ironing and marking (now replaced by microchip). An ethnographic section, with objects donated by the inhabitants and video-interviews to the elderly, documents the agropastoral culture; educational space for schools and families.
The Duomo on the ancient forum.

Castle of the ninth century with three walls, to protect the lord, soldiers and the population; today remains imposing ruins of towers and walls in a very panoramic position. At his feet the village of Tribbio with Palazzo Simonelli and the former church of Santa Lucia, partly frescoed; not far from the church of San Benedetto. Montalto was the scene of the massacre of 32 young partisans by the Nazis.
The hole linked to Ottaviano and the House of the Knights of Rhodes, a building born from the stratification of several centuries overlooking the Forums.
The towers that characterize the city, such as the Julia de Jacopo Tower and the Clock Tower, with Palazzo Visconti and the Town Hall from the neoclassical portico.
The terracotta of Sansovino and Della Robbia.
To the north of the village, the slopes of Aspromonte plunge into the sea forming natural caves, which can be visited or used for underwater fishing.
The square dominated by the statue of Dante, next to the Scaligere Arches and the Palazzo della Ragione.
Three wars on a strategic border.
The Norman cathedral on the sea.
The goddess of the woods.
The pulpit of lions and the source of the fifteenth century.
In the Park, connected by a boulevard of hornbeams; the Mirabellino was the favorite residence of Eugenio di Beauharnais.
Protected wetland between Castelfranco Emilia and San Giovanni in Persiceto, with water mirrors and reeds where you can observe herons, wild ducks and swamp hawks from huts and paths.
A Romanesque church on the Arno with Gothic and Renaissance frescoes from Piero's school.
The stories of the Eolian immigrants in the world.
One of the best readable Canavesian recipes, with fifteenth-century frescoes.
The most imposing Doric temples of Selinunte.
Paths between maquis, sea and Roman ruins.
Rembrandt and Dürer inside an abbey.

Country of the Spluga Valley, in a narrow glacial valley born from the union of several nuclei, linked to the traffic with Switzerland along the Via Spluga; you can visit the Museum of the Via Spluga, the bridge called Roman on the Caurga della Rabbiosa and Fraciscio the birthplace of Saint Luigi Guanella.
The court church of the Gonzaga.
Ancient stronghold of the dukes of Ventimiglia, with cobbled alleys, squares, the ancient walls, the Parliament Loggia and the sixteenth-century palaces of Via Garibaldi.
The palace of Nerone started after the fire of A.D. 64, whose remains are visited under the Oppio Hill.
One of the great art galleries in Italy.
Seven kilometers of coast between Valverde, Villamarina, Zadina and Ponente.

In the marble basins between Ravaccione and Fantiscritti, a tunnel cave dug since Roman times: the large rooms of the marble cathedral, the extraction machinery and the Ozmo mural on Michelangelo's Genesis.
The 67 meters high bell tower overlooking the square, from which you photograph the Baptistery "face to face."
The Gothic-Catalan of the Marquisate Orani.
The Austrian guard body of 1854 with five arches and pillars decorated with helmets and armor, today room for conferences and exhibitions.
The large public park set up since 1975 in front of the Albornoz Fortress and dedicated to the Resistance, with panoramic views of the city.
Cells in the rock above the Horn Throat.
The fifteenth century palace with the art collection of the twentieth century.
The main street for a quiet walk, shopping or an aperitif.
The house of the saint of immigrants.

Borgo was born around the Cistercian abbey founded in 1134-1136 by the monks of Morimond, the first Cistercian abbey of Lombardy, with the exposed brick church, the monastery that can be visited on four levels and the museum of the painter Angelo Comolli, in the countryside of the Ticino Park.
Baroque church with organ Agati and tower of the thirteenth century.
Wellness in the hills of Pisa.

The ancient oak woods of Serpentara inspired many artists, including Gustave Doré, who designed the dark forest of Dante's Hell; in 1873 the German romantics bought them to save them and in the early twentieth century the sculptor Heinrich Gerhardt built a refuge, donated to the Berlin Academy of Arts. Today it is managed by the Accademia Tedesca Roma Villa Massimo.
A view of the Garda from the hinterland of Verona.

Born for defensive purpose around a thirteenth-century tower with Ghibelline battlements, at the base of which opened the door of the village, it was inherited in 1643 by the Morozzo, who expanded it with a massive body towards the square, a Doric portal and a large staircase. The residence of the family until 1823, today it is of the Municipality: it has salons restored on the first floor and a park with centuries-old trees, it houses temporary exhibitions. Visits from the end of April to October on Sundays and holidays in the afternoon, recommended booking.

It tells the military history of the Julian Alps between Veneto, Carinthia and Slovenia: an introductory multimedia room and it rises on the Napoleonic Wars, the First and the Second World War. Outside there is an open-air museum with the strong Carinthias and the works of Vallo Littorio, partly in recovery. A cumulative ticket with the Geominerary Park €10, reduced €8.
Remains of a fortification of the late nineteenth century, destination of the excursions signalled by the Municipality.
Pinacoteca in the castle Doria Malaspina dedicated to the painter David Beghè.

Built between 1468 and 1473 in the center of the New City and completed in 1524, with Jörg Kölderer's multi-gonal crenellated erker; the Gothic council hall has wooden walls and ceiling beams, the most beautiful of its kind in all Tyrol, and the palace houses the Sala Vigil Raber, one of the oldest theatres in Tyrol, and an art collection. In the courtyard a marble copy of a Roman relief of Mithras; the Tyrolean Diet met there for the first time in 1502 with Massimiliano.
Arts and crafts of rural Calabria.
One of the great historical gardens of the Marche, just returned public.
The church of the ancient village, under the castle.
A live Bronze Age dig.

Instruments, scores, posters, photographs and historical uniforms of the band founded in 1900, with a banner of fanfare of 1885. Open Tuesday and Friday evening and on the first Sunday of the month in the morning; guided tours by reservation.

The museum occupies the original rooms of the monastery, medieval (XII-XIII century) with renovations between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries and restorations concluded in 2009: cloisters, capitular hall, working rooms of the monks, hall of the founders, loggia, refectory and dormitory on four levels. You can visit only with a guide by reservation (about 90 minutes); the cloister also with a separate ticket.
Sabina's wild asparagus.

Ecomuseum spread born from the municipal project of recovery of material culture started in 1996, dedicated to chestnut, once a basic food of the mountain (the bread tree) The heart is an ancient water mill still working, which grinds chestnuts to make flour and houses over 700 ancient tools; from the square a path marked salt in the chestnut groves among centuries-old trees, "benne" for the leaves, curls and dryers. Free admission, also for the holders of Museum Subscription; in 2025 it was open on Sundays from July to October, 10-12 and 15-18. Accessible, with workshops for schools.

Permanent artistic installation in public gardens: a short and accessible path with wooden sculptures, paintings, tree houses and fairy-tale figures that tell the history of the forest; for children there is audio history "The Awakening of the Bosco" on the tourist portal of the municipality.
The place of memory.
the official website announces that the new times of visit of the Apostolic Palace will be published shortly; reservation on tickets.museivaticani.va

In the six rooms of the former canonical house of Roscigno Vecchia, restored by the Superintendence of Salerno: social life, tools of work and everyday life of the peasant world; visits with the volunteers of the Pro Loco.
The church of the balcony.
€3; free with full ticket of the museum area; table for groups €20

Borgo on a hill between citrus groves and vineyards, known worldwide as the set of "Il Padrino" of Coppola: the Mother Church of Norman origin, the church of San Nicolò on the rocky spur, the ruins of the castle of Pentefur and the crypt of the Capuchins with the mummies of the notables.
The birds of the Lario in a small museum of the village.

On the hill of Mattarella, reached on foot along the Via Crucis, built from 1656: fifteen chapels with terracotta statues in life size and the sanctuary; here in 1828 Antonio Rosmini founded the Institute of Charity. UNESCO World Heritage Site, in a nature reserve.
The peasant life of a country of zolfatari.
The historic aquarium of the city, with shapes, lights and colours that recall the sea, among the experiences most loved by children.
The Italian design awarded.
The spa of the city, reported by Visit Tuscany among the wellness places of the Sienese Valdichiana.
Euganean nature and panorama from the top of Gemola.
€4, reduced €2

The village on the hill preserves the remains of the medieval loggia of the Universitas, the Comital Palace of the Gaetani, the churches of Santa Maria de Stampatis and the Santissima Annunziata, Piazza del Pozzo, Piazza San Bernardino, Porta San Marco and the ancient Mulino Florio; in the streams near the ravines for the active wool between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries.
The culture of the Verona mountain in one museum.
The monumental portal.
€8, reduced 6-18 years €4, free FAI membership; with guided tour €15, reduced €11, registered FAI €7

San Bortolo has been inhabited by the Cimbri since 1287; the first church of San Bartolomeo dates back to the beginning of the fifteenth century, and the new, larger one, was built between 1894 and 1904 with the parish priest Don Giobatta Valentini, with facade completed in 1960. Neoclassical façade with four semi-colons Corinthians, tympanum and rose window; single nave interior with four side chapels and dome on the presbytery. Next to the old church the stone bell tower of Lessinia.
Roman finds and frescoes found just a stone's throw from the Duomo.

Guided tour by reservation at the Calvisius plant in Agroittica Lombarda, a caviar producer with a genetic reserve of sturgeons: the route illustrates the life cycles of sturgeons, the fountains and an educational observatory; in the pools flows resurgence water that flows into the property. Six packages combine the visit to the tasting in restaurants in the area. Visits from Monday to Friday at 11 or 5.30 p.m., on Saturday at 11 am only for large groups.

Park of 6,851 hectares shared with Trodena, Mountain, Egna and Salorno, among the foothills of the Val di Fiemme, the Val di Cembra and the valley of the Adige; it takes its name from the Horn of Trodena (1,781 m) and, thanks to the sub-Mediterranean climate, has the flora and fauna richest of species among the natural parks of South Tyrol, with red lilies, martagons and orchids.

Outside the historical walls, it preserves above the main altar a Umbrian-Sienese fresco of the mid-15th century, two other altars and a door made by the local artist Mario Balestra; it reopened in 2025 after a long restoration.
The 98.6 meters high bell tower next to the Basilica, one of the most recognizable monuments of the city.

Small town of Alto Molise, called Cameli until 1896 and now known as "the town of perfumers": the Museum of Perfume, opened in 2014 with over 1,400 pieces of perfumery and a botanical garden, tells this story. In the village the churches of San Michele Arcangelo and Santa Maria delle Grazie have frescoes by the local painter Mario De Tollis.

Founded at the end of the thirteenth century as one of the three new Florentine lands of Valdarno, together with San Giovanni and Castelfranco di Sopra, with the name of Castel Santa Maria, completed in 1337; in 1862 it took its current name in honor of the humanist Poggio Bracciolini. It preserves the fourteenth-century walls with towers of different size and function; in Piazza della Repubblica the Town Hall, and in the center the fourteenth-century churches of San Bartolomeo in Pozzo and San Biagio in Mori. Two Sundays a month the square hosts the Antique Fair.
Marsicano village from the medieval center dominated by the tower of the Rocca Vecchia dei Piccolomini, home of Cardinal Giulio Mazzarino and writer Ignazio Silone, both remembered by museum houses.
The Furious Orlando frescoed in town hall.
Pineta in the Aurunci Mountains Natural Park with picnic area and life path; at Passo Bastia, with tables and benches, starts the path to Mount Fammera.
Walk or ride at the point where the Ticino leaves the lake.
Birdwatching a stone's throw from the sea.

Small alpine village at 1,461 meters near the French border, with the capital Ferrera at the foot of the Moncenisio pass: the Ecomuseum "Le Terre al Confine" tells smugglers, pilgrims and armies past here, the Via Francigena, the Strada dei Marroni and the Fell railway; in the surroundings the Lake Foppa, a fishing reserve.

Born on the initiative of the parish priest Don Nicolao Velotti on the model of the Sacro Monte di Varallo: the project included a large reception complex around the church and a Sacro Monte of over one hundred chapels, largely never realized. The works began in 1616; the first stone of the temple was laid on September 20, 1659 with the support of the Savoys and the works ended in 1888. The Greek cross church (42 x 32 meters) has an octagonal dome 38 meters high with perspectives of Fabrizio Galliari; in the 1930s the Garden of the Madonna was created with the stone fountain called "burnel" . More than 800 meters of altitude between beech and chestnut trees, with a balcony on the plain where you can hear the echo endecasillabo.
Romanesque in pebbles.
Domus de Janas and views on foot from the village.

On the hill that dominates the city, wanted by Frederick II of Swabia in the thirteenth century to defend Vibo, expanded by Angioini and Aragonese and from 1501 fortified residence of the Pignatelli: an irregular complex around a central court, with circular and hexagonal towers and the portal with the coat of arms Pignatelli; the view arrives at the Tyrrhenian, the Serre, the Aspromonte, Sicily and the Aeolian.
Andreas Hofer's baptismal font.

Founded in 1980 in a wing of the ground floor of the Institute including          . Pope John XXIII , preserves about 1,900 pieces among paintings, graphics, sculptures and sketches; the main work is the great cycle .......... The rooms are dedicated to Realism and Abstraction of the twentieth century, Transvanguardia and Informale, photography and to the group Forma 1 (Sanfilippo, Consagra), with works among others by Arnaldo Pomodoro, Guttuso, Fontana, Accardi, Paladino, Rotella and Beuys.

The river Aventino was born in Capo di Fiume, a geosite from which many fossils of the museum come, crosses the village and after about 45 km flows into the Sangro; the Belvedere Mascij overlooks one of its waterfalls.
Fossil dunes and tower over the sea.
From here you turn through walled gardens and alleys.
18th century church in Genoese Baroque style.
Under the cathedral the underground chapel with the urns of the princes and dukes of Massa.
Even today it is the seat of theatre performances of different genres, named after the Zuccari brothers, painters born in Sant'Angelo in Vado.

On the hill of Sarzanello, above the city and the Val di Magra, documented by the X-XI century: Castruccio Castracani chose it as a residence as an imperial vicar (1314-1328) and Tomaso Campofregoso modified it in the fifteenth century. The current aspect is due to Lorenzo de' Medici and to the Francione, with works since 1493 concluded in 1502 by the Republic of Genoa: triangular plant with three corner towers and a large triangular rivet to defend the entrance, reached intact until today. Tuesday-Sunday 10-13 and 16-19, Monday closed; guided tours and audioguide.
Started in 1442 on a project by Giovanni Pace called Sodo, with the façade made by Giorgio Orsini from Šibenik between 1454 and 1459.
The world of beekeeping in the hills.
A walk in nature outside the village.
The portal of the lost castle.
One of the Romanesque churches in the historic center, declared a national monument in 1901.
